detector:cdex-10.summary_technical: Array of 10 kg of p-type point-contact germanium detectors (triple-element strings) immersed directly in liquid nitrogen; physics data from 26 Feb 2017 (C10-B1: Feb 2017 - Aug 2018, 160 eVee threshold). First results 102.8 kg d: SI 8e-42 cm^2 and SD 3e-36 cm^2 at 5 GeV/c^2; 205 kg d later used for sub-GeV, exotic and ultraheavy dark matter searches.

detector:cdex-50.summary_technical: Next-generation CDEX project with a 50 kg germanium detector array in a 1725 m^3 liquid-nitrogen tank at Hall C1 of CJPL-II. Projected spin-independent sensitivity 5.1e-45 cm^2 at 5 GeV/c^2 for a 150 kg yr exposure and a 160 eVee threshold; expected background ~0.01 counts/keVee/kg/day in 2-2.5 keVee.

notes: Placed at site:fermilab-cdf-collision-hall-b0 (the Tevatron B0 interaction hall), created by this owner (colliders-historical); coordinates on that site are campus-precision only, see the site record.
detector:cdf.summary_technical: General-purpose solenoidal collider detector: silicon microstrip tracking plus a large open-cell drift chamber inside a 1.4 T, 4.8 m long, 1.5 m radius superconducting solenoid; lead/scintillator electromagnetic and steel/scintillator hadronic sampling calorimeters (23 layers each); outer muon drift chambers.

notes: Dore (EPJ H 37, 2012): circular magnetised iron plates interspersed with drift chambers, total mass 1250 tonnes.
detector:cdhs-detector.summary_technical: 1250 t iron-plate (toroidal) spectrometer/calorimeter of 19 magnetised iron modules separated by wire drift chambers; a 31 m^3 liquid-hydrogen target was later placed in front to study neutrino interactions in hydrogen.

detector:cdms-i.summary_technical: Four 165 g Ge BLIP (NTD phonon) detectors and a 100 g Si ZIP detector measuring ionization and phonons, in a 20 mK cold volume behind 15 cm Pb, 25 cm polyethylene and a scintillator muon veto at ~17 m.w.e. (Stanford Underground Facility). 1998 Si run (33 live days) and 1998-99 Ge run (96 live days, 3 of 4 detectors; 10.6 kg d after cuts, 15.8 kg d in the later relaxed-fiducial analysis). Limits exclude unexplored space for 10-70 GeV/c^2; 23 candidates consistent with neutron background.

detector:cdms-ii.summary_technical: 19 Ge (~230 g) and 11 Si (~100 g) ionization-and-phonon detectors, 76 mm diameter x ~10 mm thick disks, grouped into five 6-detector towers, operated below 50 mK at Soudan.

detector:cello.summary_technical: CELLO detector at PETRA (1980-1986), described in 'Cello - A New Detector at PETRA', Physica Scripta 23 (1981) 610-622.

detector:charm-detector.summary_technical: 78 marble (CaCO3) plates with proportional tubes and scintillators, surrounded by magnetised iron frames, followed by a muon spectrometer of magnetised iron toroids.

detector:charm-ii-detector.summary_technical: 692 t fine-grained calorimeter with a low-density glass target followed by a magnetic spectrometer.

detector:chooz-detector.summary_technical: Three-region liquid-scintillator calorimeter: ~5 t Gd-loaded (0.09 % by weight) target, unloaded-scintillator gamma catcher and outer veto, about 112 t of scintillator in all, read out by photomultipliers; delayed positron/neutron-capture coincidence.

detector:chorus-detector.summary_technical: 770 kg emulsion target (four stacks of eight modules of 36 plates) with scintillating-fibre target tracker and diamond tracker, air-core hadron spectrometer, calorimeters and magnetised-iron muon spectrometer; tau decays occur on average 1.7 mm from the neutrino vertex.

notes: Some CLAS components (electromagnetic calorimeter, parts of the time-of-flight wall, forward Cherenkov counters) were reused in CLAS12 according to a search-engine summary of CLAS12 design papers that was not verified here; no reuse is asserted.
detector:clas.summary_technical: CEBAF Large Acceptance Spectrometer: six-coil toroidal magnet (largely azimuthal field), drift chambers (0.5% momentum resolution at forward angles), Cherenkov counters, time-of-flight scintillators and electromagnetic calorimeters; designed for a luminosity of ~10^34 nucleon cm^-2 s^-1.

detector:clas12.summary_technical: CLAS12: superconducting torus (forward polar angles up to 35 degrees, drift chambers) plus a superconducting solenoid and vertex tracker (35 to 125 degrees); Cherenkov counters, time-of-flight scintillators and electromagnetic calorimeters for particle identification; momentum resolution 1% forward and 3% central.

detector:class.summary_technical: Four telescopes at 40, 90, 150/220 GHz with front-end variable-delay polarization modulators on constant-elevation (45 deg) scans over 720 deg of azimuth; 40 GHz since 2016, 90 GHz since June 2018.

detector:cleo.summary_technical: CLEO detector: five major upgrades (CLEO-1, CLEO-1.5, CLEO-2 with CsI calorimeter, CLEO-2.5 with silicon vertex detector, CLEO-3 with RICH, CLEO-c); described in 'The CLEO II detector', NIM A320 (1992) 66-113.

notes: Instrument was never built; the record exists so the experiment has a located placement.
detector:cmb-s4.summary_technical: Proposed Stage-4 ground-based CMB experiment: large- and small-aperture telescopes with predominantly dichroic detectors in 11 bands at the South Pole (Dark Sector) and the Parque Astronómico Atacama; never built.

detector:cmd-1.summary_technical: CMD-1 detector, 1979-1984; a published technical description was not retrieved for this record.

detector:cmd-2.summary_technical: CMD-2 detector at VEPP-2M, 1992-2000; a published technical description was not retrieved for this record.

detector:cmd-3.summary_technical: CMD-3: magnetic field 1.0-1.3 T; drift chamber (σ ~100 µm in the transverse plane, 2-3 mm along z); EM calorimeter (LXe, CsI, BGO, 13.5 X0, σ_E/E ~3-10%); TOF; muon counters.

notes: Total mass is recorded as 12 500 t following the source used (2008 JINST paper). The 14 000 t figure that also circulates comes from CMS outreach pages and is recorded as a conflict rather than silently averaged.
ECAL crystal count, tracker silicon area in m² and the tracker |η| acceptance were not found in any source consulted and are therefore absent.
detector:cms.summary_technical: General-purpose 4π collider detector at LHC Point 5: 21.6 m long, 14.6 m in diameter, 12 500 t, built around a 3.8 T superconducting solenoid enclosing an all-silicon pixel and strip tracker, a PbWO4 crystal ECAL and a brass/scintillator HCAL, with four muon stations in the iron flux-return yoke and forward calorimetry to |η| ≤ 5.

detector:cogent.summary_technical: Single modified BEGe p-type point-contact germanium diode (440 g; ~0.4 keVee noise threshold) in a Pb/Cu/polyethylene shield at Soudan (2090 m.w.e.), installed 21 Aug 2009, data from 4 Dec 2009. 2010 PRL: an irreducible excess of bulk-like events below 3 keVee. 2011 PRL (442 live days): a ~2.8 sigma annual modulation. 2013 PRD: detailed background model; no viable background explanation found. 2014: 3.4-year release (1,129 live days) with a modulation amplitude ~4-7 times the standard-halo expectation; maximum-likelihood significance 1.7 sigma, 'well below evidentiary'. An excess is not a discovery.

notes: The technology class is 'other' rather than a TPC class (argon_tpc/noble_liquid_tpc): no source consulted describes CENNS-10 as a time-projection chamber (drift/tracking); it is described as a liquid argon calorimeter.
detector:coherent-cenns-10.summary_technical: 22 kg liquid argon calorimeter (CENNS-10), operating in Neutrino Alley at the SNS since October 2016; produced the first CEvNS-on-argon measurement (2021, >3σ, two independent analyses).

detector:coherent-csi.summary_technical: 14.6 kg CsI[Na] scintillating crystal, low-background configuration, deployed in Neutrino Alley at the SNS; produced the 2017 first observation of CEvNS (6.7σ) and the 2022 cross-section measurement from the full dataset before decommissioning.

notes: Mass conflict: the official detector-suite page (undated, accessed 2026) describes a planned 10 kg array for 2020; the 2024 evidence paper (arXiv:2406.13806) describes an 8 × 2.2 kg = 17.6 kg array (Ge-Mini) operated June-August 2023, when seven of the eight detectors were installed in the shield and five were stable enough for analysis (active mass (10.66 ± 0.09) kg). specs.target_mass below uses the Ge-Mini figure, which is the one that actually produced the sourced physics result; the 10 kg figure is recorded only in the interval note above.
detector:coherent-ge.summary_technical: Ge-Mini: array of eight 2.2 kg inverted-coaxial point-contact (ICPC) high-purity germanium detectors, 1.5 keVee analysis threshold, operated at the SNS June-August 2023; yielded a 3.9σ rejection of the no-CEvNS hypothesis on natural germanium (2024).

notes: The detector-suite page also describes a planned expansion to several tonnes of NaI[Tl] ('NaIvETe'); no primary source consulted describes its actual (as opposed to planned) mass or commissioning date, so it is not recorded as a separate sourced interval or spec.
detector:coherent-nai.summary_technical: NaIvE-185: 185 kg NaI[Tl] scintillator detector installed in Neutrino Alley at the SNS in June 2016, used for charged-current neutrino interaction studies on 127-I and CEvNS background characterization ahead of a planned ton-scale expansion.

notes: technology_classes uses 'other': no listed technology_class names a curved-solenoid muon-transport spectrometer of this kind.
detector:comet.summary_technical: Curved-solenoid pion capture and muon transport system selecting low-momentum, negatively-charged muons off an 8 GeV, 3.2 kW J-PARC proton beam, feeding a detector solenoid instrumented for Phase-I with CyDet (cylindrical drift chamber + trigger hodoscope) and, for background studies toward Phase-II, StrECAL (straw tracker + electromagnetic calorimeter).

detector:compass.summary_technical: COMPASS: polarised target in a superconducting solenoid (muon beam), two-stage large-angle / large-momentum spectrometer with several types of tracking detectors, RICH counter, hadron and electromagnetic calorimeters and muon filters; reused as the AMBER backbone.

detector:connie-detector.summary_technical: Cryogenic array of low-noise fully depleted scientific CCDs (readout noise < 2 e- RMS) in a vacuum vessel inside a 30 cm polyethylene / 15 cm lead / 30 cm polyethylene shield; 8 CCDs analysed in 2016 and 2019; skipper-CCDs added in 2021.

notes: One detector record covers both phases: the CONUS+ overview paper (arXiv:2407.11912) states the CEvNS signature 'will be measured with the same four point-contact high-purity germanium (HPGe) detectors produced for the former experiment, however refurbished'.
detector:conus-hpge-array.summary_technical: Array of four 1 kg point-contact high-purity germanium (HPGe) spectrometers with sub-300 eV ionization thresholds; operated at Brokdorf (2018-2023, 17.1 m from a 3.9 GWth reactor core) and, refurbished, at Leibstadt from November 2023 (20.7 m from a 3.6 GWth reactor core; 2.83 kg active mass from 3 of 4 detectors in the first CONUS+ analysis).

detector:cosine-100.summary_technical: Eight NaI(Tl) crystals (106 kg, two 3-inch PMTs each) immersed in 2,200 L of LAB liquid scintillator (active veto) inside a copper box, a 20 cm lead castle and plastic-scintillator muon panels, in the Y2L A5 tunnel (700 m overburden). Physics data 21 Oct 2016 - 14 Mar 2023 (6.4 yr). Annual-modulation analyses (1.7 yr, 3 yr, 6.4 yr full data set), WIMP limits with a 1 keV and then 0.7 keV threshold, and a combined analysis with ANAIS-112.

detector:cosine-100u.summary_technical: Eight NaI(Tl) crystals (99.1 kg) with direct PMT coupling through silicone optical pads and 45-degree beveled crystal edges (light yield 15.8-27.7 p.e./keV), liquid-scintillator veto in a low-temperature room at about -30 C at Yemilab (the 2024 facility paper planned to reuse the copper box with about 2 tonnes of liquid scintillator and to remake the shielding) (about 1,000 m overburden, muon flux about 1e-7 /cm2/s). Physics data since September 2025 at room temperature and since May 2026 at -30 C.

notes: Design values of the first configuration: eight modules (COSINUS-1pi Run 1).
detector:cosinus.summary_technical: Undoped NaI crystals operated as cryogenic scintillating calorimeters: phonon channel read by transition edge sensors on a carrier crystal (remoTES) and light channel by a silicon beaker detector, giving event-by-event e/gamma versus nuclear-recoil discrimination and a low nuclear-recoil threshold; dry dilution refrigerator (9.3 mK reached) in a 7 m water tank with a Cherenkov muon veto of about 30 PMTs, in Hall B of LNGS (3600 m.w.e.). COSINUS-1pi Run 1: eight modules, goal 100 kg d; Run 2: up to 1000 kg d. Prototype: 441 eV nuclear-recoil baseline resolution (3.67 g crystal); O(pb) spin-independent sensitivity with 11.6 g d (underground, 2023).

detector:cosme.summary_technical: 234 g natural-abundance p-type coaxial HPGe crystal (0.43 keV FWHM at 10.37 keV; 2.5 keV threshold), in a PNNL electroformed-copper cryostat inside the IGEX archaeological-lead shield with muon veto at 2450 m.w.e. 72.7 kg d (1998-1999) give WIMP exclusion plots for low masses and a 95% C.L. limit g < 2.8e-9 GeV^-1 on the axion-photon coupling (Primakoff conversion with Bragg scattering).

detector:coupp-2kg.summary_technical: 1.5 kg CF3I, natural-quartz bell jar, cameras; built at the University of Chicago, operated in the NuMI/MINOS tunnel at Fermilab; pressure vessel reused for COUPP-4kg.

detector:coupp-4kg.summary_technical: Synthetic fused-silica bell jar in the stainless-steel pressure vessel of COUPP-2kg, CF3I (3.5 kg at Fermilab, 4.0 kg at SNOLAB), piezoelectric acoustic sensors, cameras, water shield (and a liquid-scintillator muon veto at the Fermilab site).

notes: No page consulted gives the number of modules in operation or a precise operating temperature (mK).
detector:cresst.summary_technical: Cryogenic transition-edge-sensor calorimeters on scintillating crystal absorbers: sapphire in CRESST-I (2000-2003), 300 g CaWO4 crystals in CRESST-II (2003-2019), and ~25 g CaWO4/Al2O3/LiAlO4 crystals in CRESST-III (from 2019) reaching nuclear-recoil thresholds of 10 eV and lower.

detector:crex.summary_technical: Hall A high-resolution spectrometers with an isotopically enriched 48Ca target measuring the parity-violating asymmetry in elastic scattering of longitudinally polarised electrons.

detector:crystal-ball.summary_technical: Crystal Ball: 672 NaI(Tl) crystals, covering 94% of 4π steradians, hermetically sealed in two stainless-steel hemispheres; later used at BNL and Mainz.

notes: The document list is derived from the document records and is not stored here.

No source consulted (checked 2026-10-25) gives the current per-site counts of installed and operating Medium- and Small-Sized Telescopes, as opposed to the design maximums; the press release of 15 October 2026 reports the four-telescope LST sub-array at CTAO-North as complete, with commissioning of the array still ahead.
detector:ctao.summary_technical: Imaging-atmospheric-Cherenkov arrays at two sites (La Palma / Paranal), using Large-, Medium- and Small-Sized Telescope classes (design maximum 4 LST + 23 MST + 37 SST) to cover 20 GeV-300 TeV; under construction as of 2026-10-25 (CTAO press release of 2026-10-15 on the completed LST sub-array).

notes: The cited source for this placement (checked 2026-09-17) only confirms 'INFN's Gran Sasso National Laboratory' generally, not the Hall A designation specifically. CUORE's presence in Hall A is well established in the literature (e.g. CUORE cryostat papers), but no directly fetchable primary or official source stating 'Hall A' verbatim for CUORE was found, so the placement's confidence is 'approximate' rather than 'verified'.
detector:cuore.summary_technical: Array of 988 TeO2 bolometric crystals (19 towers, ~0.8 t crystal mass) operated at ~10 mK in a dedicated cryostat in LNGS Hall A.

detector:cuoricino-detector.summary_technical: 13 planes of 62 TeO2 bolometers (44 cubes of 5 cm and 18 of 3x3x6 cm), 40.7 kg active mass, NTD thermistors, ~8 mK base temperature, dilution refrigerator shielded against radioactivity and neutrons.

notes: The cited sources confirm LNGS generally, not the Hall A designation specifically. CUPID is planned to reuse the CUORE cryostat, which the atlas places in Hall A (detector:cuore), but no source consulted (checked 2026-10-25) states 'Hall A' for CUPID verbatim; confidence in the placement is 'uncertain' for this reason as well as the unconfirmed construction timeline.
detector:cupid.summary_technical: Planned array of ~1500 Li2MoO4 scintillating bolometers targeting 100Mo (Qbb = 3034 keV), to be installed in the existing CUORE cryostat at LNGS.

detector:cusb.summary_technical: CUSB: non-magnetic NaI and lead-glass shower detector (CUSB-II: BGO scintillation counters replacing the tracking chambers).

notes: One record for the PHASE 0 prototype (LIME, 50 L) and the PHASE 1 demonstrator (CYGNO-04, 0.4 m^3, under construction); the volumes are separate specs.
detector:cygno.summary_technical: CYGNus module with Optical readout: He:CF4 (60:40) atmospheric-pressure TPC with triple-GEM amplification and optical readout (sCMOS camera for X-Y, PMTs for the drift coordinate). PHASE 0: 50 L LIME prototype, commissioned overground at LNF and installed underground at LNGS in February 2022 (about 27 months of data in five shielding configurations). PHASE 1: CYGNO-04, a 0.4 m^3 back-to-back TPC in LNGS Hall F, under construction; PHASE 2 aims at O(30) m^3. Part of the CYGNUS proto-collaboration; INITIUM ERC grant.

notes: Placed at site:fermilab-d0-collision-hall (the Tevatron D0 interaction hall), created by this owner (colliders-historical); coordinates on that site are campus-precision only, see the site record.
detector:d0.summary_technical: General-purpose collider detector, complementary to CDF, with uranium/liquid-argon calorimetry retained from Run I; upgraded for Run II (2001) with a silicon microstrip tracker, central fiber tracker, solenoidal magnet, preshower detectors, forward muon detector and forward proton detector added around the original calorimeters and muon system.

detector:dama-libra.summary_technical: 25 NaI(Tl) detectors (9.70 kg each) in a 5x5 configuration, two PMTs each; phase1 PMTs replaced in 2010 by Hamamatsu R6233MOD PMTs (quantum efficiency 33-39% at 420 nm) for phase2, lowering the software threshold to 1 keV.

detector:dama-nai.summary_technical: Nine NaI(Tl) crystals of 9.70 kg, two PMTs each, 10 cm quartz light guides, sealed Cu box flushed with high-purity nitrogen, Cu/Pb/Cd foils/polyethylene-paraffin shield and 1 m of concrete (arXiv:astro-ph/0307403).

detector:damic.summary_technical: CCD array: seven 16-Mpixel CCDs (6.0 g each, ~42 g total) in the 2017-2018 SNOLAB run (11 kg-day exposure); later replaced/supplemented by two 24-Mpixel skipper CCDs for a low-energy-threshold run through at least January 2024. Per a 2025 SNOLAB workshop report, the detector has since been repurposed as a background test stand.

notes: 'LBC' (Low Background Chamber) is a prototype-scale device; no source consulted describes a larger final-scale DAMIC-M detector as installed.
detector:damic-m.summary_technical: 20 g skipper-CCD 'Low Background Chamber' prototype at LSM (Modane); commissioned 2022, with a 1.257 kg-day analysed exposure reported in a November 2025 daily-modulation search for sub-MeV hidden-sector dark matter.

detector:danss-detector.summary_technical: Highly segmented plastic scintillator (2500 one-metre strips with Gd-loaded reflective cover), 1 m^3 sensitive volume, SiPM/PMT readout, composite shield; movable by a lifting gear between 10.7 and 12.7 m from the core.

detector:darkside-20k.summary_technical: Dual-phase (two-phase) liquid argon TPC, 50 t active mass, SiPM-based light readout, in LNGS Hall C. Under construction as of 2026-10-25 (LNGS DarkSide page, undated: 'currently under construction in the LNGS Hall-C'; arXiv:2402.07566, February 2024, reports the construction phase under way).

detector:darkside-50.summary_technical: Dual-phase argon TPC, ~50 kg nominal active mass (46.4±0.7 kg measured), surrounded by a 30 t liquid-scintillator neutron veto inside a 1 kt water-Cherenkov muon veto, in LNGS Hall C.

detector:darkside-lowmass.summary_technical: Conceptual design (Phys. Rev. D 107, 112006): dual-phase LAr TPC in an acrylic vessel viewed by two photosensor arrays, inside a bath of underground argon (veto) in a cryostat in a water tank, optimised for an electron-counting (ionisation-only) analysis with 2 or 4 electron thresholds; projected sensitivity to GeV-scale dark matter down to the solar-neutrino floor and to 10 MeV/c^2 with the Migdal effect or electron scattering. The 2025 SNOLAB report gives 1.5 t (1 t fiducial) and a primary plan to place the inner detector in the DEAP-3600 water tank; the 2022 paper left the site open ('LNGS or a lab comparably far from Aria'). No approval or funding decision was found.

detector:darksphere.summary_technical: Proposed 3 m diameter electroformed-copper spherical proportional counter with a 60-anode ACHINOS sensor, He-isobutane gas, inside a 2.5 m water shield in the Large Experimental Cavern at Boulby.

detector:dasi.summary_technical: 13-element, co-planar interferometric array operating in ten 1-GHz bands spanning 26-36 GHz, on the inner of two towers attached to MAPO; temperature anisotropy 140 < l < 900 (2000) and polarization (2001-2003).

notes: Modelled as a single detector-system record covering all (six, later eight) functionally identical antineutrino detectors, per the detector paper's own description of them as 'functionally identical'; individual AD1-AD8 unit records are not in the Atlas.
detector:daya-bay-antineutrino-detectors.summary_technical: Six (2011-2012), then eight (2012-2016), then seven (2017-2020) functionally identical Gd-doped liquid-scintillator antineutrino detectors, each ~20 t target mass, deployed across the Daya Bay near, Ling Ao near and far underground halls.

notes: DEAP-3600 is a single-phase liquid argon scintillation detector, not a two-phase TPC: it has no drift field and no ionization/charge readout, and detects only scintillation light via its 255 PMTs (see the sourced 'technology' field above). Its technology classes list 'noble_liquid_tpc'/'argon_tpc' only because the available classes have no dedicated scintillator-only class; this is a classification accommodation, not a claim that DEAP-3600 has TPC charge readout.

Energy threshold: not recorded as a spec. The detector paper's design table (Table 1) gives a nominal analysis threshold of 15 keVee (electron-equivalent) for a 3 tonne-year exposure, not a nuclear-recoil energy; no source consulted (checked 2026-10-25) states a single nuclear-recoil analysis energy threshold for DEAP-3600.
detector:deap-3600.summary_technical: Single-phase LAr scintillation detector: 85 cm radius, 5 cm thick acrylic vessel, TPB-coated for VUV-to-visible wavelength shifting, holding a 3600 kg design/~3300 kg maintained fill (1000 kg, 55 cm-radius fiducial volume), read out by 255 8-inch Hamamatsu R5912-HQE PMTs. No drift field or charge readout; particle identification relies entirely on pulse-shape discrimination of the scintillation pulse. Located 2 km underground (6000 m.w.e.) at SNOLAB.

detector:dear.summary_technical: DEAR: pressurised cryogenic target cell (11 cm diameter, 75 µm kapton) surrounded by 16 CCD-55 chips (116 cm² in total, 150 eV resolution at 6 keV) with in-beam calibration from fluorescence foils in the cell; soft X-ray background about 70 times the signal (Marton 2007).

detector:decam.summary_technical: DECam: 2.2-degree diameter field, 62 2k×4k imaging CCDs and 12 guide/focus CCDs, five-element corrector, seven filters, at the prime focus of the Blanco 4-m telescope.

detector:deeme.summary_technical: H-line spectrometer with a 110 msr acceptance, dipole magnet and four high-voltage-switched MWPCs with FADC readout; electrons of 105 MeV/c from a graphite target.

detector:delight.summary_technical: ~1 L superfluid 4He cell (first cell planned at 10 L in earlier papers) with about 50 sapphire-wafer LAMCALs (40 cm^2 each), SQUID readout, film burner, dilution refrigerator at ~10 mK.

detector:delphi.summary_technical: General-purpose LEP detector, about 10 m in length and diameter, with roughly 20 subdetectors: a Ring Imaging Cherenkov (RICH) system for full charged-particle identification and a high-precision silicon vertex detector for short-lived-particle tracking, alongside standard tracking, calorimetry and muon systems.

notes: No detector-level specs are recorded beyond the experiment key specs; the telescope itself (Mayall 4-m) belongs to Kitt Peak.
detector:desi-instrument.summary_technical: DESI prime-focus system on the 4-m Mayall telescope: 3.2-deg diameter corrector, 5020 robotic fibre positioners on a 0.812 m focal surface, ten spectrographs covering 360–980 nm at resolution 2000–5000.

detector:dm-ice17.summary_technical: Two modules, each an 8.5 kg NaI(Tl) crystal with two photomultipliers in a stainless-steel pressure vessel, co-deployed with IceCube at 2457 m depth (about 2200 m.w.e.). Physics run 16 June 2011 - 28 January 2015, exposure 60.8 kg yr; background 7.9 +- 0.4 counts/day/keV/kg at 6.5-8.0 keVee; no annual modulation in 4-20 keV. The crystals were previously used by NAIAD at Boulby.

detector:dm32.summary_technical: Three 10.7 kg NaI(Tl) modules (32.1 kg in all), originally an active veto of a germanium double-beta experiment, at Canfranc; 4613.6 kg d of data (May 1993 - December 1994) analysed for an excess in the total rate and for annual modulation; competitive spin-independent and spin-dependent limits, with the modulation analysis improving the excluded parameter space by about two orders of magnitude (per the 2026 review).

detector:dmradio.summary_technical: Lumped-element LC-resonator axion haloscopes: DMRadio-50L (1 T toroidal magnet, 5 kHz-5 MHz) on the Stanford University campus and DMRadio-m3 (4 T solenoidal magnet, 30-200 MHz) at SLAC; under construction as of the October 2022 status paper (arXiv:2210.07215); a July 2026 paper (arXiv:2607.05771) reports measured performance of the DMRadio-50L cryogenic system and refers to future data taking.

notes: Records the 10-liter detector (surface run at MIT, then WIPP). The 20-liter and 1 m^3 detectors were only plans or under commissioning in the sources read and are not recorded.
detector:dmtpc.summary_technical: Low-pressure (75 Torr) CF4 dual back-to-back TPC with CCD (proportional scintillation) and charge readout, 10-liter detector with a 3.3 g CF4 target. MIT surface run (35.7 g d, 80-200 keV): spin-dependent WIMP-proton limit 2.0e-33 cm^2 at 115 GeV/c^2 (90% CL). Moved to the Waste Isolation Pilot Plant (1.6 km w.e.) in October 2010; a 20-liter detector was commissioned at MIT. 2017: model of the directional response of two detectors at 30-60 torr.

detector:donut.summary_technical: Hybrid emulsion-target (nuclear-emulsion sheets interspersed with steel/iron sheets, an emulsion-cloud-chamber-style target) followed by electronic scintillator counters and drift-chamber spectrometers, at a Tevatron fixed-target beam dump.

notes: Modelled as a single detector record covering both the near and far detectors, which the sources describe as (near-)identical designs.
detector:double-chooz.summary_technical: Gd-loaded liquid-scintillator detectors (four nested cylindrical liquid volumes: Gd-loaded target, Gd-free gamma catcher, buffer oil, scintillator veto), ~10.3 m³ fiducial volume, at near (400 m, from the end of 2014) and far (1050 m, from the 2012 result onward) halls at the Chooz reactor site.

detector:drift.summary_technical: Directional Recoil Identification From Tracks: low-pressure negative-ion CS2 (with CF4) time projection chambers (DRIFT-I, DRIFT-IIa-d, 0.8 m^3 fiducial) at Boulby, 1100 m rock (2800 m.w.e.). DRIFT-IId spin-dependent WIMP-proton limits: 0.5 pb at 100 GeV/c^2 (47.4 live days, 2010) improved to 0.28 pb (54.7 live days, 2017).

detector:dune-far-detector-1.summary_technical: Single-phase horizontal-drift LArTPC: 17.5 kt of liquid argon in a 15.1 × 14.0 × 62.0 m membrane cryostat, at least 10 kt fiducial, four drift volumes at 500 V/cm with a 3.5 m maximum drift and 150 APAs of wire readout, plus a photon detection system.

notes: Most quantities are unresolved: only the arXiv abstract of the vertical-drift TDR was consulted.
detector:dune-far-detector-2.summary_technical: Vertical-drift LArTPC module: a horizontal cathode bisects the volume, creating two stacked drift regions with charge readout planes at top and bottom. Technical Design Report published December 2023. Masses and drift length not sourced.

notes: Status "proposed" reflects the evidence available: the ND CDR (2021) is the latest near-detector design document consulted (checked 2026-09-16), and none of the sources consulted gives a construction milestone.
detector:dune-near-detector.summary_technical: Composite near detector just downstream of the LBNF target: ND-LAr (modular ArgonCube LArTPC), a downstream muon spectrometer (TMS on day one, later ND-GAr) that can move off axis for DUNE-PRISM, and SAND, a magnetised on-axis beam monitor reusing the KLOE solenoid and calorimeter.

detector:e821.summary_technical: Muon storage ring fed by a 24 GeV/c AGS proton beam through a pion/muon channel and inflector; positron calorimeters measure the spin-precession frequency. The same magnet was relocated to Fermilab in 2013.

detector:e949.summary_technical: Stopped-kaon spectrometer at BNL, successor to the E787 apparatus, tracking the decay pion's range, energy and kinematics to isolate K⁺ → π⁺ ν ν̄ candidates from background.

detector:echo-detector.summary_technical: ECHo-1k: 72-pixel MMC array (gold or silver absorbers, Au:Er/Ag:Er sensors, 163Ho implanted) with SQUID readout; ECHo-100k uses wafer-scale implanted multiplexed arrays.

notes: The NbSi transition-edge sensor is operated at about 44 mK (arXiv:2211.04176: 'The TES is operated around 44 mK'; arXiv:2203.03993 gives the same working temperature). The cryostat base temperature and the operating temperatures of earlier detector generations (Ge-NTD sensors, EDELWEISS-I/II/III arrays) are not given by the sources consulted (checked 2026-10-25), and no official site could be reached for them.
detector:edelweiss.summary_technical: Germanium bolometer with combined ionization and phonon readout; the current sub-GeV programme instruments a 200 g crystal with an NbSi TES and Neganov-Trofimov-Luke phonon amplification, reaching a 30 eV analysis threshold and 4.46 eV electron-recoil resolution.

detector:elegant-v-nai.summary_technical: ELEGANT V (ELEctron GAmma-ray Neutrino Telescope V) at the Oto Cosmo Observatory: 16 NaI(Tl) scintillators (0.76 tons) inside lead and copper shields with drift chambers and plastic scintillators around a 100Mo double-beta source; the NaI array was used for dark matter searches (spin-dependent limits and an annual modulation search per the 2002 overview). An earlier configuration with nine NaI modules (central 36.5 kg detector) was deployed at Kamioka in 1992 (threshold 4 keV, background ~5.1 cpd/kg/keV at 5 keV).

detector:epic.summary_technical: ePIC central detector (about 9.5 m long, 2.67 m radius, 3-177 degrees) in a 1.7 T field from a 2.8 m bore superconducting solenoid: silicon vertex/tracking layers and micro-pattern gas detectors (about 7.5 m^2 and 34.4 m^2), fast timing and Cherenkov PID, electromagnetic and hadronic calorimeters; far-forward and far-backward detectors extend the acceptance to |eta| > 6.

detector:essnusb-far-detector.summary_technical: Two cylindrical caverns (78 m high, 78 m diameter) at 1000 m depth in the Zinkgruvan mine with 540 kt of water, about 92,000 PMTs and 30 % photocathode coverage; 1.2 us time gate for each of the 14 beam pulses per second.

detector:essnusb-near-detector.summary_technical: Proposed 1 kt underground water-Cherenkov near detector on the ESS site 250 m from the target station, with a tracking detector of one million 1 cm^3 scintillator cubes in a dipole magnet and an emulsion stack immersed in water.

notes: Placed at site:wipp-surface-campus (kind: campus, approximate); no rank<=7 source gives an underground coordinate distinct from the WIPP campus point.
detector:exo-200.summary_technical: Cylindrical liquid-xenon time projection chamber, xenon enriched to 80.6% in 136Xe, with combined ionization and scintillation readout; located ~655 m underground at WIPP.

notes: No dimension/mass specs were sourced; left out rather than guessed.
Status shutdown matches experiment:faser (Long Shutdown 3).
detector:faser.summary_technical: Forward spectrometer plus FASERv (emulsion film / tungsten target-detector) subdetector, installed in TI12 during LS2 (2019-2021), operating since LHC Run 3 (July 2022).

notes: The detector technology is not described in the sources fetched, so `technology` is null.
detector:fenice.summary_technical: FENICE detector: technology not described in the sources fetched (the INFN-LNF page shows a picture only).

notes: No coordinate for the DAΦNE second interaction region is published in the sources fetched.
detector:finuda.summary_technical: FINUDA: TOFINO scintillator barrel (12 slabs), ISIM silicon microstrip octagon around eight targets, OSIM silicon modules, planar low-mass drift chambers (70% He, 30% isobutane), six-layer straw tubes and the 72-slab TOFONE time-of-flight barrel inside a 1.0 T superconducting solenoid; design momentum resolution 0.4% FWHM for 270 MeV/c π⁻.

notes: The placement site is an approximate region marker (see site:dugway-flys-eye).
detector:flys-eye.summary_technical: Air-fluorescence detector: Fly's Eye I with 67 mirrors (1.5 m diameter, 880 PMT pixels, full-sky coverage) and Fly's Eye II with 36 mirrors, 3.3-3.4 km away, giving monocular and stereo reconstruction at 1017-1020 eV.

detector:frejus-detector.summary_technical: Tracking calorimeter: 912 flash-chamber planes (5 mm x 5 mm cells) between 3 mm iron plates, with 113 planes of Geiger tubes (15 mm cells) giving a trigger of grouped hits in about 1 m^3 (threshold about 200 MeV); cells alternate vertical and horizontal for two orthogonal views.

detector:g0.summary_technical: G0: superconducting toroidal magnetic spectrometer (eight octants) with plastic scintillation detectors, aerogel Cherenkov counters for the backward-angle configuration, cryogenic hydrogen/deuterium target, beam monitors and fast time-encoding electronics counting individual events; forward configuration detects recoil protons, backward configuration scattered electrons near 110 degrees.

detector:gallex-gno.summary_technical: Radiochemical gallium detector, 30.3 t Ga as 101 t GaCl3-HCl solution, at LNGS Hall A; 71Ga(νe,e⁻)71Ge reaction, chemically extracted and counted in campaigns rather than observed in real time.

notes: No placement is recorded: no fetched source locates the hall of the PS neutrino area, and the chamber later moved to the SPS (home.cern: before moving to the SPS until 1979). Placing it on the CERN campus point would make that site take its timeline from this detector alone (the globe derives a site's presence from the detectors placed there) and hide the campus outside 1970-1979, so the experiment sits on facility:cern and the collaboration names the campus site as its host, as for UA1.
detector:gargamelle.summary_technical: Heavy-liquid bubble chamber (CF3Br), 4.8 m long and 2 m in diameter, about 1000 t, photographed in the PS (1970-76) and SPS neutrino beams.

detector:gbar.summary_technical: Positron source (9 MeV linac on a tungsten target), positron accumulation traps, a positronium converter, a pulsed drift tube for the ELENA antiprotons and a free-fall chamber with annihilation detectors.

detector:genius-tf.summary_technical: Test facility between halls A and B of LNGS: first four naked HPGe diodes (10.52 kg total) installed in liquid nitrogen on 5 May 2003, six (15 kg) from October 2004 (GENIUS-TF-II); planned 40 kg of natural Ge to test the DAMA annual-modulation signature. Found a 222Rn-daughter background about 200 times the simulation and limited long-term stability (rising leakage currents).

detector:gerda.summary_technical: Array of bare, enriched (76Ge) high-purity germanium point-contact detectors (~40 kg total) submerged directly in a 64 m³ liquid-argon cryostat that serves as both cooling medium and active veto, in LNGS Hall A.

detector:gluex.summary_technical: GlueX beamline and detector: tagged linearly polarised photon beam; central straw-tube drift chamber and six packages of planar cathode-strip/drift-wire chambers in a 2 T solenoid; cylindrical scintillating-fibre barrel calorimeter inside the magnet and a lead-glass forward calorimeter; time-of-flight and a later DIRC for kaon identification.

notes: No source consulted gives surveyed antenna coordinates for the array itself; the placement uses the XiaoDuShan site position published by the GRAND Collaboration (arXiv:2307.12769: E 93.94177, N 40.99434, about 150 km north of Dunhuang city), see site:grandproto300-dunhuang.
detector:grand.summary_technical: GRANDProto300 pathfinder array in the Gobi Desert near Dunhuang, China: grew from a 13-antenna stage (deployed 2023-06) to a 65-antenna stage covering ~30 km² (2025-04), validating the radio-detection approach for the full GRAND design.

detector:grapes-3.summary_technical: GRAPES-3: 400 scintillator detectors (1 m2 each, 25,000 m2) and the 560 m2 muon telescope G3MT (3,712 proportional counters, 16 modules, 1 GeV threshold).

notes: The document list is derived from the document records and is not stored here.
detector:h-e-s-s.summary_technical: Hybrid imaging-atmospheric-Cherenkov array: four 12 m telescopes (since 2002) plus a central 28 m telescope (CT5, commissioning date not given by the collaboration's pages as read on 2026-10-25) at 1800 m in the Khomas Highland, Namibia.

notes: No detector paper or technical design report was consulted for H1 subsystem specifications, so no specs are recorded.
detector:h1.summary_technical: General-purpose ep collider detector at HERA, combining high-precision tracking, calorimetry and muon systems to reconstruct deep inelastic scattering events; exact subsystem specifications are not sourced.

detector:hades.summary_technical: HADES: ring imaging gas Cherenkov detector, tracking system of 6 superconducting coils with drift chambers, multiplicity and electron trigger array, two-stage trigger; 85% azimuthal coverage over 18-85 degrees, single-electron efficiency 50%, vector-meson mass resolution 2.5%.

notes: No Appendix A technology class fits a non-imaging wavefront-sampling Cherenkov array; `other` is used with the technique described in the sourced `technology` string (A24).
detector:hagar.summary_technical: Seven telescopes at the centre and corners of a hexagon inscribed in a circle of 50 m radius; each has seven parabolic glass mirrors of 0.9 m diameter with f/d = 1; total reflector area about 31 m2.

detector:happex.summary_technical: HAPPEX in Hall A: twin High Resolution Spectrometers (5 msr each in HAPPEX-III) focusing elastically scattered electrons onto total-absorption shower counters read out by integration over the helicity period; Compton and Moller polarimeters; superconducting septum magnets for the 6-degree HAPPEX-II and HAPPEX-He runs.

notes: The tank count (commonly cited elsewhere as 300) is not recorded: no source consulted states it (the design paper's text could not be extracted and the official site was unreachable). A technical source that states it would settle it.
detector:hawc.summary_technical: Water-Cherenkov extensive-air-shower array at 4100 m on Sierra Negra, Mexico; full-array operations since March 2015. Tank count and individual tank dimensions are not recorded (the source papers with those specifications could not be read).

detector:haystac.summary_technical: Tunable microwave cavity haloscope at Yale Wright Laboratory using inverse-Primakoff axion-to-photon conversion in a static magnetic field, with a Josephson parametric amplifier / squeezed-vacuum receiver for sub-quantum-limited noise.

detector:hdms.summary_technical: Two concentric HPGe detectors in one cryostat: a small p-type inner crystal (202 g in the prototype; later replaced by a crystal of enriched 73Ge, which adds spin-dependent sensitivity) is the WIMP target; a 2.1 kg well-type outer crystal is the anticoincidence shield. Prototype at LNGS March 1998 to July 1999 (natural Ge; 9.9 kg d, 2 keV threshold); final setup from August 2000 (5 keV threshold; 26.74 kg d in 2002; 85.48 kg d in a spin-dependent WIMP-neutron analysis cited in 2006).

notes: The imaging telescopes were dismantled in September 2002 (official page).
detector:hegra.summary_technical: Combined complex: stereoscopic IACT system (8.5 m2 mirrors, 271-pixel cameras, FoV about 4.6 deg), AIROBICC wide-angle Cherenkov counters, scintillator array, muon towers, plus CRT and CLUE.

detector:heidelberg-moscow-detector.summary_technical: Five p-type HPGe crystals (19.2 kg of 86 % enriched 76Ge in total, 10.96 kg active mass); four in a common 30 cm lead shield in a radon-free nitrogen atmosphere with 10 cm borated polyethylene and scintillator veto, one in a separate copper and lead box.

detector:hera-b.summary_technical: HERA-B: vertex detector, extensive tracking and particle-identification systems with large geometrical acceptance (up to 160 mrad vertically), target system of two stations of four wires.

detector:herald.summary_technical: Superfluid 4He cell (HeRALD v0.1: 2.75 cm high, 6 cm diameter, ~10 g He) facing a photon/4He TES calorimeter wafer; a Cs-coated film stopper blocks superfluid film flow so the sensor stays dry.

detector:hermes.summary_technical: HERMES forward spectrometer: numerous tracking chambers (micro-strip gas chambers, drift and proportional chambers) in front of and behind a 1.3 T m dipole magnet, RICH and calorimetry, internal polarised gas target; a recoil detector was added in 2006.

detector:hires.summary_technical: HiRes-I (22 telescope modules, 3-17 degrees elevation) and HiRes-II (42 modules, 3-31 degrees), each module a 3.7 m2 spherical mirror with a 256-PMT camera of 1 degree pixels; 12.6 km apart for stereo.

detector:holmes-detector.summary_technical: Mo/Cu TES microcalorimeters on SiNx membranes with 163Ho implanted at about 100 Å depth in a 180×180 µm² gold layer, rf-SQUID microwave multiplexing; 48 active pixels in the 2025 runs.

notes: Coordinate caveat: the site referenced (site:surf-surface-campus) is a surface campus point, not the detector's true ~1478 m underground location; see placement note.
detector:homestake.summary_technical: Radiochemical chlorine-argon detector, 380 m³ perchloroethylene target, 1478 m (4850 ft) underground in the Homestake mine; built 1965-1967, operational from 1967 (standard data set 1970-1994), measured 37Ar production rate 2.56±0.16(stat)±0.16(syst) SNU.

detector:hps.summary_technical: HPS: tungsten foil target, silicon micro-strip vertex tracker (SVT) in a dipole magnet, PbWO4 electromagnetic calorimeter (ECal) providing the trigger and timing, and a scintillation hodoscope (SH).

detector:hrs.summary_technical: HRS detector at PEP (29 GeV e⁺e⁻); the 1990 four-lepton QED paper used 291 pb⁻¹. Subsystems were not recorded.

notes: PMT count is unresolved between two figures on the same official site (20,000 vs 'about 40,000'); both are noted rather than picking one silently.

experiment_ids includes experiment:t2k alongside experiment:hyper-kamiokande: Hyper-Kamiokande is sited and designed (Tochibora mine, ~295 km from J-PARC, same 2.5 degree off-axis angle) to serve as the far detector for the continuing J-PARC neutrino beam programme that T2K operates, as its successor experiment comes online; see src:hk-design-report-2018 and src:t2k-and-beyond-page.
detector:hyper-kamiokande.summary_technical: Water Cherenkov detector under construction, 68 m diameter x 71 m height, 260 kt total / 188 kt fiducial mass. Inner detector design centres on new large-aperture PMTs (order 20,000-40,000 depending on which official figure is used) plus ~1,000 multi-PMT 'compound eye' modules; outer veto up to 10,000 smaller PMTs. Housed in a purpose-excavated 69 m × 94 m cavern in the Tochibora mine, about 8 km from Super-Kamiokande.

notes: No placement is recorded: no sourced site has been assigned to this detector in the Atlas.
detector:iaxo.summary_technical: Purpose-built axion helioscope hardware (double-bore toroidal magnet for full IAXO; a smaller toroidal magnet for the BabyIAXO prototype) with X-ray optics and detectors, currently under construction (BabyIAXO stage) at DESY.

notes: Placed at site:fermilab-main-campus: no separately sourceable site record exists for this detector hall.
No value is taken from the original ICARUS T600 construction paper (Nucl. Instrum. Meth. A 527 (2004) 329), which could not be read (publisher site blocked access).
detector:icarus-t600.summary_technical: Two adjacent 3.6 × 3.9 × 19.6 m liquid argon TPC modules holding 760 t of argon with 476 t active mass; operated in LNGS Hall B 2010-2013 on the CNGS beam, overhauled at CERN 2014-2017, and running at Fermilab as the SBN far detector 600 m from the BNB target.

notes: About 5,500 sensors were deployed in total including spares and IceTop; “fewer than 100 of the approximately 5,500 sensors are currently nonoperational” (official Detector page).
Derived fields (facility_id, document_ids) are not written; placement carries the site.
detector:icecube.summary_technical: Cubic-kilometre in-ice Cherenkov array: 5,160 DOMs on 86 strings between 1,450 m and 2,450 m depth, 125 m string spacing on a hexagonal grid, 17 m DOM spacing; ~98% of deployed DOMs operational and ~99% detector uptime (JINST 12 P03012).

notes: Sensor count for DeepCore is not published on the official pages and is left unrecorded.
detector:icecube-deepcore.summary_technical: Low-energy infill subdetector: eight specially deployed strings at the centre of IceCube with ~70 m horizontal and 7 m vertical DOM spacing, lowering the neutrino energy threshold to about 10 GeV and enabling atmospheric-oscillation measurements.

notes: The area covered by IceTop (≈1 km², matching the in-ice array footprint) is not stated on the fetched official pages and is not recorded.
detector:icetop.summary_technical: Surface air-shower array of 162 ice-filled Cherenkov tanks in 81 stations (324 DOMs) above the IceCube strings; serves as a cosmic-ray veto and calibration detector and measures cosmic-ray flux, composition and Southern-Hemisphere arrival directions from 300 TeV to 1 EeV.

detector:igex-dm.summary_technical: The low-energy data acquisition of an IGEX 76Ge (enriched to 86%) double-beta detector (2.2 kg, ~2.0 kg active; called RG-2 in a 2000 proceedings) with ~4 keV threshold, in IGEX's 2.5 t archaeological-lead shield with muon veto and neutron moderator, in the Canfranc laboratory (2450 m.w.e.). Spin-independent WIMP-nucleon exclusion plots from 30 days (2000) and 40 days (2002) of raw data; the 2002 contour enters the DAMA region.

detector:index-dm.summary_technical: Indian Dark matter search Experiment: superheated emulsion droplet detectors with C2H2F4 (tetrafluoroethane), acoustic readout. Run 1: 500 ml, 48.6 effective days at a 5.87 keV threshold, 2.47 kg d; Run 2: 1.95 keV threshold, 70.4 g active liquid, 102.48 days, constraints on spin-independent (20.4 GeV/c^2) and spin-dependent (21.0 GeV/c^2) WIMP-nucleus interactions.

notes: Module count, per-module mass and iron/scintillator layer counts are not stated in the T2K experiment paper (NIM A 659); a dedicated INGRID instrumentation paper was not consulted. They are left unrecorded rather than estimated.
detector:ingrid.summary_technical: On-axis near detector: iron/scintillator sandwich modules arranged horizontally and vertically around the beam axis at 280 m, monitoring the neutrino beam's direction and profile spill-by-spill. Detailed module and mass specifications are not available from the sources consulted.

detector:jade.summary_technical: JADE detector: cylindrical drift chambers (the jet chamber has 96 drift cells in three concentric rings with 16 sense wires each) inside a thin normal-conducting solenoid, a modular array of lead-glass shower counters around the coil, an iron-yoke muon filter with drift chambers covering 92% of the solid angle, and small-angle luminosity and two-photon taggers; upgraded between 1981 and 1985.

detector:jinping-neutrino-experiment-det.summary_technical: Proposed detector in a CJPL-II tunnel with 4 kt of liquid scintillator or water-based (slow) liquid scintillator; the 2017 design paper discusses cylindrical and spherical vessels and plans two detectors in the CJPL experimental hall.

detector:jparc-muon-g-2-edm.summary_technical: Cooling muon source (muonium ionised by UV laser), RF acceleration cavities, vertical beam injection into a 3 T storage solenoid, field-measurement system and a positron track detector.

detector:jsns2-detector.summary_technical: Liquid-scintillator detector: acrylic vessel with 17 t (fiducial) 0.1 % Gd-loaded scintillator, unloaded scintillator in the surrounding stainless-steel tank (about 50 t in all), 120 PMTs as installed; 24 m from the mercury target on the 3rd floor of the MLF.

detector:juno.summary_technical: 20 kt liquid-scintillator central detector in a 35 m acrylic sphere, read out by 17,596 20-inch PMTs (4,939 dynode + 12,657 MCP) and 25,587 3-inch PMTs, immersed in a water-Cherenkov veto pool with an overhead Top Tracker; design energy resolution 3.02%/√E (MeV), first measured at 3.4% for 0.511 MeV γ-rays.

detector:juno-tao-detector.summary_technical: Central detector: 2.8 t GdLS in a 1.8 m inner-diameter acrylic vessel, ~10 m^2 SiPM tiles on a 1.882 m copper shell, LAB buffer, cryogenic stainless-steel tank, water and HDPE shield, top muon veto; operates at -50 C.

notes: `detector:kamland` is the id that KamLAND-Zen references: KamLAND-Zen loads a xenon-doped mini-balloon inside this same liquid-scintillator volume. This detector record describes KamLAND's own reactor-antineutrino configuration only; KamLAND-Zen's own specs and intervals are not recorded here.

Structural specs (target mass, PMT count) are quoted from the KamLAND first-results paper (arXiv:hep-ex/0212021) and the collaboration's 2026 full-dataset paper (arXiv:2606.29381); no official KamLAND detector page was reachable (the 'About KamLAND' sub-page returned 404 on every URL tried). The veto mass and containment vessel in `technology` rest on the first-results paper.
detector:kamland.summary_technical: ~1000 t liquid-scintillator antineutrino detector in an 18 m diameter vessel with 1,879 PMTs, surrounded by a water-Cherenkov muon veto, in the old Kamiokande cavity of the Kamioka mine; operating since January 2002.

detector:karmen.summary_technical: Rectangular high-resolution liquid-scintillation calorimeter, 56 t total mass, 65 m³ active liquid-scintillator volume (75% vol. paraffin oil, 25% vol. pseudocumene, 2 g/l PMP wavelength shifter) optically segmented into 512 independent central modules with gadolinium loading between module walls for thermal-neutron capture; located 17.7 m from the ISIS beam-stop target at 100 degrees to the proton beam.

detector:kascade.summary_technical: KASCADE: 200 m × 200 m field array of unshielded and shielded scintillators (electrons and muons), central detector with hadron calorimeter and muon tracking detector.

detector:kascade-grande.summary_technical: KASCADE-Grande: Grande array (37 stations of 10 m2, 700 m × 700 m) plus the KASCADE array, muon tracking detector and calorimeter; triggered by the Piccolo cluster for full efficiency above about 1016 eV.

notes: Placed at site:kit-campus-north (a geocoder-derived campus point; no more precise coordinate is sourced).
detector:katrin.summary_technical: MAC-E (Magnetic Adiabatic Collimation with Electrostatic) filter spectrometer fed by a windowless gaseous molecular tritium source (WGTS), analysing the endpoint region of the tritium beta-decay spectrum.

detector:keck-array.summary_technical: Five BICEP2-style 260 mm receivers (150 GHz, later 95, 220 and 270 GHz) on a single mount on the Martin A. Pomerantz Observatory (the mount formerly used by DASI and QUaD); observed 2012 to late 2019.

detector:kedr.summary_technical: KEDR: vertex detector, central drift chamber, aerogel Cherenkov counters, time-of-flight counters, LKr calorimeter, CsI calorimeter, muon system, superconducting coil, magnet yoke, electron tagging system, luminosity monitor.

detector:kims.summary_technical: CsI(Tl) scintillating-crystal array, 12 modules (103.4 kg) with pulse-shape discrimination of nuclear recoils, in a copper/polyethylene/lead/mineral-oil shield at Y2L (700 m overburden). 24524.3 kg d (2009-10 data): the most stringent spin-dependent WIMP-proton limits above 20 GeV/c^2 at the time; low-mass analysis rejects most of the low-mass region favoured by DAMA; 34,596 kg d solar-axion search.

detector:kims-nai.summary_technical: NaI(Tl) crystal development and WIMP search at Y2L in the shield previously used for KIMS-CsI: two crystals (8.26 kg and 9.15 kg), 2967.4 kg d (November 2013 - January 2015), pulse-shape discrimination of nuclear recoils; limits partially exclude the DAMA/LIBRA allowed region for WIMP-sodium scattering. A 200 kg array was planned (arXiv:1510.04519).

detector:kloe.summary_technical: KLOE: 4 m-diameter drift chamber surrounded by a lead-scintillating-fibre electromagnetic calorimeter; KLOE-2 upgrades include a cylindrical gas-electron-multiplier (GEM) inner tracker, the first high-energy use of cylindrical GEMs (CERN Courier); tracker described in NIM A488 (2002) 51.

notes: sensor_count (total optical-module or PMT count) is left unset: the LoI states 18 optical modules per string and 31 PMTs per optical module, but no source consulted states a total ARCA-wide optical-module or PMT count directly, and multiplying per-string figures by the design string count would be an unsourced derived computation.
depth_min (top of the instrumented array) is left unset for the same reason: the LoI states a ~700 m detection-unit height but no source states the resulting top-of-array depth directly.
detector:km3net-arca.summary_technical: KM3NeT/ARCA (Astroparticle Research with Cosmics in the Abyss): sea-water Cherenkov neutrino telescope at the KM3NeT-It site off Capo Passero, Sicily (3500 m depth), designed as two building blocks of 115 detection units each (~1 km3 instrumented volume) for high-energy astrophysical neutrino detection; 51 detection units were operating as of the 2026 access date, with construction ongoing.

notes: sensor_count and depth_min left unset for the same reason given on detector:km3net-arca: no fetched source states a total ORCA-wide optical-module/PMT count or top-of-array depth directly.
detector:km3net-orca.summary_technical: KM3NeT/ORCA (Oscillation Research with Cosmics in the Abyss): sea-water Cherenkov neutrino telescope at the KM3NeT-Fr site off Toulon, France (2450 m depth), designed as one building block of 115 detection units (~7 Mt instrumented seawater) for atmospheric neutrino oscillation measurements and neutrino mass ordering; 42 detection units were installed as of July 2026, with construction ongoing.

detector:kolar-gold-fields-phase-i-detec.summary_technical: Phase I: about 1600 iron-walled proportional counters (10 cm x 10 cm, 2.3 mm walls, 4 m or 6 m long) in 34 crossed layers with 1.2 cm iron plates, 4 x 6 m^2 floor area, 140 t, at 7000 hg/cm^2.

detector:kolar-gold-fields-phase-ii-dete.summary_technical: Phase II: about 4000 proportional counters (6 m long) in 60 layers with 0.6 cm iron plates, 6 x 6 m^2 floor area, 260 t, at 6045 hg/cm^2.

detector:koto.summary_technical: Hermetic CsI electromagnetic calorimeter with surrounding veto counters at the J-PARC Hadron Experimental Facility, reconstructing KL → π⁰(→γγ) ν ν̄ candidates against visible-particle vetoes.

detector:koto-ii.summary_technical: Proposed detector with a 12 m signal decay region and a 3 m diameter calorimeter in a neutral beam extracted at 5 degrees, optimized for K_L -> pi0 nu nubar.

detector:ktev.summary_technical: Fixed-target neutral-kaon spectrometer (E799-II/E832) with CsI electromagnetic calorimetry, drift-chamber tracking, a transition-radiation detector system and hermetic photon/charged-particle vetoes.

detector:l3.summary_technical: L3-optimised (not fully general-purpose) LEP detector: silicon-strip microvertex detector and time-expansion chamber for tracking, a bismuth-germanate (BGO) electromagnetic calorimeter, a hadron calorimeter, a muon spectrometer and scintillation counters, all inside a very large solenoid magnet. That magnet was left in place after LEP shut down and now forms the core of the ALICE detector at the same point.

notes: The LEGEND official-site quote confirms LNGS but not the Hall A designation specifically; the LBL Nuclear Science Division item of 2023-07-01 (src:0vbb-verify-legend-200-hall-a-lbl) states LEGEND-200 'reuses the GERDA cryostat in Hall A of ... LNGS', which supports the Hall A placement.
detector:legend-200.summary_technical: LEGEND-200: up to 200 kg of enriched (>86% 76Ge) HPGe detectors immersed in a liquid-argon active shield at LNGS, reusing the GERDA cryostat infrastructure; taking data since 2023.

notes: Sub-array unit counts (KM2A/WCDA/WFCTA) are not sourced, so they are left out of the specs and subsystems.
detector:lhaaso.summary_technical: Multi-component air-shower array at 4410 m on Haizi Mountain, Sichuan, China. Sub-array names and specifications (KM2A/WCDA/WFCTA unit counts) are not recorded here: no source consulted gave them (the IHEP site's technical pages could not be read).

notes: Placed at site:cern-point-8-lhcb. The detector paper (2008 JINST 3 S08005) was found but its full text was blocked by CERN's document-server bot protection (cds.cern.ch) and exceeded the fetch size limit at the SISSA mirror; only its abstract (via the INSPIRE literature API) is cited. Pseudorapidity coverage, dipole bending power and the RICH/VELO/calorimeter/muon-system specs are left unsourced rather than guessed.
The detector record carries the same Long Shutdown 3 interval and status as experiment:lhcb, so that the two agree.
detector:lhcb.summary_technical: Single-arm forward spectrometer at LHC Point 8: VELO, dipole magnet, two RICH detectors, tracking stations, calorimeters and a muon system arranged sequentially along the outgoing beam direction over ~20 m; 5600 t (per INSPIRE/home.cern; lhcb-outreach states 4500 t, unresolved conflict), 21 m × 10 m × 13 m.

notes: home.cern gives detector mass (40 kg) and dimensions (30 cm × 80 cm × 10 cm) per arm as of a November 2012 page snapshot; recorded in specs below.
Status shutdown matches experiment:lhcf (Long Shutdown 3).
detector:lhcf.summary_technical: Two identical imaging sampling calorimeters (Arm1, Arm2), tungsten/scintillator/position-sensitive-sensor construction, each ~40 kg, 30 cm × 80 cm × 10 cm, at zero-degree collision angle ±140 m from IP1.

detector:lsnd.summary_technical: Approximately cylindrical tank (8.3 m long, 5.7 m diameter) filled with 167 t of mineral-oil-based liquid scintillator (0.031 g/l b-PBD wavelength shifter), instrumented with 1220 photomultiplier tubes detecting both Cherenkov and scintillation light; centred 30 m from the LAMPF/LANSCE A6 beam-stop neutrino source.

detector:lux.summary_technical: Dual-phase xenon TPC, 370 kg total xenon, 250 kg active, 118 kg fiducial in WS2013, in the Davis Cavern at SURF; its cavern was reused for LZ.

notes: Energy threshold: not recorded. No official page or fetched paper states a single nuclear-recoil analysis threshold; the SR1 paper reports detection efficiency reaching 50% near 5.5 keV_nr, which is an efficiency point rather than a threshold. Left null.

The detector paper mentions "Twenty-two tonnes of GdLS contained in 150 55-gallon drums", which is the quantity procured/shipped rather than the outer detector mass, so no GdLS mass quantity is recorded.
detector:lz.summary_technical: Dual-phase xenon TPC, ~1.5 m diameter and height, 145.6 cm drift, 7 active tonnes of a 10 t inventory, 5.5 t SR1 fiducial, 494 R11410 PMTs (253 top / 241 bottom), surrounded by a ~2 t instrumented Xe skin (131 PMTs), a gadolinium-loaded liquid scintillator outer detector (120 R5912 PMTs) and an 8 m × 6 m water shield in the Davis Cavern.

detector:mac.summary_technical: MAC: large solid-angle electromagnetic/hadronic calorimeter, magnetised iron for muon momentum measurement, tracking drift chambers in a 5.7 kG solenoid and scintillator triggering.

detector:mace.summary_technical: 21 m quasi-parabolic reflector, f-ratio 1.2, focal length 25 m, 356 panels of four spherical aluminium facets (about 337 m2); camera of 1088 PMTs in 68 modules of 16 PMTs, 0.125 deg pixels.

detector:macro-detector.summary_technical: Modular detector of supermodules (each 12.6 x 12 x 9.3 m^3) combining liquid scintillation counters, limited streamer tubes and nuclear-track detectors, with a rock absorber; global size 76.5 x 12 x 9.3 m^3.

detector:magic.summary_technical: Two 17 m imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes at Roque de los Muchachos, La Palma; MAGIC-I active since October 2003, stereoscopic operation with MAGIC-II since around 2009, camera/readout upgrade in 2011-2012.

detector:magix.summary_technical: MAGIX: gas-jet target, two magnetic spectrometers each with a time projection chamber and a trigger/veto system, silicon-strip recoil detector.

detector:mainz-neutrino-mass-detector.summary_technical: MAC-E filter: frozen molecular-tritium film source in a solenoid, 27-electrode spectrometer vessel of 1 m diameter, source-to-detector distance about 6 m, electron detector in a refocussing solenoid.

notes: Placed at the existing site:surf-davis-campus-lz, not a new Majorana-specific site: no source consulted gives a coordinate distinct from LZ's point in the Davis Campus. See the experiment:majorana-demonstrator notes for detail.
detector:majorana-demonstrator.summary_technical: Two modules of p-type point-contact HPGe detectors (40.4 kg total, 27.2 kg enriched to ~88% 76Ge) in electroformed-copper vacuum cryostats with a low-background passive/active shield, at the Davis Campus, 4850 Level (1478 m), SURF.

detector:mark-i.summary_technical: Mark I: solenoidal field about 4 kilogauss over about 20 cubic metres; 16 concentric cylinders of magnetostrictive wire spark chambers; 48 scintillators (trigger and time of flight); aluminium coil; 24 lead-scintillator shower counters; iron flux return; muon spark chambers.

detector:mark-ii.summary_technical: Mark II detector, a general-purpose solenoidal detector that began life at SPEAR, moved to PEP, was upgraded and then installed on the SLC.

detector:mark-iii.summary_technical: Mark III detector at SPEAR (1981-1988); a published technical description was not retrieved for this record.

detector:mark-j.summary_technical: MARK J detector at PETRA (1979-1986); its 1979 energy-flow analysis introduced the 'oblateness' variable to expose three-jet structure. A published detector description was not retrieved for this record.

notes: The technology class is 'other': no listed class specifically names a liquid-xenon-calorimeter-plus-magnetic-spectrometer combination detector of this kind (the 'xenon_tpc'/'noble_liquid_tpc' classes are for xenon time-projection-chamber dark-matter detectors, a different technology from MEG's scintillation calorimeter).
detector:meg.summary_technical: Liquid xenon (LXe) scintillation calorimeter for the 52.8 MeV monochromatic gamma ray, combined with a drift chamber and scintillator timing counter positron spectrometer, on the PSI piE5 DC surface muon beamline. Operated 2009-2013; no separately sourced total LXe mass or chamber dimensions are recorded (left absent rather than guessed).

notes: The technology class is 'other', matching detector:meg: no liquid-xenon scintillation calorimeter class exists among the available technology classes.
detector:meg-ii.summary_technical: Upgrade of the MEG detector: higher-granularity LXe calorimeter, single-volume cylindrical drift chamber (replacing MEG's drift chamber array), upgraded plastic-scintillator timing counter and a new radiative decay counter (RDC) for normalization, on the PSI piE5 beamline. First physics run 2021, ongoing data-taking through at least 2023 per the most recent source consulted. No separately sourced subsystem dimensions are recorded.

notes: Placed at site:fermilab-main-campus: no separately sourceable site record exists for this detector hall.
detector:microboone.summary_technical: Single-phase liquid argon time projection chamber with 170 t total argon mass and 90 t inside the TPC, 2.56 × 2.325 × 10.368 m active volume, 2.6 m maximum drift, 8256 wires on three planes, 470 m from the BNB target.

notes: The water-tank outrigger count varies between sources (170 in the 2001 status paper); it is not recorded here.
detector:milagro.summary_technical: Central 60 m x 80 m x 8 m water reservoir with 723 8-inch PMTs in two layers (top layer for direction, bottom layer for gamma/hadron discrimination) and an outrigger array of water tanks instrumented with the same PMTs.

notes: The MIMAC-35cm detector (35 x 35 x 29 cm^3, measured in a surface laboratory per arXiv:2602.17880) is the planned upgrade and is not a separate record.
detector:mimac.summary_technical: MIcro-tpc MAtrix of Chambers: low-pressure (30 mbar) micro-TPCs, gas 50% i-C4H10 + 50% CHF3, pixelated Micromegas anode (424 um pitch) read every 20 ns by self-triggered electronics; bi-chamber module (two 10.8 x 10.8 x 25 cm^3 chambers) at the Laboratoire Souterrain de Modane since June 2012, unshielded. 2026: no excess towards Cygnus, sigma_SD-p < 6.65e-36 cm^2 (90% CL) from 495.1 and 354.2 day exposures. Next: MIMAC-35cm (twelve times the active volume, 100 eV threshold).

notes: Placed at site:fermilab-main-campus: no separately sourceable site record exists for this detector hall.
No mass, dimension or channel-count quantity is recorded: the MINERvA detector paper abstract page and the official site do not state them, and the full paper was not consulted.
detector:minerva.summary_technical: Finely segmented scintillator-strip inner tracker surrounded by electromagnetic and hadronic sampling calorimetry, with upstream passive targets of graphite, iron and lead interleaved between tracking planes, in the NuMI near detector hall at Fermilab.

notes: Placed at site:fermilab-main-campus: no separately sourceable site record exists for this detector hall.
detector:miniboone.summary_technical: Spherical 12.2 m diameter mineral-oil Cherenkov/scintillation detector with 1520 usable 8-inch photomultipliers, 818 t of mineral oil, centred 541 m from the upstream face of the Booster Neutrino Beam target.

detector:miniclean.summary_technical: Single-phase liquid argon/neon scintillation detector: 92 cryogenic PMTs with nearly 4pi coverage of a 500 kg (150 kg fiducial) target in a stainless-steel inner vessel, inside a vacuum outer vessel and a water shield tank with a 48-PMT muon veto in the SNOLAB Cube Hall. Pulse-shape discrimination separates nuclear recoils from 39Ar beta events; a 39Ar spike was planned to demonstrate its reach. Prototype for a multi-tonne CLEAN detector. Only a cold-gas run (February-April 2017) is documented; it gave a triplet lifetime of 3.480 us in gaseous argon. No WIMP-search result is published.

detector:minos-far-detector.summary_technical: 5.4 kt magnetised steel-scintillator tracking calorimeter of 486 octagonal planes in two supermodules, 1.42 T average field, at 705 m depth (2070 m.w.e.) in the Soudan Underground Laboratory, 735.3 km from the NuMI target.

notes: Placed at site:fermilab-main-campus: no separately sourceable site record exists for this detector hall.
detector:minos-near-detector.summary_technical: 0.98 kt magnetised steel-scintillator tracking calorimeter of 282 planes, 1.28 T average fiducial field, in a 100 m deep cavern at Fermilab (225 m.w.e.), about 1 km from the NuMI target.

detector:moedal.summary_technical: 125 NTD stacks (47 m² total plastic), ~1 t of paramagnetic trapping detectors, TimePix pixel monitors; deployed in the LHCb cavern at Point 8, requiring no trigger or online DAQ for its main passive elements.

detector:moller.summary_technical: MOLLER apparatus with 11 major subsystems: liquid-hydrogen target, toroidal spectrometer and collimators focusing Møller electrons to a ring about 30 m downstream, fused-silica Cherenkov main detectors, beam monitors, polarimetry (two independent polarimeters), tracking detectors for Q^2 calibration and auxiliary background detectors.

detector:moscab.summary_technical: Geyser technique (a variant of the superheated-liquid technique introduced by Hahn and Reist): the bottom part with the target liquid at Tliq, the vapour above at a lower Tvap, a buffer liquid in between; vessels of 0.7 L (surface), 2 L and 18 L (arXiv:1708.00101, arXiv:2106.13654).

detector:mpd.summary_technical: MPD: superconducting solenoid (0.57 T), central time projection chamber, time-of-flight system, electromagnetic calorimeter and forward hadron calorimeters, in the MPD hall; magnet fully commissioned in 2026, ECAL and TOF modules being installed.

notes: technology_classes uses 'spectrometer': the detector's function (momentum/energy analysis of a mono-energetic conversion electron via tracker + calorimeter behind a solenoidal magnet chain) is closer to a spectrometer than to any of the other listed classes (none of which name a solenoidal charged-lepton spectrometer specifically).
Overall solenoid-system length not stated in any fetched source; an unsupported 25 m value was removed on 2026-09-18 verification.
detector:mu2e.summary_technical: Production, transport and detector superconducting solenoids (25 m combined length) with a straw-tube tracker and fast CsI crystal calorimeter behind the stopping target, plus a cosmic ray veto system covering the solenoids, per the Mu2e TDR and subsequent status reports. Under construction; no data yet.

notes: The technology class is 'other': none of the listed classes names a silicon-pixel HV-MAPS tracker specifically; Mu3e's tracker is solid-state silicon, not a gas TPC, so 'gaseous_tpc' does not fit.
detector:mu3e.summary_technical: Multi-layer HV-MAPS silicon pixel tracker (vertex + outer tracking layers; third layer installed 2026-09) combined with scintillating-fibre and scintillating-tile timing systems, on the PSI HiMB/piE5 beamline. Under construction; no data yet.

detector:muedm.summary_technical: Frozen-spin storage solenoid with a radial electric field and positron tracking; precursor phase with 28 MeV/c muons, second phase with 125 MeV/c muons.

detector:mulan.summary_technical: Segmented plastic-scintillator positron detector with ferromagnetic and quartz stopping targets and a kicked muon beam; pi E3 beamline.

notes: The technology class is 'other': no listed class specifically names a muon storage ring; 'spectrometer' was considered, but the ring's function (long-term storage in a precision magnetic field, not momentum analysis) fits it less well than the generic 'other' with a descriptive technology string.
detector:muon-g-2.summary_technical: Superferric muon storage ring (7.112 m central orbit radius, 14.224 m diameter, 1.45 T field), the same magnet used in BNL E821, relocated to Fermilab in 2013 and instrumented with 24 calorimeter/tracker stations around its inner radius for the Muon g-2 (E989) precession measurement.

detector:muse.summary_technical: Non-magnetic large-acceptance spectrometer with beam-line tracking, a liquid hydrogen target and trigger vetoes such as the Target Chamber Post Veto.

detector:n2edm.summary_technical: Double-chamber UCN Ramsey spectrometer in a magnetically shielded room (passive) with an eight-coil active magnetic shield; Hg and Cs magnetometers for field control.

notes: Placement: see experiment:na34-helios (generic North Area site).
detector:na34-helios.summary_technical: HELIOS: uranium/scintillator and uranium/liquid-argon calorimeters covering essentially the complete centre-of-mass solid angle, silicon strip detectors, high-resolution drift chambers, a transition radiation detector (proton set-up), a hadron spectrometer, NaI photon detectors and the NA3 muon spectrometer.

notes: Placement: see experiment:na35 (hall inferred from the H2 beam line).
detector:na35.summary_technical: NA35: streamer chamber (sensitive volume 200x120x70 cm3) in a 1.5 T vertical magnetic field, followed by four calorimeters; components inherited from NA5 and NA24.

notes: Placement: see experiment:na38 (generic North Area site).
detector:na38.summary_technical: NA38: NA10 dimuon spectrometer (air-core hexagonal toroid, two sets of four multiwire proportional chambers, four scintillator hodoscopes, 4.8 m absorber), scintillating-fibre electromagnetic calorimeter (2 < eta < 4.2), ten-subtarget uranium active target and beam hodoscope/Cherenkov detectors.

notes: Placement: see experiment:na44 (generic North Area site).
detector:na44.summary_technical: NA44: focusing spectrometer for one- and two-particle measurements near mid-rapidity; threshold imaging Cherenkov detector (CsI photocathodes) for pi/K separation at 4-8 GeV/c, time-of-flight, silicon pad multiplicity array and a lead target.

detector:na45-ceres.summary_technical: CERES: two RICH detectors in a field-free region downstream of a segmented target, silicon drift chambers and (from 1999) a radial drift TPC with a magnetic field, for low-mass e+e- pair detection.

notes: No key specs from a detector paper were independently re-verified; only run-interval facts (taken from primary sources) carry confidence 'verified'.
detector:na48.summary_technical: Magnetic-spectrometer plus liquid-krypton-calorimeter detector in the ECN3 cavern, run 1997-2004 across the main NA48 programme and its NA48/2 continuation.

detector:na49.summary_technical: NA49 large-acceptance hadron detector: four large-volume Time Projection Chambers (two in superconducting dipole magnets), time-of-flight walls and a forward calorimeter; its ownership was transferred to NA61/SHINE.

detector:na50.summary_technical: NA50: beam hodoscope and anti-halo counters, three centrality detectors (electromagnetic calorimeter for transverse energy, zero-degree calorimeter, multiplicity detector) and a muon spectrometer behind a hadron absorber (beryllium oxide, carbon, iron) with multi-wire proportional chambers.

detector:na57.summary_technical: NA57: pixel telescope of about one million channels (50 x 500 micrometre pixels) in the Goliath magnet moved from the West Area, conceptually similar to WA97.

detector:na60.summary_technical: NA60: pixel vertex telescope in a dipole magnet in front of the NA50-type muon spectrometer, with a mass resolution of about 2% for the 360000-dimuon In-In sample.

detector:na61-shine.summary_technical: NA61/SHINE: four Time Projection Chambers (two Vertex TPCs inside superconducting magnets with combined bending power up to 9 Tm, two Main TPCs), time-of-flight walls and the Projectile Spectator Detector calorimeter, with beam position detectors and trigger counters, on the H2 beam line.

notes: The detector paper PDF (cds.cern.ch mirror) could not be read (blocked by a bot-detection challenge); specs beyond the GigaTracker figures confirmed via a separate arXiv subsystem paper were not independently re-verified against the full JINST text and are therefore limited to what the abstract/search-indexed text stated.
detector:na62.summary_technical: Decay-in-flight spectrometer in the ECN3 cavern: GigaTracker beam-timing spectrometer (65 ps track time resolution, up to 2.0 MHz/mm² flux), RICH counter, LKr electromagnetic calorimeter, straw trackers and hermetic photon/particle veto systems, built 2009-2014 and operating since 2015.

notes: Placed at the existing site:cern-neutrino-platform-ehn1; see the experiment:na64 notes for the H4-in-EHN1 citation.
detector:na64.summary_technical: Active beam-dump missing-energy spectrometer on the NA64 H4 beamline (EHN1), combining an electromagnetic calorimeter with hermetic veto detectors to reject visible final states.

detector:nab.summary_technical: Asymmetric spectrometer with a main electrode system; hexagonally segmented silicon detectors for electron energy and proton time-of-flight (momentum); gaseous-helium detector cooling.

detector:naiad.summary_technical: NaI Advanced Detector: array of 2 encapsulated and 4 unencapsulated NaI(Tl) crystals with high light yield and pulse shape discrimination; 44.9 kg yr analysed in the final results; no WIMP nuclear-recoil signal in any run. The abstract says it imposed the most stringent constraints on the spin-dependent WIMP-proton cross-section 'so far'. UKDMC experiment, a DAMA-type target.

detector:nd.summary_technical: ND: 168 rectangular NaI(Tl) scintillation counters in four layers around the interaction region.

notes: Total detector mass and per-subsystem masses are not stated in the sources consulted; the T2K ND280 Upgrade TDR (arXiv:1901.03750) was consulted only via its abstract.
detector:nd280.summary_technical: Off-axis near detector in the recycled UA1 0.2 T dipole magnet: P0D, three TPCs and two FGDs as the tracking/target region, an ECal shell, and SMRD scintillator in the magnet yoke. Upgraded in 2023 with a Super-FGD and two additional high-angle TPCs plus time-of-flight planes.

detector:nedm-sns.summary_technical: Two measurement cells with opposite electric fields (75 kV/cm, Cavallo multiplier, 630 kV) in liquid 4He at 0.5 K; polarized 3He co-magnetometer; multilayer magnetic shield enclosure; magnet tested at Caltech and moved to ORNL.

detector:nemo-3-detector.summary_technical: Cylinder with 20 sectors of source foils (100Mo 6.914 kg, 96.5 % enriched) between two Geiger-mode tracking volumes (6180 open drift cells) and plastic-scintillator walls read by PMTs; 25 G solenoid; 19 cm iron shield and borated-water neutron shield.

detector:neos-detector.summary_technical: About one tonne of Gd-loaded liquid scintillator read out by PMTs (trigger on >= 30 PMT signals above 6 mV), with pulse-shape discrimination and muon veto, in the tendon gallery of Hanbit unit 5.

detector:neutrino-4-detector.summary_technical: Inner vessel divided into 10 rows x 5 sections (0.225 x 0.225 x 0.85 m^3) filled with 0.1 % Gd liquid scintillator (1.8 m^3 total), PMT readout, passive and active (muon veto) shielding; movable on rails to measure 6-12 m from the core.

notes: Detector generations (0.3a 2008, 0.3b/0.3b' 2013-2017, 0.3b'' 2017-2020 with the low-alpha mu-PIC, upgraded detector 2025) are one record; the specs quoted are those of the 0.3b'' (2018 run).
detector:newage.summary_technical: NEw generation WIMP-search with an Advanced Gaseous tracking device Experiment: direction-sensitive WIMP search with low-pressure CF4 micro-TPCs read out by a micro pixel chamber (mu-PIC) with GEM pre-amplification, in Laboratory B of the Kamioka Observatory (2700 m.w.e.). Spin-dependent WIMP-proton limits from direction-sensitive analyses: 5400 pb at 150 GeV/c^2 (NEWAGE-0.3a, 0.524 kg d, 2010), 50 pb at 100 GeV/c^2 (NEWAGE-0.3b'', 2021) and 25.7 pb at 150 GeV/c^2 (3.18 kg d, 2023).
