detector:news-g.summary_technical: Spherical proportional counter: 60 cm SEDINE sphere (Ne+CH4, 3.1 bar) operated at LSM through 2015; 135 cm 'S140' copper sphere (pure CH4, 135 mbar) installed at SNOLAB 2020-2021, operating since summer 2021; a 135 cm sphere also ran a 10-day methane run at LSM reported in 2024.

notes: Prototype/demonstration detector; the one-kilogram pilot and 10 kg module are plans, not recorded as separate detectors.
detector:newsdm.summary_technical: NEWSdm (Nuclear Emulsions for WIMP Search with directional measurement): Nano Imaging Tracker (NIT) super-fine-grained emulsion films, ~100 nm track recording, read with optical microscopy and machine-learning selection, exposed inside a shield on an equatorial telescope mount that cancels Earth rotation. Emulsion produced underground in LNGS hall F; demonstration runs 2021-2022 with the shield in hall C. 2023: first direction-sensitive limit from a surface exposure (39 days, 0.59 g d, Nagoya).

notes: Placed at site:snolab-underground-lab, the SNOLAB underground laboratory.
detector:nexo.summary_technical: Proposed single-phase liquid-xenon TPC, 5 t of 136Xe enriched to ~90%, planned for the SNOLAB 2 km level; scales up the EXO-200 design by roughly 25x in xenon mass.

detector:next-100.summary_technical: NEXT-100: main-phase detector of the NEXT programme, a radiopure high-pressure gaseous xenon (136Xe, 100 kg) TPC with electroluminescence (SOFT) readout at LSC; commissioned May 2024.

notes: Start/end years are from secondary summaries, not a directly fetched primary source; see interval note. `status: completed` itself is directly sourced.
detector:next-white.summary_technical: NEXT-White (NEW): smaller-scale (~5 kg xenon, per secondary literature not independently re-verified) prototype phase of the NEXT high-pressure xenon gas TPC programme at LSC, preceding NEXT-100.

detector:nist-bl1.summary_technical: Segmented proton trap in a superconducting solenoid with electrostatic end barriers, a silicon proton detector and a 6Li-deposit neutron monitor; the BL2 apparatus is largely the same as that used in 2003.

detector:nist-bl2.summary_technical: Segmented proton trap with radial magnetic confinement and axial electrostatic potential, periodic release and silicon-detector counting; neutron flux monitor.

detector:nist-bl3.summary_technical: Larger superconducting magnet and proton trap, larger neutron beam, segmented silicon proton detector, improved neutron flux monitor and upgraded alpha-gamma device for absolute flux calibration.

detector:nomad-detector.summary_technical: Drift-chamber active target (405 cm, about one radiation length, 0.1 g/cm3) in a 0.4 T field (the UA1 magnet), then TRD, preshower, lead-glass ECAL, HCAL and two muon-chamber stations; momentum resolution sigma_p/p = 0.008 p[GeV/c] (+) 0.05/sqrt(L[m]).

detector:nova-far-detector.summary_technical: 14 kt totally-active segmented tracking calorimeter of extruded PVC cells filled with mineral-oil-based liquid scintillator, 15.5 × 15.5 × 59.8 m, on the surface at Ash River 810 km from the NuMI target and 14.6 mrad off axis.

notes: Placed at site:fermilab-main-campus: no separately sourceable site record exists for this detector hall.
detector:nova-near-detector.summary_technical: Functionally identical 0.3 kt PVC-cell liquid-scintillator tracking calorimeter 1 km downstream of the NuMI target and 100 m underground at Fermilab, on the same 14.6 mrad off-axis line as the far detector.

notes: Mass figures differ by publication phase: the 2017 founding concept paper describes a combined CaWO4 + Al2O3 array of about 10 g total; the 2026 sensitivity-projection paper describes the current 'Technical Run' target as 7 g of CaWO4 specifically. Both are recorded; neither supersedes the other in the sources consulted.
detector:nucleus-calorimeter-array.summary_technical: NUCLEUS cryogenic calorimeter array: gram-scale CaWO4 (and, in the original concept, Al2O3) target crystals operated at millikelvin temperatures with a ~20 eV(nr) nuclear-recoil threshold; Technical Run target mass 7 g CaWO4; under construction by 2022, in commissioning (with an observed low-energy excess under study) by 2026.

detector:nusex-detector.summary_technical: 136 horizontal iron plates (1 cm, 3.5 m x 3.5 m) interleaved with planes of 320 resistive-cathode PVC streamer tubes (1 cm^2) read out by two orthogonal sets of aluminium strips; 150 t total.

detector:nutev-detector.summary_technical: 18 m long, 690 t target calorimeter of 168 steel plates (3 m x 3 m x 5.1 cm) with scintillator and drift chambers, followed by an iron-toroid spectrometer; continuously calibrated with a test beam; shared with CCFR.

notes: No site placement is recorded (see experiment:opal notes): no fetched source states which LEP interaction point hosted OPAL.
detector:opal.summary_technical: General-purpose LEP detector, about 12 m × 12 m × 12 m, arranged as concentric layers of tracking detectors, calorimeters and muon detectors around the beam pipe.

notes: Placed at site:lngs-hall-c (LNGS Hall C).
detector:opera.summary_technical: Hybrid emulsion-cloud-chamber detector: about 150,000 emulsion/lead 'bricks' (8.3 kg each) arranged in two supermodules interleaved with plastic-scintillator trigger planes, followed by muon spectrometers, at LNGS Hall C on the CNGS beam line.

detector:orpheus.summary_technical: 56 pick-up coils (1.8 cm diameter, 6.8 cm long) filled with SSG; flip signals read by RLC circuits with a signal-to-noise ratio of 10 to 20; dilution refrigerator of 300 uW cooling power with an L-shaped side access (arXiv:astro-ph/0404311).

detector:oscura.summary_technical: About 28 gigapixels of skipper-CCDs (15 um pixels) in 1500 multi-chip modules arranged in 100 supermodules of 16, read out by cold electronics, in a liquid-nitrogen pressure vessel inside a lead and polyethylene shield.

notes: No numeric coordinate for the actual seafloor mooring positions was found in any source consulted; the placement uses the Cascadia Basin site position (47°46'N, 127°46'W, to 1 arcminute) that the STRAW pathfinder paper (arXiv:1810.13265) gives for the site's cabled infrastructure, not a surveyed seafloor position.
This record models the pathfinder-stage hardware (STRAW/STRAW-b/P-ONE-1), not the full planned P-ONE array, which does not yet exist; experiment:p-one's own status remains 'proposed' for that reason.
detector:p-one.summary_technical: STRAW pathfinder mooring line(s) at the Cascadia Basin ONC site (2660 m depth): deployed Spring 2018, operating with ~98% duty cycle since commissioning completed January 2019, characterizing optical background and water absorption/scattering ahead of the full P-ONE array.

detector:p2-mesa.summary_technical: P2: liquid-hydrogen target, integrating solenoid spectrometer with full azimuthal acceptance and Cherenkov detectors, tracking detectors (micromegas) and precision beam polarimetry (Moller and hydrogen-atom-trap polarimeters).

detector:padme.summary_technical: PADME detector: 20×20 mm² active polycrystalline diamond target in 10⁻⁶ mbar vacuum; dipole magnet with positron, electron and high-energy-positron vetoes; 616 BGO crystals (21×21 mm², from L3) in the electromagnetic calorimeter with a central hole; small-angle calorimeter (SAC) for bremsstrahlung photons; TimePix3 pixel beam monitor; ETag hodoscope added in Run III.

detector:palo-verde-detector.summary_technical: Segmented detector of 66 acrylic cells (9 m long) filled with 11.34 t Gd-loaded liquid scintillator, 0.8 m oil buffers, a 1 m water buffer (105 t) and a 4-pi active muon veto; delayed positron / Gd-capture coincidence.

detector:panda.summary_technical: PANDA: target spectrometer (solenoid around the interaction region) and forward spectrometer (dipole) with tracking, particle identification and electromagnetic calorimetry providing nearly full solid-angle coverage.

notes: The detector phase (dual- or single-phase) is not recorded: no source consulted used "dual-phase"/"two-phase" for PandaX-4T specifically (the abstract of arXiv:2107.13438 uses neither term).
detector:pandax-4t.summary_technical: Xenon time projection chamber, 6 t total inventory / 4 t sensitive target (design); 3.7 t target mass used in the 2021 commissioning-run analysis. Located at CJPL-II, 2400 m underground.

detector:pandax-i.summary_technical: Low-threshold dual-phase xenon TPC (stage I of a staged programme, about 120 kg target mass) at CJPL under 2,400 m of marble (6,800 m.w.e.). Full 80.1 live-day exposure (26 May - 16 Oct 2014) with a 54.0 kg fiducial target: no excess; the data disfavour the positive low-mass WIMP signals in the literature; first results (17.4 live days, 37 kg) gave 3.7e-44 cm^2 at 49 GeV/c^2.

detector:pandax-ii.summary_technical: Dual-phase xenon TPC with a 500 kg liquid xenon target at CJPL. Commissioning run 21 Nov - 14 Dec 2015; physics Runs 9, 10, 11 (March 2016 - August 2018, 132 ton day total); official shutdown 29 June 2019. Full-exposure spin-independent limit 2.2e-46 cm^2 at 30 GeV/c^2. Successor of PandaX-I; superseded by PandaX-4T.

detector:pandax-iii-detector.summary_technical: Cylindrical TPC (height 120 cm, diameter 160 cm) in a stainless-steel high-pressure vessel; 52 thermal-bonding Micromegas modules with Ge-film resistive anode read the charge; electric-field-shaping cage; 20 kg-scale prototype tested in Shanghai.

detector:pandax-xt.summary_technical: Proposed multi-phase upgrade of PandaX-4T to a 43-tonne active liquid xenon target (natural xenon first, isotopic separation later), at CJPL; sensitivity of nearly two orders of magnitude beyond current limits for WIMPs above 10 GeV/c^2 and a [10 - 41] meV/c^2 effective Majorana mass sensitivity from 136Xe; 200 t y exposure goal for WIMPs. No construction start or schedule date is given in the proposal paper.

detector:pen.summary_technical: Pion-stopping target with a large calorimeter and tracking at the PSI pion beam, building on the PIBETA detector; details not recorded because no source consulted states them.

detector:pep-4-tpc.summary_technical: PEP-4 TPC: 2 m long cylindrical drift volume (40 cm inner, 2 m outer diameter), 80% argon / 20% methane gas at 8.5 atm, central cathode membrane at -75 kV, six end-cap sectors with multiwire proportional chambers, solenoidal field.

detector:perkeo-iii.summary_technical: 8 m, 54-coil magnet system with a large decay volume accepting a large part of the natural beam divergence, two connected detector systems and a pulsed, polarized cold neutron beam at PF1B.

notes: Interaction point 8 (IP8) was used first by PHENIX, then by sPHENIX.

technology_class 'spectrometer' chosen over the more collider-specific classes because PHENIX is described as a multi-arm spectrometer rather than a single hermetic general-purpose detector; no closer technology class exists.
specs left empty: see experiment:phenix notes on unverifiable secondary-source numbers.
detector:phenix.summary_technical: PHENIX: a multi-arm heavy-ion spectrometer at RHIC IP8 combining central-arm and muon-arm subdetectors, operational 2000-06-15 to 2016.

detector:phobos.summary_technical: PHOBOS: silicon detector arrays surrounding the interaction region for multiplicity and angular distributions, two magnetic spectrometers (about one percent of produced particles), time-of-flight walls moved farther out before the 2003 run, and calorimeters.

detector:picasso.summary_technical: Acrylic modules (17 cm diameter, 40 cm high) filled with polyacrylamide gel and C4F10 droplets, read by nine piezoelectric transducers per module; 50 cm of water shielding around the final 32-module installation (arXiv:1611.01499).

detector:pico-2l.summary_technical: Two-litre fused-silica jar (run 2: all-synthetic-quartz vessel) with stainless-steel bellows, stereoscopic cameras and piezoelectric acoustic sensors, in a water shield.

detector:pico-40l.summary_technical: Right-side-up design: two concentric nested quartz jars, bellows, mineral-oil hydraulic fluid, ~70 kg C3F8, a thermal system with a temperature gradient across the bellows, 4 cameras, 12 piezoelectric transducers, 2 Dytran pressure transducers; in the water tank of the former PICO-60 location at SNOLAB.

detector:pico-500.summary_technical: Right-side-up design scaled up from PICO-40L: ~250 L active volume, synthetic quartz vessel (the largest silica jar made for a bubble chamber), stainless-steel pressure vessel suspended in SNOLAB's Cube Hall; assembled underground because of its size.

detector:pico-60.summary_technical: 30-cm-diameter by 1-m-long synthetic fused-silica bell jar sealed to a stainless-steel bellows, hydraulic fluid (propylene glycol), water buffer above the target, two (run 1) then more (run 2) cameras, piezoelectric sensors; 60 cm by 167 cm pressure vessel in a 2.9 m by 3.7 m water tank.

detector:picolon.summary_technical: Ultra-pure NaI(Tl) crystals made by hybrid purification (recrystallisation plus ion-exchange resins; natural K below 20 ppb, 210Pb below 5.7 uBq/kg), read by a 3-inch low-background Hamamatsu R11065-20 PMT, in a lead and copper shield in the KamLAND area of Kamioka (2700 m.w.e.). Ingot #94 (1.34 kg, ~10 photoelectrons/keV): background ~1.5 /d/kg/keV in 2-6 keVee; first six-month modulation test (2021-2022 data) finds a finite amplitude attributed to non-physical causes. A 250 kg array in the KamLAND area is planned.

detector:pienu.summary_technical: Plastic scintillator and wire-chamber pion tracking, an 8 mm scintillator stopping target and a large NaI(Tl) crystal calorimeter surrounded by CsI crystals, for the pi -> e nu / pi -> mu nu ratio.

notes: No per-tank or per-telescope coordinates are recorded; only the single campus placement point.
detector:pierre-auger-observatory.summary_technical: Hybrid surface-detector/fluorescence-detector system: 1660 water-Cherenkov tanks on a 1.5 km grid across 3000 km², plus 27 fluorescence telescopes in four buildings; currently being upgraded (AugerPrime) with scintillator panels, radio antennas, upgraded electronics and underground muon counters on each surface station.

detector:pioneer.summary_technical: Planned detector: LGAD active target, 3pi sr 25-radiation-length calorimeter (LXe or LYSO), high-speed readout.

detector:pluto.summary_technical: PLUTO detector: placed at a DORIS collision point at the end of 1974; moved into the PETRA beam in October 1978; replaced at PETRA by CELLO in March 1980. A published detector description was not retrieved for this record.

detector:polarbear.summary_technical: 2.5 m off-axis Gregorian Huan Tran Telescope with the 1274-bolometer POLARBEAR-1 receiver (150 GHz) and later POLARBEAR-2 receivers (7588 dichroic pixels at 95/150 GHz) of the Simons Array; James Ax Observatory, 5200 m.

detector:prad.summary_technical: PRad: windowless cryo-cooled continuous-flow hydrogen gas target (4 cm cell), two-section 5.5 m vacuum chamber, two X-Y GEM detectors and the HyCal hybrid electromagnetic calorimeter covering 0.7-7.0 degrees with full azimuth, which also detects e-e (Moller) pairs for normalisation.

detector:prex.summary_technical: Hall A with its two high-resolution spectrometers measuring elastic scattering of polarised electrons from a 208Pb target (diamond-lead-diamond sandwich in PREX-II) at about 5 degrees; transverse-asymmetry detector and SBS GEM detectors were added in PREX-II.

notes: The placement references site:uw-cenpa-campus, a geocoder-derived campus point (also hosting ADMX).
detector:project-8.summary_technical: Project 8 Phase I CRES apparatus: single-electron cyclotron-radiation detection cell in a ~1 T magnetic field, demonstrated on 83mKr conversion electrons at the University of Washington (CRES first demonstrated in 2014); later phases add gaseous tritium sources.

detector:prospect-antineutrino-detector.summary_technical: Segmented 6Li-doped (0.1 % by mass) liquid-scintillator detector: an 11 x 14 array of 154 optically isolated segments (14.5 cm x 14.5 cm x 117.6 cm) read out by 308 PMTs; pulse-shape discrimination separates electron-like from neutron-capture signals.

notes: The liquid argon mass is not stated in the sources consulted. Start and end are known to the year only (2019 to 2020), from the CERN newsletter.

The CERN newsletter says that new solutions emerged from the ProtoDUNE-SP and ProtoDUNE-DP work for the second DUNE far detector module, which uses a vertical-drift layout, and that signal amplification in the gas phase was found not to be required.
detector:protodune-dp.summary_technical: Dual-phase LArTPC prototype at the CERN Neutrino Platform with a single homogeneous drift volume and a 6 m maximum drift, about one twentieth of a DUNE far-detector module. The dual-phase technology was later superseded by the vertical-drift design for FD2.

notes: Only the total liquid argon mass is entered (about 750 t, from the CERN newsletter); the active (instrumented) mass is not given in the sources consulted.
detector:protodune-sp.summary_technical: Single-phase LArTPC prototype at the CERN Neutrino Platform (EHN1) with a 7.2 × 6.0 × 6.9 m³ active volume, 3.6 m drift at 500 V/cm, full-size DUNE APAs, photon detectors and a cosmic-ray tagger, in a 0.3-7 GeV/c tagged charged-particle beam. Operated from August 2018 to July 2020; decommissioning for ProtoDUNE-II began in November 2020.

detector:ps210.summary_technical: Internal xenon gas-jet target in LEAR with downstream detectors identifying neutral antihydrogen atoms by their positron and antiproton signatures after the atoms travelled about ten metres.

detector:psi-nedm.summary_technical: UCN precession chamber with electric-field reversal, 199Hg co-magnetometer and caesium-vapour magnetometer array; apparatus originally built by the RAL/Sussex/ILL collaboration and upgraded and moved to PSI.

detector:puma.summary_technical: Two-zone Penning trap (antiproton storage trap and collision trap) in a transportable frame with a surrounding annihilation-product detector, plus an offline ion source.

detector:qweak.summary_technical: Custom Qweak apparatus in Hall C: 34.4 cm liquid-hydrogen target, collimators and a toroidal spectrometer focusing elastically scattered electrons onto fused-silica Cherenkov detectors with integrating readout (the apparatus is described in the Nature paper methods).

notes: No target mass, PMT count, or other detector spec was found in the sources consulted beyond the reactor baselines already recorded; none is recorded rather than guessed.
detector:reno.summary_technical: Two identical Gd-doped liquid-scintillator antineutrino detectors at 294 m and 1383 m from the Hanbit reactor array; per-detector target mass is not sourced. Data taking ran 2011-08 to 2023-03 (3800 live days).

notes: Placed at site:ill-grenoble-reactor-hall.

Two mass figures from two different papers/phases: the commissioning-phase mini-CryoCube module actually operated and characterized (arXiv:2507.22751) is precisely 3 × 42 g = 126 g of germanium; the same paper describes the planned CryoCube as eighteen 42-gram germanium calorimeters (two floors of nine, 756 g by the same arithmetic), and the 2022 background paper (arXiv:2208.01760) describes the planned Ricochet payload as a kg-scale Ge+Zn array. specs.target_mass below records the precisely-quoted mini-CryoCube figure.
detector:ricochet-cryocube.summary_technical: Ricochet CryoCube: planned kg-scale array of Ge and Zn cryogenic calorimeters; a mini-CryoCube commissioning module of three 42 g germanium calorimeters (126 g total) achieved 40 eV ionization / 50-80 eV phonon baseline resolutions during 2025 commissioning at the ILL.

detector:rno-g.summary_technical: RNO-G station design: three boreholes (~100 m depth) holding 15 receiving antennas in total plus 9 near-surface antennas (24 receiving channels) per station, on a 1.25 km grid; 7 stations built over the 2021-2022 field seasons, deployment paused in 2023 pending a performance/design review.

detector:rosebud.summary_technical: Cryogenic bolometers (sapphire Al2O3 25-50 g, Ge 67 g, then scintillating CaWO4 54 g, BGO 46 g, LiF) with NTD-Ge thermistors in a mobile dilution refrigerator at 20 mK, in the Canfranc laboratory (2450 m.w.e.); thresholds below 1 keV (sapphire) and 450 eV (Ge); phase two added light read-out for nuclear-recoil discrimination. A move to Hall B of the new LSC was planned for 2012.

detector:sabre-north.summary_technical: Planned array of nine ~5 kg NaI(Tl) crystals read by Hamamatsu R11065 photomultipliers in a fully passive copper and polyethylene shield, in a new experimental area at LNGS between Hall B and Hall A; crystals grown by Radiation Monitoring Devices from zone-refined NaI powder. Proof-of-Principle phase (crystal NaI-33, 2020-2022): 1.20 +- 0.05 counts/day/kg/keV in 1-6 keV with a liquid-scintillator veto and 1.39 +- 0.02 with passive shielding only. Target background 0.5 cpd/kg/keV with zone refining (2024 talk); data taking planned from 2028.

detector:sabre-south.summary_technical: Seven ultra-high-purity NaI(Tl) crystals (35 kg or 50 kg in all) in oxygen-free copper enclosures, with Hamamatsu R11065 photomultipliers at both ends, suspended in an 11.6 kL linear alkylbenzene liquid-scintillator veto (at least 18 R5912 photomultipliers) inside steel and polyethylene shielding, with a muon veto of eight EJ-200 plastic scintillator panels. Expected background 0.72 cpd/kg/keV in 1-6 keV; 5 sigma discovery or 3 sigma exclusion of a DAMA/LIBRA-like modulation after two years. Muon flux at SUPL measured at (6.33 +- 0.04 +- 0.35) x 10^-8 cm^-2 s^-1 with the veto panels (2026).

detector:sage.summary_technical: Radiochemical liquid-gallium-metal detector (50 t), 71Ga(νe,e⁻)71Ge reaction, at Baksan; chemically extracted and counted in periodic campaigns rather than observed in real time.

detector:sbc-lar10.summary_technical: 10-kg liquid-argon bubble chamber (LAr doped with ~100 ppm Xe, 32 Hamamatsu VUV4 SiPMs, quartz jar, liquid CF4 hydraulic fluid, cameras, piezo sensors); calibration detector for the SBC programme, designed for thresholds down to 100 eV.

detector:sbc-snolab.summary_technical: Functionally identical to SBC-LAr10 with radiopure construction: 10-kg liquid-argon bubble chamber, ~10 ppm Xe dopant, 48 FBK VUV SiPMs, two quartz jars, liquid CF4 hydraulic fluid.

notes: Placed at site:fermilab-main-campus: no separately sourceable site record exists for this detector hall.
The SBN proposal (2015) describes the same detector under its earlier name LAr1-ND, with an active volume of 4.0 × 4.0 × 5.0 m containing 112 tons of liquid argon.
Event rate is not recorded as a quantity: the SBND detector paper states "~7,000 neutrino events per day", and the schema's rate dimension has no per-day unit.
detector:sbnd.summary_technical: 112 t active mass single-phase liquid argon TPC 110 m from the Booster Neutrino Beam target, the near detector of the Short-Baseline Neutrino programme; 4.0 × 4.0 × 5.0 m active volume in the SBN proposal design.

notes: A concept: no detector has been built.
detector:sctf.summary_technical: SCTF detector concept (CDR Part One 2018): universal magnetic detector, inner tracker (time projection chamber option, arXiv:2005.09878) and drift chamber, FARICH particle identification, electromagnetic calorimeter, data collection for 300-400 kHz event frequency.

detector:sdss-2-5m-telescope.summary_technical: 2.5-m f/5 modified Ritchey-Chrétien alt-az telescope with a 1.08 m secondary and two corrector lenses giving a 3-degree distortion-free field; fibre-fed spectrographs since the late 2000s.

detector:seaquest.summary_technical: Dimuon spectrometer: target system, two dipole magnets, four tracking/hodoscope stations and an FPGA trigger, detecting Drell-Yan muon pairs from a 120 GeV proton beam on liquid-hydrogen, liquid-deuterium and solid nuclear targets.

notes: The device changed generations over the experiment's history (0.0947 g protoSENSEI in 2019 to a ~2 g Skipper-CCD from 2020); none of the sources consulted (checked 2026-10-25) gives a single 'current' mass or pixel count for 2026.
detector:sensei.summary_technical: Skipper-CCD detector operated in the MINOS cavern at Fermilab; protoSENSEI (2018-2019) had 0.0947 g active mass across ~904,000 pixels in four amplifier quadrants, superseded by a ~2 g high-resistivity Skipper-CCD from 2020, with operations continuing as of the May 2026 spurious-charge paper (arXiv:2605.30281).

notes: Not yet constructed; the 2033 start in the intervals and placement is `planned: true` and rests on the SHiP Collaboration's 2026 proceedings (arXiv:2606.11039), per experiment:ship notes.
detector:ship.summary_technical: Planned beam-dump/decay-volume detector at ECN3: heavy target absorbing the SPS proton beam, active muon shield, large vacuum decay vessel and downstream spectrometer/calorimeter for reconstructing displaced decays of feebly interacting particles.

detector:siddharta.summary_technical: SIDDHARTA: large-area silicon drift detectors (183 eV FWHM at 8 keV at about 170 K, timing resolution below 1 µs) used with the coincidence between K⁺K⁻ pairs and X-rays to suppress beam-loss background; signal-to-background improved by more than a factor of 10 relative to DEAR (Phys. Lett. B 704, 113).

detector:siddharta-2.summary_technical: SIDDHARTA-2: cryogenic gaseous target (deuterium) surrounded by silicon drift detectors specially developed for high-precision spectroscopy, with a scintillator kaon trigger, two veto systems and mostly lead shielding; first configuration SIDDHARTINO (kaonic helium).

detector:simons-observatory.summary_technical: Large Aperture Telescope (6 m crossed Dragone) plus three 0.5 m Small Aperture Telescopes at 5190 m on Cerro Toco; six bands 27-280 GHz; three more SATs (SO:UK, SO:JP) to be added.

notes: The detector operations interval starts at the LSST survey start; the commissioning interval is recorded on the experiment.
detector:simonyi-survey-telescope-lsst-c.summary_technical: Simonyi Survey Telescope (8.4 m combined primary/tertiary, 3.42 m secondary, 3.5-degree field) with the 3.2-gigapixel LSST Camera (64 cm focal plane).

detector:simple.summary_technical: Phase II: two arrays of 15 C2ClF5 SDDs (active mass 0.208 kg in Stage 1, 0.215 kg in Stage 2) in a 700 L water pool with water and polyethylene shielding, operated at 2 bar and 8 keV threshold; acoustic recoil/alpha discrimination better than 99% (arXiv:1404.4309).

detector:slac-e158.summary_technical: E158: 1.57 m liquid-hydrogen target, magnetic spectrometer/collimator, primary copper/fused-silica-fibre sandwich calorimeter 60 m downstream (four radial rings, 10-20-20-10 photomultipliers), quartz pion detectors and gas ionisation-chamber luminosity monitors.

detector:sld.summary_technical: General-purpose SLC detector: CCD pixel vertex detector (VXD, upgraded to VXD3), cylindrical central drift chamber with endcap drift chambers, a Cherenkov Ring-Imaging Detector (CRID), finely segmented projective-tower calorimetry, and a muon tracking system.

detector:snd.summary_technical: SND: three-layer spherical NaI(Tl) calorimeter of 1632 crystals, 13.5 radiation lengths thick, total mass 3.6 t; cylindrical drift chambers for charged-particle tracking; muon/veto system of streamer tubes and scintillation counters.

notes: Status shutdown: the detector has a sourced 'active' interval from 2022 (the collaboration's 2023 PRL, arXiv:2305.09383, states data were collected 'in 2022'), capped at the LHC-wide start of Long Shutdown 3 as in experiment:snd-lhc.

Technology and the TI18/480 m placement are corroborated by the SND@LHC detector-description paper (arXiv:2210.02784), which states the detector sits '480 m downstream of the ATLAS interaction point, in the TI18 tunnel'; the notes of site:cern-ti18-snd-lhc still flag the site's lat/lon as unverified.
detector:snd-lhc.summary_technical: Compact stand-alone detector in the TI18 tunnel, 480 m downstream of the ATLAS interaction point: an 830 kg tungsten target interleaved with emulsion and electronic trackers (also acting as an electromagnetic calorimeter), followed by a hadronic calorimeter and a muon identification system. Operated 2022 - June 2026; off since CERN's Long Shutdown 3 began.

detector:sno.summary_technical: Water-Cherenkov detector: 1000 t D2O in a 12 m diameter acrylic vessel viewed by 9600 PMTs, run in three configurations (pure D2O; NaCl-doped; D2O plus an NCD proportional-counter array) between 1999 and 2006.

notes: Modelled as a distinct detector record from detector:sno despite sharing the same physical acrylic vessel/cavern, because the target medium and physics program changed materially (heavy water -> water -> liquid scintillator, eventually tellurium-loaded); see experiment:sno-plus.lineage (`upgrade_of` experiment:sno).
detector:sno-plus.summary_technical: SNO's original acrylic vessel and PMT support structure, water-filled 2017-2019 for commissioning, then filled with 780 t of LAB+PPO liquid scintillator from 2022; a future phase will load natural tellurium for a 0νββ search.

detector:solid-detector.summary_technical: Highly 3D-segmented detector: voxels of PVT plastic scintillator with 6LiF:ZnS(Ag) neutron screens read out by wavelength-shifting fibres and MPPCs; 1.6 t, in a lightproof shipping container with 50 cm HDPE and water-wall shielding.

detector:solid-jlab.summary_technical: Planned SoLID spectrometer: large-acceptance forward scattering device with full azimuthal coverage and a solenoid magnet, configured for SIDIS/J/psi and (with different detectors) for PVDIS at an event rate of 500 kHz.

detector:soudan-2-detector.summary_technical: 224 iron-and-gas drift-tube modules (1 m x 1 m x 2.7 m, 4.3 t each; 8 m wide x 5.5 m high x 16.1 m long), vertical anode wires and cathode strips read out; surrounded by an active aluminium proportional-tube shield covering about 97 % of the solid angle.

detector:spd-nica.summary_technical: SPD: superconducting solenoid with a thousand-tonne yoke (contract pending June 2026), silicon vertex detector, straw tracker, time-of-flight, electromagnetic calorimeter, muon system and beam-beam counters / zero-degree calorimeters.

notes: Interaction point 8 (IP8) was used first by PHENIX, then by sPHENIX.

technology_class 'general_purpose_collider' chosen as the closest available class for a hermetic, calorimeter+tracking collider detector; sPHENIX is not itself a collider, the class describes the detector design pattern.
detector:sphenix.summary_technical: sPHENIX: a 1,000 t hermetic collider detector at RHIC IP8 built around a reused 20-ton BaBar solenoid (4 K) with tungsten-scintillating-fiber electromagnetic calorimetry; construction completed April 2023, commissioned with first Au+Au data in 2023.

detector:spice.summary_technical: 1 cm^3 Al2O3 and SiO2 crystals and GaAs cubes instrumented on one face with TES athermal-phonon sensors (two independent arrays per pixel); GaAs also read out through an optical cavity with an instrumented Ge photon collector.

detector:spinquest.summary_technical: Dimuon spectrometer reused from SeaQuest (FMag hadron absorber and beam dump, KMag from KTeV, four tracking/hodoscope stations, iron hadron absorbers) with a new dynamically polarised NH3/ND3 target in a 5 T magnet (8 cm homogeneous region) placed farther upstream.

detector:spt.summary_technical: 10 m diameter offset Gregorian millimetre-wave telescope at the South Pole with, in turn, the SPT-SZ (966-pixel), SPTpol (1536-bolometer) and SPT-3G (~16,000-detector, 95/150/220 GHz) cameras.

notes: Magnet field strength is not recorded (see the experiment:star notes); the technology class 'gaseous_tpc' was chosen because the TPC is described as the detector's central/defining subsystem.
detector:star.summary_technical: STAR: a 1,200 t heavy-ion collider detector at RHIC IP6, built around a 4 m diameter x 4.2 m long gaseous Time Projection Chamber inside a solenoidal magnet, providing full-azimuth charged-particle tracking within |η| < 1.8.

notes: A concept: no detector has been built. No placement is recorded: the host area (Hefei Future Big Science City) has no hall position, and a placement on the area-marker site would add an A23 approximate-coordinate warning; the experiment is located through facility:stcf-hefei and accelerator:stcf.
detector:stcf.summary_technical: STCF conceptual design (Physics & Detector CDR 2023): µRWELL inner tracker (6, 11, 16 cm) or CMOS MAPS option, main drift chamber, RICH with CsI-MPGD photon detectors (barrel), DIRC-like TOF (endcaps), pure CsI + APD calorimeter, RPC + scintillator-strip muon detector, 1 T superconducting solenoid, solid-angle coverage 94% of 4π.

detector:stereo-detector.summary_technical: Acrylic target aquarium (2.233 m x 0.889 m x 1.230 m) divided longitudinally into six identical optically separated cells filled with Gd-loaded liquid scintillator, surrounded by a gamma catcher, veto and passive shielding; PMT readout with pulse-shape discrimination.

notes: A detector-paper PMT count (NIM A 501, 2003) could not be extracted (PDF not machine-readable); the 11,129 figure is instead sourced from the official detector page, which is consistent with the 2026 INSPIRE experiment-record summary ('11,200 PMTs', an approximate paraphrase) and the SK-III restoration figure on the history page.

experiment_ids includes experiment:t2k and experiment:k2k in addition to experiment:super-kamiokande: this same physical detector serves as the far detector for both accelerator-neutrino programmes (K2K, 250 km from KEK; T2K, 295 km from J-PARC) as well as running its own solar/atmospheric/proton-decay/supernova physics programme. See src:t2k-nim-2011 ('...detected at the Super-Kamiokande...') and src:k2k-tutorial-page ('Neutrinos generated at KEK will be detected by the Super-kamiokande detector 250 km away.').
detector:super-kamiokande.summary_technical: 39.3 m diameter x 41.4 m height stainless-steel tank; inner detector of 11,129 inward-facing 20-inch PMTs (~40% photocoverage), outer veto of 1,885 8-inch PMTs; 50 kt total / 22.5 kt fiducial mass. Rebuilt/upgraded through SK-I - SK-IV after a November 2001 PMT-implosion accident (full density restored June 2006); gadolinium-loaded since August 2020 (SK-Gd).

notes: Detector total, active and fiducial mass in kg are not given on any page consulted; only the crystal count (24) is sourced.
Split on 2026-09-18: this record now covers only the SNOLAB payload. The earlier Soudan-era iZIP payload is now detector:supercdms-soudan (see experiment:supercdms.lineage).
detector:supercdms.summary_technical: 24-crystal Si/Ge cryogenic ionization-and-phonon payload operated at 15-30 mK at SNOLAB, succeeding an earlier-generation iZIP payload (detector:supercdms-soudan) that ran at the Soudan Underground Laboratory 2009-2015; multiple shielding layers (Cu, polyethylene, ultrapure Pb, radon barrier) suppress backgrounds.

notes: No source consulted gives a Soudan-specific crystal count or total mass; they are left unsourced rather than assumed from the later SNOLAB payload's 24-crystal figure.
detector:supercdms-soudan.summary_technical: iZIP (interleaved Z-sensitive Ionization and Phonon) cryogenic Ge/Si detector payload operated at the Soudan Underground Laboratory, 2009-2015; an evolution of the CDMS-II detector design with substantially improved surface-event background rejection.

detector:supernemo-demonstrator-detector.summary_technical: Source frame with 34 82Se foils (96-99 % enriched, 250 um), 2034 Geiger cells (14970 wires) in a He/ethanol/Ar mixture, 712 optical modules (440 8-inch and 272 5-inch PMTs on polystyrene scintillator), magnetic coil ~25 G, 18 cm iron and 24 cm polyethylene shielding, anti-radon tent.

detector:sussex-ral-ill-nedm.summary_technical: UCN storage chamber with electrodes in a magnetically shielded volume, Ramsey separated oscillating fields and a cohabiting 199Hg magnetometer; the apparatus was originally built by the RAL/Sussex/ILL collaboration.

notes: Design not final: the home page describes the concept and the 2025 science paper describes the baseline design; counts and dimensions are not recorded.
detector:swgo.summary_technical: Planned array of primarily water-Cherenkov detector units: a high fill-factor core with area considerably larger than HAWC and a low-density outer array, at 4770 m.

detector:taiga.summary_technical: TAIGA-1: 120 HiSCORE stations (1 km2), three IACTs (about 9.6 degree field of view), Tunka-Grande and TAIGA-MUON scintillators (250 m2), Tunka-Rex radio array, and the older Tunka-133 Cherenkov array.

detector:tasso.summary_technical: TASSO detector at one of the four PETRA collision regions (South-Eastern hall); recorded e⁺e⁻ annihilation at PETRA from January 1979 to November 1986. A published detector description was not retrieved for this record.

notes: No per-station or per-telescope coordinates are recorded; only the single approximate campus placement point.
detector:telescope-array.summary_technical: Hybrid surface-detector/fluorescence-detector system: 507 scintillator counters on a 1.2 km grid over ~700 km², plus 38 fluorescence telescopes at three sites; extended since 2019 by TAx4 (500 further counters on a 2.08 km grid, 12 new FD telescopes, ~3000 km² target coverage).

detector:tesseract.summary_technical: Proposed LSM setup: central cryostat in nested shielding (outer HDPE neutron shield, lead, inner polyethylene, mu-metal), ISO-6 clean room and radon suppression, in the former EDELWEISS-III area; payload of SPICE, HeRALD and Ge/Si modules sharing TES phonon readout; two similar cryostats are envisioned.

detector:texono.summary_technical: Sub-keV germanium detectors at the Kuo-Sheng Reactor Neutrino Laboratory (30 m.w.e., 28 m from a 2.9 GW reactor core): 4-channel 5 g ULEGe array at 220 eV threshold (0.338 kg d; limits for 3-6 GeV WIMPs), 840 g fiducial p-type point-contact Ge at 39.5 kg d (spin-independent limits that probe the CoGeNT region), and an n-type point-contact Ge (314.15 kg d) for bosonic super-WIMPs. The same detectors serve reactor-neutrino and CEvNS searches; CDEX adopted the KSNL design.

detector:tibet-asgamma.summary_technical: Tibet AS array (597 scintillation detectors of 0.5 m2 in 2019, 65,700 m2) plus underground water-Cherenkov muon-detector array (3,400 m2, since 2014); angular resolution about 1 degree measured with the Moon's shadow.

detector:tokyo-dark-matter-search.summary_technical: Arrays of eight LiF (168 g) or NaF (176 g) bolometers with NTD-Ge thermistors in a dilution refrigerator below 10 mK, 2700 m.w.e., in a laboratory excavated near Super-Kamiokande (Mozumi mine). Spin-dependent WIMP searches: 4.1 kg d of LiF (2001-2002) and 3.38 kg d of NaF (2002-2003) give limits in the a_p-a_n plane, excluding much of the UKDMC-allowed region.

detector:topaz.summary_technical: TOPAZ: superconducting solenoidal magnet and a time-projection tracking chamber (TPC).

notes: Status shutdown matches experiment:totem (Long Shutdown 3).
detector:totem.summary_technical: Roman Pot silicon-strip stations (26 total) symmetric about IP5, plus T1 (CSC) and T2 (GEM) forward tracking telescopes covering pseudo-rapidity 3-7; ~3000 kg total equipment.

detector:trex-dm.summary_technical: Two side-by-side common-cathode TPC modules, a 0.5 m diameter, 0.5 m long copper vessel 6 cm thick, Teflon field cage with Kapton copper-strip shaping rings, aluminised Mylar cathode, X-Y strips of 1 mm pitch on 25x25 cm^2 microbulk Micromegas (official TREX-DM page).

detector:trident-detector.summary_technical: Proposed array of 1211 strings with 20 hybrid digital optical modules each (multi-PMT plus SiPM), vertical spacing 30 m, 2800-3400 m below sea level, Penrose-tiling string pattern with 70 m and 110 m spacings, ~7.5 km^3.

detector:troitsk-nu-mass-detector.summary_technical: Windowless gaseous tritium source (about 0.8 T, 5 T plugs) feeding an integrating electrostatic spectrometer with adiabatic magnetic collimation; resolution 3-4 eV.

detector:tucan.summary_technical: Spallation target on the TRIUMF 520 MeV cyclotron beam, liquid-deuterium cold moderator (installation planned), superfluid-helium UCN converter and an EDM spectrometer with magnetic shielding and magnetometry.

detector:tunka-133.summary_technical: Tunka-133: 175 optical detectors in 25 hexagonal clusters (six plus one central) over about 3 km2 at 670 m; PMT-based Cherenkov-light lateral-distribution measurement; winter-season operation.

detector:twist.summary_technical: Planar drift and proportional chamber stack in a solenoid measuring the positron momentum and angle from polarized surface-muon decay; details not recorded because no source consulted gives them.

notes: Detector site placement carries the same LSS4-vs-LSS5 caveat as site:cern-sps-lss5-ua1 (see that record's notes): the specific SPS hall was not independently verified by a source consulted.
detector:ua1.summary_technical: General-purpose (4π) collider detector: central six-chambered imaging drift chamber (5.8 m long, 2.3 m diameter) inside an 800-tonne conventional dipole magnet, 48 lead-layer ('gondola') electromagnetic subdetectors, hadron calorimetry and muon chambers requiring about 30 km of extruded aluminium.

notes: Detector site placement carries the same LSS4-vs-LSS5 caveat as site:cern-sps-lss4-ua2 (see that record's notes): the specific SPS hall was not independently verified by a source consulted.

technology_class 'spectrometer' is used rather than 'general_purpose_collider' because UA2 explicitly had no muon detector and relied on calorimetry rather than a magnetic central tracker for its core physics case (home.cern: 'There was no muon detector').
detector:ua2.summary_technical: Non-magnetic, highly segmented calorimetric spectrometer: complete electromagnetic and hadronic calorimetry down to about 5 degrees from the beam, 6,096 independent silicon dE/dx counters, no muon detector; upgraded in 1985-1987 with a scintillating-fibre tracker (and later a silicon pad detector) to improve tracking and electron identification.

detector:ua4.summary_technical: UA4 detector system for elastic scattering at the SppS; a published technical description was not retrieved for this record.

detector:ua5.summary_technical: UA5: streamer chamber detection system (Greybook title); described in the Physics Reports review 'UA5: A general study of proton-antiproton physics at √s = 546 GeV'.

detector:ucntau.summary_technical: Halbach-array magneto-gravitational trap with a repulsive magnetic field gradient, spin-flip loading, an in situ detector and monitor detectors; no material walls for the stored UCN.

detector:venus.summary_technical: VENUS: superconducting solenoidal magnet, cylindrical drift chamber, liquid-argon electromagnetic endcap calorimeter.

detector:veritas.summary_technical: Array of four 12 m imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes at Mount Hopkins, Arizona; full array completed January 2007, sensitive 85 GeV to >30 TeV.

detector:wa97.summary_technical: WA97 in the Omega spectrometer: seven-layer silicon micro-pattern pixel telescope (0.5 million channels) interleaved with ten silicon microstrip planes, above the beam line pointing at the target; Omega2 pixel readout chips.

notes: Placement: see experiment:wa98 (West Area, campus-level site).
detector:wa98.summary_technical: WA98: Plastic Ball (655 modules) around a thin lead target; silicon drift and pad multiplicity detectors; two tracking spectrometer arms with scintillator-slat time-of-flight in the 1.6 Tm Goliath magnet; lead-glass photon detector array with charged-particle veto; photon multiplicity detector (21 m2, 21.5 m from the target); MIRAC and zero-degree calorimeters.

detector:warp.summary_technical: Two-phase (liquid and gas) argon detector reading both scintillation (S1) and ionisation through electroluminescence (S2) with PMTs, using the S2/S1 ratio and the pulse shape to reject electron recoils. Prototype: 2.3 l chamber (1.87 l sensitive volume), 96.5 kg d, first physics results published 2007-2008 (a 2013 review quotes a WIMP-nucleon limit of 1e-42 cm^2). Main detector: WARP140, 100 l target (140 kg of argon, 37 PMTs) inside an 8 t liquid-argon active veto in a double-walled cryostat; assembled in 2008, high-voltage and wavelength-shifter problems halted its technical runs in 2009-2010, a technical run was taken in 2011; no physics run.

notes: Technology wording from the first-results abstract; the same abstract describes a 2.3 litre test chamber.
detector:warp-2-3-litre.summary_technical: Two-phase argon chamber with a 1.87 l sensitive volume (2.6 kg) viewed from above by PMTs, inside a lead and polyethylene passive shield; results from 52.76 live days (96.5 kg d). Operated at LNGS from 2004 or earlier; still operating in April 2008 (arXiv:0804.1222).

notes: Camera history: 37 pixels installed in 1984 (VERITAS timeline), 109 photomultipliers in the mid-1990s (arXiv:astro-ph/9602068), 379 in the final camera (Whipple page).
detector:whipple-10m.summary_technical: Davies-Cotton reflector, 248 hexagonal mirrors, 75 m2; camera at the focal point (37-pixel imaging camera from 1984, 109 tubes in the mid-1990s, 379 PMTs finally; 2.6 deg field of view, 0.117 deg angular resolution).

detector:xenon10.summary_technical: First two-phase xenon TPC of the XENON programme: about 14 kg active (15 kg total) liquid xenon, 5.4 kg fiducial in the first science run (58.6 live days, Oct 2006 - Feb 2007), spin-independent limit 8.8e-44 cm^2 at 100 GeV/c^2 (90% CL). Also produced the first XENON spin-dependent limits and a single-electron-threshold search for light dark matter.

detector:xenon100.summary_technical: Dual-phase xenon TPC: 62 kg active target inside a 99 kg LXe veto (161 kg total). Science runs of 11.2, 100.9 and 224.6 live days; the 477-live-day combination (Jan 2010 - Jan 2014, 48 kg yr) set a spin-independent limit with a minimum of 1.1e-45 cm^2 at 50 GeV/c^2. Successor of XENON10, predecessor of XENON1T.

detector:xenon1t.summary_technical: Dual-phase xenon TPC, 3.2 t total / 2.0 t active liquid xenon, in LNGS Hall B. Operated 2015-2018; predecessor of the XENONnT detector.

detector:xenonnt.summary_technical: Dual-phase (two-phase) xenon TPC, 8.5 t total / 5.9 t active liquid xenon, in LNGS Hall B. Upgrade of the XENON1T detector, reusing its water shield; adds a cryogenic radon-distillation column and a dedicated neutron veto.

detector:xmass.summary_technical: Single-phase liquid xenon scintillation detector: 642 PMTs viewing 835 kg of xenon in a copper vessel, inside a 72-PMT water-Cherenkov muon veto, at 2700 m.w.e. Stable data taking Nov 2013 - Feb 2019 (1590.9 live days); 97 kg fiducial volume. Full-dataset WIMP-nucleon limit 1.4e-44 cm^2 at 60 GeV/c^2; annual-modulation, Migdal and bremsstrahlung searches for lighter WIMPs.

detector:yakutsk-eas-array.summary_technical: Yakutsk array: stations on a triangular pattern (Trigger-500, Trigger-1000), 49 surface stations over 11 km2 in 2021 and 5.62 km2 after the 2019-2021 modernization, six underground muon detectors, Cherenkov-light PMTs with an autonomous subset since 1995.

detector:zeplin-i.summary_technical: Single-phase liquid xenon scintillation detector with pulse-shape discrimination, 3.2 kg fiducial mass, 2800 m.w.e. at Boulby, with a liquid-scintillator Compton veto and lead shield. Three runs totalling 293 kg d fiducial exposure; spin-independent limit minimum 1.1e-6 pb. Predecessor of ZEPLIN-II and ZEPLIN-III.

detector:zeplin-ii.summary_technical: Two-phase (liquid/gas) xenon detector with 31 kg of xenon; first underground run of 31 live days (225 kg d after fiducial and stability cuts) gave a spin-independent minimum of 6.6e-7 pb. Successor of ZEPLIN-I, predecessor of ZEPLIN-III.

detector:zeplin-iii.summary_technical: Two-phase xenon TPC with 12 kg of liquid xenon in the Palmer Laboratory (1070 m, 2850 m.w.e.). First science run 27 Feb - 20 May 2008 (83 days) gave a spin-independent limit of 8.1e-8 pb at 55 GeV/c^2; after an upgrade (low-background PMTs, plastic-scintillator veto) the second run (24 Jun 2010 - 7 May 2011, 319 days, 1344 kg d raw) gave 4.8e-8 pb near 50 GeV/c^2 (3.9e-8 pb combined).

detector:zeus.summary_technical: General-purpose ep collider detector: high-resolution compensating uranium-scintillator calorimeter, central tracking detector inside a superconducting coil, silicon micro-vertex detector, forward/backward drift-chamber and straw-tube trackers, an instrumented iron absorber for hadronic-shower tails and muon identification, and additional muon detectors covering a large solid angle.

document:aleph-detector-nim-1990.summary_technical: Nucl. Instrum. Meth. A 294 (1990) 121-178 (report CERN-EP-90-25); the standard ALEPH detector-paper reference, describing the vertex detector, inner tracking chamber, time projection chamber, calorimeters, magnet and muon system as installed at LEP start-up.

document:alice-detector-paper-2008.summary_technical: 2008 JINST 3 S08002: the standard ALICE detector-paper reference, describing the Inner Tracking System, TPC, TOF/HMPID/TRD particle-identification arrays, PHOS/EMCal calorimeters, the L3 solenoid and the forward muon spectrometer as installed for the LHC's first collisions.

notes: Report number (CERN-LHCC-2013-024) dates LHCC submission to 2013; the journal publication (J. Phys. G 41, 087002) appeared in July 2014. `date` uses the publication month; both years are consistent with the same document.
document:alice-its2-upgrade-tdr-2014.summary_technical: ALICE ITS2 TDR (CERN-LHCC-2013-024, ALICE-TDR-017; J. Phys. G 41 (2014) 087002): design of the seven-layer MAPS-based (ALPIDE) Inner Tracking System replacing the original six-layer SPD/SDD/SSD ITS, installed during Long Shutdown 2 (2018-2021).

notes: The TDR itself (cds.cern.ch/record/1622286) could not be read: CERN Document Server returned only a bot-protection challenge page on every attempt, so no title, abstract or date was recovered from it and it is not cited as a source. The report number, its 2013 LHCC submission year and its subject (replacing the MWPC-based TPC readout with GEM-based, continuous, ungated readout for Run 3) are corroborated instead by arXiv:1511.04988, an ALICE Collaboration paper that describes the same GEM-based TPC upgrade. Confidence is 'uncertain' because the TDR document itself was not read.
document:alice-tpc-upgrade-tdr-2013.summary_technical: ALICE TPC upgrade TDR (CERN-LHCC-2013-020, ALICE-TDR-016, 2013): replaces the original MWPC-based TPC readout chambers with GEM-based Micro-Pattern Gaseous Detectors enabling continuous, ungated readout at the Pb-Pb interaction rates (up to 50 kHz) expected in LHC Run 3.

document:atlas-detector-paper-2008.summary_technical: 2008 JINST 3 S08003: the standard ATLAS detector-paper reference, describing the inner detector, calorimeters, muon spectrometer, magnet system and trigger as installed for first collisions.

notes: Date recorded at year precision: the INSPIRE literature-record listing (src:atlas-tdrs-inspire-1990s) gives the report number and recid but not an exact month/day.
document:atlas-inner-detector-tdr-1997.summary_technical: ATLAS Inner Detector TDR Vol. 1 (CERN-LHCC-97-16, ATLAS-TDR-4, 1997): design of the pixel, SCT and TRT sub-detectors inside the 2 T solenoid.

notes: Date recorded at year precision from the report number (CERN-LHCC-2017-021); the INSPIRE literature listing (src:atlas-phase2-tdrs-inspire) does not give an exact month/day.
document:atlas-itk-pixel-tdr-2017.summary_technical: ATLAS ITk Pixel TDR (CERN-LHCC-2017-021, ATLAS-TDR-030, 2017): design of the Phase-II Inner Tracker pixel system replacing the current pixel detector and SCT for HL-LHC running.

document:atlas-itk-strip-tdr-2017.summary_technical: ATLAS ITk Strip TDR (CERN-LHCC-2017-005, ATLAS-TDR-025, 1 Apr 2017): design of the Phase-II Inner Tracker strip system replacing the current SCT and TRT for HL-LHC running.

notes: Date recorded at year precision: the INSPIRE literature-record listing (src:atlas-tdrs-inspire-1990s) gives the report number and recid but not an exact month/day.
document:atlas-lar-calorimeter-tdr-1996.summary_technical: ATLAS LAr Calorimeter TDR (CERN-LHCC-96-41, 1996): design of the accordion-geometry electromagnetic calorimeter and the LAr hadronic end-cap and forward calorimeters.

document:atlas-technical-proposal-1994.summary_technical: ATLAS Technical Proposal (CERN-LHCC-94-43, LHCC-P-2, Dec 1994): the general-purpose pp detector concept submitted to the LHC Committee, following the 1992 Letter of Intent.

notes: Date recorded at year precision: the INSPIRE literature-record listing (src:atlas-tdrs-inspire-1990s) gives the report number and recid but not an exact month/day.
document:atlas-tile-calorimeter-tdr-1996.summary_technical: ATLAS Tile Calorimeter TDR (CERN-LHCC-96-42, 1996): design of the steel/scintillator sampling hadronic calorimeter, about 420,000 tiles read out by wavelength-shifting fibres.

notes: The Elsevier full text is paywalled and blocked to automated fetching; only the title, abstract, DOI and journal reference were read (via INSPIRE literature record 541364).
document:belle-detector-nima-2002.summary_technical: Belle Collaboration, 'The Belle Detector', Nucl. Instrum. Meth. A 479 (2002) 117-232: the full technical description of the 1.5 T solenoid spectrometer at the KEKB Tsukuba interaction region.

notes: The PTEP article number commonly cited as 123C01 was not confirmed by any source consulted; only the journal, year and DOI (10.1093/ptep/ptz106) were read.
document:belle-ii-physics-book-2019.summary_technical: E. Kou, P. Urquijo et al., 'The Belle II Physics Book', Prog. Theor. Exp. Phys. (2019), arXiv:1808.10567: the physics programme across nine working groups for data sets up to 50 ab⁻¹.

notes: Only the arXiv abstract page was read; the body of the report was not consulted.
document:belle-ii-tdr-2010.summary_technical: T. Abe et al. (Belle II Collaboration), 'Belle II Technical Design Report', KEK Report 2010-1, arXiv:1011.0352: physics motivation, SuperKEKB upgrade methods and the detector upgrade specification.

document:cepc-cdr-volume-1-2018.summary_technical: CEPC CDR vol. 1 (arXiv:1809.00285): the accelerator complex in a 100 km circumference underground tunnel, with space reserved for a later SPPC; the project is "initiated and hosted by China".

document:cepc-cdr-volume-2-2018.summary_technical: CEPC CDR vol. 2 (arXiv:1811.10545): physics case, conceptual detector designs and performance for a 240 GeV Higgs factory with two interaction points.

document:cepc-tdr-accelerator-2023.summary_technical: CEPC accelerator TDR (arXiv:2312.14363, Radiat. Detect. Technol. Methods 2024, DOI 10.1007/s41605-024-00463-y): Linac, Damping Ring, Booster and Collider, cost estimate and a preliminary construction timeline.

document:clic-cdr-volume-2-2012.summary_technical: CLIC CDR vol. 2 (arXiv:1202.5940): physics scenarios and two detector concepts based on those studied for the ILC.

notes: Date is the arXiv posting (20 March 2019); the report was published as a CERN Yellow Report whose DOI carries 2018.
document:clic-project-implementation-pla.summary_technical: CLIC Project Implementation Plan (CERN Yellow Report CERN-2018-010-M, DOI 10.23731/CYRM-2018-004, arXiv:1903.08655): staged 380 GeV / 1.5 TeV / 3 TeV design hosted by CERN.

notes: The report number CMS-00-001 is not confirmed by any source consulted; the DOI and INSPIRE recid are.
document:cms-detector-paper-jinst-2008.summary_technical: JINST 3 (2008) S08004: the reference description of the CMS detector as built, part of the JINST volume "The CERN Large Hadron Collider: Accelerator and Experiments".

document:cms-ecal-tdr-1997.summary_technical: ECAL Technical Design Report: lead-tungstate (PbWO4) scintillating-crystal electromagnetic calorimeter.

document:cms-hcal-tdr-1997.summary_technical: HCAL Technical Design Report: brass-scintillator sampling hadron calorimeter.

notes: Date taken from the CERN-LHCC report number year; the INSPIRE query returned no imprint date.
document:cms-phase2-endcap-calorimeter-t.summary_technical: Phase-2 endcap calorimeter TDR: the high-granularity calorimeter (HGCAL).

notes: Date taken from the CERN-LHCC report number year; the INSPIRE query returned no imprint date.
document:cms-phase2-mip-timing-detector-.summary_technical: Phase-2 MIP timing detector TDR: barrel timing layer (LYSO:Ce + SiPM) and endcap timing layer (LGAD), ~30-40 ps resolution.

notes: Date taken from the CERN-LHCC report number year; the INSPIRE query returned no imprint date.
document:cms-phase2-muon-tdr-2017.summary_technical: Phase-2 muon TDR: new GEM and improved RPC stations, electronics upgrades for DT and CSC systems.

document:cms-phase2-tracker-tdr-2017.summary_technical: Phase-2 tracker TDR for the HL-LHC: new outer tracker with track-trigger modules and a new inner pixel detector.

notes: Date recorded at year precision: the INSPIRE record gives no imprint date and CERN Document Server could not be read, so the December 1994 submission month is not recorded.
document:cms-technical-proposal-1994.summary_technical: CMS Technical Proposal submitted to the LHC Experiments Committee; the basis of the January 1996 approval of the experiment.

notes: INSPIRE gives the imprint year as 1997 while the report number is CERN-LHCC-98-006; the INSPIRE imprint year is recorded and the discrepancy noted.
document:cms-tracker-tdr-1998.summary_technical: Tracker Technical Design Report: silicon pixel and microstrip tracking system.

document:coherent-proposal-2015.summary_technical: COHERENT's founding proposal (arXiv:1509.08702, Sept. 2015): physics motivation, sensitivity projections, and a phased four-year deployment plan for a 14 kg CsI[Na] crystal, 15 kg of p-type point-contact germanium detectors, and a 100 kg two-phase liquid-xenon TPC in the SNS basement ("Neutrino Alley").

document:comet-phase1-tdr.summary_technical: arXiv:1812.09018: COMET Phase-I Technical Design Report, describing the CyDet/StrECAL detector design, the 3.2 kW 8 GeV J-PARC proton beam, and the Phase-I sensitivity goal of 3.1×10⁻¹⁵ (7×10⁻¹⁵ 90% C.L. upper limit).

notes: Preprint date (src:lep-inspire-detector-papers) is 1990-09; the journal issue is 1991. Both report numbers CERN-PPE-90-128 and CERN-EF-90-5 are listed by INSPIRE; only the first is carried in reference.report_number.
document:delphi-detector-nim-1991.summary_technical: Nucl. Instrum. Meth. A 303 (1991) 233-276 (reports CERN-PPE-90-128, CERN-EF-90-5); the standard DELPHI detector-paper reference, describing the RICH particle-identification system, silicon vertex detector, tracking, calorimetry and muon systems.

notes: doc_type is recorded as technical_design_report: the enum (§3.13) has no "interim design report" value. This report predates and was superseded by the Feb 2020 Far Detector TDR series (document:dune-fd-tdr-vol-1..4).
document:dune-fd-idr-2018.summary_technical: DUNE FD IDR Vol. 1 (arXiv:1807.10334, Jul 2018): physics motivation, technology choices and strategy for the far detector, superseded by the 2020 TDR volumes.

document:dune-fd-tdr-vol-1.summary_technical: DUNE FD TDR Vol. I (arXiv:2002.02967, Feb 2020): overview of the DUNE physics programme, the LBNF beam, near and far detectors, and the collaboration's organisation.

The 2023 results paper (arXiv:2304.07179) mentions RNO-G in Greenland as ARIANNA's larger planned successor array ('a larger array of autonomous radio detector stations is being constructed in Greenland (RNO-G)'); the Atlas models RNO-G as its own experiment (experiment:rno-g), not as part of ARIANNA's lineage, since no source frames it as a formal predecessor/successor relationship rather than a separate, related programme.
physics_goals: Search for ultra-high-energy cosmogenic neutrinos using a surface radio (Askaryan-effect) array on the Ross Ice Shelf, as a pathfinder for a much larger planned array
experiment:arianna.summary_technical: ARIANNA: surface-deployed radio (Askaryan-effect) neutrino pathfinder on the Ross Ice Shelf. Single prototype station deployed December 2009 (ice thickness 572±6 m); 7-station Hexagonal Radio Array pilot commissioned November 2014 (data through February 2019, described elsewhere as 'completed' in 2015); expanded to 8 stations per the official research page; now decommissioned per the collaboration's own home page. Full ~1000-station design was never built.
unique_capabilities: Surface-deployed (not deep in-ice) radio stations sitting directly on the flat, radio-transparent Ross Ice Shelf, simplifying station deployment and maintenance compared to deep-ice arrays

physics_goals: Study the fundamental symmetries between matter and antimatter by precision spectroscopy of atoms containing an antiproton, and study matter-antimatter collisions
experiment:asacusa.summary_technical: ASACUSA (Atomic Spectroscopy And Collisions Using Slow Antiprotons, AD-1): laser spectroscopy of antiprotonic helium, a cusp-trap antihydrogen beam for ground-state hyperfine spectroscopy in flight, and antiproton-atom collision studies, using the AD radio-frequency decelerator. At the AD since 2000; paused for LS3.

physics_goals: Compare hydrogen and antihydrogen spectra as a test of CPT invariance by producing cold antihydrogen
experiment:athena.summary_technical: ATHENA at the AD: mixed trapped antiprotons and positrons in a cryogenic Penning trap and detected the annihilations of the neutral antihydrogen atoms with an imaging detector. Ran 2000-2004; ALPHA is its successor.

experiment:atlas.summary_technical: General-purpose pp and heavy-ion collider experiment at LHC Point 1. Proposed by Letter of Intent in October 1992, approved in January 1996, first collisions November 2009; Runs 1-3 at 7-13.6 TeV. Physics programme spans Higgs, electroweak, top, QCD, heavy ions and searches beyond the Standard Model.

experiment:atrap.summary_technical: ATRAP (Antihydrogen Trap, AD-2): Penning-Ioffe traps in which cold positrons cool antiprotons and form antihydrogen; successor of TRAP at LEAR and a sister of ATHENA. At the AD from 2000; CERN now lists it as completed.

experiment:babar.summary_technical: General-purpose detector at the PEP-II asymmetric e⁺e⁻ B-factory (SLAC), operating at the Υ(4S) resonance (10.58 GeV) to study CP violation in neutral B-meson decays via the entangled B⁰-B̄⁰ pairs produced. unique_capabilities: An asymmetric-energy e⁺e⁻ collider tuned to the Υ(4S) resonance, giving the produced B and anti-B mesons a relativistic boost that lets their decay points be resolved -- essential for time-dependent CP-violation measurements

experiment:baksan-underground-scintillat.summary_technical: Multipurpose underground scintillation telescope (17 x 17 x 11 m^3; four horizontal and four vertical planes of 3184 standard 0.7 x 0.7 x 0.3 m^3 liquid-scintillator counters, 330 t) at 850 m w.e. in the Baksan Neutrino Observatory (INR RAS). Neutrino-burst monitor (240 t target): 35.8 yr of live time to 2021, no Galactic collapse candidate, f < 0.064 per year (90 % CL); also upward-muon, indirect WIMP and GW170817 neutrino searches.

experiment:base.summary_technical: BASE (Baryon Antibaryon Symmetry Experiment, AD-8): multi-Penning-trap system (analysis, precision, cooling and reservoir traps) for proton/antiproton magnetic-moment and charge-to-mass-ratio comparisons; antiproton magnetic moment to 1.5 ppb (2017), q/m to 16 ppt (2022). CoGeNT = 'Coherent Germanium Neutrino Technology'. Soudan hall: CoGeNT sat in the Soudan-2 (proton-decay) hall: the PRD paper says its shield rests on 'base I-beams that once supported the Soudan-2 proton decay experiment' at 2090 m.w.e., whereas the Atlas's only Soudan site is the MINOS far-detector cavern (2070 m.w.e.). They are different halls of the same mine level; no source read gives the Soudan-2 hall's coordinates, so the MINOS-cavern point stands for the laboratory.

An excess or modulation of unknown origin is not a discovery: the authors themselves quote ~2.8 sigma (2011) and 1.7 sigma, 'well below evidentiary' (2014). Contradicting results (CDEX-1 and CDMS II low-threshold analyses, TEXONO) are recorded under their own experiments.

An excess is not a discovery.

Dates: the experiment became operational in 1967 (Davis, Nobel Lecture) after construction in 1965-1967 (Cleveland et al. 1998). The 1998 paper's standard data set of 108 observations runs from 1970, when rise-time counting was introduced, to 1994, but operation did not stop then: Davis writes that the experiment continued until the late 1990s, when the Homestake Mine ceased operating, and SURF dates the end of the mine's operation to 2001. The end of operation is therefore bounded between 1997 and 2001 and marked approximate.
physics_goals: Detect solar neutrinos via the inverse beta-decay reaction on chlorine-37, converting it to argon-37
experiment:homestake.summary_technical: Radiochemical chlorine-argon solar-neutrino experiment in the Homestake Gold Mine, Lead, South Dakota, 1478 m (4850 ft) underground; 380 m³ (100,000 gal) perchloroethylene target. Built 1965-1967 and operational from 1967; the standard data set of 108 observations spans 1970-1994 and gives a 37Ar production rate of 2.56±0.16(stat)±0.16(syst) SNU, about one-third of the Standard Solar Model prediction -- the original 'solar neutrino problem', later resolved by neutrino oscillation (SNO, Super-Kamiokande).
unique_capabilities: First experiment to detect solar neutrinos, and the one that revealed the 'solar neutrino problem' (a measured rate about one-third of the theoretical prediction)

experiment:kascade.summary_technical: KArlsruhe Shower Core and Array DEtector: 200 m × 200 m array of scintillation detectors (electromagnetic and muon), a muon tracking detector and a hadron calorimeter at 110 m a.s.l.; measured spectra of elemental groups around the knee (3-5 PeV). Ran 1996-2012; extended by KASCADE-Grande in 2003.

notes: Placed at the existing campus-grade site:kit-campus-north (see experiment:kascade).
The 37 Grande stations were reassembled from the EAS-TOP experiment at Campo Imperatore (running 1987-2000 per the KASCADE-Grande page); EAS-TOP is not recorded here.

experiment:kascade-grande.summary_technical: Extension of KASCADE by the 37-station Grande array (10 m2 scintillators, 700 m × 700 m, stations reassembled from EAS-TOP), joint operation with KASCADE detectors and LOPES radio antennas from December 2003 to the end of 2012; covers 1016-1018 eV. experiment:katrin.summary_technical: KATRIN: precision tritium beta-decay endpoint spectroscopy using a windowless gaseous tritium source and a large MAC-E (Magnetic Adiabatic Collimation with Electrostatic) filter spectrometer at KIT Campus North. The 2025 Science result, based on the first five measurement campaigns (259 measurement days, 36 million electrons), set an upper limit mν < 0.45 eV (90% CL), improving on the 2022 result of 0.8 eV by nearly a factor of two.
unique_capabilities: Model-independent, kinematic (not cosmological) measurement of the absolute neutrino mass scale via the tritium beta-decay endpoint

experiment:kloe.summary_technical: KLOE at DAΦNE (√s = 1.02 GeV): 4 m-diameter drift chamber inside a lead-scintillating-fibre electromagnetic calorimeter; first data 1999 (CERN Courier) or 2000 (LNF), end 2006; physics on neutral and charged kaon properties, discrete-symmetry tests, CKM unitarity, light-scalar spectroscopy, η decays, hadronic cross sections and the muon g-2, dark-photon searches. Succeeded by KLOE-2.

experiment:kloe-2.summary_technical: KLOE-2: upgraded KLOE detector at DAΦNE with crab-waist collisions; expression of interest 31 March 2006; run November 2014-30 March 2018 with 5.5 fb⁻¹ acquired (about 8 fb⁻¹, 24 billion φ mesons, with KLOE); roughly 60-strong collaboration; physics on discrete symmetries, entangled neutral-kaon coherence, rare K_S and η decays, γγ physics and dark-matter searches.

experiment:km3net.summary_technical: KM3NeT: Mediterranean deep-sea Cherenkov neutrino observatory comprising the ARCA (high-energy astrophysical neutrino) and ORCA (atmospheric neutrino oscillation / mass-ordering) detector arrays, operated by the KM3NeT Collaboration. Under construction since December 2015 with progressively larger partial configurations already taking physics data, including the February 2023 KM3-230213A ultra-high-energy neutrino event.

notes: Scope: the series of Tata Institute (TIFR) / Osaka City University underground experiments at Kolar Gold Fields from 1960 to 1993: cosmic-ray muon depth-intensity measurements, the atmospheric-neutrino telescopes of 1965 and the Phase I and II proton-decay detectors. The Indian Neutrino Observatory (INO), a later proposal, is a separate project.

The collaboration's claim of proton decay at about 1e31 years conflicts with the limits of about 1e33 years from other experiments, as the collaboration's own paper acknowledges: "Contrary to this conclusion, as shown in our earlier reports (Ref. 9), our result is that protons are decaying with lifetime of about 10 31 years."
No official website exists (the experiments ended in 1993); none is recorded.
physics_goals: Search for proton decay deep underground
Detect neutrinos produced by cosmic rays in the atmosphere deep underground
experiment:kolar-gold-fields-experiments.summary_technical: Tata Institute of Fundamental Research and Osaka City University underground programme at KGF: cosmic-ray muon depth-intensity measurement to about 2.7 km; 1965 neutrino telescopes at 2300 m; Phase I (140 t, 1600 proportional counters, 7000 hg/cm^2, from end of 1980) and Phase II (260 t, about 4000 counters, 6045 hg/cm^2, from 1985) proton-decay detectors, stopped in 1993 when the mines closed. The collaboration reports a proton lifetime of about 1e31 years; larger detectors set limits near 1e33 years.

experiment:koto.summary_technical: J-PARC E14 KOTO: fixed-target experiment at the J-PARC Hadron Experimental Facility measuring/bounding the branching ratio of the CP-violating decay KL → π⁰ ν ν̄. First physics run May 2013 (100 hours, 24 kW beam); physics running resumed April 2015; has published results from 2015, 2016-2018, 2018 and 2021 data, most recently in February 2025; successor to the KEK-PS E391a experiment.

experiment:koto-ii.summary_technical: KOTO II (J-PARC E107, proposal P107): K_L -> pi0 nu nubar with a K_L beamline at 5 degrees from the production target in a new area behind the primary beam dump of the Hadron Experimental Facility; single event sensitivity 8.5e-13, to reach a significance above 5 sigma at the Standard Model rate of 3e-11. Successor to KOTO.

experiment:ktev.summary_technical: Fermilab fixed-target kaon experiment (jointly E799-II and E832, together called KTeV / 'Kaons at the Tevatron'), designed 1992, measuring direct CP violation (Re(ε′/ε)) and rare KL decays; announced its landmark direct-CP-violation observation in 1999. Contemporary and complementary to CERN's NA48.

experiment:l3.summary_technical: General-purpose LEP detector at interaction Point 2, optimised (rather than generalised) for electron, muon and photon measurements: a silicon-strip microvertex detector and time-expansion chamber for tracking, a BGO electromagnetic calorimeter, a hadron calorimeter and a muon spectrometer inside a very large solenoid. Approved by the CERN LEPC on 18 November 1982; ran from August 1989 to November 2000. Its magnet was reused as ALICE's solenoid at the same point after LEP shut down.
unique_capabilities: A bismuth-germanate (BGO) electromagnetic calorimeter for very high resolution photon and electron measurements

LEGEND-200 (up to 200 kg of enriched-76Ge detectors in liquid argon at LNGS) began data taking in 2023 and reported a first-result exposure of 61 kg·yr and T1/2 0ν > 0.5×10²⁶ yr (90% CL); a combined GERDA+MAJORANA+LEGEND-200 analysis gives T1/2 0ν > 1.9×10²⁶ yr (90% CL). LEGEND-1000 (1 t enriched Ge) is in preparation, targeting a discovery sensitivity beyond 10²⁸ yr.

experiment:lhaaso.summary_technical: Multi-component air-shower observatory at 4410 m on Haizi Mountain, Sichuan, China, combining water-Cherenkov, muon/electromagnetic and Cherenkov-telescope sub-arrays (per public description; individual KM2A/WCDA/WFCTA specifications not sourced) to cover cosmic-ray energies of 10¹²-10¹⁸ eV and gamma rays above 100 TeV. experiment:lhcb.summary_technical: Single-arm forward-spectrometer experiment at LHC Point 8 (Ferney-Voltaire, France), covering low pseudorapidity in the forward direction to exploit the strongly forward-peaked production of b-hadrons and c-hadrons at hadron colliders. Proposed by Letter of Intent in August 1995, approved September 1998, installed by September 2008, first collisions November 2009. Physics programme centres on CP violation and rare decays of heavy-flavour hadrons; Upgrade I (new VELO, silicon tracker, removal of the hardware trigger) was installed by April 2023.
unique_capabilities: A single forward-arm spectrometer (not a 4π enclosure) optimised for the forward-peaked production of b and c hadrons at a hadron collider

physics_goals: Measure neutral particles produced at very small angles in LHC collisions to calibrate the hadronic-interaction models used to interpret ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray air showers
experiment:lhcf.summary_technical: Forward-physics/cosmic-ray-calibration experiment: two compact imaging sampling calorimeters (tungsten plates, plastic scintillator, position-sensitive sensors) at zero-degree collision angle, ±140 m from LHC interaction point 1, covering pseudo-rapidity > 8.4. Proposed and approved May 2004; operated (mainly during early low-luminosity periods of each LHC run) from first collisions (23 Nov 2009) through June 2026; off since CERN's Long Shutdown 3 began.
unique_capabilities: Compact imaging calorimeters at zero-degree collision angle, sensitive to the pseudo-rapidity range greater than 8.4, giving LHCf access to particle production kinematics equivalent to a laboratory cosmic-ray energy of 10¹⁷ eV

Took data 1993-1998 and reported a statistically significant excess of ν̄e candidate events consistent with ν̄μ → ν̄e oscillation at short baseline, a result in tension with standard three-flavour oscillation and a long-standing driver of sterile-neutrino searches.

experiment:lz.summary_technical: Second-generation G2 direct-detection experiment using a dual-phase xenon TPC with 7 active tonnes (5.5 t SR1 fiducial) in the Davis Cavern at SURF (~1480 m rock, ~4300 m.w.e.). SR1 (60 live days, Dec 2021 - May 2022) set a spin-independent WIMP-nucleon limit of 9.2 × 10⁻⁴⁸ cm² at 36 GeV/c²; the 4.2 tonne-year WS2024 analysis reached 2.2 × 10⁻⁴⁸ cm² at 40 GeV/c². The programme targets 1,000 live days and also searches for 136Xe double beta decay.

experiment:na62.summary_technical: Fixed-target kaon-decay experiment in the ECN3 cavern of the CERN SPS North Area, using a 400 GeV/c primary proton beam to produce a secondary/tertiary charged-kaon beam. Measures the branching ratio of K⁺ → π⁺ ν ν̄ via a decay-in-flight technique with GigaTracker beam-timing, RICH, LKr calorimeter and veto subsystems (arXiv:1703.08501). Constructed 2009-2014, commissioned 2014-2015, Run 1 data 2016-2018 (arXiv:2103.15389, 3.4σ evidence-level measurement), Run 2 from 2021 with upgraded beam intensity, reaching a 5σ observation with 2016-2022 data (arXiv:2412.12015) and a further refined measurement including 2023-2024 data reported in 2026.
unique_capabilities: A decay-in-flight technique using a high-intensity (~750 MHz) unseparated hadron beam and precision timing (the GigaTracker beam spectrometer reaches 65 ps time resolution on tracks) to identify K⁺ → π⁺ ν ν̄ events against enormous backgrounds
