notes: ANTARES (site:antares-toulon, detector:antares) sits about 10 km east of this site per the Letter of Intent ('ORCA ... approximately 10 kilometers west of the existing ANTARES telescope site'), but site:antares-toulon belongs to no Atlas facility (its facility_id is null), so it is outside this map's inventory: it is not drawn and not listed as not drawn. Its own coordinate is only 'approximate' with precision_m 12000 (a corroborated estimate, not a directly published lat/lon), which is too coarse to add a defensibly placed context point here anyway.

The ORCA shore control station has moved between buildings (Institut Michel Pacha, La Seyne-sur-Mer originally; the Brégaillon/Ifremer site since January 2024; the MEUST building once ready), so no single building was confidently identified as the shore station to draw as OpenStreetMap context; it is not drawn.
OpenStreetMap was not used for the two drawn features: a sea site has no OSM footprint.
map:km3net-orca.summary_technical: Local map for the KM3NeT-Fr / ORCA deep-sea site (facility:km3net). One surveyed point (the collaboration's own published 42°48' N 06°02' E) and one derived ~200 m-diameter circle for the single ORCA building block, its radius estimated by scaling ARCA's sourced R=500 m by the two blocks' relative string spacing (both from the KM3NeT 2.0 Letter of Intent). ARCA and ORCA are ~900 km apart and cannot share a to-scale map; see map:km3net-arca (linked).

notes: Correction: the earlier map drew an unrelated building (way 567961020) as the reactor building; the reactor building is the dome-roofed part (way 608881797) at the plant's OSM generator node.
map:leibstadt-nuclear-power-plant.summary_technical: Dome-roofed reactor building (OSM building:part) identified by its roof and the plant's generator node; the surrounding main building complex is context; CONUS+ drawn as a derived point at the fitted reactor axis with 30 m accuracy (12.45 m horizontal offset from the axis is published, its azimuth is not).

notes: Drawn: the 1188 KM2A muon detectors (15 compact blocks of at most 80), the three WCDA pools, and the outline of the 5216-detector ED array. The map format has no multi-point type, so each muon detector is a 6 m square marker (the area-equivalent of its 36 m2) in a MultiPolygon. The 5216 electromagnetic detectors are NOT drawn one by one: as 1 m markers they need 26 000 vertices and push this map file to 3.5 MB, over the 2 MB size limit for a map file; their positions were read and checked and the outline carries the ED array.

Positions are read from the vector graphic of Fig. 1 of the LHAASO Science Book (Chin. Phys. C 46, 030001, CC BY 3.0; arXiv:1905.02773 v4, PDF page 8), registered to a second published copy of the layout (Fig. 1 of arXiv:2401.01038; 5215 of 5216 EDs within 2 m), and placed at the coordinate the Collaboration gives (29 21 27.56 N, 100 08 19.66 E). Checks: 4911 EDs inside 575 m and 305 outside (stated 4911 and 305), farthest ED 635.2 m (stated 635 m), pool sides 150.1 m, 150.1 m, 300.2 m x 110.1 m (stated 150, 150, 300 x 110), pool total 78,109 m2 (stated 78,000), ED hull span 1270.2 m (stated 1270 m).

The three pools are also traced in OpenStreetMap (ways 1046559931 to 1046559933, extract 2026-10-25T11:28:50Z) and lie within 1 to 3 m east and 2 to 10 m north of the placement used here, which supports the anchor; OpenStreetMap shapes are not used in any record (the OSM "Kilometer-Square Array" way 1003419124 is a regular 38-gon of radius 619.8 m centred 2 m from the coordinate, i.e. a drawn circle, not a trace).

Not drawn: the 18 WFCTA telescopes. The Science Book figure shows them as schematic 7 x 10 m rectangles at the junction of pools 1 and 2, but the text puts them "at the southwest corner of the first pool" and their container is 4.2 m x 2.5 m x 2.6 m; no position is taken from it.
It is not stated whether the layout shows design or as-built positions: the plotted EDs have a median nearest-neighbour distance of 13.6 m (stated spacing 15 m).

The previous version carried one 50 m-precision reference point (geometry:lhaaso-array-point) at the quoted coordinate; it is kept as the anchor marker. The 2016 and 2018 papers give 29 21 31 N, 100 08 15 E (164 m away); two 2020-2024 papers print "100.01 E" (a typo, about 12.5 km west).
map:lhaaso-daocheng.summary_technical: One local map for facility:lhaaso-daocheng. KM2A ED (5216) and MD (1188) positions and the three WCDA pool rectangles are read from Fig. 1 of the LHAASO Science Book (vector graphic), registered to a second published layout (arXiv:2401.01038), centred on the Collaboration’s coordinate 29 21 27.56 N, 100 08 19.66 E and oriented by the figure’s north arrow (accuracy 30 m; the pools agree with OpenStreetMap to 10 m). The MDs, the pools and the ED-array outline are drawn; the individual EDs and WFCTA are not.

notes: Linked map: map:cern, because beamline:cngs (CERN's own beamline, facility_id facility:cern) names site:lngs-hall-c as its far_detector_site_ids target (732 km baseline, 2006-2012 beam operation for OPERA/ICARUS). The CNGS direction line itself is drawn on map:cern, not here, since the beamline entity belongs to CERN's inventory, not LNGS's.

geometry:lngs-hall-a, geometry:lngs-hall-b and geometry:lngs-hall-c intentionally share one derived coordinate (the midpoint of the sourced ~700 m access-zone stretch): no source consulted distinguishes the three halls' order or position within that zone, so the three shapes are identical. A sourced (if coarse) position is available for all three and is more informative than leaving any of the three sites undrawn.

The Pandola 2011 overview (src:geo-euro-ug-pandola-2011) names several LNGS experiments that are not in the Atlas (Gator, MACRO, WArP, LUNA, COBRA, DAMA/Libra, STELLA/GEMPI2); they are therefore not listed as not drawn.
map:lngs.summary_technical: One local map for facility:lngs. The A24 Gran Sasso road tunnel (OSM relation 9617984) is drawn as context; the underground laboratory's own position is derived from the official emergency plan's motorway chainage of its entrance/exit doors (km 124.150/123.440 against the tunnel's own km 117.653-127.829), giving a ~700 m sourced zone about 5.8-6.5 km from the Assergi portal. Halls A, B and C are drawn at that zone's midpoint, undifferentiated. The surface External Laboratories / Centro Direzionale complex at Assergi carries both an OSM building footprint and the emergency plan's own surveyed WGS84 coordinate (79.6 m apart, corroborating each other).

notes: TA-53 is a security-sensitive area of Los Alamos National Laboratory, so only accelerator and experimental areas shown on public LANSCE maps are depicted, never fences or gates. No fence, gate or access-control feature is drawn or was found.
TA-53 is security-sensitive; only the public technical-area line and named accelerator and experimental-area buildings from a county map service are drawn, no gates or fences.

An OSM API extract of the LANSCE building cluster (2026-10-25) holds 118 TA-53 features, many tagged with the LANL building number in `ref` (53-0003, 53-0007, 53-0017, 53-0030, 53-0364, 53-0365 ...), and Los Alamos County publishes a TA-53 boundary and building footprints with the same numbers (the OSM and county outlines of buildings 6, 14, 17, 18, 19, 365 agree to 1-9 m). OSM node 8041862150 'LANSCE' is the west end of TA-53, 2.8 km from the building cluster, so a search around that node alone finds almost nothing and would wrongly suggest that TA-53 is unmapped.

The old marker geometry:lansce-site-marker (OSM point at the western tip of TA-53, tied to site:lanl-lansce, whose only timeline is LSND's 1993-98 placement, so it vanished in 2026) is retired. The linac structure carries accelerator:lansce (active since 1972); the other features have no entity and no `valid` (timeless) and carry site_id site:lanl-lansce.

Building 53-3 is drawn from two sources: the long wing from OSM (linac, ODbL) and the main hall from the county layer. OSM building 53-0007 (WNR, 22 m across) and the county's 'Weapons Neutron Research Build' (BLDG_ID 7, 205 m long, thin) are different outlines of the same number; the county outline is drawn.
TA-53 is security-sensitive; only the public technical-area line and named accelerator and experimental-area buildings are drawn, no gates or fences.
map:los-alamos-national-laboratory.summary_technical: Local map for facility:los-alamos-national-laboratory. geometry:lansce-linac-building is OSM way 370719333 (ref 53-0003, 695 m x 26 m, east-west) as the linac structure (accelerator:lansce); county 'Structures' footprints (BLDG_ID, DESC_) give the main hall, the Proton Storage Ring facility (span 31.8 m vs the 30 m diameter in LA-UR-05-9402), the Lujan Center, WNR, a 'Gta Facility', a neutrino-experiment service building and 70 others; the county TA-53 polygon is the boundary. detector:lsnd is unlocated. OSM and county outlines of the same building numbers agree to a few metres.

notes: Positions on the Ross Ice Shelf are time-dependent (the shelf flows and skiways are re-groomed), so the Williams Field outline is a mapped position, not a fixed survey point.
The site coordinate (167.05667 E, 77.8675 S, 20 km precision, from the gns: tags of the OpenStreetMap Williams Field way) falls inside the drawn outline, 0.7 km from its centroid.
map:mcmurdo-ldb.summary_technical: One local map for facility:mcmurdo-ldb. OpenStreetMap: the Williams Field aerodrome polygon (way 821080729, source ADD, ICAO NZWD, 5.4 km2) as a timeless context outline at the place of site:mcmurdo-ldb-launch-site, and the McMurdo Station place node (515065315). The facility is placed at Williams Field by a NASA balloon-team diary. The LDB camp buildings and detector:anita's launch pads are unlocated; ANITA has no ground position.

notes: The only Atlas experiment that references MIT is ABRACADABRA (experiment:abracadabra, detector:abracadabra at site:mit-cambridge-campus); no other MIT experiment or site exists in the Atlas, so only these buildings are drawn.
map:mit.summary_technical: One local map for facility:mit. OpenStreetMap: campus multipolygon (relation 65066) and buildings 26 (way 32525936) and 24 (way 29127459), tied to the Winslow Lab by its contact page ('Building 26-524 Building 24-036'). The Winslow group's link to ABRACADABRA is src:axions-abracadabra-mit-winslow-page. detector:abracadabra is unlocated: its room is not stated.

notes: The site coordinate of site:lsm-frejus used to be an OSM/Nominatim point (45.1962509, 6.6667021, precision_m 500, src:lsm-osm-nominatim) essentially co-located with the Carré Science surface outreach building (geometry:modane-carre-sciences-point), about 6.4 km from the underground laboratory itself by tunnel; it has been replaced by the point of geometry:modane-lsm-underground.

The Fréjus road tunnel gained a second, parallel tube in July 2025 (src:geo-modane-sftrf-second-tube-pr); geometry:modane-tunnel-frejus's representation is kept 'approximate' because OSM tags alone do not confirm which of the two tubes its traced line follows over its full length (a check of relation membership would resolve it). Both tubes run closely parallel and are the same length, so the practical effect on the laboratory's derived position is small.
map:modane-underground-laboratory.summary_technical: One local map for facility:modane-underground-laboratory. The Fréjus road tunnel (OSM ways 101986702 + 317397424) is drawn as context; the laboratory itself is OSM's own tagged area (way 235115147, addr:housename 'PK 6.5, Tunnel du Fréjus'), independently corroborated by the geometric midpoint of the tunnel line (148 m apart) and by a 2009 CNRS Images caption describing the access point as exactly at the tunnel's centre.

notes: The linac structure and the Instrument Hall were placed by georeferencing ORNL's own interactive map ('Chestnut Ridge', labelled building polygons without coordinates) onto OpenStreetMap footprints; both are approximate, and each record states the method, its residuals and its limits.

The dashed outline is the whole SNS complex (the site 'Spallation Neutron Source (SNS) accelerator and target complex'). It is not Neutrino Alley. COHERENT's four operating sub-detectors (CENNS-10, CsI, Ge, NaI) all sit in Neutrino Alley, officially 'about 20 meters from the SNS target' at its closest point and 50 m long overall (src:geo-ornl-neutrino-alley-qa); none is drawn, since no source gives the alley's coordinates or heading, or any detector's position along it.
map:oak-ridge-national-laboratory.summary_technical: One local map for facility:oak-ridge-national-laboratory. Drawn: the OSM footprint of the linac structure (front-end building, klystron gallery and tunnel; 370 m, accelerator:sns) and of the Instrument Hall (building 8700), both identified by georeferencing the polygons of ORNL's interactive map, plus the Guest House and 22 other OSM buildings. Not located: the 248 m accumulator ring, the HEBT (169 m), the RTBT (151 m), the target's position inside building 8700 and Neutrino Alley.

notes: map-center-far warning is expected and accepted: the map centre is the array's own geometric centroid (about 40 km from site:malargue-auger, the Observatory's administrative address in the town of Malargue).

Every active surface-detector station is drawn individually: 1587 main-array stations in 20 north-to-south bands of 79 or 80 and 49 infill-only stations, from sdMap.csv in the Auger Open Data release 3 (CC BY-SA 4.0). The map format has no multi-point type, so each station is a 3.6 m square marker (the tank diameter) in a MultiPolygon of at most 80 stations.

The four fluorescence-detector buildings (Los Leones, Los Morados, Loma Amarilla, Coihueco) are not drawn: no fetched source states their coordinates. Overpass (extract 2026-10-25T11:11:23Z) has Pierre Auger Observatory communication-tower nodes at (-35.496078, -69.4498211) on Cerro Los Leones, (-35.1143142, -69.6000234) and at the Malargue campus, and the peaks Cerro Los Leones and Loma Amarilla, but no fluorescence building footprint, and a tower is not the building; the Open Data fdPixelMap.csv gives pixel pointing only and the Open Data event display is a binary Unity build.
geometry:auger-sd750-infill-boundary: the 71 stations flagged sd750 enclose 29.3 km2, not the "23.5 km2, 61-detector" infill of the Observatory paper; no check is asserted (unresolved.
The Auger Open Data page does not state the UTM zone or datum of sdMap.csv; zone 19 south on WGS 84 is this work's reading (the numbers only fall at Malargue in zone 19).
map:pierre-auger-observatory.summary_technical: One local map for facility:pierre-auger-observatory. 1587 main-array (1500 m grid) and 49 infill-only (750 m grid) stations are the northing/easting columns of sdMap.csv in the Auger Open Data release 3 (read as UTM 19S, WGS 84), drawn as 3.6 m markers; convex hulls of the active main array (3098 km2 against the quoted 3000 km2) and of the sd750 stations are computed outlines. The four fluorescence-detector buildings are not placed.

notes: The campus is drawn with its experimental hall WEHA (a hall whose OSM footprint, 134.0 m x 52.4 m, matches PSI's own 'dimensions experimental hall: 130x50x20 m3'), the Injector 2 hall WIHA, the SINQ building, the UCN hall WNAB and 109 other buildings, all from OpenStreetMap elements fetched through the OSM API on 2026-10-25.
The identity of each named building rests on PSI's own 2015 site-map legend (PSI four-letter codes) matched to the OSM name tag of the same code; the OSM names themselves are third-party.

geometry:psi-campus-boundary (entity site:psi-villigen) accounts for the site and, through it, the placements of detector:meg, detector:meg-ii and detector:mu3e; no source was found that says in which hall MEG II or Mu3e stands, so none is attributed to a hall.
map:psi.summary_technical: Local map for facility:psi: campus boundary (OSM ways 28028409, 26680824, 26680821), the WEHA experimental hall as a 'hall' feature verified by identity (PSI Arealplan legend 'WEHA Experimentierhalle') and by perimeter/area checks against PSI's 130 m x 50 m (Seidel 2009; measured 370 m / 6916 m2), WIHA (Injektorhalle 2), SINQ and the UCN hall WNAB as approximate context buildings, and 109 further OSM buildings as one MultiPolygon. accelerator:psi-hipa is unlocated: no fetched source names the building of the 590 MeV Ring Cyclotron (ø15 m).

notes: Telescope footprints are OpenStreetMap ways (MAGIC I and II, LST-1, three newer LSTs), read with the OSM API map call on 2026-10-25 because Overpass answered 502 at capacity. The MAGIC separation (85 m) and the LST-1 distance from MAGIC ('~100 m') come from the joint LST-1/MAGIC paper (arXiv:2310.01954).

The three newer LSTs are not numbered in OSM or in any fetched source; they are named by OSM way. CTAO announced the inauguration of the four-LST sub-array on 2026-10-15 and says the telescopes will now be commissioned. All CTAO features inherit experiment:ctao's 'construction' status, so LST-1 (observing since 2018) is drawn with the same status as the new LSTs.

The planned CTAO-North layout (four LSTs and nine MSTs over about 0.5 km2) is published only as an unscaled figure; the nine MSTs are not drawn. OSM also maps FACT (a small Cherenkov telescope that is not an atlas entity) and many optical telescopes, which are not part of this facility's inventory.
map:roque-de-los-muchachos-observatory.summary_technical: Six telescope footprints and the MAGIC counting house from OpenStreetMap; the MAGIC-I to MAGIC-II distance is checked against the published 85 m, LST-1 against the published ~100 m from MAGIC. The outline is the convex hull of the six footprints. Map centre is CTAO-North's published array coordinate.

notes: Tank positions are OpenStreetMap footprints (300 ways traced together in 2017), read with the OSM API map call on 2026-10-25 because Overpass answered 502 at capacity. The tank count (300), the field area (hull 22.4 thousand m2 against the paper's 22,000 and 22,395 m2) and the summed tank area (13.1 thousand m2 against 12.6 thousand m2 for 300 circles of 7.3 m) all match the HAWC paper.

The 345 outrigger tanks (1.55 m diameter, 'concentric circular symmetric' around the main array, 12 to 18 m apart; arXiv:1908.06650) are not drawn: no fetched source gives their positions and OSM has none of them. Backlog: the outrigger layout table or GIS from the HAWC collaboration.

The HAWC Utility Building ('installed East to the tank array platform') and the counting house have no named OSM polygon; the LMT on the Sierra Negra summit is a separate facility about 1.3 km to the south-west and is not drawn.
site:hawc-sierra-negra carries the paper's coordinate rounded to 0.01 degree (precision_m 600); a tighter position could be derived from the layout of the tank field, but none is recorded.
map:sierra-negra.summary_technical: The 300 tank footprints come from OpenStreetMap and are checked by summed area against 300 circles of the published 7.3 m diameter; the tank-field outline is their convex hull, checked against the published 22,000 m2 array area and the 22,395 m2 platform. Map centre is the hull centroid.

notes: geometry:slac-collider-experimental-hall-sld and geometry:slac-collider-experimental-hall-dmradio are drawn over the SAME OpenStreetMap polygon (way 232494549, Building 750): the SLD detector occupied this hall 1991-1998, and the DMRadio-m3 axion search is independently sourced (src:geo-slac-dmradio-prd-2022) to occupy the same building today. This is an intentional geometry-duplicate-shape pair, not an error: two different, independently sourced entities in the same physical hall at different times.

PEP-II's ring is drawn only partially (geometry:slac-pep-ii-partial-ring): the two 'PEP Ring Road' ways found in OpenStreetMap do not close into a loop and together cover only about 2,019 m of the collider's official 2,200 m circumference (src:geo-slac-pepii-cdr-osti), so no ring-length check is asserted. A fuller trace of the ring, such as a survey drawing, would allow the check.
All SLAC geometry in this map comes from a single Overpass extract of the campus plus the sources cited above.
map:slac.summary_technical: One local map for facility:slac. Geometry sourced from a single OpenStreetMap Overpass extract (the SLAC property boundary way 634083231; the Klystron Gallery building way 162058026, checked against SLAC's own '3,073.72 m' figure for that structure; the two 'PEP Ring Road' ways; the PEP Interaction Region 2 / BaBar hall and Collider Experimental Hall / SLD-DMRadio-m3 hall buildings; and nine other campus buildings drawn as context), cross-referenced against the official SLAC Area Map building-number table and the PEP-II Conceptual Design Report's circumference figure.

map:snolab.summary_technical: Local map for facility:snolab. Surface geometry from OpenStreetMap (the SNOLAB office node and the Creighton Mine industrial landuse polygon). The underground cavity is a derived 22 m circle centred on the SNO NIM detector paper's own published coordinate, cross-checked against the same paper's stated diameter. SNOLAB's other experiment halls (SNO+, DEAP-3600, DAMIC, SuperCDMS SNOLAB, nEXO, NEWS-G) share this one sourced site coordinate and have no distinct footprint located.

notes: The detector is drawn at its surveyed midpoint (six decimals, 3 m accuracy), with its steel-plane envelope built from the published axis azimuth and dimensions. The cavern itself is not drawn.
map:soudan-underground-laboratory.summary_technical: Surveyed MINOS far-detector midpoint (arXiv:0805.3170, 0.7 m inertial survey precision), derived 8 m x 30.3 m steel-plane envelope along the published 333.4452° axis, OSM shaft house and Shaft #8; cavern and CDMS laboratory unlocated.

notes: The planned 28 further RNO-G stations (35 in all, same grid) are not drawn: only the seven installed stations have as-installed positions.
The earlier RNO-G design paper (arXiv:2010.12279, Figure 7) says the planned grid spacing was about 1 km; the 2024 as-built paper says 1.25 km, which the installed positions (1.20 to 1.28 km) match.
map:summit-station-greenland.summary_technical: One local map for facility:summit-station-greenland. Seven RNO-G station points derived from RNO_season_2022.json offsets (m) about the published DISC-borehole origin (72.582793 N, -38.455815 E), each with 1.25 km grid-spacing checks to its neighbours (all within 5 %); the OSM skiway line (5101 m against 16,800 ft = 5120.6 m on the official page: pass); eleven unnamed OSM camp building footprints; the DISC borehole. Named camp buildings are unlocated.

notes: Central Utility Cavern (190 m x 19.3 m, between the two detector caverns per DUNE TDR Vol. III 5.2) is not drawn: no fetched source gives its offset along the cavern axis.
Conflict: detector caverns are 144.5 m long in the DUNE TDR (design, 2020) and 521.5 ft = 158.95 m on a December 2023 Fermilab slide; the drawn length is the latter (see geometry records).
Heise (arXiv:2603.06504) Table 4 prints its Latitude and Longitude column headings interchanged; the values carry hemisphere letters and are unambiguous.
map:surf.summary_technical: Local map for facility:surf: OSM building footprints for the Yates and Ross head-frames and hoists, the Davis Campus cavern at its surveyed coordinate (SURF Physics Procedia Table 5), and the LBNF/DUNE north and south detector caverns on the 4850 Level, derived from the published FD1-FD4 module coordinates (Heise 2026, Table 4) and the as-excavated cavern size (521.5 ft x 65 ft). The Central Utility Cavern and access drifts are not drawn.

notes: All 507 surface-detector stations are drawn from TASDPosition.dat in the Telescope Array Collaboration data release on Zenodo (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.8405760, CC BY 4.0), in 7 west-to-east strips of 72 or 73 as 1.73 m markers (the map format has no multi-point type). The release states no origin or orientation; the frame (origin at the CLF, axes true east and north) was found by registering the table against Fig. 5 of arXiv:2103.01086, a plot on latitude and longitude axes: median residual 14 m, rotation -0.001 deg. Accuracy 100 m.

The three fluorescence stations (Black Rock Mesa, Long Ridge, Middle Drum) are read from the triangle markers of Fig. 1 of arXiv:1410.3151 registered to the station table, so each is good to about 500 m and is a figure reading, not a published coordinate. No document fetched gives their latitude and longitude. The three are 20.8 km from the CLF, which the papers describe as equidistant from all three, about 21 km.

An earlier version of this map drew one 6 km-precision point (geometry:ta-array-point) at the centre quoted as "39.3 N and 112.9 W" in arXiv:1201.4964; it is removed because the stations and the laser carry the location. The address telescopearray.org redirects to a dynamic-DNS host that was not followed (checked 2026-10-25).
TAx4 (500 further stations at 2.08 km spacing, arXiv:2103.01086) is not drawn: its positions are published only as a figure of deployed and planned locations.
The array is a square 1.2 km grid of 507 stations, whose centroid is 4.0 km south of the CLF; the CLF is the centre of the three-telescope triangle.
map:telescope-array-utah.summary_technical: One local map for facility:telescope-array-utah. The 507 SD stations are the x, y columns of TASDPosition.dat (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.8405760), placed with the origin at the Central Laser Facility (39.296918 N, 112.908733 W from arXiv:1410.3151) and axes true east and north, a frame established by registration against a published latitude-longitude plot (median residual 14 m). The three FD stations are read from a published layout figure registered to the table (accuracy 500 m). TAx4 is not drawn.

notes: The building is a single-building map by design: CENPA 'is located at the North Physics Lab: a 53,500-sq. ft. stand-alone facility'.
map:university-of-washington-cenpa.summary_technical: One local map for facility:university-of-washington-cenpa. Single OpenStreetMap footprint (way 885743335, 3833 m2, 104 m span; King County GIS origin) identified as CENPA's building by CENPA's About page. detector:admx and detector:project-8 are unlocated (rooms not stated).

map:wipp.summary_technical: Local map for facility:wipp. Surface geometry is OpenStreetMap's 'Waste Isolation Pilot Plant' landuse polygon (the fenced protected/exclusive-use area) plus two unidentified shaft features. EXO-200's own underground position within the North Experimental Area is not sourced beyond its 655 m depth, so nothing is drawn on that level.

notes: The Wright Lab site is under construction (a new front entrance as of 2026-08-03 on the laboratory's visit page; an addition to Wright Lab, an instrumentation centre and a Physical Sciences and Engineering Building on its history page), so the footprint may change.
map:yale-wright-lab.summary_technical: One local map for facility:yale-wright-lab. Single OpenStreetMap footprint (way 228473354, 2590 m2, 78 m span, last edited 2024-06-02), tied to the laboratory by its official navigation address. detector:haystac is unlocated (room not stated). Other OSM buildings named Wright Laboratory West, Electron Accelerator Laboratory and Wright Annex are not drawn: no official source ties them to the laboratory.

notes: The near hall's distance checks to units 3–6 sit 3–4 % from the TDR figures (10–28 m), consistent with using reactor-building centroids as proxies for core centres over 300–740 m baselines; the tolerance on those checks is widened to 5 % with that reason and accuracy_m raised accordingly — see the geometry record.
map:yonggwang-hanbit-reactor-site.summary_technical: Reactor-unit footprints and plant boundary from OpenStreetMap; near/far hall positions derived by multilateration from the six units using Table 1.2 of the RENO TDR (arXiv:1003.1391); the assignment of reactor numbers to buildings is the only one of the 720 permutations that fits.

claim.quote: New precise results of a measurement of the elastic electron-proton scattering cross section performed at the Mainz Microtron MAMI are presented.

result:a1-proton-form-factors-high-preci.summary_technical: About 1400 elastic e-p cross sections measured with the three A1 spectrometers for Q^2 up to 1 (GeV/c)^2 with statistical errors below 0.2%; electric and magnetic form factors extracted by direct fits of form-factor models to the cross sections, showing features at the pion-cloud scale.
result:a1-proton-form-factors-high-preci.why_it_matters: The result feeds the proton charge radius determination and the proton radius puzzle, and tests the pion-cloud description of the nucleon.

claim.quote: Differential cross sections for the gamma p -> pi^0 p reaction have been measured with the A2 tagged-photon facilities at the Mainz Microtron, MAMI C, up to the center-of-mass energy W=1.9 GeV.

result:a2-pi0-photoproduction-proton-mam.summary_technical: Differential cross sections for gamma p -> pi0 p with the A2 tagged-photon facilities at MAMI C (1557 and 1604 MeV beams, 2013 and 2014) up to W = 1.9 GeV, fine energy and angular binning, increasing the existing pi0 photoproduction data by about 47% and sensitive to high partial waves.
result:a2-pi0-photoproduction-proton-mam.why_it_matters: Constrains the nucleon-resonance spectrum through partial-wave analysis of the most precisely measured meson photoproduction channel.

claim.quote: We report on a new measurement of the beam transverse single spin asymmetry in electron-proton elastic scattering,

result:a4-beam-transverse-asymmetry-wide.summary_technical: Beam transverse single-spin asymmetry A_perp^ep at five beam energies from 315.1 to 1508.4 MeV (30 < theta < 40 degrees, Q^2 = 0.032, 0.057, 0.082, 0.218, 0.613 (GeV/c)^2): significant inelastic contributions to the two-photon-exchange amplitude at low Q^2; no theoretical calculation reproduces the result.
result:a4-beam-transverse-asymmetry-wide.why_it_matters: A wide-energy benchmark for calculations of two-photon exchange, a quantum correction that limits the interpretation of precision electron-scattering measurements.

claim.quote: A new measurement of the parity violating asymmetry in elastic electron scattering on hydrogen at backward angles and at a four momentum transfer of Q^2=0.22 (GeV/c)^2 is reported here.

result:a4-strange-form-factors-backward-.summary_technical: A_LR = (-17.23 +- 0.82 stat +- 0.89 syst) ppm at backward angles (beam energy 315.1 MeV), Standard Model expectation without strangeness A_0 = (-15.87 +- 1.22) ppm; combined with the forward-angle data, G_E^s(0.22) = 0.050 +- 0.038 +- 0.019 and G_M^s(0.22) = -0.14 +- 0.11 +- 0.11.
result:a4-strange-form-factors-backward-.why_it_matters: Separates the strange electric and magnetic form factors at Q^2 = 0.22 (GeV/c)^2 within a single experiment.

claim.quote: The difference is a direct measurement of the strangeness contribution to the vector form factors of the proton.

result:a4-strange-form-factors-q2-0230-2.summary_technical: A_phys = (-5.44 +- 0.54 stat +- 0.27 sys) x 10^-6 at Q^2 = 0.230 (GeV/c)^2 and theta_e = 30-40 degrees, against A_0 = (-6.30 +- 0.43) x 10^-6 without strangeness, giving G_E^s + 0.225 G_M^s = 0.039 +- 0.034; first parity-violation experiment to count individual scattering events (PbF2 calorimeter, 0.62 sr).
result:a4-strange-form-factors-q2-0230-2.why_it_matters: A counting-mode measurement whose systematic effects differ from those of the earlier integrating experiments.

claim.quote: We report the first detection of the gravitational lensing of the cosmic microwave background through a measurement of the four-point correlation function in the temperature maps made by the Atacama Cosmology Telescope.

result:act-cmb-lensing-first-detection-2.summary_technical: ACT MBAC temperature maps: four-point-function estimate of the lensing convergence power spectrum at 2-degree scales; 4-sigma detection, density-fluctuation amplitude measured to 12%, consistent with LCDM.
result:act-cmb-lensing-first-detection-2.why_it_matters: The abstract says the lensing power spectrum measures "the amplitude of matter density fluctuations on comoving length scales of around 100 Mpc at redshifts around 0.5 to 3".

claim.quote: When combined with CMB lensing from ACT and Planck, and baryon acoustic oscillation data from DESI DR1, we measure a baryon density of $\Omega_b h^2=0.0226\pm0.0001$, a cold dark matter density of $\Omega_c h^2=0.118\pm0.001$, a Hubble constant of $H_0=68.22\pm0.36$ km/s/Mpc

result:act-dr6-power-spectra-lcdm-2025.summary_technical: ACT DR6 (19,000 deg^2 at 98/150/220 GHz): TT/TE/EE spectra over 10,000 deg^2 fit by LCDM + foregrounds; with Planck (P-ACT), lensing and DESI DR1 BAO: H0 = 68.22 +/- 0.36, n_s = 0.974 +/- 0.003, sigma_8 = 0.813 +/- 0.005; no evidence for excess lensing or departure from flatness.
result:act-dr6-power-spectra-lcdm-2025.why_it_matters: The abstract reports "no evidence for excess lensing in the power spectrum, and no departure from spatial flatness" and agreement of LCDM parameters between P-ACT and DESI DR2 at the 1.6σ level.

claim.quote: We report on the results at ADONE to study the properties of the newly found 3.1-BeV particle.

notes: The abstract page says '3.1-BeV' (the 1974 unit). The paper is signed by three groups; the Gamma-Gamma Group is attributed to Gamma-Gamma 2 (second-generation), see the experiment record.
key_value_text is null: the abstract states no numerical value.
The paper is a preliminary result; the result type is 'measurement'.
result:adone-new-3-1-gev-particle-proper.summary_technical: Gamma-Gamma, MEA and Baryon-Antibaryon groups at ADONE: study of the properties of the newly found 3.1 GeV particle (J/psi) in e⁺e⁻ annihilation after the machine was pushed beyond its standard 3.0 GeV, Phys. Rev. Lett. 33, 1408 (received 18 November 1974); an erratum is Phys. Rev. Lett. 33, 1649.
result:adone-new-3-1-gev-particle-proper.why_it_matters: The INFN-LNF page says the second-generation detectors at ADONE gave significant contributions to the measurement of the new particle's properties, and that ADONE could reach the energy only by pushing the machine beyond its standard parameters.

claim.quote: We present here experimental results on the production of antihydrogen in a pulsed mode in which the time when 90% of the atoms are produced is known with an uncertainty of ~250 ns.

result:aegis-pulsed-antihydrogen-2021.summary_technical: Charge exchange between laser-excited Rydberg positronium (from a pulsed positron beam on a nanochanneled Si target) and trapped, cooled antiprotons gives pulsed antihydrogen with a production time known to ~250 ns for 90% of the atoms.
result:aegis-pulsed-antihydrogen-2021.why_it_matters: The abstract calls pulsed production a major landmark in the AEgIS experiment to perform direct measurements of the validity of the Weak Equivalence Principle for antimatter.

claim.quote: The energy spectrum extends beyond 10^{20} eV and the energy gap between the highest energy event and the others is being filled up with recently observed events.

notes: AGASA's own results page gives the published spectrum's epoch as Feb. 17, 1990 to Jul. 31, 2002 for the later, extended data set (Takeda et al. 2003, arXiv:astro-ph/0209422).
result:agasa-spectrum-beyond-gzk-cutoff-.summary_technical: Energy spectrum above 10^18.5 eV from AGASA data from February 1990 to October 1997; extends beyond 10^20 eV, the shape suggesting absence of the 2.7 K (GZK) cutoff or a new component beyond it. Later HiRes (2007) reported the suppression at 6 × 10¹⁹ eV.
result:agasa-spectrum-beyond-gzk-cutoff-.why_it_matters: The abstract says the spectral shape suggests the absence of the 2.7 K cutoff in the energy spectrum or a possible presence of a new component beyond it, which made the GZK question a central puzzle until HiRes and Auger reported a suppression.

claim.quote: Observation of High-Energy Neutrino Reactions and the Existence of Two Kinds of Neutrinos

notes: The paper title says "Observation"; the discovery label comes from BNL and the Nobel citation, so the type follows the title (A16).
result:ags-two-neutrinos-observation-196.summary_technical: High-energy neutrinos from pion decay interacted in a spark chamber to give muons; of 34 single-track events 29 were attributed to neutrino-produced muons, while 6 shower candidates were far fewer than the showers expected for a single neutrino type.
result:ags-two-neutrinos-observation-196.why_it_matters: The 1988 Nobel Prize in Physics went to Lederman, Schwartz and Steinberger "for the neutrino beam method and the demonstration of the doublet structure of the leptons through the discovery of the muon neutrino"; BNL notes that at the time only the electron-neutrino was known.

claim.quote: An improved value for the lifetime of the (anti-)hypertriton has been obtained using the data sample of Pb-Pb collisions at sqrt(s_NN) = 5.02 TeV collected by the ALICE experiment at the LHC.

notes: STAR's hypertriton measurement is a different paper and is not used for this record.
result:alice-hypertriton-lifetime-2019.summary_technical: ALICE measurement of the (anti-)hypertriton lifetime via its charged two-body mesonic decay channel in Pb–Pb collisions at √sNN = 5.02 TeV: τ = 242 +34/−38 (stat) ± 17 (syst) ps, compatible with representative theoretical predictions and, in the collaboration's words, contributing to the solution of the longstanding hypertriton lifetime puzzle.
result:alice-hypertriton-lifetime-2019.why_it_matters: The hypertriton (a proton, neutron and Lambda hyperon bound together) is the lightest hypernucleus. Its Lambda is only weakly bound, so the paper cites calculations expecting a lifetime close to that of a free Lambda, while earlier heavy-ion measurements came out lower: the 'hypertriton lifetime puzzle'. The paper links hypernuclear lifetimes to the hyperon-nucleon interaction, which matters for models of neutron-star interiors.

claim.quote: A suppression of the inclusive J/psi yield in Pb-Pb is observed with respect to the one measured in pp collisions scaled by the number of binary nucleon-nucleon collisions.

notes: Classified as a measurement rather than an observation: J/ψ suppression was already established at SPS and RHIC energies before ALICE. This paper measures the effect at LHC energy and reports a suppression factor with quoted uncertainties, so it is not presented as a first observation, even though the abstract says the suppression 'is observed'.
result:alice-jpsi-suppression-pbpb-2012.summary_technical: ALICE measurement of inclusive J/ψ production at forward rapidity (2.5 < y < 4) in Pb-Pb collisions at √sNN = 2.76 TeV: nuclear modification factor R_AA = 0.545 ± 0.032 (stat) ± 0.083 (syst) for the 0-80% most central collisions, with no significant dependence on centrality. The paper states that R_AA is larger than at the SPS and RHIC for most central collisions (the abstract says these features 'appear significantly different from measurements at lower collision energies') and that models including J/ψ production from charm quarks in a deconfined partonic phase can describe the data.
result:alice-jpsi-suppression-pbpb-2012.why_it_matters: Charmonium (J/ψ) production is studied in heavy-ion collisions as a probe of the quark-gluon plasma: in the colour-screening model, the in-medium dissociation probability of quarkonium states is expected to give an estimate of the initial temperature of the system. At LHC energy ALICE finds R_AA larger than at SPS and RHIC for the most central collisions, and reports that models with J/ψ production from charm quarks in a deconfined partonic phase can describe the data.

claim.quote: Here we present the first observation of strangeness enhancement in high-multiplicity pp collisions.

result:alice-strangeness-enhancement-pp-.summary_technical: ALICE measurement (pp at √s = 7 TeV) of strange (K0S, Lambda) and multi-strange (Xi, Omega) hadron yields relative to pions as a function of charged-particle multiplicity. The collaboration presents 'the first observation of strangeness enhancement in high-multiplicity pp collisions': the yields relative to pions increase significantly with multiplicity and, at the highest multiplicities, reach values similar to those observed in Pb-Pb collisions.
result:alice-strangeness-enhancement-pp-.why_it_matters: Strangeness enhancement was originally proposed as a signature of QGP formation in nuclear collisions, where it is more pronounced for multi-strange baryons. The paper reports it in high-multiplicity pp collisions and says the agreement with p-Pb results indicates that the phenomenon is related to the final system created in the collision.

claim.quote: Here we report the observation of the 1S–2S transition in magnetically trapped atoms of antihydrogen.

result:alpha-1s-2s-spectroscopy-2016.summary_technical: Two-photon (243 nm) 1S–2S excitation of magnetically trapped antihydrogen; the transition frequency is consistent with that expected for hydrogen in the same environment, consistent with CPT invariance at a relative precision of about 2 x 10^-10.
result:alpha-1s-2s-spectroscopy-2016.why_it_matters: The abstract says the CPT theorem requires hydrogen and antihydrogen to have the same spectrum, so any difference would signal CPT violation.

claim.quote: Here we report measurements of the fine structure in the n = 2 states of antihydrogen, the antimatter counterpart of the hydrogen atom.

result:alpha-fine-structure-2020.summary_technical: Optical excitation of the 1S–2P Lyman-alpha transitions at 1 T to 16 ppb; the inferred zero-field 2P1/2–2P3/2 splitting is consistent with QED to 2 per cent, and, with the earlier 1S–2S value, the Lamb shift is consistent with theory at 11 per cent.
result:alpha-fine-structure-2020.why_it_matters: The abstract calls the result an important step towards precision tests of charge–parity–time symmetry and towards the antiproton charge radius.

claim.quote: Here we show that antihydrogen atoms, released from magnetic confinement in the ALPHA-g apparatus, behave in a way consistent with gravitational attraction to the Earth.

result:alpha-g-gravity-2023.summary_technical: Antihydrogen released from magnetic confinement in the vertical ALPHA-g apparatus behaves consistently with gravitational attraction to the Earth; repulsive antigravity is ruled out. The abstract describes it as paving the way for precision tests of the weak equivalence principle for antimatter.
result:alpha-g-gravity-2023.why_it_matters: The abstract says the experiment paves the way for precision studies of the gravitational acceleration between anti-atoms and the Earth to test the weak equivalence principle.

claim.quote: Here we demonstrate laser cooling of antihydrogen ... we Doppler-cool a sample of magnetically trapped antihydrogen.

result:alpha-laser-cooling-2021.summary_technical: One-dimensional Doppler cooling on the 1S–2P Lyman-alpha transition of magnetically trapped antihydrogen; median transverse energy reduced by more than an order of magnitude, and the 1S–2S line is about four times narrower than without cooling.
result:alpha-laser-cooling-2021.why_it_matters: The abstract says a colder, denser antihydrogen sample will drastically improve spectroscopic and gravitational studies.

claim.quote: Here we report spectroscopy of a pure antimatter atom, demonstrating resonant quantum transitions in antihydrogen.

result:alpha-resonant-transitions-2012.summary_technical: Microwave spin-flip spectroscopy between hyperfine levels of trapped antihydrogen: in one variant, 23 atoms survived 110 trapping attempts with microwaves off-resonance (0.21 per attempt) and two atoms survived 103 attempts on-resonance (0.02 per attempt).
result:alpha-resonant-transitions-2012.why_it_matters: The abstract frames it as spectroscopy of a pure antimatter atom, allowing comparison with hydrogen and a test of the validity of CPT symmetry.

claim.quote: Here we demonstrate trapping of antihydrogen atoms.

result:alpha-trapped-antihydrogen-2010.summary_technical: Trapping of antihydrogen atoms in the ALPHA magnetic trap: from about 10^7 antiprotons and 7 x 10^8 positrons, 38 annihilation events were observed consistent with controlled release of trapped antihydrogen; the measured background is 1.4 ± 1.4 events.
result:alpha-trapped-antihydrogen-2010.why_it_matters: The abstract says trapping opens the door to precision measurements on anti-atoms, which can soon be subjected to the same techniques as developed for hydrogen.

claim.quote: No significant excess is observed, and a lower limit on the half-life is obtained as $T^{0\nu}_{1/2} > 1.7 \times 10^{22}$ yr at 90$\%$ confidence level.

result:amore-i-ca40-double-electron-capt.summary_technical: Exposure 7.32 kg yr from thirteen 40Ca100MoO4 crystals; a probe of lepton-number violation beyond the primary 100Mo search (arXiv preprint).
result:amore-i-ca40-double-electron-capt.why_it_matters: Shows the CaMoO4 detectors reach other rare decays.

claim.quote:
We observed no indication of $0
u eta eta$ decay and report a new lower limit of the half-life of $^{100}$Mo $0
u eta eta$ decay as $ T^{0
u}_{1/2}>2.9	imes10^{24}~\mathrm{yr}$ at 90\% confidence level.

result:amore-i-improved-limit-2025.summary_technical: Exposure 8.02 kg yr (3.89 kg yr of 100Mo), background 0.025 +/- 0.002 counts/keV/kg/yr near the Q-value; effective Majorana mass limit m_bb < (210-610) meV with several nuclear matrix-element models (Phys. Rev. Lett. 134, 082501 (2025)).
result:amore-i-improved-limit-2025.why_it_matters: The strongest 100Mo half-life limit among the AMoRE results recorded here; sets the stage for AMoRE-II.

claim.quote: show energy resolutions (FWHM) of 7.55 - 8.82 keV at the 2.615 MeV $^{208}$Tl $\gamma$ line, and effective light detection of 0.79 - 0.96 keV/MeV.

result:amore-ii-lmo-calorimeters-2025.summary_technical: Baseline AMoRE-II module design: Li2 100MoO4 crystals of 316 g and 517-521 g operated at 10 mK; alpha discrimination power 12.37-19.50 around the 6Li(n,alpha)3H Q-value of 4.785 MeV (Eur. Phys. J. C 85, 172 (2025)).
result:amore-ii-lmo-calorimeters-2025.why_it_matters: Shows the detector design for AMoRE-II meets its resolution and discrimination needs.

claim.quote:
No evidence for $0
u eta eta$ decay of $^{100}$Mo is found, and a upper limit is set for the half-life of 0$
u eta eta$ of $^{100}$Mo of $T^{0
u}_{1/2} > 9.5	imes10^{22}$ y at 90% C.L..

result:amore-pilot-first-results-2019.summary_technical: 111 kg d live exposure of six 48depl-Ca100MoO4 crystals (1.9 kg) at Y2L; the limit corresponds to an effective Majorana mass limit of (1.2-2.1) eV (Eur. Phys. J. C 79 (2019) 791).
result:amore-pilot-first-results-2019.why_it_matters: The first physics result of the AMoRE project.

claim.quote: A limit on the half-life of $0\nu\beta\beta$ decay of $^{100}$Mo was found at $T_{1/2}^{0\nu} \ge 3.0\times 10^{23}$ years at 90\% confidence level, based on the measured background and its modeling.

result:amore-pilot-improved-limit-2024.summary_technical: Pilot stage with ~1.9 kg CaMoO4 at Y2L from 2015 to 2018; the limit is derived from the measured background and its Monte Carlo model (arXiv preprint; no journal reference in the abstract page).
result:amore-pilot-improved-limit-2024.why_it_matters: Updates the pilot's limit three-fold over the first results.

claim.quote: ANAIS-112 data are consistent with the null hypothesis (p-values of 0.65 and 0.16 for [2-6] and [1-6] keV energy regions, respectively).

result:anais-112-first-results-2019.summary_technical: 1.5 years of data (157.55 kg yr), blind annual-modulation analysis: best-fit amplitudes S_m = -0.0044 +- 0.0058 cpd/kg/keV ([2-6] keV) and -0.0015 +- 0.0063 cpd/kg/keV ([1-6] keV); in agreement with the estimated sensitivity, supporting a 3 sigma sensitivity to DAMA/LIBRA in 5 years.
result:anais-112-first-results-2019.why_it_matters: First annual-modulation result from a NaI(Tl) experiment designed to test DAMA/LIBRA with the same target; the abstract describes the DAMA/LIBRA result as neither confirmed nor ruled out by any other experiment in a model-independent way.

claim.quote: Our results, the most sensitive to date with the same target material, NaI(Tl), are incompatible with the DAMA/LIBRA modulation signal at a 4$\sigma$ confidence level.

notes: Published in Physical Review Letters 135 (2025) 051001 according to the experiment's own news page.
result:anais-112-six-year-2025.summary_technical: Annual modulation analysis of six years of ANAIS-112 data (625.75 kg yr exposure per the 2026 review), the most sensitive to date with a NaI(Tl) target; the abstract highlights the need to address systematic uncertainties in the comparison, particularly those related to the detector response to nuclear recoils, which may require further characterisation of the DAMA crystals.
result:anais-112-six-year-2025.why_it_matters: The strongest published ANAIS-112 statement on the DAMA/LIBRA signal; a later, still preliminary full-exposure analysis (June 2026 conference news on the ANAIS site) reports no hint of modulation and a sensitivity of about 5 sigma.

claim.quote: supporting the absence of modulation in our data, and incompatible with DAMA/LIBRA result at 3.3 (2.6) $\sigma$, for a sensitivity of 2.5 (2.7) $\sigma$

result:anais-112-three-year-2021.summary_technical: Blind analysis of three years (effective exposure 313.95 kg yr): modulation amplitude -0.0034 +- 0.0042 cpd/kg/keV in [1-6] keV and 0.0003 +- 0.0037 cpd/kg/keV in [2-6] keV; incompatible with DAMA/LIBRA at 3.3 (2.6) sigma for a sensitivity of 2.5 (2.7) sigma; also a phase-free search and a search for periodic signals at other frequencies.
result:anais-112-three-year-2021.why_it_matters: The first ANAIS-112 result to state a statistical (in)compatibility with the DAMA/LIBRA modulation, with the same target material.

claim.quote: establishing the first detection of neutrino-induced Cherenkov light with an LAPPD

result:annie-first-lappd-beam-neutrinos-.summary_technical: Packaged ANNIE LAPPD (PAL): waterproof self-triggering module with fast waveform digitization and precision timing synchronised to the ANNIE subsystems; beam-correlated LAPPD frames consistent with CC interactions seen in multiple subsystems; long-term stability, timing synchronisation and event matching validated.
result:annie-first-lappd-beam-neutrinos-.why_it_matters: A step towards deploying fast photodetectors in future large neutrino and particle detectors.

claim.quote: Using APEX test run data, we searched in the mass range 175--250 MeV, found no evidence for an $A'\to e^+e^-$ reaction, and set an upper limit of $\alpha'/\alpha \simeq 10^{-6}$.

result:apex-test-run-search-2011.summary_technical: Search for A' -> e+e- in electron-nucleus fixed-target scattering with APEX test-run data: no evidence in the mass range 175-250 MeV; upper limit alpha'/alpha ~ 1e-6.
result:apex-test-run-search-2011.why_it_matters: Demonstrated that fixed-target searches can explore a wide new range of sub-GeV masses and couplings.

claim.quote: we derive values for the electron recoil statistical rejection power of more than 10$^8$ in the tonne-scale liquid argon target for events with more than 50 detected photons at a 50% acceptance for nuclear recoils.

result:ardm-backgrounds-and-psd-2017.summary_technical: Pulse-shape discrimination estimated from a Cf-252 neutron calibration (Gaussian electron- and nuclear-recoil bands); the abstract also gives the Rn-222 emanation rate of the cryostat (65.6+-0.4 microHz/l), the 39Ar activity of the atmospheric argon (0.95+-0.05 Bq/kg) and the cosmic muon flux at Canfranc.
result:ardm-backgrounds-and-psd-2017.why_it_matters: The abstract says the results pave the way for the next physics run of ArDM in double-phase mode.

claim.quote: We show first data recorded during a single-phase commissioning run in 2015 (ArDM Run I), which overall confirm the good and stable performance of the ton-scale LAr detector.

result:ardm-detector-and-run1-2016.summary_technical: Detector paper: liquid argon TPC with an 850 kg active target installed underground at LSC; first data from the single-phase commissioning run in 2015 (ArDM Run I).
result:ardm-detector-and-run1-2016.why_it_matters: The standard reference for the ArDM apparatus at Canfranc.

claim.quote: ArDM-1t is the first operating ton-scale liquid argon detector for direct search of Dark Matter particles.

notes: Preliminary report of May 2015; no journal publication was found.
result:ardm-first-ton-scale-lar-operatio.summary_technical: Commissioning achievements and preliminary observations of single-phase Run I with a full ton-scale liquid argon target, including a first indication of the background discrimination power of LAr detectors at the ton scale, and an outlook for completing the detector with a drift field and SiPM light readout.
result:ardm-first-ton-scale-lar-operatio.why_it_matters: The collaboration describes it as the first operating ton-scale liquid argon detector for direct dark matter searches.

claim.quote: A relatively low value close to 0.5 m was found for the attenuation length of the liquid argon bulk to its own scintillation light.

result:ardm-scintillation-attenuation-le.summary_technical: Attenuation length of the argon scintillation light in the tonne-scale target from 39Ar and 83mKr light-yield spectra compared with a ray-tracing model (single-phase run); the low value is interpreted as optically active impurities not removed by the purification systems.
result:ardm-scintillation-attenuation-le.why_it_matters: It shows that impurity control matters for large liquid argon detectors; the abstract interprets the low value as optically active impurities.

claim.quote: We describe the status of the installation and present first results from data collected underground with the detector filled with gas argon at room temperature.

notes: Commissioning-stage technical result; not a dark matter search.
result:ardm-underground-commissioning-20.summary_technical: Status of the installation of the ton-scale double-phase argon TPC at LSC and first results from underground data collected with gas argon at room temperature; the commissioning phase was ongoing.
result:ardm-underground-commissioning-20.why_it_matters: Marks the start of ArDM's underground commissioning at Canfranc after its operation on the surface at CERN.

claim.quote: The ARGO-YBJ air shower detector monitored the Crab Nebula gamma ray emission from 2007 November to 2013 February.

result:argo-ybj-crab-nebula-five-years-2.summary_technical: Integrated signal of about 3.3 × 10⁵ events at 21.1 standard deviations; spectrum in 0.3-20 TeV fitted by a power law with index 2.63 ± 0.05; 200-day light curve compatible with steady emission; no flare above four standard deviations in a 1-15 day search.
result:argo-ybj-crab-nebula-five-years-2.why_it_matters: The abstract reports a five-year energy spectrum and light curve of the Crab Nebula, a standard candle of TeV astronomy, and a correlation analysis with Fermi-LAT over about 4.5 years.

claim.quote: The ArgoNeuT collaboration presents the first measurements of inclusive muon neutrino charged current differential cross sections on argon.

result:argoneut-first-argon-cc-cross-sec.summary_technical: Inclusive nu_mu CC differential cross sections on argon in outgoing muon angle (0-36 deg) and momentum (0-25 GeV/c) in the NuMI beam, consistent with Monte Carlo expectation across the sampled kinematics.
result:argoneut-first-argon-cc-cross-sec.why_it_matters: The first liquid-argon cross-section measurements, a basis for DUNE and the short-baseline programme.

claim.locator: Phys. Lett. B 192 (1987) 245, paper title (Crossref record; the antiparticle bar is lost in the metadata)
claim.quote: Observation of B0-B0 mixing

notes: The abstract could not be retrieved (publisher site blocks automated access); the claim is the paper title only.
result:argus-b-mixing-observation-1987.summary_technical: ARGUS (DORIS II, Υ(4S) region), 'Observation of B⁰-B̄⁰ mixing', Phys. Lett. B 192 (1987) 245-252: the first observation of neutral B-meson oscillation, a process closely linked to CP violation.
result:argus-b-mixing-observation-1987.why_it_matters: Ziemann's history of German accelerators calls it the first observation of B-B̄ mixing, a process closely linked to the prevalence of matter over antimatter in our universe that is referred to as CP-violation.

claim.quote: Here we report the development of an antihydrogen source using a cusp trap for in-flight spectroscopy.

result:asacusa-antihydrogen-source-2014.summary_technical: Cusp-trap antihydrogen source for in-flight spectroscopy: a total of 80 antihydrogen atoms unambiguously detected 2.7 m downstream of the production region, a step towards Rabi-like beam spectroscopy of the ground-state hyperfine splitting.
result:asacusa-antihydrogen-source-2014.why_it_matters: The abstract says high-resolution comparisons of hydrogen and antihydrogen sensitively test CPT symmetry and any difference would point to new physics.

claim.quote: By comparing the results with three-body quantum electrodynamics calculations, we derived an antiproton-to-electron mass ratio of 1,836.1526736(23), where the parenthetical error represents one standard deviation.

result:asacusa-antiprotonic-helium-spect.summary_technical: Two-photon spectroscopy of 3He+ and 4He+ antiprotonic helium at 139.8, 193.0 and 197.0 nm, three transition frequencies to fractional precisions of 2.3–5 parts in 10^9; antiproton-to-electron mass ratio 1,836.1526736(23) from three-body QED, in agreement with the proton-to-electron value.
result:asacusa-antiprotonic-helium-spect.why_it_matters: The abstract says an antimatter particle should have exactly the same mass and absolute charge as its counterpart under CPT symmetry, and that such spectroscopy can constrain the equality of the antiproton and proton charges and masses.

claim.quote: Here we demonstrate the production of antihydrogen atoms at very low energy by mixing trapped antiprotons and positrons in a cryogenic environment.

result:athena-cold-antihydrogen-2002.summary_technical: Production of antihydrogen at very low energy by mixing trapped antiprotons and positrons in a cryogenic environment; the neutral anti-atoms are detected when they escape the trap and annihilate, producing a characteristic signature in an imaging particle detector.
result:athena-cold-antihydrogen-2002.why_it_matters: The abstract says that cold atoms and anti-atoms could form the basis of a new precise test of CPT invariance, which implies that they must have the same spectrum.

claim.quote: which yields an observed (expected) significance of 5.4 (5.5) standard deviations, thus providing direct observation of the Higgs boson decay into b-quarks.

result:atlas-hbb-observation-2018.summary_technical: Search for H → bb̄ produced with a W or Z boson (VH) in 79.8 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV data: observed (expected) significance 4.9 (4.3) standard deviations; combined with Run 1 and other Run 2 H → bb̄ searches: 5.4 (5.5) standard deviations, 'direct observation of the Higgs boson decay into b-quarks'. Ratio of the measured H → bb̄ yield to the Standard Model expectation 1.01 ± 0.12 (stat) +0.16/−0.15 (syst); VH production observed at 5.3 (4.8) standard deviations (Run 2 combination).
result:atlas-hbb-observation-2018.why_it_matters: H → bb̄ is the dominant decay of the Standard Model Higgs boson, but large multijet backgrounds make a search in the dominant gluon–gluon fusion production mode difficult, so the search uses production with a W or Z boson. The ratio of the measured H → bb̄ yield to the Standard Model expectation is 1.01 ± 0.12 (stat) +0.16/−0.15 (syst).

claim.quote: This observation, which has a significance of 5.9 standard deviations, corresponding to a background fluctuation probability of 1.7x10^-9, is compatible with the production and decay of the Standard Model Higgs boson.

notes: Collaboration wording is "observation of a new particle", not "discovery of the Higgs boson"; see result:atlas-nature-higgs-2022 for ATLAS's later combined Higgs measurements.

ATLAS and CMS presented their preliminary results at a CERN seminar on 4 July 2012 (CERN press release of that date); the cited arXiv preprint was submitted 31 July 2012 and published as Phys. Lett. B 716 (2012) 1.
result:atlas-higgs-observation-2012.summary_technical: Combined search: H → ZZ(*) → 4ℓ, γγ and WW(*) → eνμν in 8 TeV data (about 5.8 fb⁻¹) combined with 7 TeV results (about 4.8 fb⁻¹: ZZ(*), WW(*), bb̄, τ⁺τ⁻, plus improved ZZ(*) → 4ℓ and γγ analyses). 'Clear evidence for the production of a neutral boson with a measured mass of 126.0 ± 0.4 (stat) ± 0.4 (sys) GeV is presented'; the observation has a local significance of 5.9σ (background fluctuation probability 1.7×10⁻⁹) and is compatible with the production and decay of the Standard Model Higgs boson.
result:atlas-higgs-observation-2012.why_it_matters: The paper's introduction notes that the mechanism that breaks electroweak symmetry in the Standard Model, which gives mass to massive elementary particles, implies a scalar particle, the Higgs boson, and had not been verified experimentally. ATLAS reports clear evidence for a new neutral boson of mass 126.0 GeV whose observation is compatible with the production and decay of the Standard Model Higgs boson.

claim.quote: the observed (expected) significance amounts to 6.4 (5.4) standard deviations and constitutes an observation of H->tautau decays.

result:atlas-htautau-observation-2018.summary_technical: 36.1 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV data: H → ττ signal established with observed (expected) significance 4.4 (4.1) standard deviations; combined with 7 and 8 TeV data, 6.4 (5.4) standard deviations, which 'constitutes an observation of H → ττ decays'. Total H → ττ cross section at 13 TeV 3.77 +0.60/−0.59 (stat) +0.87/−0.74 (syst) pb; all measurements in agreement with Standard Model expectations.
result:atlas-htautau-observation-2018.why_it_matters: Tau leptons are heavier cousins of the electron, so this decay tests how the Higgs boson couples to leptons. The paper states that the combined significance constitutes an observation of H → ττ decays by the ATLAS experiment, with all measurements in agreement with Standard Model expectations.

claim.quote: This letter describes the observation of the light-by-light scattering process, γγ → γγ, ... in Pb+Pb collisions at sNN = 5.02 TeV.

result:atlas-lbyl-observation-2019.summary_technical: Ultraperipheral Pb+Pb collisions at 5.02 TeV per nucleon pair, 1.73 nb⁻¹ (Nov 2018): 59 γγ → γγ candidates against a background of 12 ± 3 events, 8.2σ significance, fiducial cross section 78 ± 13 (stat.) ± 7 (syst.) ± 3 (lumi.) nb.
result:atlas-lbyl-observation-2019.why_it_matters: Light-by-light scattering is forbidden in the classical theory of electrodynamics; in the Standard Model it proceeds at one-loop level via virtual box diagrams involving electrically charged fermions or W bosons. The paper notes that extensions of the Standard Model (for example magnetic monopoles, vector-like fermions and axion-like particles) can add contributions, so the measurement is sensitive to new physics.

claim.quote: These tests reveal that the Higgs boson discovered ten years ago is remarkably consistent with the predictions of the theory and provide stringent constraints on many models of new phenomena beyond the Standard Model.

result:atlas-nature-higgs-2022.summary_technical: Combination of ATLAS measurements of Higgs boson production and decay rates using the full Run 2 dataset (139 fb⁻¹ at 13 TeV) to study the Higgs boson's interactions with gluons, photons, W and Z bosons, b and t quarks and tau leptons, with indications of interactions with muons; published in Nature 607, 52–59 (2022).
result:atlas-nature-higgs-2022.why_it_matters: The abstract says these tests reveal that the Higgs boson is remarkably consistent with the predictions of the theory and provide stringent constraints on many models of new phenomena beyond the Standard Model.

claim.quote: An exclusion limit at the 95% confidence level on the mass of the gluino is set at 2.30 TeV for a simplified model containing only a gluino and the lightest neutralino, assuming the latter is massless.

result:atlas-squark-gluino-limit-2020.summary_technical: Search for squarks and gluinos in final states with jets and missing transverse momentum, no electrons or muons (139 fb⁻¹ at 13 TeV): no statistically significant deviation from the background expectation for any search strategy; 95% CL exclusion limit on the gluino mass of 2.30 TeV for a simplified model containing only a gluino and the lightest neutralino, assuming the latter is massless; in a simplified model of strong production of mass-degenerate first- and second-generation squarks, squark masses below 1.85 TeV are excluded for a massless lightest neutralino.
result:atlas-squark-gluino-limit-2020.why_it_matters: Squarks and gluinos are the supersymmetric partners of quarks and gluons. The paper states that these limits 'extend substantially beyond the region of supersymmetric parameter space excluded previously by similar searches with the ATLAS detector'.

claim.quote: The mass of the top quark is measured to be m_top = 172.08 +/- 0.39 (stat) +/- 0.82 (syst) GeV.

result:atlas-topmass-measurement-2018.summary_technical: Lepton+jets tt̄ candidates from 20.2 fb⁻¹ of 8 TeV data, three-dimensional template method: m_top = 172.08 ± 0.39 (stat) ± 0.82 (syst) GeV; a combination with previous ATLAS m_top measurements gives m_top = 172.69 ± 0.25 (stat) ± 0.41 (syst) GeV.
result:atlas-topmass-measurement-2018.why_it_matters: The top-quark mass enters the electroweak fit and the calculation of the stability of the Higgs potential, so sharper top-mass measurements sharpen Standard Model consistency tests.

claim.quote: the observed significance is 5.8 standard deviations, compared to an expectation of 4.9 standard deviations.

result:atlas-tth-observation-2018.summary_technical: ttH production searched for with Higgs decays into bb̄, WW*, τ⁺τ⁻, γγ and ZZ* in up to 79.8 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV data: observed significance 5.8 standard deviations (4.9 expected). Combined with ttH searches in 4.5 fb⁻¹ at 7 TeV and 20.3 fb⁻¹ at 8 TeV: 6.3 (5.1) standard deviations. Total ttH cross section at 13 TeV: 670 ± 90 (stat) +110/−100 (syst) fb, in agreement with the Standard Model prediction.
result:atlas-tth-observation-2018.why_it_matters: The paper describes ttH production as a more direct test of the Higgs boson's coupling to the top quark than indirect measurements, which assume no contribution from unknown particles in the gluon-gluon fusion loop. The 13 TeV ttH cross section is measured as 670 ± 90 (stat) +110/−100 (syst) fb, in agreement with the Standard Model prediction.

claim.quote: yielding m_W = 80370 +/- 7 (stat.) +/- 11 (exp. syst.) +/- 14 (mod. syst.) MeV = 80370 +/- 19 MeV

result:atlas-wmass-measurement-2017.summary_technical: W → lepton ν candidates from 4.6 fb⁻¹ of 7 TeV data, template fits to lepton transverse momentum and transverse mass: m_W = 80370 ± 19 MeV, combining statistical, experimental-systematic and modelling uncertainties.
result:atlas-wmass-measurement-2017.why_it_matters: In the Standard Model the W-boson mass is related to the top-quark and Higgs-boson masses through a radiative correction that is sensitive to them, and in extended theories that correction receives contributions from additional particles. The paper says that improving the precision of the W-mass measurement is of high importance for testing the overall consistency of the Standard Model.

claim.quote: Experimental Observation of a Heavy Particle J

notes: The paper title says "Observation"; the discovery label comes from the Nobel citation and BNL, so the type follows the title (A16).
The SLAC side of the same discovery is not recorded in this stream.
result:aubert-ting-j-particle-observatio.summary_technical: e⁺e⁻ mass spectrum from p + Be at the AGS measured with a precise pair spectrometer shows a resonance at m = 3.1 GeV with width approximately zero (less than 5 MeV, per Ting's lecture).
result:aubert-ting-j-particle-observatio.why_it_matters: The 1976 Nobel Prize in Physics went to Burton Richter and Samuel Ting "for their pioneering work in the discovery of a heavy elementary particle of a new kind"; BNL says Ting's use of the AGS helped confirm the existence of the charmed quark.

claim.quote: No candidate for the stellar core collapse has been detected during the observation period.

result:baksan-bust-neutrino-burst-limit-.summary_technical: Neutrino-burst monitor with a 240 t target: observation time 33.02 yr (1980-06-30 to 2018-12-31), no core-collapse candidate; upper bound 0.070 per year (90 % CL) on the mean Galactic core-collapse supernova frequency.
result:baksan-bust-neutrino-burst-limit-.why_it_matters: A continuous, decades-long watch for Galactic supernova neutrinos; the same instrument recorded neutrinos from SN 1987A.

claim.quote: Observation of a Hyperon with Strangeness Minus Three

notes: The paper title says "Observation"; BNL says its team "discovered" the particle, so the type follows the title (A16).
result:barnes-omega-minus-observation-19.summary_technical: A single event in the Brookhaven 80-inch bubble chamber identified the strangeness -3 hyperon, the missing member of the baryon decuplet of SU(3) flavour symmetry.
result:barnes-omega-minus-observation-19.why_it_matters: The CERN Courier writes that with that single event "any remaining doubt about SU(3) symmetry and Gell-Mann’s Eightfold Way evaporated".

claim.quote: Here we report high-precision cyclotron frequency comparisons of a single antiproton and a negatively charged hydrogen ion (H−) carried out in a Penning trap system.

result:base-antiproton-charge-to-mass-20.summary_technical: Cyclotron-frequency comparison of a single antiproton and an H− ion in a Penning trap at 29.6 MHz, 13,000 measurements; antiproton-to-proton charge-to-mass ratio compared at a precision of 69 parts per trillion, consistent with CPT invariance at the atto-electronvolt scale.
result:base-antiproton-charge-to-mass-20.why_it_matters: The abstract says the precision exceeds the energy resolution of previous antiproton-to-proton mass comparisons by a factor of four.

claim.quote: Here we report a high-precision measurement of ... in units of the nuclear magneton μN with a fractional precision of 1.5 parts per billion (68% confidence level).

result:base-antiproton-magnetic-moment-2.summary_technical: Two-particle spectroscopy in a cryogenic multi-Penning trap system: antiproton magnetic moment −2.7928473441(42) μN, consistent with the proton value 2.792847350(9) μN and with CPT invariance; improves the previous best measurement by a factor of approximately 350.
result:base-antiproton-magnetic-moment-2.why_it_matters: The abstract says the result constrains the magnitude of certain CPT-violating effects to below 1.8 × 10−24 gigaelectronvolts.

claim.quote: Evidence of the Purely Leptonic Decay B- --> tau- nu_tau-bar

notes: The collaboration's word for this result is 'evidence' (in the title); it is not recorded as an observation.
result:belle-b-to-tau-nu-evidence-2006.summary_technical: First evidence for B⁻ → τ⁻ ν̅_τ in 414 fb⁻¹ at the Υ(4S) with 3.5σ significance, B = (1.79 ⁺⁰·⁵⁶₋₀.₄₉(stat) ⁺⁰·⁴⁶₋₀.₅₁(syst)) × 10⁻⁴, giving the first direct determination of the B decay constant f_B.
result:belle-b-to-tau-nu-evidence-2006.why_it_matters: In the Standard Model the decay proceeds via annihilation of the b and u quarks into a W boson; the paper notes that physics beyond the Standard Model, such as supersymmetry or two-Higgs-doublet models, could modify the branching fraction through a charged Higgs boson. The abstract says the measurement implies f_B = 0.229 +0.036/−0.031 (stat) +0.034/−0.037 (syst) GeV and 'is the first direct measurement of this quantity'.

claim.quote: Observation of Large CP Violation in the Neutral B Meson System

notes: Companion measurement to BaBar's contemporaneous result; that is not recorded here.
result:belle-cp-violation-observation-20.summary_technical: Time-dependent measurement of the CP asymmetry with 29.1 fb⁻¹ at the Υ(4S), one B⁰ fully reconstructed as J/ψ K_S, ψ(2S) K_S, χ_c1 K_S, η_c K_S, J/ψ K_L or J/ψ K*⁰ and the flavour of the other identified from its decay products: sin 2φ₁ = 0.99 ± 0.14 (stat) ± 0.06 (syst). 'We conclude that we have observed CP violation in the neutral B meson system'; a zero value of sin 2φ₁ is ruled out at a level greater than 6σ.
result:belle-cp-violation-observation-20.why_it_matters: The paper explains that the Kobayashi–Maskawa model predicts large CP violation in certain B-meson decays, so that measurements of CP violation in B meson decays provide important tests of the KM model; it reports that the result is consistent with the higher range of values allowed by the constraints of the KM model.

claim.quote: Evidence for $D^0 - \bar{D}^0$ Mixing

result:belle-d0-mixing-evidence-2007.summary_technical: Measurement of y_CP = (1.31 ± 0.32(stat) ± 0.25(syst))% from lifetime differences between CP-eigenstate and flavour-eigenstate D⁰ decays in 540 fb⁻¹, 3.2σ from zero, with no evidence for CP violation.
result:belle-d0-mixing-evidence-2007.why_it_matters: The paper says mixing between a particle and its antiparticle had been observed in neutral kaons, B⁰ and, most recently, B_s mesons. In the Standard Model D-mixing is expected to be small, loop diagrams with new, as-yet-unobserved particles could significantly affect the measured values, and CP-violating effects in D-mixing would be a clear signal of new physics; Belle finds no evidence for CP violation.

claim.quote: we determine the branching fraction of the decay $B^{+}\rightarrow K^{+}\nu\bar{\nu}$ to be $[2.3 \pm 0.5(\mathrm{stat})^{+0.5}_{-0.4}(\mathrm{syst})]\times 10^{-5}$, providing the first evidence for this decay at $3.5$ standard deviations.

notes: The collaboration's own word is 'evidence'; the paper is not described as an observation.
result:belle-ii-b-to-k-nunu-evidence-202.summary_technical: Inclusive-tag analysis (B(B⁺ → K⁺ νν̅) = [2.7 ± 0.5 (stat) ± 0.5 (syst)] × 10⁻⁵) and an auxiliary hadronic-tag analysis ([1.1 +0.9/−0.8 (stat) +0.8/−0.5 (syst)] × 10⁻⁵) in 362 fb⁻¹ at the Υ(4S), combined to B(B⁺ → K⁺ νν̅) = [2.3 ± 0.5 (stat) +0.5/−0.4 (syst)] × 10⁻⁵, 'the first evidence for this decay at 3.5 standard deviations'; the combined result is 2.7 standard deviations above the Standard Model expectation.
result:belle-ii-b-to-k-nunu-evidence-202.why_it_matters: B⁺ → K⁺ νν̅ is a flavour-changing neutral-current transition, suppressed in the Standard Model; the paper says its rate predictions are relatively precise and that the rate can be significantly modified in models with non-SM particles such as leptoquarks, or the B⁺ could decay to a kaon and an undetectable particle such as an axion or a dark-sector mediator. All earlier analyses found no evidence for a signal.

claim.quote: measure the τ mass to be 1777.09 ± 0.08 ± 0.11 MeV/c2 , where the first uncertainty is statistical and the second systematic. This result is the most precise to date.

notes: Journal publication was not confirmed by any source consulted.
result:belle-ii-tau-mass-measurement-202.summary_technical: Pseudomass-endpoint measurement in τ⁻ → π⁻π⁺π⁻ ντ using ~175 million e⁺e⁻ → τ⁺τ⁻ events in 190 fb⁻¹ at √s = 10.579 GeV, giving m_τ = 1777.09 ± 0.08(stat) ± 0.11(syst) MeV/c².
result:belle-ii-tau-mass-measurement-202.why_it_matters: The paper says the tau mass is one of the fundamental parameters of the Standard Model, that a precise value matters for tests of lepton-flavour universality between the tau and lighter leptons (the tau mass enters to the fifth power), for predictions of the tau's branching fractions, and for determining the strong-interaction coupling at the tau-mass scale.

claim.quote: We present a determination of the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix element |Vcb | from the decay B → Dℓνℓ using a 365 fb−1 e+ e− → Υ(4S) → B B̄ data sample recorded by the Belle II experiment at the SuperKEKB collider.

result:belle-ii-vcb-measurement-2025.summary_technical: Inclusive-tag determination of |Vcb| from B⁰→D⁻(→K⁺π⁻π⁻) l⁺ νl and B⁺→D̄⁰(→K⁺π⁻) l⁺ νl decays in 365 fb⁻¹ of Belle II Υ(4S) data, using the recoil variable w=v_B.v_D and lattice-QCD form-factor averages. Reports B(B⁰→D⁻ l⁺ νl) = (2.06 ± 0.05stat ± 0.10sys)%, B(B⁺→D̄⁰ l⁺ νl) = (2.31 ± 0.04stat ± 0.09sys)%, a lepton-flavor-universality ratio B(B→D e νe)/B(B→D μ νμ) = 1.020 ± 0.020stat ± 0.022sys, and |Vcb| = (39.2 ± 0.4stat ± 0.6sys ± 0.5th)×10⁻³.
result:belle-ii-vcb-measurement-2025.why_it_matters: The paper says |Vcb| determines the b → c transition rate and must be determined experimentally. Determinations from inclusive and from exclusive decays currently differ by about three standard deviations, which motivates further research; B → Dℓν has received less attention than B → D*ℓν, and the B → D transition has smaller theoretical uncertainties because it is described by a single vector form factor.

claim.quote: We report the observation of a narrow charmonium-like state produced in the exclusive decay process B+ -> K+ pi+pi- J/psi.

result:belle-x3872-observation-2003.summary_technical: Observation of a narrow state decaying to π⁺π⁻ J/ψ in B⁺ → K⁺ π⁺π⁻ J/ψ, mass 3872.0 ± 0.6(stat) ± 0.5(syst) MeV, very close to the D⁰D̅*⁰ threshold, with a statistical significance in excess of 10σ in 152M BB̅ events.
result:belle-x3872-observation-2003.why_it_matters: The paper says the mass and the absence of a strong signal in the γχc1 channel 'are in some disagreement with potential model expectations for the 3Dc2 charmonium state', and that the mass is within errors of the D⁰D̄*⁰ threshold, which is 'suggestive of a loosely bound D D̄* multiquark molecular state, as proposed by some authors'.

claim.quote: Observation of a near-threshold enhancement in th p pbar mass spectrum from radiative J/psi-->gamma p pbar decays

notes: result_type is observation because the title says "Observation"; no significance is quoted in the abstract.
result:bes-ii-ppbar-threshold-observatio.summary_technical: BES: narrow enhancement near 2m_p in the invariant-mass spectrum of p p̄ pairs from radiative J/ψ → γ p p̄ decays; fit with an S- or P-wave Breit-Wigner function; for the S-wave fit the peak mass is below the 2m_p threshold and the full width is less than 30 MeV; 'not consistent with the properties of any known meson resonance'.
result:bes-ii-ppbar-threshold-observatio.why_it_matters: The abstract states that the mass and width values are not consistent with the properties of any known meson resonance.

claim.quote: We report values of $R = \sigma(e^+e^-\to {hadrons})/\sigma(e^+e^-\to\mu^+\mu^-)$ for 85 center-of-mass energies between 2 and 5 GeV measured with the upgraded Beijing Spectrometer at the Beijing Electron-Positron Collider.

result:bes-ii-r-measurement-2002.summary_technical: BES: R = σ(e⁺e⁻ → hadrons)/σ(e⁺e⁻ → μ⁺μ⁻) at 85 centre-of-mass energies between 2 and 5 GeV with the upgraded Beijing Spectrometer at BEPC (hep-ex/0102003; Phys. Rev. Lett. 88, 101802, 2002).
result:bes-ii-r-measurement-2002.why_it_matters: The abstract reports R values at 85 energies between 2 and 5 GeV measured with the upgraded Beijing Spectrometer.

claim.locator: Phys. Rev. Lett. 69, 3021 (1992), abstract (TeX markup on the APS page)
claim.quote: The mass of the ... lepton has been measured at the Beijing Electron-Positron Collider using the Beijing Spectrometer.
