notes: The mass value in the key-value text is read from the TeX markup of the APS abstract; the tau mass fits the standard value used today but this record only reports what the abstract says.
result:bes-tau-mass-measurement-1992.summary_technical: BES: search near the e⁺e⁻ → τ⁺τ⁻ threshold, with one τ decaying to eνν̄ and the other to μνν̄; mass from a fit to the energy dependence of the cross section, m_τ = 1776.9 +0.4/−0.5 ± 0.2 MeV (Phys. Rev. Lett. 69, 3021, 1992).
result:bes-tau-mass-measurement-1992.why_it_matters: IHEP says the precision tau-mass measurement removed doubts about lepton universality.

claim.quote: Observation of a charged charmoniumlike structure in e+e- to pi+pi-J/psi at \sqrt{s}=4.26 GeV

notes: The same structure was reported by Belle shortly afterwards (not recorded here).
result:besiii-zc3900-observation-2013.summary_technical: BESIII: e⁺e⁻ → π⁺π⁻J/ψ at √s = 4.260 GeV with 525 pb⁻¹; Born cross section (62.9 ± 1.9 ± 3.7) pb consistent with Y(4260) production; a structure at about 3.9 GeV/c² in the π^±J/ψ mass spectrum, the Zc(3900), with M = (3899.0 ± 3.6 ± 4.9) MeV/c² and Γ = (46 ± 10 ± 20) MeV; 'if interpreted as a new particle, it is unusual in that it carries an electric charge and couples to charmonium'.
result:besiii-zc3900-observation-2013.why_it_matters: The abstract notes that, if it is a new particle, it is unusual in that it carries an electric charge and couples to charmonium.

claim.quote: The likelihood analysis yields the constraint $r_{0.05}<0.036$ at 95% confidence.

notes: Published in Phys. Rev. Lett. 127, 151301 (2021) per the official BICEP/Keck publication list.
result:bicep-keck-bk18-r-limit-2021.summary_technical: BK18: joint likelihood of BICEP2/Keck/BICEP3 (95/150/220 GHz, ~400-600 deg^2, depths 2.8, 2.8, 8.8 uK-arcmin) with WMAP and Planck maps vs lensed-LCDM + r + dust + synchrotron + noise; r_0.05 < 0.036 at 95% CL, sigma(r) = 0.009.
result:bicep-keck-bk18-r-limit-2021.why_it_matters: The abstract calls these "the strongest constraints to date on primordial gravitational waves", which bound the energy scale of cosmic inflation.

claim.quote: The tensor-to-scalar ratio derived from the B-mode spectrum is r = 0.03+0.31-0.26, or r < 0.72 at 95% confidence, the first meaningful constraint on the inflationary gravitational wave background to come directly from CMB B-mode polarization.

result:bicep1-b-mode-limit-2010.summary_technical: BICEP1 2006-2007 subset (~2% of sky): E-mode spectrum at 21 < l < 335 with high precision; B modes consistent with zero; r < 0.72 (95%). The three-year data set later gave r < 0.65 (BICEP2 paper).
result:bicep1-b-mode-limit-2010.why_it_matters: The abstract calls it "the first meaningful constraint on the inflationary gravitational wave background to come directly from CMB B-mode polarization".

claim.quote: We find an excess of $B$-mode power over the base lensed-LCDM expectation in the range $30< \ell< 150$, inconsistent with the null hypothesis at a significance of $> 5\sigma$.

notes: The paper's own title says "Detection of B-mode Polarization". The Atlas result type `anomaly` records that the excess was later attributed largely to dust, per the joint BICEP2/Keck/Planck paper cited in `why_it_matters`.
result:bicep2-b-mode-detection-claim-201.summary_technical: BICEP2 I: 3 seasons, 380 deg^2, 87 nK deg depth; B-mode excess at 30 < l < 150 > 5 sigma over lensed-LCDM; r = 0.20 (+0.07/-0.05) with r = 0 disfavored at 7.0 sigma before dust correction; the abstract itself warned that dust models could not exclude explaining the entire excess.
result:bicep2-b-mode-detection-claim-201.why_it_matters: The abstract says "Accounting for the contribution of foreground dust will shift this value downward"; the 2015 BICEP2/Keck/Planck joint analysis found "strong evidence for dust and no statistically significant evidence for tensor modes" (arXiv:1502.00612). Recorded as an anomaly because the signal was reported as a detection but was not confirmed as primordial.

claim.quote: The final result is expressed as a likelihood curve for $r$, and yields an upper limit $r_{0.05}<0.12$ at 95% confidence.

result:bicep2-keck-planck-joint-r-limit-.summary_technical: Joint BICEP2/Keck Array + Planck (30-353 GHz) fit to lensed-LCDM + dust + r: 150x353 GHz cross-correlation in B modes detected at high significance; r_0.05 < 0.12 at 95%; lensing B modes detected at 7.0 sigma.
result:bicep2-keck-planck-joint-r-limit-.why_it_matters: It resolved the status of the BICEP2 B-mode excess: strong evidence for dust, no statistically significant evidence for primordial tensor modes.

claim.quote: In this work, data on the interactions of a carbon-ion beam with kinetic energies of 4.0A~GeV and 4.5A~GeV with C, Al, Cu, and Pb targets are used to measure transverse momentum spectra and rapidity distributions of $\Lambda$ hyperon yields.

notes: Published in JHEP (August 2026) according to a search result; dated by the arXiv v1 submission.
result:bmn-lambda-production-carbon-nucl.summary_technical: Transverse-momentum spectra and rapidity distributions of Lambda hyperon yields in C+C, C+Al, C+Cu and C+Pb at 4.0A and 4.5A GeV, compared with DCM-SMM, UrQMD and PHSD predictions and with Lambda measurements at similar energies; the first fixed-target experiment at the NICA complex.
result:bmn-lambda-production-carbon-nucl.why_it_matters: Strangeness production just above threshold is sensitive to the equation of state of dense nuclear matter that BM@N and the future CBM and NICA experiments study.

claim.quote: Experimental evidence of neutrinos produced in the CNO fusion cycle in the Sun

result:borexino-cno-evidence-2020.summary_technical: Direct observation, with high statistical significance, of CNO-cycle solar neutrinos, identified as an excess of a few counts per day per 100 t of target above the backgrounds in the Borexino liquid-scintillator detector at LNGS, which the collaboration calls the first experimental evidence of this process.
result:borexino-cno-evidence-2020.why_it_matters: The abstract says this result quantifies the relative contribution of CNO fusion in the Sun as of the order of 1%, that the process is dominant in the energy production of massive stars, and that the result paves the way to a direct measurement of the solar metallicity by CNO neutrinos.

claim.quote: those from proton–proton fusion have hitherto eluded direct detection. Here we report spectral observations of pp neutrinos, demonstrating that about 99 per cent of the power of the Sun, 3.84 × 1033 ergs per second, is generated by the proton–proton fusion process.

notes: Classified as a measurement rather than a discovery, observation, evidence or first-detection claim: the paper's title makes no such claim. The abstract's own wording is 'spectral observations of pp neutrinos' that had 'hitherto eluded direct detection'.
result:borexino-pp-first-detection-2014.summary_technical: Spectral observations of pp neutrinos with the Borexino liquid-scintillator detector at LNGS: pp neutrino interaction rate 144 ± 13 (stat) ± 10 (syst) counts per day per 100 t, flux (6.6 ± 0.7) × 10¹⁰ cm⁻² s⁻¹ in good agreement with the standard solar model prediction; the absence of pp neutrinos is excluded with a statistical significance of 10σ, and about 99% of the Sun's power (3.84 × 10³³ erg/s) is generated by proton–proton fusion.
result:borexino-pp-first-detection-2014.why_it_matters: Direct spectral observation of the pp neutrinos, which make up nearly the entirety of the solar neutrino flux and had hitherto eluded direct detection, demonstrating that about 99 per cent of the Sun's power is generated by proton-proton fusion.

claim.quote: Combined with Planck 2015 cosmic microwave background measurements, our distance scale measurements simultaneously imply curvature {\Omega}_K =0.0003+/-0.0026 and a dark energy equation of state parameter w = -1.01+/-0.06, in strong affirmation of the spatially flat cold dark matter model

result:boss-dr12-galaxy-clustering-cosmo.summary_technical: BOSS DR12: 1.2 million massive galaxies over 9329 deg² (volume 18.7 Gpc³) at effective redshifts 0.38, 0.51, 0.61; BAO DM and H after reconstruction, AP DM·H and fσ8 from RSD (6% precision). With Planck 2015: ΩK = 0.0003 ± 0.0026 and w = -1.01 ± 0.06.
result:boss-dr12-galaxy-clustering-cosmo.why_it_matters: The abstract says the combined distance and growth measurements are tighter and more robust than any single method and strongly affirm the spatially flat cold dark matter model with a cosmological constant.

claim.quote: We find significant and systematic decrease of $R_{dAu}$ with increasing rapidity.

result:brahms-dau-nuclear-modification-v.summary_technical: Transverse-momentum dependence of the nuclear modification factor R_dAu for charged hadrons in d+Au collisions at 200 GeV versus centrality and pseudorapidity (eta = 0, 1, 2.2, 3.2): a significant, systematic decrease with increasing rapidity, with mid-rapidity enhancement and forward suppression more pronounced in central collisions.
result:brahms-dau-nuclear-modification-v.why_it_matters: Relevant to the possible onset of gluon saturation (the colour glass condensate) at RHIC energies.

claim.quote: We review the main results obtained by the BRAHMS collaboration on the properties of hot and dense hadronic and partonic matter produced in ultrarelativistic heavy ion collisions at RHIC.

notes: A review/white paper recorded as a measurement result, never a discovery; the abstract poses the QGP evidence as a question.
result:brahms-rhic-white-paper-2005.summary_technical: Review of the main BRAHMS results on hot and dense hadronic and partonic matter in ultrarelativistic heavy-ion collisions at RHIC, assessing the evidence for a deconfined quark-gluon plasma and for a possible precursor, the Color Glass Condensate.
result:brahms-rhic-white-paper-2005.why_it_matters: One of the four 2005 RHIC white papers in which each experiment assessed what its data show about the matter created at RHIC.

claim.quote: the operation of 8 units with similar features shows, on average, a baseline energy resolution of $26\pm7$ eV.

notes: Technology milestone; the BULLKID prototype is the detector concept of BULLKID-DM, run in a surface laboratory.
result:bullkid-kid-array-concept-2022.summary_technical: BULLKID prototype: 64 dices of 5.4x5.4x5 mm^3 carved in a 3 inch, 5 mm thick silicon wafer with a 0.5 mm common disk hosting a 60 nm patterned aluminium KID layer; 8 units with similar features give on average 26 +- 7 eV baseline resolution.
result:bullkid-kid-array-concept-2022.why_it_matters: The paper says this makes the detector suitable for low-energy processes such as direct interactions of dark matter and CEvNS.

claim.quote: The low energy spectrum resulting from an exposure of 290 hours to ambient backgrounds, acquired with the use of external and internal radiation shields, is compatible with the simulations at the level of $(6.8\pm0.4\,{\rm stat.}\pm0.1\,{\rm syst.})\times10^4$ counts / keV kg days from 2 keV down to an energy of 600 eV.

notes: Surface background run at Sapienza University of Rome, not at LNGS.
result:bullkid-moderate-shield-backgroun.summary_technical: 15 elements of a 60-cube silicon array in a dilution refrigerator at Sapienza with inner lead pot and ~170 kg outer lead castle: (6.8 +- 0.4 stat +- 0.1 syst) x 10^4 counts/keV/kg/day from 2 keV down to 600 eV in agreement with Geant4 simulations; the 225-600 eV region shows a rise in disagreement with simulations that does not share some key traits of the low energy excess seen elsewhere.
result:bullkid-moderate-shield-backgroun.why_it_matters: The abstract says the region between 225 eV and 600 eV shows a rise in background in disagreement with the simulations.

claim.quote: We present the first continuous operation in a surface lab of BULLKID, a detector for searches of light Dark Matter and precision measurements of the coherent and elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering.

notes: Surface run at Sapienza University (no shields); a detector characterisation, not a dark matter search.
result:bullkid-surface-low-energy-spectr.summary_technical: 60 cubic silicon absorbers of 0.34 g each sensed by cryogenic KIDs, 39 hours of ambient background without shields: flat spectrum at (2.0 +- 0.1 stat +- 0.2 syst) x 10^6 counts/keV/kg/day down to a threshold of 160 +- 13 eV; the segmented monolithic structure rejects backgrounds from interactions in other array sites.
result:bullkid-surface-low-energy-spectr.why_it_matters: The abstract states the analysis demonstrates the unique capability of rejecting backgrounds generated from interactions in other sites of the array.

claim.quote: we performed the first search for 0νββ decay in a low background condition using a detector on the scale of hundreds of kg of non-enriched Ca

result:candles-iii-low-background-48ca-2.summary_technical: 130.4 live days in the Kamioka underground: measured background ~1e-3 events/keV/yr/(kg of natCa) in the 0vbb window, in good agreement with Monte Carlo of crystal impurities and (n,gamma) gamma rays; first low-background 0vbb search with a detector of hundreds of kg of non-enriched Ca. No half-life limit is stated in the abstract.
result:candles-iii-low-background-48ca-2.why_it_matters: Demonstrates the background level needed before 48Ca-enriched crystals are deployed for a more sensitive search.

claim.quote: no significant TeV gamma-ray signals have been detected from compact regions around PSR B1706-44 or within the northeast rim of SN 1006

notes: The abstract describes the reanalysis of observations "between 1993 and 1998"; the original detections of PSR B1706-44 (Kifune et al., 1995) and SN 1006 are not recorded as results because the collaboration's own reanalysis does not support them.
The original paper for these detections was not fetched, so no original result record is written.
result:cangaroo-3p8m-reanalysis-2009.summary_technical: Data taken between 1993 and 1998, reanalysed with selection criteria set exclusively from gamma-ray simulations and OFF-source data: no significant signal from compact regions around PSR B1706-44 or in the northeast rim of SN 1006; a 4.5 sigma signal from the Vela pulsar region (HESS J0835-455) from 1993-1995 data.
result:cangaroo-3p8m-reanalysis-2009.why_it_matters: The collaboration discusses why its original analyses gave the source detections; the abstract states the reanalysis was made in response to the H.E.S.S. results. It revises the collaboration's earlier detections of these sources.

claim.quote: We confirm the H.E.S.S. results about the morphology and the energy spectrum, and find the energy spectrum in the NW-rim is consistent with that of the whole remnant.

result:cangaroo-iii-rxj0852-2006.summary_technical: CANGAROO-III observations in January and February 2005 with three telescopes, using three-fold coincidence data: the morphology and energy spectrum confirm H.E.S.S., and the spectrum in the north-west rim is consistent with that of the whole remnant.
result:cangaroo-iii-rxj0852-2006.why_it_matters: The abstract notes that sub-TeV emission from the north-west rim had first been detected with the CANGAROO-II telescope and then confirmed by H.E.S.S..

claim.quote: We find that the nucleon strange quark content is suppressed with respect to the non-strange sea quarks by a factor $\kappa = 0.477 \: ^{+\:0.063}_{-\:0.053}$

result:ccfr-strange-quark-content-1995.summary_technical: NLO QCD analysis of 6090 opposite-sign dimuon events: kappa = 0.477 (+0.063 -0.053), charm mass m_c = 1.70 +- 0.19 GeV, |V_cd| = 0.232 (+0.018 -0.020).
result:ccfr-strange-quark-content-1995.why_it_matters: A key input to global parton-distribution fits and to the CKM element V_cd.

claim.quote: We report on the extraction of the structure functions F_2 and Delta xF_3 = xF_3(nu)-xF_3(nubar) from CCFR nu_mu-Fe and nubar_mu-Fe differential cross sections.

result:ccfr-structure-functions-2001.summary_technical: Physics-model-independent extraction of F2 and Delta xF3 = xF3(nu) - xF3(nubar) from CCFR nu_mu-Fe and nubar_mu-Fe differential cross sections; F2 ratios agree within 5 % with NLO massive-charm predictions; Delta xF3 is higher than theory.
result:ccfr-structure-functions-2001.why_it_matters: Resolved the neutrino-muon structure-function disagreement and tested heavy-charm production models.

claim.quote: This is the first event-by-event observation of Cherenkov photons from sub-MeV electrons in a high-yield scintillator detector, and represents a milestone in low-energy particle detector development.

result:ccm-cherenkov-event-by-event-2025.summary_technical: CCM200 with a 22Na source: prompt time region -6 <= t < 0 ns seen by the uncoated PMTs isolates Cherenkov photons at >5 sigma; basis of a low-background electromagnetic sample and of the first ALP search with a hybrid Cherenkov-scintillation detector at a beam dump.
result:ccm-cherenkov-event-by-event-2025.why_it_matters: Event-by-event Cherenkov identification at sub-MeV energies in a high-light-yield scintillator opens direction and particle-type information for low-energy neutrino and dark-sector searches.

claim.quote: have been excluded at 90% C.L. in the leptophobic model after applying the Feldman-Cousins test statistic

result:ccm-first-leptophobic-dm-search-2.summary_technical: CCM120 engineering run (Fall 2019, 17.9e20 protons on target): observed events compatible with the expected background of 115,005; for m_V/m_chi = 2.1, dark-matter masses 9 MeV to 50 MeV excluded at 90 % CL in a baryonic vector-portal model (Feldman-Cousins).
result:ccm-first-leptophobic-dm-search-2.why_it_matters: The first leptophobic dark-matter search by Coherent CAPTAIN-Mills, with only 1.5 months of beam in its engineering run: it excludes dark-matter masses of about 9 to 50 MeV in the model it tests.

claim.quote: The SI and SD limits extend the lower reach of light WIMPs to 2 GeV and improve over our earlier bounds at WIMP mass less than 6 GeV.

result:cdex-1-160-evee-2018.summary_technical: Exposure of 737.1 kg-days with a physics threshold of 160 eVee; spin-independent and spin-dependent WIMP-nucleon constraints extend the lower reach of light WIMPs to 2 GeV.

claim.quote: we placed the limit of N= 1.75 * 10^{-40} cm^{2} at 90% confidence level on the spin-independent cross-section at WIMP mass of 7 GeV before differentiating bulk signals from the surface backgrounds.

result:cdex-1-first-results-2013.summary_technical: 14.6 kg-day of data with a 994 g p-type point-contact germanium detector at CJPL (rock overburden more than 2400 m); energy threshold 400 eVee; limit 1.75e-40 cm^2 at 7 GeV before surface/bulk event discrimination.
result:cdex-1-first-results-2013.why_it_matters: First experimental limit on WIMP dark matter from CDEX.

claim.quote: Independent of interaction channels, this result contradicts the interpretation that the anomalous excesses of the CoGeNT experiment are induced by Dark Matter, since identical detector techniques are used in both experiments.

result:cdex-1-limits-light-wimps-2014.summary_technical: 53.9 kg-days from a p-type point-contact germanium detector enclosed by a NaI(Tl) anti-Compton detector; event rate and spectrum above the 475 eVee threshold consistent with the background model; part of the allowed regions for WIMP-nucleus coherent elastic scattering at 6-20 GeV is excluded.
result:cdex-1-limits-light-wimps-2014.why_it_matters: States directly that it contradicts the dark-matter interpretation of CoGeNT's anomalous excess.

claim.quote: A cross section limit for the fermionic DM absorption is set to be $\rm 2.5\times 10^{-46} cm^2$(90\% C.L.) at DM mass of 10 MeV/c$^2$.

result:cdex-10-exotic-dm-2022.summary_technical: 205 kg day from a p-type point-contact germanium detector; neutral-current fermionic DM absorption and DM-nucleus 3->2 scattering analysed with a 160 eVee threshold; no significant signal; limits extend to DM masses of 5 MeV/c^2 and 14 MeV/c^2 for the 3->2 scenarios.
result:cdex-10-exotic-dm-2022.why_it_matters: New low-mass dark matter channels tested with germanium.

claim.quote: At an analysis threshold of 160 eVee, improved limits of 8 $\times 10^{-42}$ and 3 $\times 10^{-36}$ cm$^{2}$ at a 90\% confidence level on spin-independent and spin-dependent WIMP-nucleon cross sections, respectively, at a WIMP mass ($m_{\chi}$) of 5 GeV/${c}^2$ are achieved.

result:cdex-10-first-results-2018.summary_technical: 102.8 kg day physics data from the 10 kg germanium detector array immersed in liquid nitrogen; SI 8e-42 cm^2 and SD 3e-36 cm^2 (90% CL) at 5 GeV/c^2; the lower reach of m_chi is extended to 2 GeV/c^2.

claim.quote: Within the context of the standard halo model, the 90\% C.L. allowed regions implied by the DAMA/LIBRA and CoGeNT AM-based analysis are excluded at $>$99.99\% and 98\% C.L., respectively.

result:cdex-1b-annual-modulation-2019.summary_technical: 3.2 yr live time within a 4.2 yr span, 1 kg p-type point-contact germanium detector, analysis threshold 250 eVee; the abstract states the best sensitivity at m_chi < 6 GeV/c^2 among WIMP annual-modulation measurements to date.
result:cdex-1b-annual-modulation-2019.why_it_matters: A direct germanium test of the DAMA/LIBRA and CoGeNT annual-modulation interpretations.

claim.quote: We establish the existence of the top quark using a 67 pb^-1 data sample of Pbar-P collisions at Sqrt(s) = 1.8 TeV collected with the Collider Detector at Fermilab (CDF).

notes: result_type is "observation" (not "discovery") because that is the paper's own title/abstract wording, per instructions to follow the collaboration's wording rather than press characterizations (Fermilab's own tevatron/experiments pages call this "the discovery of the top quark", but the PRL 74, 2626 title and abstract say "Observation ...\"/"We establish the existence...").

The title was confirmed verbatim on 2026-09-17 against journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.74.2626, whose title is "Observation of Top Quark Production in pbar-p Collisions with the Collider Detector at Fermilab" (shown here in Unicode notation as pp̄; the ASCII form "ppbar" is kept as an alias).
result:cdf-top-quark-observation-1995.summary_technical: CDF observation of top-quark pair production in pp̄ collisions at √s = 1.8 TeV using a 67 pb⁻¹ sample: a signal consistent with t t̄ decay to WW b b̄ but inconsistent with the background prediction by 4.8σ, with additional evidence from a peak in the reconstructed mass distribution; m_top = 176 ± 8 (stat) ± 10 (sys) GeV/c², t t̄ production cross section 6.8 +3.6/−2.4 pb.
result:cdf-top-quark-observation-1995.why_it_matters: Fermilab's page on CDF says the top quark was the last undiscovered quark of the six predicted to exist by current scientific theory, and that CDF and DZero announced the result on 2 March 1995. The CDF paper measures the top-quark mass (176 ± 8 (stat) ± 10 (sys) GeV/c²) and the t t̄ production cross section.

claim.quote: Neutrino and antineutrino total charged current cross sections on iron were measured in the 100, 160, and 200 GeV narrow band beams at the CERN SPS in the energy range 10 to 200 GeV.

result:cdhs-total-cc-cross-sections-1987.summary_technical: Total nu and nu-bar charged-current cross sections on iron in the 100, 160 and 200 GeV SPS narrow-band beams, 10-200 GeV: sigma/E = (0.686 +- 0.019)e-38 cm^2/GeV/nucleon (nu) and (0.339 +- 0.010)e-38 (nu-bar), corrected for non-isoscalarity; no energy dependence of sigma/E between 50 and 150 GeV within +-3 % (nu) and +-4 % (nu-bar).
result:cdhs-total-cc-cross-sections-1987.why_it_matters: High-precision total neutrino cross sections used for decades as normalisation of neutrino-nucleon scattering and for tests of scaling and of the quark-parton model.

claim.quote: CDMS data give limits on the spin-independent WIMP-nucleon elastic-scattering cross-section that exclude unexplored parameter space above 10 GeV c^{-2} WIMP mass and, at > 84% CL, the entire 3$\sigma$ allowed region for the WIMP signal reported by the DAMA experiment.

result:cdms-i-exclusion-limits-2000.summary_technical: 96 live days with three 165 g Ge BLIP detectors (10.6 kg d final exposure after cuts) plus a 33-live-day 100 g Si ZIP run, at 17 m.w.e. beneath Stanford; the Si nuclear recoils are used to measure the unvetoed neutron background.
result:cdms-i-exclusion-limits-2000.why_it_matters: First direct test of the DAMA claim with a different target and event-by-event background rejection.

claim.quote: Resulting limits on the spin-independent WIMP-nucleon elastic-scattering cross-section exclude unexplored parameter space for WIMPs with masses between 10-70 GeV c^{-2}.

result:cdms-i-exclusion-limits-2002.summary_technical: 15.8 kg d on Ge with a relaxed fiducial-volume cut (1998-99 data): 23 WIMP candidates consistent with neutrons; surface-event rejection >95%; limits exclude 10-70 GeV/c^2 and border but do not exclude supersymmetric parameter space.
result:cdms-i-exclusion-limits-2002.why_it_matters: The definitive CDMS I paper, describing the detectors, the shallow-site neutron background and the limits in detail.

claim.quote: Using exposures on the order of one kilogram-day from initial runs of our experiment, we have achieved (preliminary) upper limits on the WIMP-nucleon cross section that are comparable to much longer runs of other experiments.

result:cdms-i-preliminary-limits-1997.summary_technical: TAUP97 proceedings: Ge (165 g NTD, 1.60 kg d) and Si detectors at the 17 m.w.e. Stanford site; phonon plus ionization discrimination; plan to continue at the Soudan mine.
result:cdms-i-preliminary-limits-1997.why_it_matters: Marks the start of CDMS limits from cryogenic Ge/Si detectors with simultaneous phonon and ionization readout.

claim.quote: A single event with a recoil of 64 keV passes all of the cuts and is consistent with the expected misidentification rate of surface-electron recoils.

result:cdms-ii-first-run-soudan-2005.summary_technical: First exposure of the CDMS II Ge and Si detectors at Soudan (2090 m.w.e.): one 64 keV event passes all cuts; the spin-independent WIMP-nucleon limit has a minimum of 4e-43 cm^2 at 60 GeV/c^2 and the spin-dependent WIMP-neutron limit a minimum of 2e-37 cm^2 at 50 GeV/c^2.
result:cdms-ii-first-run-soudan-2005.why_it_matters: First-run result of CDMS II at Soudan.

claim.quote: Under standard halo assumptions, these data partially exclude parameter space favored by interpretations of the DAMA/LIBRA and CoGeNT experiments' data as WIMP signals, and exclude new parameter space for WIMP masses between 3 GeV/c^2 and 4 GeV/c^2.

notes: Attributed to experiment:cdms-ii (the data are from the first tower of CDMS II ZIP detectors) but taken at the Stanford Underground Facility, not at Soudan where the Atlas places CDMS II.
result:cdms-ii-shallow-site-low-threshol.summary_technical: Four ~224 g Ge and two ~105 g Si ZIP detectors at the Stanford Underground Facility, December 2001 - June 2002 (118 live days raw); low-threshold analysis down to the ~1 keV (Ge) and ~2 keV (Si) trigger thresholds; limits for WIMP masses below 9 GeV/c^2.
result:cdms-ii-shallow-site-low-threshol.why_it_matters: One of the first low-threshold germanium results to test the CoGeNT and DAMA/LIBRA light-WIMP interpretations.

claim.quote: We present the combined results on electron-pair production in 158 GeV/n {Pb-Au} ($\sqrt{s}$= 17.2 GeV) collisions taken at the CERN SPS in 1995 and 1996, and give a detailed account of the data analysis.

result:ceres-ee-pair-production-pb-au-20.summary_technical: Combined 1995 and 1996 Pb-Au data: enhancement over neutral-meson decays of 2.31 ± 0.19 (stat) ± 0.55 (syst) ± 0.69 (decays) for semi-central collisions (28% of the geometric cross section) integrated over m > 200 MeV/c^2, with stronger-than-linear scaling with N_ch and dominance of low pair pt, suggesting pi+pi- annihilation in a hot dense hadronic medium.
result:ceres-ee-pair-production-pb-au-20.why_it_matters: Established the low-mass dilepton enhancement that motivated the NA60 precision measurement and the interpretation in terms of in-medium rho modification.

claim.quote: The data clearly favor a substantial in-medium broadening of the $\rho$ spectral function over a density-dependent shift of the $\rho$ pole mass.

result:ceres-rho-modification-pb-au-2006.summary_technical: e+e- pair production in central Pb-Au collisions at 158A GeV/c with the upgraded CERES spectrometer (improved mass resolution): the excess over hadron decays favours substantial in-medium broadening of the rho spectral function over a density-dependent shift of the pole mass.
result:ceres-rho-modification-pb-au-2006.why_it_matters: Together with NA60's dimuon result, supports the broadening scenario of chiral symmetry restoration.

claim.quote: Observation of Antiprotons

notes: The paper title says "Observation"; the discovery label comes from the Nobel citation and Berkeley Lab History ("the discovery of the antiproton"), so the type follows the title (A16).
result:chamberlain-segre-antiproton-obse.summary_technical: Momentum and velocity measurements of negative particles produced in Bevatron collisions identified the antiproton; Berkeley Lab dates the first evidence to 21 September 1955.
result:chamberlain-segre-antiproton-obse.why_it_matters: The 1959 Nobel Prize in Physics went to Emilio Segrè and Owen Chamberlain "for their discovery of the antiproton".

claim.quote: We report final results on electroweak parameters from muon-neutrino electron scattering observed in the CHARM II detector from 1987 till 1991.

result:charm-ii-electroweak-parameters-1.summary_technical: Final results from nu_mu-e scattering in CHARM II (1987-1991 sample): 2677 +- 82 and 2752 +- 88 events in the nu and nu-bar beams; sin^2 theta_W = 0.2324 +- 0.0083 from the ratio of differential cross sections; effective couplings g_V = -0.035 +- 0.017 and g_A = -0.503 +- 0.017 from the absolute rate.
result:charm-ii-electroweak-parameters-1.why_it_matters: The most precise determination of the weak mixing angle from neutrino-electron scattering, free of the hadronic uncertainties of neutrino-nucleon measurements.

claim.quote: Inclusive neutrino and antineutrino charged current interactions were studied in the CHARM detector exposed to neutrino and antineutrino Wide Band Beams of the CERN 400 GeV SPS.

result:charm-structure-functions-1983.summary_technical: Inclusive nu and nu-bar charged-current scattering in the CHARM detector in the SPS wide-band beams; x and Q^2 dependence of F2 and xF3 and of the antiquark distribution determined, with the gluon distribution extracted from the Q^2 evolution.
result:charm-structure-functions-1983.why_it_matters: An early high-statistics measurement of the scaling violations of the nucleon structure functions, testing perturbative QCD with neutrino beams.

claim.quote: we find (at 90% confidence level) no evidence for neutrino oscillations in the electron antineutrino disappearance mode

result:chooz-initial-results-1997.summary_technical: Rate comparison of detected and expected positron events at ~1 km: no evidence (90 % CL) for oscillations in the anti-nu_e disappearance mode for delta m^2 > 0.9e-3 eV^2 at maximum mixing and sin^2(2 theta) > 0.18 at large delta m^2.
result:chooz-initial-results-1997.why_it_matters: Began the series of limits on the third mixing angle that Daya Bay, Double Chooz and RENO later turned into a measurement.

claim.quote: We find (at 90% confidence level) no evidence for neutrino oscillations in the anti_nue disappearance mode, for the parameter region given by approximately Delta m**2 > 7 x 10**-4 eV^2 for maximum mixing, and sin**2(2 theta) = 0.10 for large Delta m**2.

result:chooz-limits-1999.summary_technical: Entire data sample, rate analysis: no anti-nu_e disappearance at 90 % CL for delta m^2 > 7e-4 eV^2 (maximum mixing), sin^2(2 theta) < ~0.10 at large delta m^2; a spectral-shape comparison of the two reactors gives a weaker but flux-independent limit.
result:chooz-limits-1999.why_it_matters: The CHOOZ bound on theta-13, the benchmark that the Daya Bay, Double Chooz and RENO measurements were designed to improve on.

claim.quote: In a two-neutrino mixing scheme, a 90% C.L. upper limit of sin2 2θµτ < 4.4 × 10−4 is set for large ∆m2 , improving by a factor 1.5 the previously published CHORUS result.

result:chorus-final-numu-nutau-2007.summary_technical: Final nu_mu -> nu_tau appearance analysis of all CHORUS data (1994-1997) with new emulsion scanning and event reconstruction applied to the 1996-97 events without a muon in the electronic detectors, combined with earlier samples: sin^2(2 theta_mu_tau) < 4.4e-4 at 90 % CL for large delta m^2; improves the previous CHORUS limit by a factor 1.5.
result:chorus-final-numu-nutau-2007.why_it_matters: The final CHORUS limit, closing the programme the experiment was built for and 1.5 times tighter than its earlier limit; NOMAD's limit, from the same beam, is more stringent at large delta m^2.

claim.quote: Evidence for the 2π Decay of the K20 Meson

notes: Typed evidence because the Letter's title says "Evidence" (A16); the Nobel citation and BNL call the same work a discovery of CP violation.
result:christenson-cronin-fitch-turlay-k.summary_technical: Two-pion decays of K_L at about 0.2% of all decays, found with a two-arm spark-chamber spectrometer in a neutral beam at the Brookhaven AGS; interpreted as CP violation.
result:christenson-cronin-fitch-turlay-k.why_it_matters: The 1980 Nobel Prize in Physics went to James Cronin and Val Fitch "for the discovery of violations of fundamental symmetry principles in the decay of neutral K-mesons".

claim.quote: A large asymmetry with a sin(phi) modulation is observed, as predicted for the interference term of Deeply Virtual Compton Scattering and the Bethe-Heitler process.

notes: Result type follows the title wording "Observation of exclusive DVCS ...".
result:clas-dvcs-beam-spin-asymmetry-obs.summary_technical: First CLAS measurement of the beam-spin asymmetry in ep→epγ at 4.25 GeV: a large sin(φ) asymmetry from DVCS-Bethe-Heitler interference, with modulation amplitude α = 0.202 ± 0.028, directly proportional to the imaginary part of the DVCS amplitude at leading order and leading twist.
result:clas-dvcs-beam-spin-asymmetry-obs.why_it_matters: DVCS gives access to generalised parton distributions, which describe the three-dimensional structure of the nucleon; this was an early demonstration at JLab energies.

claim.quote: We report the first measurement of the DVCS beam-spin asymmetry using the CLAS12 spectrometer with a 10.2 and 10.6 GeV electron beam scattering from unpolarised protons.

notes: Preprint dated by arXiv v1; the paper was later published in Phys. Rev. Lett. (2023) according to a search-engine summary, not verified here.
result:clas12-dvcs-beam-spin-asymmetry-e.summary_technical: First CLAS12 measurement of the DVCS beam-spin asymmetry with 10.2 and 10.6 GeV electron beams on an unpolarised liquid-hydrogen target (data from Fall 2018 and Spring 2019), providing over 2000 new data points that greatly extend the Q^2 and Bjorken-x coverage in the valence region and constrain generalised parton distributions.
result:clas12-dvcs-beam-spin-asymmetry-e.why_it_matters: DVCS data constrain generalised parton distributions, the 3D structure of the nucleon, over a much larger kinematic range than before.

claim.quote: Through cross-correlation with Planck, we detected the cosmic reionization at $99.4\%$ significance and measured the reionization optical depth $\tau=0.053^{+0.018}_{-0.019}$, marking the first ground-based attempt at such a measurement.

result:class-90-ghz-reionization-optical.summary_technical: CLASS 90 GHz, 115 detector-years through 2024, variable-delay polarization modulator: polarization sensitivity 78 uK arcmin; cross-correlation with Planck gives tau = 0.053 (+0.018/-0.019) and a 99.4% detection of reionization; consistent with Planck at l > 30.
result:class-90-ghz-reionization-optical.why_it_matters: The abstract calls it "the first ground-based attempt at such a measurement" of the reionization optical depth.

claim.quote: We report the first evidence of charmless semileptonic decays of B mesons.

notes: result_type is evidence because the abstract says "first evidence"; the paper title says "Observation". CLASSE dates the b → u discovery to 1989 (submission year).
result:cleo-charmless-semileptonic-b-evi.summary_technical: CLEO (CLEO-2, Υ(4S)): first evidence of charmless semileptonic B decays b → u e ν and b → u μ ν in the lepton momentum interval 2.4-2.6 GeV/c, where the b → c background is negligible (Phys. Rev. Lett. 64, 16, 1990).
result:cleo-charmless-semileptonic-b-evi.why_it_matters: CLEO's own timeline lists the 1989 discovery of b → u transitions among its major results.

claim.quote: Observation of Three Upsilon States

notes: The Υ was first seen at Fermilab in 1977 in hadron collisions; CESR resolved the three bound states in e+e- collisions (Berkelman).
result:cleo-upsilon-three-states-observa.summary_technical: CLEO: three narrow resonances observed in e⁺e⁻ annihilation into hadrons at total energies between 9.4 and 10.4 GeV; the mass spacing and ratios of lepton-pair widths support interpreting the Υ states as the lowest triplet-S levels of the b b̄ system (Phys. Rev. Lett. 44, 1108, 1980); the first CLEO paper had 73 authors from 8 institutions.
result:cleo-upsilon-three-states-observa.why_it_matters: Berkelman describes CESR's energy as ideal for the physics of the b quark, a gift that guaranteed the productivity of CESR; the three Υ states were the subject of the first CLEO paper, submitted in February 1980.

claim.quote: We present a measurement of the pion form factor based on e+e- annihilation data from the CMD-2 detector in the energy range 0.6<sqrt(s)<1.0 GeV with a systematic uncertainty of 0.8%.

notes: The muon g-2 topic tag reflects the use of the pion form factor in that calculation; the abstract itself does not mention g-2.
result:cmd-2-pion-form-factor-measuremen.summary_technical: CMD-2 at VEPP-2M: pion form factor from e⁺e⁻ → π⁺π⁻ for 0.6 < √s < 1.0 GeV with a systematic uncertainty of 0.8%; the data sample is five times larger than in the previous CMD-2 measurement (Phys. Lett. B 648 (2007) 28).
result:cmd-2-pion-form-factor-measuremen.why_it_matters: The abstract reports the result as a measurement of the pion form factor with a systematic uncertainty of 0.8%.

claim.quote: The cross section of the process $e^+e^-\to\pi^+\pi^-$ has been measured in the center of mass energy range from 0.32 to 1.2 GeV with the CMD-3 detector at the electron-positron collider VEPP-2000.

notes: Chosen as the CMD-3 headline result; it is the most precise measurement of this channel by CMD-3 and the one discussed in connection with the muon g-2. The tension between this CMD-3 value and earlier e+e- measurements is not asserted here because the fetched abstracts do not state it.
result:cmd-3-pipi-cross-section-measurem.summary_technical: CMD-3 at VEPP-2000: e⁺e⁻ → π⁺π⁻ for 0.32 < √s < 1.2 GeV from about 62 pb⁻¹ collected below 1 GeV in three seasons; 0.7% systematic uncertainty in the ρ region; first high-resolution measurement across the φ resonance; the forward-backward charge asymmetry deviates strongly from conventional scalar QED and agrees with generalised vector-meson dominance and dispersion-based predictions (Phys. Rev. D 109, 112002).
result:cmd-3-pipi-cross-section-measurem.why_it_matters: The companion paper's title and abstract state that the results bear on the hadronic contribution to the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon.

claim.quote: An excess of events is observed above the expected background, with a local significance of 5.0 standard deviations, at a mass near 125 GeV, signalling the production of a new particle.

notes: The collaboration wording is "observation of a new boson", not "discovery of the Higgs boson".
result:cms-higgs-boson-observation-2012.summary_technical: Search for the standard model Higgs boson in five decay modes (γγ, ZZ, WW, ττ, bb̄) with up to 5.1 fb⁻¹ at 7 TeV and 5.3 fb⁻¹ at 8 TeV: an excess with local significance 5.0 standard deviations at a mass near 125 GeV (5.8 expected for a standard model Higgs boson of that mass); a fit to the γγ and ZZ signals gives 125.3 ± 0.4 (stat) ± 0.5 (syst) GeV; the diphoton decay indicates a boson with spin different from one.
result:cms-higgs-boson-observation-2012.why_it_matters: The paper's introduction says the question of how the W and Z gauge bosons acquire mass whilst the photon remains massless is still open; introducing a complex scalar doublet field leads to the generation of the W and Z masses and to the prediction of the standard model Higgs boson, and the scalar field also gives mass to the fundamental fermions through the Yukawa interaction. CMS reports an excess that signals the production of a new particle near 125 GeV.

claim.quote: Here the CMS Collaboration reports the most up-to-date combination of results on the properties of the Higgs boson, including the most stringent limit on the cross section for the production of a pair of Higgs bosons, on the basis of data from proton-proton collisions at a centre-of-mass energy of 13 TeV.

result:cms-higgs-boson-portrait-2022.summary_technical: Combination of CMS 13 TeV results on the Higgs boson: observed in numerous fermionic and bosonic decay channels, spin-parity quantum numbers established, mass determined and production cross sections measured in various modes, including what the collaboration calls 'the most stringent limit on the cross section for the production of a pair of Higgs bosons'; within the uncertainties all observations are compatible with the standard model.
result:cms-higgs-boson-portrait-2022.why_it_matters: The abstract says much evidence points to the standard model being a low-energy approximation of a more comprehensive theory, that several of the standard model issues originate in the Higgs boson sector, and that the order-of-magnitude larger number of Higgs bosons expected to be examined over the next fifteen years will help deepen understanding of this sector.

claim.quote: The combination of this result with searches by the CMS experiment for H $\to\mathrm{b\overline{b}}$ in other production processes yields an observed (expected) significance of 5.6 (5.5) standard deviations and a signal strength of 1.04 $\pm$ 0.20.

result:cms-higgs-to-bb-observation-2018.summary_technical: VH production (W or Z boson plus H → bb̄) in 41.3 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV data recorded in 2017: combined with previous VH measurements at 7, 8 and 13 TeV, an excess at m_H = 125.09 GeV with a significance of 4.8 standard deviations (4.9 expected for the SM Higgs boson), signal strength 1.01 ± 0.22. Combined with CMS searches for H → bb̄ in other production processes: observed (expected) significance 5.6 (5.5) standard deviations, signal strength 1.04 ± 0.20.
result:cms-higgs-to-bb-observation-2018.why_it_matters: The paper says a precise measurement of the H → bb rate directly probes the Yukawa coupling of the Higgs boson to a down-type quark and provides a necessary test of the hypothesis that the Higgs field is the source of mass generation in the charged fermion sector of the standard model.

claim.quote: The combination with the corresponding measurement performed with data collected by the CMS experiment at center-of-mass energies of 7 and 8 TeV leads to an observed significance of 5.9 standard deviations, equal to the expected significance.

result:cms-higgs-to-tau-tau-observation-.summary_technical: 35.9 fb⁻¹ at 13 TeV: H → ττ signal established with a significance of 4.9 standard deviations (4.7 expected), best-fit signal strength 1.09 +0.27/−0.26 times the standard model expectation; combined with 7 and 8 TeV data, observed significance 5.9 standard deviations, equal to the expected significance.
result:cms-higgs-to-tau-tau-observation-.why_it_matters: The paper says that to establish the mass generation mechanism for fermions it is necessary to probe the direct coupling of the Higgs boson to such particles, and that H → ττ is the most promising decay channel because of the large expected event rate compared with the muon-pair channel and the smaller background than in the bb̄ channel.

claim.quote: These provide the most stringent lower limits to date on the masses for various spin-1 particles, spin-2 gravitons in the Randall--Sundrum model, as well as spin-1 mediators between the SM and dark matter particles.

notes: Numerical mass limits are quoted in the body of the paper, not in the abstract that was fetched, so no key_value is recorded.
result:cms-high-mass-dilepton-search-202.summary_technical: Dielectron and dimuon mass spectra from up to 140 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV data (2016–2018): no significant deviation from the standard model background expectations; upper limits on narrow resonances relative to the Z boson (most stringent lower limits to date on masses of various spin-1 particles, Randall–Sundrum spin-2 gravitons and spin-1 dark-matter mediators), lower limits on the ultraviolet cutoff for four-fermion contact interactions and the ADD model, and a lepton-flavour-universality test at the TeV scale, which the abstract says is done for the first time.
result:cms-high-mass-dilepton-search-202.why_it_matters: The abstract reports no significant deviation from the standard model background expectations; lower limits on the masses of various spin-1 particles, Randall–Sundrum gravitons and spin-1 mediators between the standard model and dark matter; lower limits on the ultraviolet cutoff for contact interactions and the ADD large-extra-dimension model; and a TeV-scale test of lepton flavour universality.

claim.quote: The combined analysis produces the first observation of the $B^0_s\to\mu^+\mu^-$ decay, with a statistical significance exceeding six standard deviations, and the best measurement of its branching fraction so far.

notes: A joint CMS and LHCb result; only the CMS experiment and collaboration are linked on this record.
result:cms-lhcb-bs-to-mumu-observation-2.summary_technical: Joint CMS+LHCb analysis of 7 TeV (2011) and 8 TeV (2012) data: first observation of B_s → μ⁺μ⁻ with a statistical significance exceeding six standard deviations, and evidence for B⁰ → μ⁺μ⁻ with a significance of three standard deviations; the branching fractions are statistically compatible with SM predictions.
result:cms-lhcb-bs-to-mumu-observation-2.why_it_matters: The paper says a difference between the observed branching fractions and the Standard Model predictions would provide a direction in which the Standard Model should be extended; the abstract says the measurements are statistically compatible with SM predictions and impose stringent constraints on several theories beyond the SM.

claim.quote: This is the first observation of such a long-range, near-side feature in two-particle correlation functions in pp or p p-bar collisions.

result:cms-long-range-near-side-correlat.summary_technical: Two-particle Δη-Δφ correlations in 7 TeV pp collisions show a pronounced near-side ridge at 2.0 < |Δη| < 4.8 for 1-3 GeV/c tracks in high-multiplicity events (980 nb⁻¹).
result:cms-long-range-near-side-correlat.why_it_matters: The paper notes that measurements at RHIC revealed that the long-range structure of two-particle angular correlations is significantly modified by the hot and dense matter formed in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, and that because the particle densities in the highest-multiplicity pp collisions at the LHC begin to approach those in collisions of relatively small nuclei such as copper, it is natural to search for new features in high-multiplicity pp events.

claim.quote: The top quark mass is measured to be 171.77 $\pm$ 0.37 GeV.

result:cms-top-quark-mass-measurement-20.summary_technical: 36.3 fb⁻¹ at 13 TeV, lepton+jets tt̄ candidates, kinematic fit plus a profile likelihood over up to four observables: m_t = 171.77 ± 0.37 GeV.
result:cms-top-quark-mass-measurement-20.why_it_matters: The paper says that, because of its large Yukawa coupling, the top quark dominates the higher-order corrections to the Higgs boson mass and a precise top-quark mass sets strong constraints on the stability of the electroweak vacuum; precise measurements can also test the internal consistency of the Standard Model.

claim.quote: An excess of events is observed, with a significance of 5.2 standard deviations, over the expectation from the background-only hypothesis.

result:cms-tth-observation-2018.summary_technical: Combination of ttH searches in WW, ZZ, γγ, ττ and bb final states at 7, 8 and 13 TeV (up to 5.1, 19.7 and 35.9 fb⁻¹): 5.2σ observed, 4.2σ expected, signal strength 1.26 +0.31 -0.26.
result:cms-tth-observation-2018.why_it_matters: In the Standard Model the masses of elementary fermions are accounted for by Yukawa interactions, with a coupling proportional to the fermion mass. The paper says the top-quark Yukawa coupling cannot be tested from a decay rate, so constraints come from pp → ttH production; the combined best-fit signal strength normalised to the standard model prediction is 1.26 +0.31/−0.26.

claim.quote: we reach a precise measurement of the W mass, of 80 360.2 ± 9.9 MeV, in agreement with the standard model prediction.

notes: The CMS news page is titled "CMS delivers the best-precision measurement of the W boson mass at the LHC"; the plain summary attributes that wording to the collaboration.
result:cms-w-boson-mass-measurement-2024.summary_technical: W → μ ν events from 2016 13 TeV data, high-granularity maximum likelihood fit to muon kinematics with in situ constraints on theory inputs: m_W = 80 360.2 ± 9.9 MeV.
result:cms-w-boson-mass-measurement-2024.why_it_matters: The abstract says the W and Z boson masses are uniquely related in the Standard Model and that a precise determination of their masses is important because quantum loops of heavy, undiscovered particles could modify this relationship.

claim.quote: Presently available data support the presence of a modulated component of unknown origin, with parameters prima facie compatible with a galactic halo composed of light-mass WIMPs. Unoptimized estimators yield a statistical significance for a modulation of ~2.8 sigma, limited by the short exposure.

notes: Recorded as an anomaly: 'a modulated component of unknown origin' at ~2.8 sigma; the authors do not claim evidence or discovery.
result:cogent-annual-modulation-2011.summary_technical: 15 months (442 live days of 458, 4 Dec 2009 - 6 Mar 2011) of p-type point-contact germanium data; modulation with unconstrained phase, period and amplitude; ~2.8 sigma with unoptimized estimators.
result:cogent-annual-modulation-2011.why_it_matters: The first indication of annual modulation in a germanium detector, reported alongside the DAMA/LIBRA modulation; later germanium and xenon experiments did not confirm it.

claim.quote: Extensive simulations of all presently known backgrounds do not provide a viable background explanation for the excess of low-energy events in the CoGeNT data, or the previously observed temporal variation in the event rate.

result:cogent-detector-and-backgrounds-2.summary_technical: Detector description (shielding, DAQ, stability), surface (slow-rise-time) event contamination as a function of energy, and a full background model for the 442-live-day data set; concludes that the PPC technology is well suited to a DAMA/LIBRA-region annual-modulation search.
result:cogent-detector-and-backgrounds-2.why_it_matters: The collaboration's own detailed answer to whether backgrounds could mimic the excess.

claim.quote: We discuss several possible causes for an irreducible excess of bulk-like events below 3 keVee, including a dark matter candidate common to the DAMA/LIBRA annual modulation effect, the hint of a signal in CDMS, and phenomenological predictions.

notes: Recorded as an anomaly: the abstract speaks of 'an irreducible excess' and lists possible causes; it does not claim a detection.
result:cogent-low-mass-excess-2010.summary_technical: Ultra-low-noise p-type point-contact germanium detector at 2,100 m.w.e. (Soudan); a surface-event rejection technique lets cosmogenic peaks be seen for the first time; irreducible excess of bulk-like events below 3 keVee; improved constraints on a cosmological origin of the DAMA/LIBRA effect.
result:cogent-low-mass-excess-2010.why_it_matters: The paper that put CoGeNT's low-mass excess on the map; it motivated many light-WIMP interpretations and the follow-up modulation analyses.

claim.quote: We find that the significance of the extracted dark matter signal remains well below evidentiary at 1.7 $\sigma$.

result:cogent-maximum-likelihood-2014.summary_technical: Maximum-likelihood extraction in energy, time and pulse rise-time (1136 live days to 23 April 2013) for a standard-halo case and for free oscillation parameters; best-fit signal close to earlier results; significance 1.7 sigma.
result:cogent-maximum-likelihood-2014.why_it_matters: The collaboration's own statement that its signal is not statistically significant evidence.

claim.quote: A previously reported modulation persists, concentrated in a region of the energy spectrum populated by an exponential excess of unknown origin. Its phase and period agree with phenomenological expectations, but its amplitude is a factor $\sim$4-7 larger than predicted for a standard WIMP galactic halo.

notes: Recorded as an anomaly: 'excess of unknown origin'; the abstract does not claim a detection.
result:cogent-three-years-modulation-201.summary_technical: 3.4-year data set (to 23 April 2013, 1,237 days of which 1,129 live) released in time-stamp, energy and rise-time format; modulation in the exponential low-energy excess of unknown origin; non-Maxwellian halo considered.
result:cogent-three-years-modulation-201.why_it_matters: Public release of the full data set, used by many outside analyses; the amplitude mismatch is the main reason the modulation is not read as standard WIMP dark matter.

claim.quote: First Measurement of Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering on Argon

result:coherent-argon-measurement-2021.summary_technical: First CEvNS measurement on argon using the 24 kg active-mass CENNS-10 liquid-argon detector at the SNS; two independent analyses each prefer CEvNS over the background-only hypothesis at greater than 3σ, with a flux-averaged cross section of (2.2 ± 0.7)×10⁻³⁹ cm² consistent with the Standard Model prediction. The collaboration states that the neutron-number dependence of this result, together with its earlier CsI measurement, confirms the existence of the CEvNS process and improves constraints on non-standard neutrino interactions.
result:coherent-argon-measurement-2021.why_it_matters: Argon is a second, lighter target nucleus after CsI, so the pair of results traces how the CEvNS cross section depends on neutron number; the paper's introduction says this establishes the N² behavior predicted by the Standard Model. The introduction also notes that CEvNS from solar and atmospheric neutrinos forms the "neutrino floor" background in future dark-matter searches, which cross section measurements help quantify.

claim.quote: Measurement of the Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering Cross Section on CsI by COHERENT

result:coherent-csi-cross-section-2022.summary_technical: All CsI[Na] data collected before detector decommissioning (13.99 GWhr of integrated beam power passing the livetime criteria), more than doubling the dataset of the first observation, with an updated quenching model reducing systematic uncertainties: cross section (165 +30/−25)×10⁻⁴⁰ cm², consistent with the Standard Model and called the most precise measurement of CEvNS yet; weak mixing angle sin²θW = 0.220 +0.028/−0.026 at Q² ≈ (50 MeV)²; the collaboration reports leading constraints on neutrino non-standard interactions and a lepton-flavor-universality test using the beam's timing structure.
result:coherent-csi-cross-section-2022.why_it_matters: A CEvNS cross-section measurement on CsI with more than twice the data of the first observation. The abstract reports leading constraints on neutrino non-standard interactions, a test of lepton flavor universality using the timing structure of the neutrino beam, and the weak mixing angle at Q ≈ 50 MeV.

claim.quote: Evidence of Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering with COHERENT's Germanium Array

notes: Classified as evidence because the word 'Evidence' appears in the cited title.
result:coherent-germanium-evidence-2024.summary_technical: First detection of CEvNS on natural germanium using the Ge-Mini array (eight 2.2 kg ICPC high-purity germanium detectors, 1.5 keVee threshold) operated at the SNS June-August 2023: an on-beam excess of 20.6(+7.1/−6.3) counts over 10.22 GWh*kg exposure, rejecting the no-CEvNS hypothesis at 3.9σ, in agreement with the Standard Model prediction within 2σ.
result:coherent-germanium-evidence-2024.why_it_matters: The paper's introduction says CEvNS had been measured on only two nuclear targets to date; this is a 3.9σ rejection of the no-CEvNS hypothesis on natural germanium, a signal rate within 2σ of the Standard Model prediction, and the collaboration words it as evidence rather than an observation.

claim.quote: Observation of Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering

result:coherent-observation-2017.summary_technical: Observation of coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CEvNS) at a 6.7σ confidence level, using a 14.6 kg CsI[Na] scintillator exposed to the neutrino emissions from the SNS; the characteristic energy and time signatures predicted by the Standard Model are observed in high signal-to-background conditions, and improved constraints on non-standard neutrino interactions with quarks are derived.
result:coherent-observation-2017.why_it_matters: The abstract says the predicted cross section is the largest by far of all low-energy neutrino couplings, yet the process had eluded detection for four decades; it adds that the interaction offers new opportunities to study neutrino properties and leads to a miniaturization of detector size, with potential technological applications. The paper notes that WIMP direct-detection searches rely on the same coherent enhancement.

claim.quote: A narrow $J^{PC} = 1^{++}$ signal is observed in the $f_0(980)\,\pi$ channel.

result:compass-a1-1420-observation-2015.summary_technical: Partial-wave analysis (88 waves) of diffractive dissociation of 190 GeV/c pions into pi-pi-pi+ on a hydrogen target: a narrow J^PC = 1++ signal in the f0(980) pi channel, interpreted as a new a1 meson with mass 1414 +15 -13 MeV/c^2 and width 153 +8 -23 MeV/c^2, decaying only into f0(980) pi among the final states investigated.
result:compass-a1-1420-observation-2015.why_it_matters: A new light meson candidate that does not fit the ordinary quark-antiquark spectrum cleanly is a test case for exotic hadrons and for the role of rescattering effects.

claim.quote: From this value, we obtain in a leading-order QCD analysis Delta G/G=0.024 +- 0.089(stat.) +- 0.057(syst.) at x_g = 0.095 and mu^2 =~ 3 (GeV}/c)^2.

result:compass-gluon-polarisation-quasi-.summary_technical: Determination of the gluon polarisation Delta G/G in the nucleon from the helicity asymmetry of quasi-real photoproduction events (Q^2 < 1 (GeV/c)^2) with a pair of large transverse-momentum hadrons, using a 160 GeV polarised muon beam on a polarised 6LiD target: A_||/D = 0.002 ± 0.019 (stat) ± 0.003 (syst), giving Delta G/G = 0.024 ± 0.089 (stat) ± 0.057 (syst) at x_g = 0.095 and mu^2 ~ 3 (GeV/c)^2 in a leading-order QCD analysis.
result:compass-gluon-polarisation-quasi-.why_it_matters: The 'proton spin puzzle' asks how quark spin, gluon spin and orbital motion add up to the proton's spin; a small gluon polarisation at the probed momentum fraction constrains that budget.

claim.quote: The difference between the reactor-on and reactor-off spectra shows no excess at low energies and yields upper limits at 95% confidence level for the neutrino interaction rates.

result:connie-2019-data-limits-2022.summary_technical: 2019 data, 8 CCDs, 36.2 g fiducial mass, 2.2 kg-days: reactor-on minus reactor-off spectra show no low-energy excess; in 50-180 eV the expected limit is 34 (39) and the observed limit 66 (75) times the SM prediction for Sarkis (Chavarria) quenching.
result:connie-2019-data-limits-2022.why_it_matters: The most sensitive reactor CEvNS limits in the sub-keV range of the time, a step towards observing CEvNS at reactors.

claim.quote: The results show no excess in the reactor-on data, reaching the world record sensitivity down to recoil energies of about 1 keV (0.1 keV electron-equivalent).

result:connie-first-results-2019.summary_technical: 8 CCDs, 47.6 g active mass at 30 m from the 3.8 GW_th Angra 2 core: reactor-on 2.1 kg-day vs reactor-off 1.6 kg-day, no excess; 95 % CL limit on new physics at 40 times the Standard Model CEvNS rate near 1 keV.
result:connie-first-results-2019.why_it_matters: Demonstrated that CCDs reach the sub-keV thresholds needed for reactor CEvNS.

claim.quote: Performing a simple combination of the newly released 6-years datasets from both experiments find values consistent with no modulation at $0.0005 {\pm} 0.0019$ cpd/kg/keV in the 1-6 keV and $0.0027 {\pm} 0.0021$ cpd/kg/keV in the 2-6 keV energy regions with $4.68{\sigma}$ and $3.53{\sigma}$ respective exclusions of the DAMA/LIBRA signal.

notes: Joint result with ANAIS-112 (Laboratorio Subterraneo de Canfranc), which is not recorded on this branch; attributed here to COSINE-100 only. The integrator should add the ANAIS-112 experiment link.
result:cosine-100-anais-112-combined-202.summary_technical: Joint annual-modulation analysis with ANAIS-112 (Canfranc): first three years of each (Markov-chain Monte Carlo; amplitudes -0.0002 +/- 0.0026 and 0.0021 +/- 0.0028 cpd/kg/keV, not compatible with DAMA/LIBRA at 3.7 and 2.6 sigma), and a simple combination of the six-year data sets (Phys. Rev. Lett. 135, 121002 (2025)).
result:cosine-100-anais-112-combined-202.why_it_matters: A joint analysis of two NaI(Tl) experiments that use DAMA/LIBRA's target material.

claim.quote: Using a $\chi$-squared minimization method we observe best fit values for modulation amplitude and phase of 0.0092$\pm$0.0067 cpd/kg/keV and 127.2$\pm$45 d, respectively.

result:cosine-100-annual-modulation-1-7-.summary_technical: 1.7 years, exposure 97.7 kg yr, 106 kg NaI(Tl), average background 2.7 cpd/kg/keV in the 2-6 keV region of interest (the abstract does not state the energy range of the fit); chi-squared minimisation (Phys. Rev. Lett. 123, 031302 (2019)).
result:cosine-100-annual-modulation-1-7-.why_it_matters: The first annual-modulation fit from the same-target test of DAMA/LIBRA; the abstract frames it as constraints, not a signal.

claim.quote: In the 1-6 keV and 2-6 keV energy intervals, we observe best-fit values for the modulation amplitude of 0.0067$\pm$0.0042 and 0.0051$\pm$0.0047 counts/(day$\cdot$kg$\cdot$keV), respectively, with a phase fixed at 152.5 days.

result:cosine-100-annual-modulation-3-ye.summary_technical: Live time 2.82 yr, active mass 61.3 kg, exposure 173 kg yr; improved event selection (threshold 1 keV) and time-dependent background model; the abstract says the experiment 'aims to test DAMA/LIBRA's claim of dark matter discovery' (Phys. Rev. D 106, 052005 (2022)).
result:cosine-100-annual-modulation-3-ye.why_it_matters: The same energy windows and threshold as DAMA/LIBRA's published analysis.

claim.quote: No signal consistent with the dark matter interaction is identified, and rules out model-dependent dark matter interpretations of the DAMA signals in the specific context of standard halo model with the same NaI(Tl) target for various interaction hypotheses.

result:cosine-100-dama-constraints-2021.summary_technical: 1.7 years of COSINE-100 data with improved event selection and background model; model-dependent exclusion of interpretations of the DAMA signals (standard halo model, various interaction hypotheses) (Sci. Adv. 7, eabk2699 (2021)). The abstract says the experiment is 'aimed at testing DAMA's claim of dark matter observation'.
result:cosine-100-dama-constraints-2021.why_it_matters: A direct model-dependent test of DAMA's signal with the same target.

claim.quote: Initial data based on the first 59.5 days indicate that there is no excess of events over the expected background, confirming that DAMA's annual modulation signal is in severe tension with results from other experiments under the assumption of dark matter having spin independent interactions and the Standard Halo Model.

notes: The journal reference gives Nature 564 (2018); the arXiv posting (v1) is dated 2019-06-05, after the journal publication.
result:cosine-100-first-results-2018.summary_technical: First physics result (59.5 days; Nature 564, 83 (2018)). A model-dependent comparison: the paper states COSINE-100 'is designed to carry out a model-independent test of DAMA's claim', and that annual-modulation data are still being taken. No numerical limit is quoted in the abstract.
result:cosine-100-first-results-2018.why_it_matters: The first result of the experiment built to test DAMA's claim with the same target; the abstract's wording is about tension, not a modulation test.

claim.quote: Analyzing data collected over 6.4 years by the effective mass of 61.3 kg, with improved energy calibration and time-dependent background modeling, we found no evidence of an annual modulation signal, challenging the DAMA/LIBRA result with a confidence level greater than 3$\sigma$.

result:cosine-100-full-dataset-annual-mo.summary_technical: Full COSINE-100 data set (21 Oct 2016 - 14 Mar 2023; 358.4 kg yr of high-quality data; effective mass 61.3 kg); model-independent annual-modulation test with improved energy calibration and background modelling (Sci. Adv. 11, eadv6503 (2025)).
result:cosine-100-full-dataset-annual-mo.why_it_matters: The collaboration's final modulation test of DAMA/LIBRA's claim; its authors describe the DAMA/LIBRA modulation as unlikely to be caused by dark matter.

claim.quote: Our findings strongly disfavor the DAMA signal as originating from WIMP interactions, fully excluding DAMA/LIBRA 3$\sigma$ allowed regions and providing enhanced WIMP mass limits by an order of magnitude in the spin-independent model compared to previous results.

result:cosine-100-wimp-limits-0-7-kev-20.summary_technical: Three years of COSINE-100 data, 0.7 keV threshold; no excess of WIMP-like events; spin-independent WIMP mass limits improved by an order of magnitude; spin-dependent limits for 0.1-5.0 GeV/c^2 and sub-GeV sensitivity via the Migdal effect (arXiv preprint, no journal reference in the abstract page).
result:cosine-100-wimp-limits-0-7-kev-20.why_it_matters: States in the abstract that DAMA/LIBRA's three-sigma allowed regions are fully excluded under the WIMP interpretation.

claim.quote: All eight crystals showed higher light yields than in COSINE-100, with values ranging from 15.8 to 27.7~p.e./keV; six crystals exceeded 20~p.e./keV.

result:cosine-100u-crystal-encapsulation.summary_technical: Initial performance with 2462 h (102.6 d) of room-temperature COSINE-100U data at Yemilab, compared with 698 h (29.1 d) of late COSINE-100 data; direct PMT coupling via 2-mm silicone pads, beveled crystal edges, lower bulk-alpha and much lower 1-2 MeV surface-alpha rates (arXiv preprint).
result:cosine-100u-crystal-encapsulation.why_it_matters: Shows the upgrade delivered the higher light yield and lower backgrounds it was built for.

claim.quote: The detector, consisting of eight NaI(Tl) crystals with a total mass of 99.1 kg, has been relocated to Yemilab, a new underground facility in Korea, and features direct PMT-coupling technology to enhance sensitivity.

result:cosine-100u-upgrade-2025.summary_technical: Design and upgrade paper: relocation to Yemilab, improved light collection and reduced background; the abstract recalls that COSINE-100 found no significant annual-modulation signal, with a discrepancy of more than 3 sigma with DAMA/LIBRA (Commun. Phys. 8, 135 (2025)).
result:cosine-100u-upgrade-2025.why_it_matters: Documents the upgraded detector that continues the DAMA/LIBRA test at a deeper site.

claim.quote: Furthermore, we present a limit on the spin-independent dark-matter nucleon elastic scattering cross-section achieving a sensitivity of $\mathcal{O}$(pb) with an exposure of only 11.6 g d.

notes: Prototype result, not a COSINUS-1pi measurement.
result:cosinus-deep-underground-prototyp.summary_technical: 3.67 g NaI absorber with remoTES read-out and an improved silicon light detector at LNGS: nuclear-recoil baseline resolution sigma = 441 eV (five-fold improvement) and a spin-independent limit with sensitivity O(pb) at 11.6 g d (Phys. Rev. D 110, 043010).
result:cosinus-deep-underground-prototyp.why_it_matters: The paper calls the cryogenic NaI read-out a promising route to a model-independent test of the DAMA/LIBRA signal.

claim.quote: COSINUS built and commissioned a dedicated low-background cryogenic facility at the LNGS underground laboratories.

notes: Facility and schedule paper (arXiv preprint); the planned Run 1 start has not been confirmed by any source read.
result:cosinus-facility-dama-challenge-2.summary_technical: Facility and detector status: dry dilution cryostat in a water-tank shield and muon veto in Hall B of LNGS, remoTES NaI modules; COSINUS-1pi Run 1 (eight modules, 100 kg d) planned for late 2025, Run 2 up to 1000 kg d; model-independent cross-check of DAMA/LIBRA with a few hundred kg d.
result:cosinus-facility-dama-challenge-2.why_it_matters: It is the most recent description by the collaboration of the facility and the staged physics programme.

claim.quote: a NaI crystal operated as a scintillating calorimeter at milli-Kelvin temperatures simultaneously providing a phonon (heat) plus scintillation light signal and particle discrimination on an event-by-event basis.

notes: R&D prototype result.
result:cosinus-first-cryogenic-nai-detec.summary_technical: First COSINUS NaI prototype (scintillating calorimeter at mK temperatures, phonon plus light): evaluation of energy resolution, threshold and other performance parameters (JINST 12, P11007).
result:cosinus-first-cryogenic-nai-detec.why_it_matters: It is the first demonstration of the technique that COSINUS builds on.

claim.quote: With a 3.7 g NaI crystal, e$^-$/$\gamma$ events could be clearly distinguished from nuclear recoils down to the nuclear recoil energy threshold of 15 keV.

notes: Above-ground prototype measurement.
result:cosinus-remotes-particle-discrimi.summary_technical: remoTES NaI prototype operated above ground for 9.06 g d: event-by-event e/gamma versus nuclear-recoil discrimination in the dual phonon plus light read-out down to a nuclear-recoil threshold of 15 keV (Phys. Rev. D 109, 082003).
result:cosinus-remotes-particle-discrimi.why_it_matters: Particle discrimination in NaI is what lets COSINUS separate nuclear recoils from the electron background that DAMA/LIBRA cannot reject.

claim.quote: The analysis of 73 kg-days of data taken by COSME in a search for solar axions via their photon Primakoff conversion and Bragg scattering in the Ge crystal yields a 95% C.L. limit for the axion-photon coupling g < 2.8 10^-9 GeV^-1.

notes: Recorded from the proceedings abstract (73 kg d); the full-paper value for 72.7 kg d is in arXiv:hep-ex/0101037.
result:cosme-solar-axion-coupling-limit-.summary_technical: 73 kg d of COSME data analysed for Primakoff conversion with Bragg diffraction in the crystal: 95% C.L. limit g < 2.8e-9 GeV^-1 on the axion-photon coupling (conference proceedings, Dark Matter 2000 workshop).
result:cosme-solar-axion-coupling-limit-.why_it_matters: An early crystal-detector axion limit, later improved by the full 72.7 kg d analysis in Astroparticle Physics.

claim.quote: New WIMP exclusion plots improving the current bounds for low masses are reported.

result:cosme-wimp-exclusion-2001.summary_technical: 72.7 kg d (1998-1999) in an improved shield at 2450 m.w.e.: background about an order of magnitude below the earlier run; WIMP exclusion plots improving the bounds at low masses.
result:cosme-wimp-exclusion-2001.why_it_matters: Pushed germanium limits down to light WIMPs a few years before dedicated low-threshold detectors.

claim.quote: Improved limits on the spin-dependent WIMP-proton scattering cross section are extracted from this first period.

result:coupp-2kg-spin-dependent-limits-2.summary_technical: 1.5 kg CF3I room-temperature bubble chamber at the 350-ft level of the NuMI tunnel; exposure in excess of 250 kg-days with a live-time fraction reaching 80% (the limits use three data sets adding up to 52 kg-days); rejection factor for photon-induced electrons of ~1e-10; improved limits on the spin-dependent WIMP-proton cross section (Science 319, 933, 2008).
result:coupp-2kg-spin-dependent-limits-2.why_it_matters: The abstract says bubble chambers had fallen into disuse and that this work illustrates their use in a new realm, the search for dark matter particles.

claim.quote: This observation provides the strongest direct detection constraint to date on WIMP-proton spin-dependent scattering for WIMP masses $>20$ GeV/c$^{2}$.

result:coupp-4kg-minos-limits-2010.summary_technical: 3.5 kg CF3I, 19 August-18 December 2009, MINOS near-detector tunnel (300 ft overburden); acoustic alpha/nuclear-recoil discrimination; three dark matter candidate events in an effective exposure of 28.1 kg-day, consistent with a neutron background; limit for WIMP masses above 20 GeV/c^2 (Phys. Rev. Lett. 106, 021303).
result:coupp-4kg-minos-limits-2010.why_it_matters: The abstract states it as the strongest direct-detection constraint to date on WIMP-proton spin-dependent scattering for masses above 20 GeV/c^2.

claim.quote: This observation provides world best direct detection constraints on WIMP-proton spin-dependent scattering for WIMP masses $>$20 GeV/c$^{2}$ and demonstrates significant sensitivity for spin-independent interactions.

result:coupp-4kg-snolab-limits-2012.summary_technical: 4.0 kg CF3I in the SNOLAB J-Drift, September 2010-August 2011: 553 kg-days over three nucleation thresholds (437.4 kg-days effective for single bubbles); 20 single nuclear-recoil candidates and 3 multiple-bubble events; an internal neutron background estimated to account for five single-recoil events; alpha rejection >99.3% (Phys. Rev. D 86, 052001).
result:coupp-4kg-snolab-limits-2012.why_it_matters: The abstract says the observation gives world-best direct-detection constraints on WIMP-proton spin-dependent scattering for masses above 20 GeV/c^2.

claim.locator: title field of the Crossref record for DOI 10.1126/science.124.3212.103 (Science 124, 103-104)
claim.quote: Detection of the Free Neutrino: a Confirmation

notes: Classified first_detection because the paper title says "Detection" and the APS plaque says "first experiment that conclusively detected the neutrino"; the paper itself calls its own result a confirmation of the Hanford 1953 tentative identification.
date is the June 1956 APS meeting presentation (month precision); the day-precision publication date is in `published`.
result:cowan-reines-neutrino-detection-1.summary_technical: Delayed-coincidence signal with the reactor-power dependence, proton-density, shielding and cadmium tests expected of reactor antineutrinos: 0.56 ± 0.06 counts per hour (2.88 ± 0.22 with changed requirements) in 1371 h of running, a cross section within 5% of 6.3×10⁻⁴⁴ cm² against a prediction uncertain by ±25%.
result:cowan-reines-neutrino-detection-1.why_it_matters: The American Physical Society's 2014 Savannah River plaque calls it "the first experiment that conclusively detected the neutrino", and the 1995 Nobel Prize in Physics gave Frederick Reines one half "for the detection of the neutrino".

claim.quote: We report a precise measurement of the parity-violating asymmetry $A_{\rm PV}$ in the elastic scattering of longitudinally polarized electrons from $^{48}{\rm Ca}$.

result:crex-48ca-neutral-weak-form-facto.summary_technical: A_PV = 2668 ± 106 (stat) ± 40 (syst) ppb in elastic scattering from 48Ca, giving F_W(q = 0.8733 fm^-1) = 0.1304 ± 0.0052 (stat) ± 0.0020 (syst), F_ch - F_W = 0.0277 ± 0.0055 and R_n - R_p = 0.121 ± 0.026 (exp) ± 0.024 (model) fm.
result:crex-48ca-neutral-weak-form-facto.why_it_matters: Together with PREX the result challenges energy-density-functional calculations and constrains the density dependence of the symmetry energy of nuclear matter.

claim.quote: We report the final result of the CUORICINO experiment. Operated between 2003 and 2008, with a total exposure of 19.75 kg·y of 130 Te, CUORICINO was able to set a lower bound on the 130 Te 0νββ half-life of 2.8 × 10^24 years at 90% C.L.

result:cuoricino-130te-final-limit-2010.summary_technical: Final CUORICINO analysis including systematic uncertainties: T1/2(0vbb, 130Te) > 2.8e24 yr at 90 % C.L. with 19.75 kg y of 130Te; <m_ee> bound 300-710 meV depending on the nuclear matrix element.
result:cuoricino-130te-final-limit-2010.why_it_matters: The best 130Te result before CUORE; its detector techniques and the lessons about pulse-shape spread led to CUORE-0 and CUORE.

claim.quote: states have been observed at the Cornell Electron Storage Ring as narrow peaks in

notes: The title on the APS page is in TeX markup; it is given here in Unicode (Υ, Υ′, Υ″).
result:cusb-upsilon-observation-1980.summary_technical: CUSB: the Υ, Υ′ and Υ″ observed as narrow peaks in σ(e⁺e⁻ → hadrons) versus beam energy, using the Columbia University-Stony Brook segmented NaI detector with an integrated luminosity of 1000 nb⁻¹ (Phys. Rev. Lett. 44, 1111, 1980).
result:cusb-upsilon-observation-1980.why_it_matters: Berkelman notes that the CUSB experiment provided confirmation of the CLEO measurements of the Υ states at CESR.

claim.quote: Validation using data from the CYGNO LIME prototype shows accurate reconstruction of localized and extended tracks.

result:cygno-bayesian-3d-reconstruction-.summary_technical: Bayesian-network algorithm (Bayesian Analysis Toolkit, MCMC) reconstructing 3D tracks from PMT signals; validated on LIME data; combined with camera data it improves track precision.
result:cygno-bayesian-3d-reconstruction-.why_it_matters: The abstract calls this a significant step forward in directional dark matter detection.

claim.quote: We report the first observation of Negative Ion Drift (NID) at surface pressure of $900 \pm 7$ mbar at Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso in a He:CF$_4$:SF$_6$ mixture using an optically read out Time Projection Chamber (TPC) within the CYGNO/INITIUM project.

result:cygno-first-optical-negative-ion-.summary_technical: He:CF4:SF6 mixture at 900 +/- 7 mbar with an optically read out TPC (MANGO detector); first PMT waveform analysis in the NID regime; minority charge carrier drifting ~25% faster than the dominant SF6- species.
result:cygno-first-optical-negative-ion-.why_it_matters: The abstract says the results open a concrete path toward large-scale, low-diffusion optical TPCs for rare event searches.

claim.quote: It is found that the use of this additional electric field permits large light yield increases without degrading intrinsic characteristics of the amplification stage with respect to the regular use of GEMs.
