result:cygno-light-yield-enhancement-202.summary_technical: Simulation and a 10x10 cm^2 prototype test of an additional electric field below the last GEM plane in He:CF4 mixtures: large light-yield increases without degrading energy resolution or intrinsic diffusion.
result:cygno-light-yield-enhancement-202.why_it_matters: The abstract says light yield plays a major role in the energy threshold of the experiment.

claim.quote: Building on the achievements of the 50 L prototype (LIME), which successfully operated underground at LNGS, the next step is the deployment of a 0.4 m3 demonstrator, CYGNO-04, to be completed in 2026.

result:cygno-lime-underground-campaign-2.summary_technical: LIME underground at LNGS: about 27 months in five shielding configurations (no shielding, 4 cm Cu, 10 cm Cu, 10 cm Cu + 40 cm water, 10 cm Cu); up to ~1.2e7 images; trigger rates from ~34 Hz down to ~1 Hz. A review paper submitted to JINST (preprint).
result:cygno-lime-underground-campaign-2.why_it_matters: The abstract says the demonstrator will validate scalability.

claim.quote: We conclude that we have observed the top quark and measure its mass

notes: result_type is "observation" (not "discovery"), matching the paper's own title "Observation of the Top Quark" (PRL 74, 2632), per instructions to follow the collaboration's own wording.
The title was confirmed verbatim on 2026-09-17 against journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.74.2632, whose title is "Observation of the Top Quark".
result:d0-top-quark-observation-1995.summary_technical: D0 search for the Standard Model top quark in pp̄ collisions at √s=1.8 TeV, integrated luminosity about 50 pb⁻¹, in the dilepton and single-lepton channels with and without b-quark tagging: 17 events observed against an expected background of 3.8 ± 0.6 events; probability of an upward background fluctuation 2.0×10⁻⁶ (equivalent to 4.6 standard deviations). The paper concludes "we have observed the top quark" and measures its mass as 199 +19/−21 (stat) ± 22 (syst) GeV/c² and its production cross section as 6.4 ± 2.2 pb.
result:d0-top-quark-observation-1995.why_it_matters: Fermilab's Tevatron page describes the top quark as the last undiscovered quark of the six predicted to exist by current scientific theory; CDF and D0 announced their observations together on 2 March 1995, and D0's paper measures the top quark's mass and production cross section from the same data.

claim.quote: the presence of Dark Matter particles in the galactic halo is supported at 8.2 $\sigma$ C.L.

notes: Result type 'measurement': the abstract uses 'supported', not 'evidence'.
result:dama-libra-first-results-2008.summary_technical: First DAMA/LIBRA annual-modulation result: exposure 0.53 ton yr; 0.82 ton yr combined with DAMA/NaI. The abstract states that neither systematic effects nor side reactions can account for the observed modulation amplitude while satisfying all requirements of the signature.
result:dama-libra-first-results-2008.why_it_matters: First release of DAMA/LIBRA, the larger successor to DAMA/NaI; the abstract wording is 'supported at 8.2 sigma', not 'evidence'.

claim.quote: The data further confirm the model independent evidence of the presence of Dark Matter (DM) particles in the galactic halo on the basis of the DM annual modulation signature (8.9 sigma C.L. for the cumulative exposure).

result:dama-libra-new-results-2010.summary_technical: Two further annual cycles (0.34 ton yr), one before and one after the first DAMA/LIBRA upgrade of September/October 2008; cumulative exposure 1.17 ton yr over 13 annual cycles; amplitude (0.0116 +- 0.0013) cpd/kg/keV in 2-6 keV, phase (146 +- 7) d, period (0.999 +- 0.002) yr.
result:dama-libra-new-results-2010.why_it_matters: Continues the DAMA claim after the 2008 upgrade; the abstract uses the word 'evidence'.

claim.quote: The DAMA/LIBRA-phase1 data give evidence for the presence of Dark Matter (DM) particles in the galactic halo, on the basis of the exploited model independent DM annual modulation signature by using highly radio-pure NaI(Tl) target, at 7.5 sigma C.L..

result:dama-libra-phase1-final-2013.summary_technical: Total exposure 1.04 ton yr over 7 annual cycles; with DAMA/NaI (cumulative 1.33 ton yr, 14 annual cycles) the C.L. is 9.3 sigma; amplitude (0.0112 +- 0.0012) cpd/kg/keV (2-6 keV), phase (144 +- 7) d, period (0.998 +- 0.002) yr; the abstract adds that no systematic or side reaction able to mimic the signature has been found or suggested by anyone over more than a decade.
result:dama-libra-phase1-final-2013.why_it_matters: Closes the first phase of DAMA/LIBRA before the 2010 upgrade; the abstract uses the word 'evidence'.

claim.quote: The DAMA/LIBRA-phase2 data confirm the evidence of a signal that meets all the requirements of the model independent Dark Matter (DM) annual modulation signature, at 9.5 $\sigma$ C.L. in the energy region (1-6) keV.

result:dama-libra-phase2-first-results-2.summary_technical: Six annual cycles of phase2, exposure 1.13 ton yr, energy threshold 1 keV; 9.5 sigma in 1-6 keV; for the full exposure 2.46 ton yr in 2-6 keV (DAMA/NaI + phase1 + phase2) the C.L. is 12.9 sigma; amplitude (0.0103 +- 0.0008) cpd/kg/keV, phase (145 +- 5) d, period (0.999 +- 0.001) yr.
result:dama-libra-phase2-first-results-2.why_it_matters: First results from the upgraded detector, extending the claim to 1 keV; the abstract uses the word 'evidence'.

claim.quote: Including the new results, the total exposure of DAMA/LIBRA-phase2 over 8 annual cycles is 1.53 t·yr and the evidence for a signal that meets all the requirements of the model-independent Dark Matter annual modulation signature is 11.8 σ C.L. in the energy region (1 - 6) keV.

notes: Source: the Tor Vergata repository record carries the abstract (it dates the item 2022); the journal issue is 22(4), 2021 according to the LNGS page and the DOI (10.15407/jnpae2021.04.329).
result:dama-libra-phase2-further-results.summary_technical: Eight annual cycles of phase2 (1.53 t yr): 11.8 sigma in 1-6 keV; full exposure 2.86 t yr in 2-6 keV (DAMA/NaI, phase1 and phase2, 22 annual cycles): 13.7 sigma. The abstract says no systematic or side reaction mimicking the signature has been found, and mentions a preliminary result on a lower software threshold.
result:dama-libra-phase2-further-results.why_it_matters: The latest published DAMA/LIBRA significance; the abstract uses the word 'evidence'. The experiment's data taking is reported to have ended in 2024 (2026 review).

claim.quote: This cumulative exposure (107731 kg day) has given a model independent evidence for the presence of a Dark Matter particle component in the galactic halo at 6.3 sigma C.L.; this main result is summarised here.

notes: Conference summary of the same data set as result:dama-nai-seven-annual-cycles-2003; kept because its abstract uses the word 'evidence'.
result:dama-nai-evidence-summary-2003.summary_technical: Conference summary of the DAMA/NaI final result (seven annual cycles, 107731 kg day): 'model independent evidence' at 6.3 sigma C.L.; also reports that DAMA/LIBRA (about 250 kg NaI(Tl)) is taking data since March 2003.
result:dama-nai-evidence-summary-2003.why_it_matters: Records the claim in the collaboration's own wording ('evidence'); it summarises the same data set as the review-article record.

claim.quote: The effectiveness of the WIMP model independent annual modulation signature is pointed out by discussing the results obtained over 7 annual cycles (107731 kg day total exposure); the WIMP presence in the galactic halo is strongly supported at 6.3 standard deviation C.L.

notes: Result type 'measurement': the abstract says the WIMP presence is 'strongly supported'; it does not use the word 'evidence' (the 2003 conference summary of the same data does, see the next record).
result:dama-nai-seven-annual-cycles-2003.summary_technical: Review of the DAMA/NaI results: seven annual cycles, 107731 kg day; the data favour a cosine-like modulation (period one year, phase near 2 June) of the single-hit residual rate in the 2-6 keV region; the abstract's wording is 'strongly supported at 6.3 standard deviation C.L.'; the paper also examines model-dependent WIMP scenarios.
result:dama-nai-seven-annual-cycles-2003.why_it_matters: The headline DAMA/NaI claim, which DAMA/LIBRA continued and which ANAIS, COSINE, SABRE, DM-Ice and PICOLON were built to test with the same target.

claim.quote: The excluded area covers a wide range of the sterile neutrino parameters up to $\sin^22\theta_{14}<0.01$ in the most sensitive region.

result:danss-sterile-neutrino-exclusion-.summary_technical: Ratio of positron energy spectra at 10.7, 11.7 and 12.7 m (independent of reactor flux shape/normalisation and detector efficiency) from 966 k antineutrino events: 4-neutrino-model exclusion area reaching sin^2(2 theta_14) < 0.01.
result:danss-sterile-neutrino-exclusion-.why_it_matters: A flux-model-independent test of the sterile-neutrino explanation of the reactor antineutrino anomaly at a commercial reactor.

claim.quote: We report the detection of polarized anisotropy in the Cosmic Microwave Background radiation with the Degree Angular Scale Interferometer (DASI), located at the Amundsen-Scott South Pole research station.

result:dasi-first-cmb-polarization-detec.summary_technical: DASI 2001-2002 winter observations of two 3.4-degree fields: E-mode polarization detected at 4.9 sigma, TE correlation at 95% confidence, B-mode upper limit; consistent with adiabatic scalar perturbations.
result:dasi-first-cmb-polarization-detec.why_it_matters: The three-year paper says it extends "the data from which the first detection of polarization of the cosmic microwave background radiation was reported".

claim.quote: In addition, we detect a peak in the power spectrum at l approx 550 and power of similar magnitude at l approx 800 which are consistent with the second and third harmonic peaks predicted by adiabatic inflationary cosmological models.

result:dasi-first-season-power-spectrum-.summary_technical: DASI first season (2000, 32 fields): power spectrum 100 < l < 900; first peak at l ~ 200, second at l ~ 550, power of similar magnitude near l ~ 800; no foregrounds other than point sources.
result:dasi-first-season-power-spectrum-.why_it_matters: The abstract says the peaks "are consistent with the second and third harmonic peaks predicted by adiabatic inflationary cosmological models".

claim.quote: Observation of electron-antineutrino disappearance at Daya Bay

result:daya-bay-observation-2012.summary_technical: Six antineutrino detectors in two near (flux-weighted baselines 470 m and 576 m) and one far (1648 m) underground halls; 43,000 ton-GW_th-day livetime exposure in 55 days, 10416 (80376) electron antineutrino candidates at the far (near) hall. The ratio of observed to expected antineutrinos at the far hall is R = 0.940 ± 0.011(stat) ± 0.004(syst); a rate-only analysis finds sin²2θ13 = 0.092 ± 0.016(stat) ± 0.005(syst) in a three-neutrino framework, and a non-zero θ13 with a significance of 5.2 standard deviations.
result:daya-bay-observation-2012.why_it_matters: The paper's introduction says that of the three mixing angles θ13 was the least known before this result; Daya Bay reports a non-zero value with a significance of 5.2 standard deviations.

claim.locator: Phys. Rev. Lett. 94, 212302 (2005), abstract (TeX markup on the APS page)
claim.quote: The DEAR (DA$\ensuremath{\Phi}$NE exotic atom research) experiment measured the energy of x rays emitted in the transitions to the ground state of kaonic hydrogen.

notes: The claim quote is the abstract sentence as printed on the APS page, with its TeX markup; the numerical values are quoted from the SIDDHARTA collaboration's 2007 proceedings.
result:dear-kaonic-hydrogen-shift-width-.summary_technical: DEAR at DAΦNE: kaonic hydrogen K-series X-ray spectrum; strong-interaction 1s shift ε = −193 ± 37 (stat) ± 6 (syst) eV (repulsive) and width Γ = 249 ± 111 (stat) ± 30 (syst) eV; the Kα, Kβ and Kγ pattern was disentangled for the first time (Phys. Rev. Lett. 94, 212302).
result:dear-kaonic-hydrogen-shift-width-.why_it_matters: The abstract states these are the most precise values yet obtained; SIDDHARTA's 2011 measurement (arXiv:1105.3090) cites them as the previous world result.

claim.quote: we demonstrate that an unprecedented FWHM resolution of $\Delta E_\mathrm{FWHM} = \left(1.25\pm0.17\mathrm{\scriptsize{(stat)}}^{+0.05}_{-0.07}\mathrm{\scriptsize{(syst)}}\right)\,\text{eV}$ can be achieved.

notes: Component test 'towards the DELight experiment' (a sensor characterisation with an X-ray source), not a dark matter result.
result:delight-mmc-resolution-2023.summary_technical: X-ray MMC characterised with a Fe-55 source; optimum-filter-based amplitude estimation gives FWHM resolution (1.25 +- 0.17 stat +0.05/-0.07 syst) eV; the analysis pipeline is a step for the proposed superfluid-helium experiment DELight.
result:delight-mmc-resolution-2023.why_it_matters: The abstract calls the analysis pipeline an important step for the realization of the proposed superfluid helium-based experiment DELight.

claim.quote: The combination yields $w_0=-0.84^{+0.10}_{-0.10}$ and $w_a=-0.44^{+0.60}_{-0.55}$, the tightest constraints ever obtained from a single survey, with $2.2\sigma$ deviation from a cosmological constant.

notes: Posted 26 May 2026, version 2 (2 June 2026) submitted to PRL; listed on the DES home page. The 3.0σ CMB-combination figure appears in the abstract sentence beginning "Finally, when combined with primary CMB information".
result:des-dynamical-dark-energy-2026.summary_technical: Full-DES SNe Ia + BAO + 3×2pt in the w0wa model: w0 = -0.84 ± 0.10, wa = -0.44 (+0.60, -0.55), 2.2σ from a cosmological constant; adding DESI DR2 BAO: 2.3σ; adding primary CMB: w0 = -0.82 ± 0.05, wa = -0.63 (+0.21, -0.18), 3.0σ.
result:des-dynamical-dark-energy-2026.why_it_matters: The abstract says the full-DES combination gives the tightest dark-energy-evolution constraints from a single survey and that the best-fit parameters across probe combinations are consistently in the region w0 > -1 and wa < 0.

claim.quote: their combination yields clustering amplitude $S_8=0.776^{+0.017}_{-0.017}$ and matter density $\Omega_{\mathrm{m}} = 0.339^{+0.032}_{-0.031}$ in $\Lambda$CDM, mean with 68% confidence limits

notes: The paper title says "Year 3 Results"; the abstract calls it "the first cosmology results from large-scale structure in the Dark Energy Survey (DES) spanning 5000 deg2".
result:des-y3-3x2pt-cosmology-2021.summary_technical: DES Y3 3×2pt analysis (100 million source galaxies): S8 = 0.776 ± 0.017 and Ωm = 0.339 (+0.032, -0.031) in ΛCDM; S8 = 0.775 (+0.026, -0.024), Ωm = 0.352 (+0.035, -0.041) and w = -0.98 (+0.32, -0.20) in wCDM; consistent with Planck 2018 (probability-to-exceed p = 0.13 to 0.48). Combined with BAO, RSD, SNe Ia and Planck lensing: Σmν < 0.13 eV (95% CL).
result:des-y3-3x2pt-cosmology-2021.why_it_matters: The abstract says the DES data are consistent with the prediction of the model favoured by Planck 2018 CMB primary anisotropy data, quantified by a probability-to-exceed p = 0.13 to 0.48.

claim.quote: The combined analysis yields $S_8\equiv \sigma_8 (\Omega_{\rm m}/0.3)^{0.5} = 0.789^{+0.012}_{-0.012}$ and matter density $\Omega_{\rm m} = 0.333^{+0.023}_{-0.028}$ in $\Lambda$CDM (68\% CL)

notes: The abstract wording is quoted as fetched (arXiv v2, 29 January 2026). The paper is a collaboration preprint; the journal publication was not checked.
result:des-y6-3x2pt-cosmology-2026.summary_technical: DES Y6 3×2pt: S8 = 0.789 ± 0.012, Ωm = 0.333 (+0.023, -0.028) in ΛCDM, a (full-space) parameter difference of 1.8σ from Planck 2018 + ACT-DR6 + SPT-3G DR1 (2.6σ in S8 alone). wCDM: w = -1.12 (+0.26, -0.20). Combining all DES dark-energy probes (3×2pt, SNe Ia, BAO, clusters) gives a 2.8σ difference from the CMB.
result:des-y6-3x2pt-cosmology-2026.why_it_matters: The abstract states the DES Y6 constraints differ from a combination of CMB primary anisotropy datasets (Planck 2018, ACT-DR6, SPT-3G DR1) by 1.8σ in full parameter space and by 2.6σ projected onto S8.

claim.quote: This preference is 2.6$\sigma$ for the DESI+CMB combination, and persists or grows when SN~Ia are added in, giving results discrepant with the $\Lambda$CDM model at the $2.5\sigma$, $3.5\sigma$ or $3.9\sigma$ levels for the addition of Pantheon+, Union3, or DES-SN5YR datasets respectively.

notes: The abstract does not use the word "evidence"; the result type is measurement. Significance statements are quoted as the abstract gives them (they are model- and dataset-combination dependent).
result:desi-dr1-bao-cosmology-2024.summary_technical: BAO from galaxy, quasar and Lyman-α forest tracers in 7 redshift bins (0.1<z<4.2, over 6 million objects) from DESI year 1 (Data Release 1). DESI BAO alone give Ωm = 0.295 ± 0.015 and w = -0.99 (+0.15, -0.13) in flat wCDM; in the w0wa model, DESI+CMB prefer w0>-1 and wa<0 at 2.6σ, rising to 2.5σ, 3.5σ or 3.9σ discrepancy with ΛCDM when Pantheon+, Union3 or DES-SN5YR supernovae are added. Neutrino mass: Σmν < 0.072 eV (95%).
result:desi-dr1-bao-cosmology-2024.why_it_matters: The abstract reports that DESI BAO data alone are consistent with flat ΛCDM, while combinations with CMB and supernova data prefer a time-varying dark energy equation of state with w0 > -1 and wa < 0, discrepant with ΛCDM at the 2.5σ to 3.9σ level depending on the supernova sample.

claim.quote: This solution is preferred over $\Lambda$CDM at $3.1\sigma$ for the combination of DESI BAO and CMB data. When also including SNe, the preference for a dynamical dark energy model over $\Lambda$CDM ranges from $2.8-4.2\sigma$ depending on which SNe sample is used.

notes: The abstract does not use the word "evidence"; the result type is measurement. The abstract adds: "Unless there is an unknown systematic error associated with one or more datasets, it is clear that ΛCDM is being challenged by the combination of DESI BAO with other measurements."
result:desi-dr2-bao-cosmology-2025.summary_technical: BAO measurements from more than 14 million galaxies and quasars of DESI Data Release 2 (three years), combined with the Lyman-α forest BAO of a companion paper. Flat ΛCDM parameters are in 2.3σ tension with the CMB; the w0wa model (w0>-1, wa<0) is preferred over ΛCDM at 3.1σ for DESI BAO+CMB and 2.8–4.2σ when SNe are included. Σmν < 0.064 eV (ΛCDM) and < 0.16 eV (w0wa) at 95%.
result:desi-dr2-bao-cosmology-2025.why_it_matters: The abstract states that, unless there is an unknown systematic error in one or more datasets, ΛCDM is being challenged by the combination of DESI BAO with other measurements; the results favour w0 > -1 and wa < 0, so a time-evolving dark energy.

claim.quote: DM-Ice17 data are consistent with no modulation in the energy range of 4-20 keV, providing the strongest limits on weakly interacting massive particle dark matter from a direct detection experiment located in the Southern Hemisphere.

result:dm-ice17-annual-modulation-2017.summary_technical: Primary physics run 16 June 2011 - 28 January 2015, exposure 60.8 kg yr: data consistent with no modulation in 4-20 keV; limits on WIMP dark matter, the strongest from a Southern Hemisphere direct detection experiment (Phys. Rev. D 95, 032006).
result:dm-ice17-annual-modulation-2017.why_it_matters: The paper says the stable long-term operation shows the South Pole ice is viable for a high-sensitivity NaI(Tl) experiment to test the DAMA/LIBRA claim.

claim.quote: The background rate in the 6.5 - 8.0 keVee region is measured to be 7.9 +/- 0.4 counts/day/keV/kg. This is consistent with the expected background from the detector assemblies with negligible contributions from the surrounding ice.

result:dm-ice17-first-data-2014.summary_technical: Background analysis of the first two years after commissioning (July 2011 - June 2013) of the 17 kg NaI(Tl) DM-Ice17 detector, 2457 m deep in the South Pole ice; 7.9 +- 0.4 counts/day/keV/kg at 6.5-8.0 keVee (Phys. Rev. D 90, 092005).
result:dm-ice17-first-data-2014.why_it_matters: It established the South Pole ice as a viable location for future underground, low-background experiments in the Southern Hemisphere, as the paper states.

claim.quote: The measured muon rate in DM-Ice17 is 2.93 +/- 0.04 muons/crystal/day with a modulation amplitude of 12.3 +/- 1.7%, consistent with expectation.

result:dm-ice17-muon-modulation-phosphor.summary_technical: Muon rate 2.93 +- 0.04 muons/crystal/day with annual modulation amplitude 12.3 +- 1.7%; muon-induced phosphorescence with decay time 5.5 +- 0.5 s, not mimicking a scintillation signal above 2 keVee (Phys. Rev. D 93, 042001).
result:dm-ice17-muon-modulation-phosphor.why_it_matters: The paper concludes that phosphorescence with the properties observed in DM-Ice17 cannot account for the DAMA modulation.

claim.quote: In an analysis window of 80-200 keV recoil energy, based on a 35.7 g-day exposure, we set a 90% C.L. upper limit on the spin-dependent WIMP-proton cross section of 2.0 x 10^{-33} cm^{2} for 115 GeV/c^2 dark matter particle mass.

result:dmtpc-10l-surface-run-limit-2010.summary_technical: 10-L, 75 Torr CF4, surface run at MIT, 35.7 g d, 80-200 keV recoil window: 90% CL spin-dependent WIMP-proton limit 2.0e-33 cm^2 at 115 GeV/c^2 (zero expected background assumed, Feldman-Cousins).
result:dmtpc-10l-surface-run-limit-2010.why_it_matters: It is described in the abstract as the first dark matter limit from DMTPC; the detector was then moved underground.

claim.quote: we show that the addition of the charge readout analysis to the CCD allows us too obtain a statistics-limited 90% C.L. upper limit on the $e^-$ rejection factor of $5.6\times10^{-6}$ for recoils with energies between 40 and 200 keV$_{\mathrm{ee}}$

result:dmtpc-charge-signal-background-re.summary_technical: Charge readout plus CCD: statistics-limited 90% CL upper limit on the electron rejection factor of 5.6e-6 for 40-200 keVee recoils; CCD/charge coincidence reduces CCD-specific backgrounds by more than two orders of magnitude.
result:dmtpc-charge-signal-background-re.why_it_matters: It shows the surface-run backgrounds could be reduced with the combined readout.

claim.quote: In this paper, we employ measurements from two DMTPC detectors, with operating pressures of 30-60 torr, to develop and validate a model of the directional response and performance of such detectors as a function of recoil energy.

result:dmtpc-directional-sensitivity-201.summary_technical: Measurements at 30-60 torr CF4 with optical and charge readout; the model implies a 10-20 kg scale direction-sensitive detector could provide 3-sigma confirmation that a candidate signal from a non-directional experiment was induced by dark matter.
result:dmtpc-directional-sensitivity-201.why_it_matters: The abstract frames the result as the specifications needed for a scalable directional detector.

claim.quote: The technique is demonstrated by tagging the direction of the nuclear recoils created in the scattering of low-energy neutrons with CF4 in a low-pressure time-projection chamber that is developed by the DMTPC collaboration.

result:dmtpc-head-tail-observation-2007.summary_technical: Observation of the head-tail effect in CF4 nuclear recoils from low-energy neutron scattering with scintillation (CCD) readout; the decreasing ionization rate along the trajectory gives the direction tag.
result:dmtpc-head-tail-observation-2007.why_it_matters: The abstract says this proves the head-tail effect can be observed, the basis for the vector direction of dark matter recoils.

claim.quote: Observation of tau neutrino interactions

notes: The record's title and claim quote are the paper's exact title, 'Observation of tau neutrino interactions' (Kodama et al., Phys. Lett. B 504 (2001) 218), so the result is classified as an observation.
result:donut-tau-neutrino-observation-20.summary_technical: DONUT analysed 203 neutrino interactions recorded in nuclear-emulsion targets; a decay search found evidence of four tau neutrino interactions with an estimated background of 0.34 events; the abstract adds 'This number is consistent with the Standard Model expectation' (Phys. Lett. B 504, 218). Fermilab's announcement described this as the first direct evidence for the tau neutrino.
result:donut-tau-neutrino-observation-20.why_it_matters: Fermilab's announcement calls the tau neutrino the third kind of neutrino known to particle physicists and says earlier experiments had produced indirect evidence; DONUT's four events, in which a neutrino interacts to produce a tau lepton, are described there as the first direct evidence for it.

claim.quote: The deficit is interpreted as evidence of electron antineutrino disappearance.

result:double-chooz-evidence-2012.summary_technical: In 227.93 live days (33.71 GW-ton-years exposure), Double Chooz observed 8,249 candidate events versus an expectation of 8,937 for θ₁₃ = 0. A rate-plus-spectral-shape analysis gives sin²(2θ₁₃) = 0.109±0.030(stat)±0.025(syst), excluding the no-oscillation hypothesis at 99.8% CL (2.9σ).
result:double-chooz-evidence-2012.why_it_matters: Double Chooz's rate-plus-spectral-shape analysis gives sin²2θ13 = 0.109 ± 0.030(stat) ± 0.025(syst), and the data exclude the no-oscillation hypothesis at 99.8% CL (2.9σ); the collaboration words this as evidence of electron antineutrino disappearance, not as an observation.

claim.quote: After analysis, no events remain in our fiducial region leading to an exclusion curve for spin-dependent WIMP-proton interactions which reaches 0.28 pb at 100 GeV/c^2 a fourfold improvement on our previous work.

result:drift-iid-low-threshold-2017.summary_technical: 54.7 live-day shielded run: no events in the fiducial region, exclusion curve for spin-dependent WIMP-proton interactions reaching 0.28 pb at 100 GeV/c^2; a 45.4 live-day unshielded run saw 14 nuclear-recoil-like events at 0.31 +/- 0.08 per day, consistent with ambient fast neutrons from the walls of the Boulby Underground Science Facility.
result:drift-iid-low-threshold-2017.why_it_matters: The abstract calls DRIFT-IId the world's most sensitive directional dark matter detector.

claim.quote: The response of the detector is then interpreted, using the F nuclei content of the gas, in terms of sensitivity to proton spin-dependent WIMP-nucleon interactions, displaying a minimum in sensitivity cross section at 0.5 pb for a WIMP mass of 100 GeV/c^2.

result:drift-iid-spin-dependent-2010.summary_technical: 47.4 live days with a 0.8 m^3 fiducial volume (30 Torr CS2 + 10 Torr CF4) and passive shielding; radon-progeny recoils from the central cathode rejected by their large diffusion; spin-dependent WIMP-proton sensitivity minimum 0.5 pb at 100 GeV/c^2.
result:drift-iid-spin-dependent-2010.why_it_matters: First spin-dependent limit from the DRIFT-IId directional detector.

claim.quote: The excavation of the caverns that will house the gigantic particle detectors of the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment in Lead, South Dakota is complete.

notes: Two related Fermilab announcements are cited: the 1 February 2024 completion-of-excavation press release (used for the result date) and the 15 August 2024 underground ribbon-cutting event marking the same milestone publicly; both describe the same excavation completion, not two separate results.
This atlas holds no DUNE physics result; this milestone and the ProtoDUNE-SP performance paper are the only DUNE entries in results/.
result:dune-far-site-excavation-2024.summary_technical: Excavation of the three DUNE far-site caverns at the 4,850-foot level of SURF (two caverns, each more than 500 feet long and about seven stories tall, for the detector modules; a third for utilities), announced complete by Fermilab on 1 February 2024; the underground teams had been working there since 2021. A ribbon-cutting event marking the completion of excavation was held on 15 August 2024.
result:dune-far-site-excavation-2024.why_it_matters: The DUNE U.S. Project Director said completing the excavation prepares the project for installation of the detectors starting later in 2024; final outfitting of the caverns comes first.

claim.locator: title (arXiv abstract page; v4 PDF p. 1)
claim.quote: First results on ProtoDUNE-SP liquid argon time projection chamber performance from a beam test at the CERN Neutrino Platform

notes: date_kind is preprint (arXiv v1, 13 July 2020); the paper was published as JINST 15 (2020) P12004.
This is a construction/technology milestone, not a physics discovery, evidence claim or measurement; this atlas holds no DUNE physics result.
result:dune-protodune-sp-performance-202.summary_technical: ProtoDUNE-SP (NP04), a single-phase LArTPC with an active volume of 7.2 × 6.0 × 6.9 m³ at the CERN Neutrino Platform, exposed to a charged-particle beam of 0.3-7 GeV/c; the paper reports first performance results (noise and gain, dE/dx calibration, drift electron lifetime, photon-detector noise, sensitivity and time resolution): the measured values meet or exceed the DUNE far-detector specifications, in several cases by large margins.
result:dune-protodune-sp-performance-202.why_it_matters: The abstract states that the measured values meet or exceed the specifications for the DUNE far detector, and that ProtoDUNE-SP's successful operation starting in 2018 and its large samples of high-quality data demonstrate the effectiveness of the single-phase far detector design.

claim.quote: Data obtained at Brookhaven National Laboratory, using nearly equal samples of positive and negative muons, were used to deduce a_mu(Expt) = 11 659 208.0(5.4)(3.3) x 10^-10, where the statistical and systematic uncertainties are given, respectively.

result:e821-final-report-2006.summary_technical: Final E821 report: a_mu(Expt) = 11 659 208.0(5.4)(3.3) x 10^-10 (0.54 ppm) from nearly equal samples of mu+ and mu-, a 14-fold improvement over CERN; standard model evaluations based on e+e- hadronic cross sections lie 2.2-2.7 standard deviations below the experimental result.
result:e821-final-report-2006.why_it_matters: The abstract says the largest theoretical uncertainty (about 0.55 ppm) is the first-order hadronic vacuum polarization, so the comparison tests the Standard Model at the level of virtual QED, weak and hadronic loops.

claim.quote: We show that the BAO data alone are able to rule out dark-energy-free models at more than eight standard deviations in an extension to the flat, $\Lambda$CDM model that allows for curvature.

notes: The eBOSS paper summarises the whole SDSS lineage (SDSS, SDSS-II, BOSS and eBOSS), so the result is attributed to eBOSS (the completing survey) and not to BOSS or the SDSS programme record.
result:eboss-final-cosmological-implicat.summary_technical: Combined SDSS, SDSS-II, BOSS and eBOSS BAO (eight samples) and RSD fσ8 (six measurements) constraints: BAO alone exclude dark-energy-free models at >8σ in a flat-ΛCDM extension with curvature; with Planck, BAO improve curvature constraints by nearly an order of magnitude; all multiple-parameter extensions remain consistent with ΛCDM.
result:eboss-final-cosmological-implicat.why_it_matters: The abstract states that the RSD measurements indicate a growth rate consistent with Planck primary-data predictions and General Relativity, and that all multiple-parameter extensions remain consistent with ΛCDM when SDSS BAO and RSD are combined with external data.

claim.quote: The upper limit of the effective electron neutrino mass is improved by almost a factor 2 compared to the lowest current value [2], reaching mνe < 15 eV/c2 (90% credible interval).

result:echo-1k-neutrino-mass-limit-2025.summary_technical: ECHo-1k spectrum of about 2×10⁸ events with background 9.1×10⁻⁶ /eV/pixel/day: endpoint Q = 2862(4) eV (Penning trap: 2863.2(6) eV) and m(νe) < 15 eV/c² (90% credible interval), almost a factor 2 better than the previous lowest calorimetric value.
result:echo-1k-neutrino-mass-limit-2025.why_it_matters: Brings calorimetric 163Ho measurements to the 10 eV scale, an independent cross-check of tritium-based neutrino-mass limits and the stepping stone to ECHo-100k.

claim.quote: Λ-hypernuclei are produced and studied, with the FINUDA spectrometer, for the first time at an e+ e− collider: DAΦNE, the Frascati φ-factory.

notes: The Atlas keeps the arXiv v1 submission date; the abstract page text is the v3 listing.
result:finuda-12c-hypernuclear-spectrosc.summary_technical: FINUDA at DAΦNE: first Λ-hypernuclear spectroscopy with K⁻ from φ decay stopped in thin targets (K⁻ stop + ᴬZ → ᴬΛZ + π⁻), from the first data taking (December 2003 to March 2004); preliminary analysis of 12ΛC gives 1.29 MeV FWHM resolution and capture rates for the ground and excited states (Phys. Lett. B 622 (2005) 35).
result:finuda-12c-hypernuclear-spectrosc.why_it_matters: The abstract says the resolution is the best obtained so far with magnetic spectrometers at hadron facilities and that the study was made at an e+e- collider for the first time.

claim.quote: Evidence for the neutron-rich hypernucleus 6ΛH is presented from the FINUDA experiment at DAΦNE, Frascati

notes: The abstract uses the word 'evidence'; the record keeps the result type 'evidence'.
The Atlas writes the title as on the arXiv listing (6ΛH).
result:finuda-6lh-evidence-2011.summary_technical: FINUDA at DAΦNE: evidence for the neutron-rich hypernucleus 6ΛH from (π⁺, π⁻) pairs in coincidence, K⁻ stop + ⁶Li → 6ΛH + π⁺ followed by 6ΛH → ⁶He + π⁻; the production rate of the two-body π⁻ decay channel is (2.9 ± 2.0)×10⁻⁶ per stopped K⁻ and B_Λ(6ΛH) = (4.0 ± 1.1) MeV relative to ⁵H + Λ (Phys. Rev. Lett. 108 (2012) 042501).
result:finuda-6lh-evidence-2011.why_it_matters: The abstract presents the observation as evidence, not a discovery, for a hypernucleus built on a particle-unstable nuclear core.

claim.quote: We report the detection of a 51-joule (320 +/- 90 EeV) cosmic ray by the Fly's Eye air shower detector in Utah.

notes: Often called the "Oh-My-God" particle in later talks; the paper itself does not use that name.
result:flys-eye-highest-energy-cosmic-ra.summary_technical: Monocular fluorescence measurement of a single air shower of 320 ± 90 EeV (51 J) recorded 15 October 1991; the Greisen-Zatsepin-Kuzmin cutoff should lie below this energy unless the primary came from within about 30 Mpc; shower maximum near 815 g/cm2 does not identify the primary type.
result:flys-eye-highest-energy-cosmic-ra.why_it_matters: The abstract states this is substantially greater than the energy of any previously reported cosmic ray and that a GZK cutoff should occur below this energy unless the highest-energy cosmic rays have travelled less than about 30 Mpc.

claim.quote: Three independent analyses have been performed and no evidence for neutrino oscillations has been found. The resulting limits onAm 2 for maximal mixing are more restrictive by more than one order of magnitude with respect to earlier measurements.

result:frejus-atmospheric-neutrino-oscil.summary_technical: 1.56 kt yr of fiducial sensitivity; electron-to-muon charged-current ratio compared with a Monte Carlo including nu_mu-nu_e, nu_e-nu_tau and nu_mu-nu_tau oscillations; three independent analyses find no evidence for oscillations.
result:frejus-atmospheric-neutrino-oscil.why_it_matters: An early underground limit on atmospheric-neutrino oscillations, set well before the Super-Kamiokande oscillation evidence of 1998.

claim.quote: No signal is found for a sensitivity of 2.0 kiloton year.

result:frejus-bl-violating-nucleon-decay.summary_technical: Fully contained events (2.0 kt yr exposure, 700 t fiducial) searched for B-L-violating nucleon decay and di-nucleon decay: no signal, lower partial-lifetime limits at 90% CL for 35 channels with a visible particle plus limits on neutron and di-neutron decay to neutrinos.
result:frejus-bl-violating-nucleon-decay.why_it_matters: Extended the baryon-number-violation limits to decay modes that unified models such as SO(10) allow but minimal SU(5) forbids.

claim.quote: Lower limits on the nucleon lifetime in channels containing at least one positron or muon are given. The analysis is based on 4 years of data taking with the Fréjus detector.

result:frejus-nucleon-decay-charged-lept.summary_technical: No signal in channels containing at least one positron or muon; lower nucleon-lifetime limits of about 1e31 yr (p to e+ K*0) to 1.5e32 yr (p to mu+ gamma), with the atmospheric-neutrino background estimated in several ways and two nuclear models used for the event simulation.
result:frejus-nucleon-decay-charged-lept.why_it_matters: One of the first-generation proton-decay searches that ruled out the simplest grand unified models alongside IMB and Kamiokande; no experiment has seen nucleon decay.

claim.quote: The results indicate strange quark contributions of < 10% of the charge and magnetic nucleon form factors at these four-momentum transfers.

result:g0-backward-angle-strange-quark-2.summary_technical: Parity-violating asymmetries in elastic e-p and quasi-elastic e-d scattering at Q^2 = 0.22 and 0.63 GeV^2 (359 and 684 MeV beams); strange-quark contributions < 10% of the charge and magnetic form factors, and the first measurement of anapole effects in the axial current at these momentum transfers.
result:g0-backward-angle-strange-quark-2.why_it_matters: Separated the strange electric and magnetic form factors, and the axial form factor, at two momentum transfers in one experiment.

claim.quote: The results indicate non-zero, Q^2 dependent, strange quark contributions and provide new information beyond that obtained in previous experiments.

notes: Later results (HAPPEX-III, result:happex-iii-strange-vector-form-factors-2011) found the world data consistent with zero; the HAPPEX-III introduction notes that G0, A4 and others had presented evidence for non-zero strange form factors of limited significance.
result:g0-forward-angle-strange-quark-20.summary_technical: Parity-violating asymmetries in elastic e-p scattering over 0.12 < Q^2 < 1.0 GeV^2 using a toroidal spectrometer to detect the recoiling protons from a liquid-hydrogen target; the forward-angle data indicate non-zero, Q^2 dependent strange-quark contributions.
result:g0-forward-angle-strange-quark-20.why_it_matters: Covered the whole momentum-transfer range from 0.1 to 1 GeV^2 in one experiment and motivated higher-precision follow-up measurements (HAPPEX-III, A4).

claim.locator: Title, Phys. Lett. B 46 (1973) 138; Crossref record, `title` field (the publisher page refused the fetch, so the abstract was not read)
claim.quote: Observation of neutrino-like interactions without muon or electron in the gargamelle neutrino experiment

result:gargamelle-neutral-currents-1973.summary_technical: Hasert et al. (Gargamelle), Phys. Lett. B 46 (1973) 138 (hadronic events without muon or electron) and 121 (a single antineutrino-electron scattering event), published together on 3 September 1973 after a CERN seminar on 19 July 1973. The collaboration's own title says 'Observation'; CERN's account calls it the first direct evidence of the weak neutral current.
result:gargamelle-neutral-currents-1973.why_it_matters: The Glashow-Salam-Weinberg theory had predicted the weak neutral current in the mid-1960s, a process that required a neutral particle to carry the weak force.

claim.quote: Observations of the Failure of Conservation of Parity and Charge Conjugation in Meson Decays: the Magnetic Moment of the Free Muon

notes: The paper title says "Observations"; typed observation per A16.
result:garwin-lederman-weinrich-parity-o.summary_technical: Large decay-electron asymmetry from polarized, stopped mu+ at the Nevis cyclotron; parity and charge-conjugation invariance both fail in pi → mu → e decay; g(μ⁺) = +2.00 ± 0.10.
result:garwin-lederman-weinrich-parity-o.why_it_matters: Lederman: this large effect "established the two-component neutrinos" and, with details of the decay parameters, "the V-A structure of the weak interactions".

claim.quote: We report on the first production of an antihydrogen beam by charge exchange of 6.1 keV antiprotons with a cloud of positronium in the GBAR experiment at CERN.

result:gbar-antihydrogen-production-2023.summary_technical: First production of an antihydrogen beam by charge exchange of 6.1 keV antiprotons delivered by AD/ELENA with a positronium cloud made from a linac-driven positron beam; an excess over background indicates production with a significance of 3-4 standard deviations.
result:gbar-antihydrogen-production-2023.why_it_matters: This is the first step of the GBAR scheme, which will go on to antihydrogen ions and a free-fall measurement; the CERN news item states the aim of testing the equivalence principle with antimatter.

claim.quote: The first four naked high purity Germanium detectors were installed successfully in liquid nitrogen in the GENIUS-Test-Facility (GENIUS-TF) in the GRAN SASSO Underground Laboratory on May 5, 2003. This is the first time ever that this novel technique

result:genius-tf-first-naked-ge-detector.summary_technical: Four naked HPGe detectors (10.52 kg) in a thin-walled copper box of purified liquid nitrogen, installed 5 May 2003 in LNGS; first operating parameters reported.
result:genius-tf-first-naked-ge-detector.why_it_matters: First underground test of naked Ge detectors in liquid nitrogen, the key idea of the proposed GENIUS observatory.

claim.quote: After operation of GENIUS-TF over three years with finally six naked Ge detectors (15kg) in liquid nitrogen in Gran Sasso, we realize serious problems for realization of a full-size GENIUS-like experiment

result:genius-tf-ii-iii-long-term-stabil.summary_technical: Background from 222Rn diffusing into the setup far above expectation, and limited long-term stability of naked detectors in liquid nitrogen from increasing leakage current: none of the six detectors ran after three years with the nominal leakage current, and three no longer worked at all.
result:genius-tf-ii-iii-long-term-stabil.why_it_matters: The end-of-run verdict on the naked-germanium-in-liquid-nitrogen technique at LNGS.

claim.quote: We focus especially on the background coming from {sup 222}Rn daughters. This is found to be at present by a factor of 200 higher than expected from simulation. It is still compatible with the scientific goal of GENIUS-TF, namely to search for cold dark matter by the modulation signal

result:genius-tf-radon-daughter-backgrou.summary_technical: Background from 222Rn daughters after the completion of the external shielding (December 2003), a factor of about 200 above the simulation; compatible with the annual-modulation search but a serious problem for a full-size liquid-nitrogen GENIUS.
result:genius-tf-radon-daughter-backgrou.why_it_matters: Told the field that naked germanium in liquid nitrogen needs much cleaner nitrogen and shielding than simulated.

claim.quote: The asymmetries, measured as a function of the proton momentum transfer, possess greater precision than previous

notes: Classified as a measurement: the abstract reports measurements and comparisons with models, not a discovery.
result:gluex-beam-asymmetry-pi0-eta-2017.summary_technical: Measurement of the photon beam asymmetry Σ for γp→pπ0 and γp→pη with a 9 GeV linearly polarised tagged photon beam on liquid hydrogen in Hall D, as a function of momentum transfer; data collected in spring 2016, the first from GlueX and the first measurement with a 12 GeV electron beam at Jefferson Lab. Compared with t-channel quasi-particle exchange predictions.
result:gluex-beam-asymmetry-pi0-eta-2017.why_it_matters: The beam asymmetry tests the exchange mechanism that produces light mesons in photoproduction, which GlueX must understand before it can pick out exotic hybrid mesons in amplitude analyses.

claim.quote: We find the total cross section falls toward the threshold less steeply than expected from two-gluon exchange models.

notes: Published as Phys. Rev. Lett. 123, 072001 (2019); dated by the arXiv v1 submission.
result:gluex-jpsi-near-threshold-photopr.summary_technical: First measurement of the γp→J/ψp cross section from Eγ=11.8 GeV down to threshold (8.2 GeV) with the tagged photon beam; the total cross section falls toward threshold less steeply than two-gluon exchange models expect; dσ/dt slope 1.67±0.39 GeV^-2 at 10.7 GeV; no evidence for LHCb Pc+ states in the s-channel, with model-dependent upper limits on their branching fractions.
result:gluex-jpsi-near-threshold-photopr.why_it_matters: Near-threshold J/ψ production is sensitive to the gluonic structure of the proton and is the channel in which s-channel pentaquark resonances could appear.

claim.quote: Out of a total of 184 thunderstorms recorded during the interval April 2011-December 2014, the one on 1 December 2014 produced a massive potential of 1.3 GV.

notes: Atmospheric-electricity result obtained with a cosmic-ray muon telescope; included as the GRAPES-3 collaboration's PRL headline, not as particle physics proper.
result:grapes-3-thundercloud-potential-2.summary_technical: Rapid (about 10 min) muon-intensity variations in the GRAPES-3 muon telescope during 184 thunderstorms (April 2011-December 2014); the storm of 1 December 2014 produced 1.3 GV; field monitors up to 6 km apart give cloud altitude 11.4 km amsl and area ≥ 380 km2; charging time 6 min implies power ≥ 2 GW.
result:grapes-3-thundercloud-potential-2.why_it_matters: The abstract says this work possibly provides the first direct evidence for the generation of GV potentials in thunderclouds, which could also explain the highest-energy (100 MeV) gamma rays of terrestrial gamma-ray flashes.

claim.quote: The invariant-mass spectrum of $e^+ e^-$ pairs produced in $^{12}$C+$^{12}$C collisions at an incident energy of 2 GeV per nucleon has been measured for the first time.

result:hades-cc-dielectron-first-measure.summary_technical: Invariant-mass spectrum of e+e- pairs in 12C+12C at 2 GeV per nucleon measured for the first time; Dalitz decays of pi0 and eta account for the yield up to 0.15 GeV/c^2 but only about 50% above; the excess is likely from baryon-resonance and vector-meson decays.
result:hades-cc-dielectron-first-measure.why_it_matters: Resolved the 'DLS puzzle' of the earlier Bevalac data and set the baseline for the Au+Au measurements.

claim.locator: Introduction (HZDR repository copy of the published paper)
claim.quote: In this contribution we report the first observation of dilepton emission from QCD matter at high net-baryon density

notes: The claim is the paper's own wording ("we report the first observation of dilepton emission from QCD matter at high net-baryon density"), taken from the repository copy of the published paper (the arXiv version was not located).
result:hades-dilepton-emission-baryon-ri.summary_technical: Dielectron emission from Au+Au collisions at sqrt(sNN) = 2.42 GeV: after subtraction of the contribution from hadron decays the excess is thermal-like radiation; the average temperature of the radiating fireball is 71.8 ± 2.1 MeV with densities up to three times normal nuclear density, with an in-medium rho spectral function strongly broadened by baryons.
result:hades-dilepton-emission-baryon-ri.why_it_matters: Dilepton thermometry of matter at high net-baryon density complements the NA60 and CERES measurements at high energy and supports the equation-of-state studies of neutron-star mergers.

claim.quote: The high precision information on higher order flow coefficients is a major step forward in constraining the equation-of-state of dense baryonic matter.

result:hades-flow-harmonics-au-au-2020.summary_technical: Flow coefficients v_n (n = 1-6) for p, d and t versus centrality, transverse momentum and rapidity in Au+Au at sqrt(sNN) = 2.4 GeV, constructing a multi-differential angular emission pattern for the first time at a few GeV; a step forward in constraining the equation of state of dense baryonic matter.
result:hades-flow-harmonics-au-au-2020.why_it_matters: High-precision higher-order flow data at the energy of neutron-star mergers constrain the stiffness of nuclear matter.

claim.quote: we report the detection of $\gamma$-rays from the Crab Nebula at a significance level of about 20$\sigma$, corresponding to a time averaged flux of (1.64$\pm$0.09) $\times10^{-10}$ photons cm$^{-2}$ sec$^{-1}$ above 230 GeV

result:hagar-crab-detection-2019.summary_technical: About 219 hours of Crab data from October 2008 to December 2017 analysed with the wavefront-sampling technique: detection at about 20 sigma, time-averaged flux (1.64 +- 0.09) x 10^-10 photons cm^-2 s^-1 above 230 GeV; study of systematic effects of the analysis.
result:hagar-crab-detection-2019.why_it_matters: The abstract frames the Crab observations as an assessment of the performance of the HAGAR telescopes.

claim.quote: We have measured the parity-violating electroweak asymmetry in the elastic scattering of polarized electrons from the proton.

result:happex-i-ep-asymmetry-q2-0477-200.summary_technical: A = -15.05 +- 0.98 stat +- 0.56 syst ppm at <theta_lab> = 12.3 degrees and Q^2 = 0.477 (GeV/c)^2, giving G_E^s + 0.392 G_M^s = 0.025 +- 0.020 +- 0.014; first fixed-target parity-violation experiment to use a strained GaAs photocathode or a Compton polarimeter.
result:happex-i-ep-asymmetry-q2-0477-200.why_it_matters: Showed that the parity-violation technique reaches the precision needed to test for strange-quark effects in the proton.

claim.quote: These results significantly improve constraints on the electric and magnetic strange form factors G_E^s and G_M^s.

result:happex-ii-nucleon-strange-form-fa.why_it_matters: The tightest limits on the strange electric and magnetic form factors at Q^2 about 0.1 GeV^2 when published.

claim.quote: With this measurement, the world data on strange contributions to nucleon form factors are seen to be consistent with zero and not more than a few percent of the proton form factors.

result:happex-iii-strange-vector-form-fa.summary_technical: A_PV = -23.80 +- 0.78 stat +- 0.36 syst ppm at Q^2 = 0.624 GeV^2 and beam energy 3.48 GeV, giving G_E^s + 0.517 G_M^s = 0.003 +- 0.010 stat +- 0.004 syst +- 0.009 ff; the world data on strange form factors are consistent with zero.
result:happex-iii-strange-vector-form-fa.why_it_matters: Closed the question left open by earlier hints of a strange-quark effect at higher momentum transfer.

claim.quote: The final setup started data taking in Gran Sasso in August 2000. The performance and the first results of the measurement with the final setup are discussed.

notes: The abstract states a measurement of performance and first results, not a limit; the paper's body also reports an exclusion plot slightly better than Heidelberg-Moscow at low WIMP masses.
result:hdms-final-setup-first-results-20.summary_technical: Final setup with an enriched 73Ge inner detector; data from February to September 2001 (the last 132.4 days, 26.74 kg d) with an anticoincidence background reduction factor of about 4.5 at 50-100 keV and a 5 keV threshold (body of the paper); a WIMP-nucleon limit is shown in a figure.
result:hdms-final-setup-first-results-20.why_it_matters: Showed the nested-crystal design with an enriched 73Ge target working at LNGS, the basis for the later spin-dependent limit.

claim.quote: We present first results after successfully running the prototype detector for a period of about 15 months in the Gran Sasso Underground Laboratory. We analyze the results in terms of limits on WIMP-nucleon cross sections

notes: The numerical limit is shown only in a figure of the paper; the abstract gives no value, so no key value is recorded.
result:hdms-prototype-first-results-2000.summary_technical: Prototype with natural Ge crystals (inner 202 g, outer 2111 g); the last 49 days (9.9 kg d) analysed without background subtraction; spin-independent WIMP-nucleon limits better than Heidelberg-Moscow below about 40 GeV thanks to a 2 keV threshold (body of the paper; the abstract states only that limits are derived).
result:hdms-prototype-first-results-2000.why_it_matters: One of the first low-threshold germanium limits that did not rely on background subtraction, and the proof of the nested-crystal idea before the enriched-73Ge final setup.

claim.quote: The results (85.48 kg d) improve the best present existing limits on the WIMP-neutron spin-dependent cross-section (obtained from {sup 129}Xe) for low WIMP masses

notes: The primary paper is Klapdor-Kleingrothaus et al., Phys. Lett. B 609 (2005) 226-231, which could not be read (not on arXiv; publisher page blocked); this record rests on the 2006 conference paper's abstract that cites it. The abstract states the exposure but no cross-section value.
result:hdms-spin-dependent-wimp-neutron-.summary_technical: HDMS inner detector of enriched 73Ge (the only Ge isotope with nuclear spin); 85.48 kg d; spin-dependent WIMP-neutron cross-section limit improving the xenon-129 limit at low WIMP masses.
result:hdms-spin-dependent-wimp-neutron-.why_it_matters: Spin-dependent sensitivity from a germanium target, complementary to xenon and sodium iodide results.

claim.quote: TeV gamma ray emission was detected at the 5 sigma level, and a flux of (5.8 +- 1.2(stat) +- 1.2(syst)) 10^(-9) ph m^(-2) s^(-1) above 1 TeV was derived.

result:hegra-cassiopeia-a-evidence-2001.summary_technical: 232 hours of HEGRA stereoscopic IACT data (1997-1999): TeV emission detected at 5 sigma, flux (5.8 +- 1.2 stat +- 1.2 syst) x 10^-9 ph m^-2 s^-1 above 1 TeV, differential index -2.5 +- 0.4 stat +- 0.1 syst between 1 and 10 TeV.
result:hegra-cassiopeia-a-evidence-2001.why_it_matters: The abstract says this is the first report of the detection of a TeV gamma-ray source on the "centi-Crab" scale.

claim.quote: The spectrum extends up to energies of 80 TeV and is well matched by model calculations in the framework of inverse Compton scattering of various seed photons in the nebula

result:hegra-crab-spectrum-2004.summary_technical: Close to 400 hours of useful stereoscopic data from 1997 to 2002; spectrum to 80 TeV matched by inverse-Compton models including a compact mm-wave emission region; average magnetic field (161.6 +- 0.8 stat +- 18 sys) microgauss; emission region position shifted 13 arcsec west of the pulsar.
result:hegra-crab-spectrum-2004.why_it_matters: The abstract says the presence of protons in the nebula is not required to explain the observed flux.

claim.quote: First evidence for neutrinoless double beta decay is observed giving first evidence for lepton number violation.

notes: Authors: Klapdor-Kleingrothaus, Dietz, Harney, Krivosheina (the paper's affiliations are the Max-Planck-Institut fuer Kernphysik and the Radiophysical-Research Institute, Nishnii-Novgorod). It is a claim by part of the collaboration, not the collaboration's headline result.

The CUORICINO PRL (hep-ex/0501034) calls it 'the claimed discovery of the decay of 76Ge reported by a subset of the Heidelberg-Moscow collaboration' and states: 'This claim has been contested by various authors [14, 29, 30] and also by other members of the same Heidelberg-Moscow Collaboration [31].'

GERDA's Phase I paper (arXiv:1307.4720) states: "Part of HdM published a claim to have observed". The same group's 2004 paper (hep-ph/0404088, full data 1990-2003) reports the confidence level improved to 4.2 sigma in its abstract; it is not recorded as a separate result.
result:heidelberg-moscow-evidence-claim-.summary_technical: Bayesian re-analysis of 54.98 kg y (Aug 1990 - May 2000): 97 % (2.2 sigma) with the Bayesian method, 99.8 % c.l. (3.1 sigma) with the PDG-recommended method; T1/2 = (0.8-18.3)e25 yr (95 % c.l.), best value 1.5e25 yr; <m> = 0.11-0.56 eV (95 % c.l.). Not the collaboration's own headline result: see the notes.
result:heidelberg-moscow-evidence-claim-.why_it_matters: The only claimed signal of neutrinoless double beta decay in germanium; it motivated GERDA, whose first phase was designed to test it.

claim.quote: we set a lower limit on the half-life of the neutrinoless double beta decay in 76Ge of T_1/2 > 5.7 * 10^{25} yr at 90% C.L., thus excluding an effective Majorana neutrino mass greater than 0.2 eV

result:heidelberg-moscow-majorana-mass-l.summary_technical: Pulse-shape-selected data, 24 kg y: T1/2(0vbb, 76Ge) > 5.7e25 yr at 90 % C.L., corresponding to <m_ee> < 0.2 eV for the matrix elements used; the full-spectrum 41.55 kg y set gave a weaker limit.
result:heidelberg-moscow-majorana-mass-l.why_it_matters: One of the two most sensitive 76Ge searches of its time; its limit set the bar that the GERDA Phase I test of the later claim compared against.

claim.quote: for oxygen-nucleus collisions at incident energies of 60 and 200 GeV per nucleon for Al, Ag, and W target nuclei

result:helios-transverse-energy-o-nucleu.summary_technical: Transverse-energy distributions in -0.1 < eta_lab < 2.9 for 16O-nucleus collisions (Al, Ag, W targets) at 60 and 200 GeV/nucleon, measured over 5 orders of magnitude in cross-section to ET of 200 GeV; dET/deta as a function of eta; for central collisions ET in this region scales roughly as A^0.5; compared with a dual parton model; the energy density is addressed.
result:helios-transverse-energy-o-nucleu.why_it_matters: One of the first transverse-energy measurements with ion beams at the SPS; a 1991 review of HELIOS results states the energy density reached is in the region of the lattice-QCD critical value (2.5 GeV/fm3) for deconfinement.

claim.quote: Using the HERA-B detector, the b-bbar production cross section has been measured in 920 GeV proton collisions on carbon and titanium targets.

result:herab-bbbar-production-cross-sect.summary_technical: b-bbar production cross section from inclusive b -> J/psi X decays tagged by the longitudinal separation of the J/psi -> l+l- vertex, in both e+e- and mu+mu- channels: sigma(b-bbar) = 32 +14 -12 (stat) +6 -7 (sys) nb/nucleon.
result:herab-bbbar-production-cross-sect.why_it_matters: The b-bbar cross section at fixed-target energies was poorly known and sets the expected B yield of such experiments.

claim.quote: The mid-rapidity (dsigma_(pN)/dy at y=0) and total sigma_(pN) production cross sections of J/Psi mesons are measured in proton-nucleus interactions.

result:herab-jpsi-production-cross-secti.summary_technical: Mid-rapidity and total J/psi production cross sections in proton-nucleus interactions at 920 GeV/c with carbon, titanium and tungsten targets, J/psi reconstructed from lepton pairs: total cross section sigma_pN(J/psi) = 663 ± 74 ± 46 nb/nucleon.
result:herab-jpsi-production-cross-secti.why_it_matters: Provides J/psi production data at sqrt(s) = 41.6 GeV for tests of QCD production models and for nuclear-dependence studies.

claim.quote: A key result of this work is the measurement of the quantum evaporation channel's gain of 0.15 $\pm$ 0.01, which will enable $^4$He-based dark matter experiments in the near term.

notes: Listed on the TESSERACT papers page; published as Phys. Rev. D 110, 072006 (2024) (the arXiv abstract page gives no journal reference, so the publication year is not recorded).
result:herald-first-demonstration-2023.summary_technical: HeRALD v0.1 (~10 g): heat-free film blocking with an unoxidized Cs film, TES-calorimeter readout of scintillation and 4He quasiparticle (quantum evaporation) channels; quantum-evaporation gain 0.15 +- 0.01; energy threshold 145 eV at 5 sigma, corresponding to dark matter masses down to 220 MeV/c^2.
result:herald-first-demonstration-2023.why_it_matters: The abstract says this gain will enable helium-4-based dark matter experiments in the near term.

claim.quote: we measured the scintillation from electronic recoils ranging between 36.3 and 185 keV$_\mathrm{ee}$, yielding a mean signal size of $1.25^{+0.03}_{-0.03}$~phe/keV$_\mathrm{ee}$, and nuclear recoils from 53.2 to 1090 keV$_\mathrm{nr}$.

notes: Collaboration tag on the paper is 'SPICE/HeRALD Collaboration'.
result:herald-scintillation-yield-2021.summary_technical: Scintillation yield of 1.75 K superfluid 4He for electronic recoils (36.3-185 keVee) and nuclear recoils (53.2-1090 keVnr) read out by six immersed PMTs, compared to a semiempirical model; delayed scintillation components studied as a handle on recoil-type discrimination.
result:herald-scintillation-yield-2021.why_it_matters: The abstract says the relative yields set the sensitivity and discrimination power of a superfluid 4He dark matter detector.

claim.quote: Observation of a Dimuon Resonance at 9.5 GeV in 400-GeV Proton-Nucleus Collisions

notes: The paper title says "Observation"; the discovery label comes from Fermilab ("Discovery of the bottom quark"), so the type follows the title (A16).
The text of Lederman's lecture ("a paper was sent off in August of 1977") disagrees with the Fermilab and APS dates; the APS publication date is used.
result:herb-e288-upsilon-observation-197.summary_technical: A strong enhancement at 9.5 GeV in a sample of 9000 dimuon events with m(μ⁺μ⁻) > 5 GeV from 400-GeV protons on nuclei; later understood as the bound state of a bottom quark and its antiquark.
result:herb-e288-upsilon-observation-197.why_it_matters: Fermilab History and Archives says the upsilon "was later understood to be the bound state of the bottom quark and its antiquark".

claim.quote: Precise measurements of the spin structure functions of the proton $g_1^p(x,Q^2)$ and deuteron $g_1^d(x,Q^2)$ are presented over the kinematic range $0.0041 \leq x \leq 0.9$ and $0.18 $ GeV$^2$ $\leq Q^2 \leq 20$ GeV$^2$.

result:hermes-g1-proton-deuteron-neutron.summary_technical: Precise measurements of g1^p(x,Q^2) and g1^d(x,Q^2) over 0.0041 <= x <= 0.9 and 0.18 <= Q^2 <= 20 GeV^2 in deep-inelastic scattering of 27.6 GeV longitudinally polarised positrons off longitudinally polarised hydrogen and deuterium gas targets internal to HERA, using 1996-97 proton and 2000 deuteron data; combined with g1^d to give g1^n.
result:hermes-g1-proton-deuteron-neutron.why_it_matters: g1 fixes how much of the nucleon spin is carried by quark spins; its first moment is a central input to the proton spin puzzle.

claim.quote: Polarized deep--inelastic scattering data on longitudinally polarized hydrogen and deuterium targets have been used to determine double spin asymmetries of cross sections.

result:hermes-quark-helicity-distributio.summary_technical: Inclusive and semi-inclusive double-spin asymmetries for charged pions and kaons from longitudinally polarised hydrogen and deuterium targets, used with a leading-order analysis to extract the helicity distributions of u, d, ubar, dbar and s quarks.
result:hermes-quark-helicity-distributio.why_it_matters: First flavour-separated quark helicity distributions including the strange sea from semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering.

claim.quote: The High Resolution Fly's Eye (HiRes) experiment has observed the Greisen-Zatsepin-Kuzmin suppression (called the GZK cutoff) with a statistical significance of five standard deviations.

notes: AGASA's earlier spectrum (result:agasa-spectrum-beyond-gzk-cutoff-1998) pointed the other way; the HiRes paper itself mentions AGASA's report of events beyond the GZK threshold.
result:hires-gzk-suppression-2007.summary_technical: Monocular air-fluorescence flux measurements from HiRes-I and HiRes-II show a break (suppression) at 6 × 10¹⁹ eV, consistent with the GZK cutoff energy, and the ankle at 4 × 10¹⁸ eV; the Poisson probability of the observed deficit is 7 × 10⁻⁸ (about 5.3 standard deviations), the paper states 5 standard deviations.
result:hires-gzk-suppression-2007.why_it_matters: The abstract says HiRes measured a sharp suppression of the ultrahigh-energy cosmic-ray flux at 6 × 10¹⁹ eV, consistent with the expected cutoff energy, and also observed the ankle at 4 × 10¹⁸ eV.

claim.quote: With a total of 7 × 107 decay events recorded over two months and a Bayesian statistical analysis, we derive an upper limit of mβ < 27 eV/c2 at 90% credibility.

result:holmes-neutrino-mass-limit-2025.summary_technical: Two physics runs (about 2 months, about 7×10⁷ events, 48 active TES pixels, 6 eV FWHM): Bayesian limit m_β < 27 eV/c² (90% credibility). The paper states this is the most stringent bound ever obtained with a calorimetric 163Ho measurement (March 2025); ECHo-1k (arXiv:2509.03423) later reported m < 15 eV/c² (90%).
result:holmes-neutrino-mass-limit-2025.why_it_matters: Shows that ion-implanted TES arrays can scale to a competitive calorimetric neutrino-mass experiment, an independent route to KATRIN's tritium measurements.

claim.quote: Measurement of the Solar Electron Neutrino Flux with the Homestake Chlorine Detector

result:homestake-flux-measurement-1998.summary_technical: Combined result of 108 extractions by the Homestake chlorine detector, which had been measuring the solar neutrino flux since 1970: solar-neutrino-induced 37Ar production rate of 2.56 ± 0.16 (stat) ± 0.16 (syst) SNU. Davis's Nobel lecture gives the standard solar model prediction of the time as 7.6 (+1.3/−1.1) SNU (Bahcall et al., 2001).
result:homestake-flux-measurement-1998.why_it_matters: The summary of all data from the multi-decade Homestake chlorine-detector experiment (Cleveland et al. 1998): a measured rate of 2.56 SNU against a standard solar model prediction of 7.6 SNU, about one-third of the predicted rate, the 'solar neutrino problem'.

claim.quote: This is the first displaced vertex search result published by HPS.

result:hps-2016-engineering-run-prompt-a.summary_technical: 2016 Engineering Run, 10608 nb^-1: prompt resonance search between 39 and 179 MeV with no evidence of dark photons above the QED background (eps^2 >= 10^-5 limit); displaced-vertex search between 60 and 150 MeV with no excess but insufficient luminosity to limit canonical heavy-photon production; first displaced-vertex search published by HPS.
result:hps-2016-engineering-run-prompt-a.why_it_matters: Establishes the displaced-vertex technique before the 2019 and 2021 high-luminosity runs.

claim.quote: A search for a resonance in the $e^{+}e^{-}$ invariant mass distribution, using 1.7 days (1170 nb$^{-1}$) of data, showed no evidence of dark photon decays above the large QED background, confirming earlier searches and demonstrating the full functionality of the experiment.

result:hps-first-search-2015-engineering.summary_technical: Resonance search in the e+e- invariant-mass distribution with 1.7 days (1170 nb^-1) of 2015 engineering-run data: no evidence of dark-photon decays above the large QED background for masses 19-81 MeV/c^2; upper limits on the squared coupling of about 6e-6.
result:hps-first-search-2015-engineering.why_it_matters: Showed that the HPS technique works and confirmed earlier prompt-resonance searches ahead of its high-luminosity runs.

claim.quote: The complete ... QED calculation agrees reasonably well with the data.

result:hrs-qed-four-lepton-test-1990.summary_technical: HRS: e⁺e⁻ → four-lepton final states at √s = 29 GeV, 17 e⁺e⁻e⁺e⁻, 24 e⁺e⁻μ⁺μ⁻ and 1 μ⁺μ⁻μ⁺μ⁻ events with pair masses above 1 GeV/c², integrated luminosity 291 pb⁻¹; the complete α⁴ QED calculation agrees reasonably well with the data (Phys. Rev. D 42, 2180, 1 October 1990).
result:hrs-qed-four-lepton-test-1990.why_it_matters: The abstract presents it as a test of QED to fourth order in the coupling constant.

claim.quote: No new physics signal is observed, and we set world-leading limits on heavy QCD axions, as well as for the Higgs portal scalar among dedicated searches.

notes: The paper calls this the first search for new physics performed with the ICARUS detector at Fermilab; it uses NuMI-beam data at a far-off-axis position (5.75°).
result:icarus-hidden-sector-scalar-limit.summary_technical: Search for long-lived particles from K → π + S decays with S → μ⁺μ⁻ inside ICARUS-T600, using 2.41×10²⁰ POT from the NuMI beam at Fermilab. No new physics signal is observed; the paper sets world-leading limits on heavy QCD axions, as well as for the Higgs portal scalar among dedicated searches, and presents limits in a model-independent way applicable to any model predicting K → π + S(→ μμ) with a long-lived S.
result:icarus-hidden-sector-scalar-limit.why_it_matters: The paper calls this the first search for new physics performed with the ICARUS detector at Fermilab, and says it paves the way for the future program of long-lived particle searches at ICARUS. The channel would be a signal of hidden-sector models that can address the strong CP problem and the microphysical origin of dark matter.

claim.quote: we constrain the atmospheric neutrino mixing parameters to be $\sin^2\theta_{23} = 0.51\pm 0.05$ and $\Delta m^2_{32} = 2.41\pm0.07\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{eV}^2$, assuming a normal mass ordering.

result:icecube-deepcore-atmospheric-osci.summary_technical: Three-flavour atmospheric oscillation fit to 2011–2019 DeepCore data with improved calibration and processing: sin²θ₂₃ = 0.51 ± 0.05 and Δm²₃₂ = (2.41 ± 0.07) × 10⁻³ eV² for normal ordering, a 40% error reduction over the previous IceCube result.
result:icecube-deepcore-atmospheric-osci.why_it_matters: The abstract says the results are compatible and complementary to those obtained using accelerator neutrino beams, which are measured at lower neutrino energies and are subject to different sources of uncertainties.

claim.quote: Evidence for High-Energy Extraterrestrial Neutrinos at the IceCube Detector

result:icecube-evidence-extraterrestrial.summary_technical: All-sky search for high-energy neutrino interactions starting inside the detector, May 2010 – May 2012. Twenty-eight events with deposited energies between 30 and 1200 TeV reject a purely atmospheric origin at 4σ; their flavours, directions and energies are inconsistent with the atmospheric muon and neutrino backgrounds and consistent with generic predictions for an additional component of extraterrestrial origin.
result:icecube-evidence-extraterrestrial.why_it_matters: The abstract says the twenty-eight events include the highest energy neutrinos ever observed and have flavors, directions and energies inconsistent with those expected from atmospheric muon and neutrino backgrounds, while being consistent with generic predictions for an additional component of extraterrestrial origin.

claim.quote: We identify neutrino emission from the Galactic plane at the 4.5$\sigma$ level of significance, by comparing diffuse emission models to a background-only hypothesis.

result:icecube-galactic-plane-neutrinos-.summary_technical: Machine-learning cascade selection applied to ten years of IceCube data identifies diffuse Galactic-plane neutrino emission at 4.5σ against a background-only hypothesis; consistent with modelled diffuse emission but also compatible with unresolved point sources.
result:icecube-galactic-plane-neutrinos-.why_it_matters: The abstract says cosmic rays from the Milky Way arrive at Earth from random directions because of deflection in interstellar magnetic fields, but near their sources and during propagation they interact with matter and produce high-energy neutrinos; the paper searches for that neutrino emission from the Galactic plane.

claim.quote: Here we report the detection by the IceCube neutrino observatory of a cascade of high-energy particles (a particle shower) consistent with being created at the Glashow resonance. ... The evidence of the Glashow resonance suggests the presence of electron antineutrinos in the astrophysical flux, while also providing further validation of the standard model of particle physics.

result:icecube-glashow-resonance-candida.summary_technical: Cascade with an energy of 6.05 ± 0.72 PeV (from Cherenkov radiation in the Antarctic ice), consistent with the Glashow resonance, which peaks at an antineutrino energy of 6.3 PeV in the electron rest frame; features consistent with secondary muons indicate the hadronic decay of a resonant W⁻ boson and, the paper says, confirm that the source is astrophysical. The paper states that the evidence suggests electron antineutrinos in the astrophysical flux and provides further validation of the Standard Model.
result:icecube-glashow-resonance-candida.why_it_matters: The abstract says the resonance's unique signature indicates a method of distinguishing neutrinos from antineutrinos, a way to identify astronomical accelerators that produce neutrinos via hadronuclear or photohadronic interactions. IceCube's press release adds that Sheldon Glashow first proposed the resonance in 1960.

claim.quote: We found an excess of $79_{-20}^{+22}$ neutrinos associated with the nearby active galaxy NGC 1068 at a significance of 4.2$\,\sigma$.

result:icecube-ngc-1068-evidence-2022.summary_technical: Point-source search over 2011–2020 data with improved reconstruction and calibration; 110 a priori selected gamma-ray sources analysed individually. An excess of 79 (+22/−20) neutrinos associated with NGC 1068 at a significance of 4.2σ, spatially consistent with the direction of the strongest clustering of neutrinos in the Northern Sky and interpreted as direct evidence of TeV neutrino emission from a nearby active galaxy; the inferred flux exceeds the potential TeV gamma-ray flux by at least one order of magnitude.
result:icecube-ngc-1068-evidence-2022.why_it_matters: The abstract interprets the excess, spatially consistent with the direction of the strongest clustering of neutrinos in the Northern Sky, as direct evidence of TeV neutrino emission from a nearby active galaxy.

claim.quote: The best-fit point is found to be at $\sin^2(2\theta_{24})=0.10$ and $\Delta m_{41}^2 = 4.5{\rm eV}^2$, which is consistent with the no sterile neutrino hypothesis with a p-value of 8.0\%.

result:icecube-sterile-neutrino-search-2.summary_technical: 3+1 sterile-neutrino search using 305,735 atmospheric muon neutrino events over eight years, testing matter-enhanced oscillations for Δm²₄₁ between 0.01 and 100 eV². Best fit sin²(2θ₂₄) = 0.10, Δm²₄₁ = 4.5 eV², consistent with no sterile neutrino at a p-value of 8.0%.
result:icecube-sterile-neutrino-search-2.why_it_matters: A test of eV-scale sterile neutrinos through matter-enhanced oscillations of atmospheric neutrinos in the Earth, relevant to the sterile-neutrino interpretation of short-baseline anomalies. The paper reports that its 99% contour is stronger than other exclusion limits at values of Δm² up to 1 eV².

claim.quote: This observation of a neutrino in spatial coincidence with a gamma-ray emitting blazar during an active phase suggests that blazars may be a source of high-energy neutrinos.

notes: The paper is authored jointly by IceCube and the Fermi-LAT, MAGIC, AGILE, ASAS-SN, HAWC, H.E.S.S., INTEGRAL, Kanata, Kiso, Kapteyn, Liverpool, Subaru, Swift/NuSTAR, VERITAS and VLA teams; this record lists collaboration:icecube only.
result:icecube-txs-0506-056-multimesseng.summary_technical: The 290 TeV track alert IceCube-170922A was spatially coincident with the flaring gamma-ray blazar TXS 0506+056. A multiwavelength campaign across radio to VHE gamma rays characterised the flare, including the first VHE gamma-ray detection of the source.
result:icecube-txs-0506-056-multimesseng.why_it_matters: The abstract notes that individual astrophysical sources previously detected in neutrinos were limited to the Sun and the supernova 1987A, and that the origins of the diffuse flux of high-energy cosmic neutrinos remained unidentified; this neutrino-blazar coincidence "suggests that blazars may be a source of high-energy neutrinos".

claim.quote: Allowing for time-variable flux, this constitutes 3.5{\sigma} evidence for neutrino emission from the direction of TXS 0506+056, independent of and prior to the 2017 flaring episode.

result:icecube-txs-0506-056-prior-neutri.summary_technical: Archival time-dependent point-source search of 9.5 years of IceCube data at the position of TXS 0506+056 finds an excess between September 2014 and March 2015 at 3.5σ for a time-variable flux hypothesis.
result:icecube-txs-0506-056-prior-neutri.why_it_matters: The abstract says the 2014–2015 excess is independent of and prior to the 2017 flaring episode and that this suggests blazars are the first identifiable sources of the high-energy astrophysical neutrino flux.

claim.quote: The new IGEX exclusion contour enters, by the first time, the DAMA region by using only raw data, with no background discrimination, and excludes its upper left part.

result:igex-dm-improved-constraints-2001.summary_technical: 40 days of data from one IGEX detector (threshold about 4 keV): spin-independent WIMP-nucleon exclusion plot improving all other germanium ionization limits from 20 to 200 GeV and excluding the upper left part of the DAMA region.
result:igex-dm-improved-constraints-2001.why_it_matters: Among the first non-sodium-iodide experiments to test DAMA's favoured WIMP region directly.

claim.quote: A new exclusion plot has been derived for WIMP-nucleon spin-independent interaction. To obtain this result, 30 days of data from one IGEX detector, which has an energy threshold of ~4 keV, have been considered.

result:igex-dm-new-constraints-2000.summary_technical: Spin-independent WIMP-nucleon exclusion plot from 30 days of data of one IGEX detector (~4 keV threshold) that improves other germanium-diode limits around 50 GeV; an additional 1 kg yr with a moderately lower background would test the DAMA region.
result:igex-dm-new-constraints-2000.why_it_matters: Showed that detectors built for double-beta decay could also test the DAMA region.

claim.quote: Lower limits on the nucleon lifetime are set for a wide variety of proposed decay modes.

notes: The individual lifetime limits are in the paper's tables, which were not fetched, so no single key value is recorded. An earlier IMB paper, Phys. Rev. Lett. 61, 2522 (1988), gave 90% C.L. lower bounds of (0.6–46.0)×10³¹ yr for 23 decay channels; it is not cited here.
result:imb-3-nucleon-decay-limits-1999.summary_technical: IMB-3 (3.3 kton fiducial) 7.6 kton-year exposure, 935 contained events consistent with atmospheric-neutrino backgrounds; lower limits on the nucleon lifetime for a wide variety of decay modes.
result:imb-3-nucleon-decay-limits-1999.why_it_matters: APS News says IMB "quickly ruled out the Georgi-Glashow model and several other proton decay lifetimes".

claim.quote: Observation of a neutrino burst in coincidence with supernova 1987A in the Large Magellanic Cloud

notes: The IMB burst was found after Kamiokande announced its own 11 events (APS News); the two results are recorded as separate results of separate experiments.
result:imb-sn1987a-neutrino-burst-observ.summary_technical: A burst of eight neutrino events with visible energies of 20-40 MeV spanning 6 s, contained in the IMB water Cherenkov detector near the estimated time of core collapse, against a background of about 2 per day.
result:imb-sn1987a-neutrino-burst-observ.why_it_matters: APS: "this was the first time that neutrinos from a supernova were measured directly", and the measurements "became the starting point for the field of neutrino astronomy".

claim.quote: The first result of the dark matter direct search experiment named InDEx with tetra-fluoro-ethane active liquid from JUSL underground laboratory is reported in this article.

result:index-run1-2025.summary_technical: 500 ml C2H2F4 detector, effective 48.6 days at a 5.87 keV threshold, exposure 2.47 kg-days; minimum sensitivity for SI-nucleon on carbon at 22.81 GeV/c^2 and SD (p) on fluorine at 30.67 GeV/c^2; WIMP mass threshold 5.16 GeV/c^2 (F) and 4.44 GeV/c^2 (C).
result:index-run1-2025.why_it_matters: First result from an Indian underground dark matter direct search.
