claim.quote: For a runtime of 102.48 days, the experimental results set constraint on spin-independent at 20.4 GeV/c2 and on spin-dependent at 21.0 GeV/c2 WIMP mass respectively.

result:index-run2-2025.summary_technical: Run 2: thresholds of 1.95 keV, active liquid mass 70.4 g, runtime 102.48 days; the abstract states a shift of the most sensitive WIMP mass towards the lower region and an improvement over run 1.
result:index-run2-2025.why_it_matters: Second InDEx result, published in Phys. Rev. D.

claim.quote: Observation of planar three-jet events in e+e− annihilation and evidence for gluon bremsstrahlung

notes: The abstract of the Phys. Lett. B paper could not be retrieved; the claim is the paper title only.

Lett. B 91, 142 paper (issue date March 1980).
result:jade-planar-three-jet-observation.summary_technical: JADE paper 'Observation of planar three-jet events in e⁺e⁻ annihilation and evidence for gluon bremsstrahlung' (Phys. Lett. B 91 (1980) 142); first results and evidence for the observation of the gluon presented by S. Orito at the 9th Lepton/Photon Symposium (Batavia, 23 August 1979).
result:jade-planar-three-jet-observation.why_it_matters: Together with TASSO, MARK J and PLUTO, JADE's three-jet analysis established the gluon as the carrier of the strong force in 1979-80.

claim.quote: After applying all event selection criteria, two events are observed, consistent with the expected background of 2.3±0.4 events.

result:jsns2-first-sterile-search-2026.summary_technical: 2022 data: two events after all selection cuts, consistent with 2.3 +- 0.4 expected background; expected number from the LSND anomaly 1.1 +- 0.5, so the result is stated as not yet conclusive. Data taking continues; JSNS2-II adds a 48 m detector.
result:jsns2-first-sterile-search-2026.why_it_matters: The first result of a dedicated, independent re-test of the LSND short-baseline excess with the same oscillation channel, a different source and a Gd-loaded detector.

claim.locator: Chinese Physics C 50, 043001 (2026), article title; confirmed verbatim against arXiv:2511.14590 and INSPIRE literature id 3084402
claim.quote: Initial performance results of the JUNO detector

notes: DOI 10.1088/1674-1137/ae3dc1 confirmed on 2026-09-18 via INSPIRE-HEP (control_number 3084402) and the IOP DOI-resolved article page.

src:juno-cpc-initial-performance-2026 (cpc.ihep.ac.cn) renders as a JavaScript shell with no article text, so its excerpt quotes could not be checked against it directly (2026-09-18). The claim and value quotes cite src:reactor-solar-verify-juno-cpc-2026-arxiv, the arXiv preprint of the identical peer-reviewed paper (same title, same INSPIRE record, DOI-confirmed), whose full text was read directly.
result:juno-initial-performance-2026.summary_technical: Initial performance results for the JUNO central detector: liquid-scintillator attenuation length 20.6 m at 430 nm; about 1785 photoelectrons per MeV at the detector centre; energy resolution 3.4% for two 0.511 MeV gamma rays at the detector centre; energy nonlinearity calibrated to better than 1%; data-acquisition duty cycle above 97.8% during the initial science runs.
result:juno-initial-performance-2026.why_it_matters: The abstract reports a data-acquisition duty cycle above 97.8% during the initial science runs, which it says demonstrates the excellent stability and readiness of JUNO for high-precision neutrino physics; IHEP's news item says early data show the key performance indicators fully meet or surpass design expectations.

claim.quote: Measurement of reactor neutrino oscillation with the first JUNO data

notes: IHEP announced these results at a press conference on 2025-11-19 (src:juno-ihep-first-results-en), one day after the arXiv posting of 2025-11-18 and ahead of the 2026-06-10 Nature publication; `date` is the earliest public date (the preprint), `announced` and `published` carry the other two dates.
result:juno-oscillation-parameters-2026.summary_technical: First 59.1 days of data since detector completion in August 2025 (data from 26 August to 2 November 2025 per IHEP): the first simultaneous high-precision determination of sin²θ₁₂ = 0.3092 ± 0.0087 and Δm²₂₁ = (7.50 ± 0.12) × 10⁻⁵ eV² for the normal mass ordering scenario, improving the precision by a factor of 1.6 relative to the combination of all previous measurements.
result:juno-oscillation-parameters-2026.why_it_matters: The Nature abstract says the results advance the basic understanding of neutrinos, validate the design of the detector and indicate the readiness of JUNO for resolving the neutrino mass ordering with a larger dataset.

claim.quote: We present measurements of nu_mu disappearance in K2K, the KEK to Kamioka long-baseline neutrino oscillation experiment. ... The probability that the observations are explained by the expectation for no neutrino oscillation is 0.0015% (4.3sigma).

result:k2k-oscillation-measurement-2006.summary_technical: 112 beam-originated events observed in the Super-Kamiokande fiducial volume versus an expectation of 158.1 (+9.2/−8.6) without oscillation; a distortion of the energy spectrum is also seen in 58 single-ring muon-like events. The probability that the observations are explained by the expectation for no neutrino oscillation is 0.0015% (4.3σ). In a two-flavor scenario the allowed Δm² region at sin²2θ = 1 is between 1.9 and 3.5 × 10⁻³ eV² at the 90% CL, with a best-fit value of 2.8 × 10⁻³ eV².
result:k2k-oscillation-measurement-2006.why_it_matters: The paper says the K2K collaboration had previously reported evidence of neutrino oscillations in a man-made neutrino beam directed 250 km across Japan; this paper presents updated νμ disappearance measurements: 112 observed events against 158.1 expected without oscillation, a distorted energy spectrum, and an allowed Δm² region of 1.9 to 3.5 × 10⁻³ eV² at 90% CL.

claim.quote: Observation of a neutrino burst from the supernova SN1987A

notes: Classified as an observation to match the publication title (“Observation of a neutrino burst...”). The summary does not call it a first detection because none of the cited pages states that for this paper. The date is the PRL publication date; the burst itself was recorded on 23 February 1987.
result:kamiokande-sn1987a-1987.summary_technical: Kamiokande-II recorded a neutrino burst on 23 February 1987, 7:35:35 UT (±1 min), during a time interval of 13 s: 11 electron events of energy 7.5 to 36 MeV, of which the first two point back to the Large Magellanic Cloud with angles 18° ± 18° and 15° ± 27°. The paper title attributes the burst to supernova SN 1987A.
result:kamiokande-sn1987a-1987.why_it_matters: Kamiokande's own history page calls the February 1987 detection of supernova neutrinos in the Large Magellanic Cloud a major breakthrough. A 2018 IceCube abstract notes that individual astrophysical sources previously detected in neutrinos are limited to the Sun and the supernova 1987A.

claim.quote: First Results from KamLAND: Evidence for Reactor Anti-Neutrino Disappearance

notes: Published as Phys. Rev. Lett. 90, 021802 (2003); its DOI was not confirmed on any page consulted, so no DOI is given for the publication.
result:kamland-first-results-2002.summary_technical: In a 162 ton·yr (145.1-day) exposure, KamLAND measured a ratio of observed to expected reactor antineutrino events of 0.611 ± 0.085(stat) ± 0.041(syst) for E > 3.4 MeV; the deficit is inconsistent with the expected rate for standard ν̄e propagation at the 99.95% confidence level, and in the context of two-flavor neutrino oscillations with CPT invariance the results exclude all oscillation solutions but the 'Large Mixing Angle' solution to the solar neutrino problem.
result:kamland-first-results-2002.why_it_matters: In the context of two-flavor oscillations with CPT invariance, the first KamLAND data exclude every oscillation solution to the solar neutrino problem except the Large Mixing Angle solution, using reactor antineutrinos.

claim.quote: We report the observation of a steepening in the cosmic ray energy spectrum of heavy primary particles at about $8 \times 10^{16}$ eV.

result:kascade-grande-heavy-knee-2011.summary_technical: Independent measurements of charged-particle and muon numbers of air showers (10^16-10^18 eV), analysed event by event with their correlation, show a steepening of the heavy-primary spectrum at about 8 × 10¹⁶ eV; weaker in the all-particle spectrum.
result:kascade-grande-heavy-knee-2011.why_it_matters: The abstract says that, whereas the knee at 3-5 × 10¹⁵ eV was assigned to light primaries by KASCADE, the new structure found by KASCADE-Grande is caused by heavy primaries.

claim.quote: The resulting primary energy spectra show that the knee in the all particle spectrum is due to a steepening of the spectra of light elements

result:kascade-knee-light-elements-2005.summary_technical: Two-dimensional unfolding of the electron-muon number spectrum with QGSJet and SIBYLL simulations gives energy spectra of elemental groups; the all-particle knee is due to a steepening of the light-element spectra, and neither simulation set describes the data consistently over the whole energy range.
result:kascade-knee-light-elements-2005.why_it_matters: The abstract says the knee in the all-particle spectrum is due to a steepening of the light-element spectra, and also that neither of the two hadronic-interaction simulation sets describes the data consistently.

claim.quote: resulting in an upper limit of m_nu < 0.45 eV at 90% confidence level

result:katrin-neutrino-mass-upper-limit-.summary_technical: Based on the first five KATRIN neutrino-mass measurement campaigns, the best-fit value is m_ν² = −0.14 (+0.13/−0.15) eV², resulting in an upper limit m_ν < 0.45 eV at 90% CL. With six times the statistics of previous data sets (36 million electrons collected in 259 measurement days), a substantial reduction of the background level and improved systematic uncertainties, the result tightens KATRIN's previous bound by a factor of almost two.
result:katrin-neutrino-mass-upper-limit-.why_it_matters: The abstract notes that a non-vanishing neutrino rest mass is evidence of physics beyond the Standard Model and that the absolute mass bears importance from particle physics to cosmology. The KATRIN site gives the earlier Mainz and Troitsk upper limit as 2.3 eV/c².

claim.quote: We report results of experiments performed with the KEDR detector at the VEPP-4M $e^+e^-$ collider. They include final results for the mass and other parameters of the $J/\psi$, $\psi(2S)$ and $\psi(3770)$ and $J/\psi\to\gamma\eta_c$ branching fraction determination.

notes: The arXiv abstract gives no mass values; they are not recorded.
result:kedr-charmonium-parameters-measur.summary_technical: KEDR at VEPP-4M: final results for the mass and other parameters of J/ψ, ψ(2S) and ψ(3770) and the J/ψ → γη_c branching fraction; beam energy calibrated by resonant depolarisation. (KEDR's own page quotes M(J/ψ) and M(ψ′) as the most precise measurements, in the top ten for elementary-particle masses.)
result:kedr-charmonium-parameters-measur.why_it_matters: KEDR's home page says its J/psi and psi' masses entered the top ten most precise measurements of masses of elementary particles.

claim.quote: Using the KEDR detector at the VEPP-4M $e^+e^-$ collider, we have determined the values of $R$ at thirteen points of the center-of-mass energy between 1.84 and 3.05 GeV.

result:kedr-r-measurement-2016.summary_technical: KEDR at VEPP-4M: R at thirteen centre-of-mass energies between 1.84 and 3.05 GeV, accuracy about or better than 3.9% at most points with systematic uncertainty below 2.4%.
result:kedr-r-measurement-2016.why_it_matters: The abstract states the achieved accuracy and the systematic uncertainty of the R values.

claim.quote: In 1965, the first cosmic ray neutrino was observed in KGF by the Tata-Osaka-Durham group (Ref.3).

notes: Priority is shared: the CERN Courier obituary says the Kolar event was recorded 'contemporaneously with the detection from another underground neutrino experiment set up by Fred Reines in a South African mine'.
The primary 1965 paper could not be fetched, so the claim quote is the collaboration's own 2000 statement.
result:kgf-first-atmospheric-neutrinos-1.summary_technical: Seven neutrino telescopes at 2300 m depth recorded muons from atmospheric-neutrino interactions in early 1965, contemporaneously with Reines' South African mine experiment; the rate agreed with the calculated flux from pion, kaon and muon decays.
result:kgf-first-atmospheric-neutrinos-1.why_it_matters: The first observation of neutrinos from cosmic rays, which opened underground neutrino physics.

claim.quote: Deep underground in Kolar Gold Fields, in southern India, an experiment to detect proton decay had been carried out since the end of 1980. Analysis of data yielded the following results; (l) the life time of proton is about 1 x 1031 years,

notes: The collaboration acknowledges the conflict: "Contrary to this conclusion, as shown in our earlier reports (Ref. 9), our result is that protons are decaying with lifetime of about 10 31 years."
result:kgf-proton-decay-claim-2000.summary_technical: Combined Phase I and II analysis (about 13 years, mines closing in 1993): candidate fully contained events interpreted as p to e+ pi0 and p to anti-nu K+ decays with tau_p about 1e31 yr, in disagreement with lower limits of order 1e33 yr from other experiments, which the paper acknowledges; four possible neutron-oscillation events are also reported.
result:kgf-proton-decay-claim-2000.why_it_matters: A rare claimed signal of baryon-number violation, from the oldest proton-decay search. Langacker's 1992 review notes that no experiment has observed proton decay and that some candidate events could be neutrino interactions.

claim.quote: We report the first result on WIMP search obtained with 237 kg$\cdot$days data using one full-size CsI(T$\ell$)crystal of 6.6 kg mass.

result:kims-csi-first-limit-2005.summary_technical: First KIMS WIMP-search limit (Phys. Lett. B 633 (2006) 201) with one full-size CsI(Tl) crystal (6.6 kg, 237 kg d); internal background reduced and pulse-shape discrimination achieved.
result:kims-csi-first-limit-2005.why_it_matters: The first WIMP limit from a Korean underground experiment.

claim.quote: The DAMA signal region for both spin independent and spin dependent interactions for the WIMP mass higher than 20 GeV/c^2are excluded by the single experiment with crystal scintillators.

result:kims-csi-limits-2007.summary_technical: 3409 kg d with four CsI(Tl) crystals at 0 C; abstract: 'The most stringent limit on the spin dependent interaction for pure proton case is obtained' and the DAMA signal regions for WIMP masses above 20 GeV/c^2 are excluded (Phys. Rev. Lett. 99, 091301 (2007)). The abstract speaks of 'the DAMA signal', not of DAMA/LIBRA.
result:kims-csi-limits-2007.why_it_matters: The abstract states that the DAMA signal region is excluded by a single crystal-scintillator experiment (CsI(Tl), a different target from DAMA's NaI(Tl)).

claim.quote: The observed limit rejects most of the low mass region of parameter space favored by the DAMA annual modulation signal.

notes: The abstract gives 24,324.3 kg d; the 2012 paper on the same data set gives 24524.3 kg d (the difference is not adjudicated).
result:kims-csi-low-mass-2014.summary_technical: 24,324.3 kg d with a 2-4 keV visible-energy window; spin-independent WIMP-proton limits at 90% C.L. for WIMP masses <= 20 GeV/c^2; observed distribution consistent with null signals (Phys. Rev. D 90, 052006 (2014)).
result:kims-csi-low-mass-2014.why_it_matters: A direct statement in the abstract about the region favoured by DAMA's modulation signal.

claim.quote: we set a 90 \% confidence level upper limit on the axion-electron coupling, $g_{ae}$, of $1.39 \times 10^{-11}$ for an axion mass less than 1 keV/$\rm c^2$.

result:kims-csi-solar-axions-2016.summary_technical: 34,596 kg d of CsI(Tl) data; solar axions converting to electrons by the axio-electric effect; the limit is below the indirect solar-neutrino bound and fully excludes QCD axions heavier than 0.48 eV/c^2 (DFSZ) and 140.9 eV/c^2 (KSVZ).
result:kims-csi-solar-axions-2016.why_it_matters: A non-WIMP use of the KIMS data.

claim.quote: We establish the most stringent cross section limits on spin-dependent WIMP-proton elastic scattering for the WIMP masses greater than 20 GeV/c2.

result:kims-csi-spin-dependent-limits-20.summary_technical: 24524.3 kg d with 9 of 12 CsI(Tl) modules (alpha-emitter surface background identified and fitted); 90% upper limit of the nuclear-recoil rate for 3.6-5.8 keV (2-4 keV in NaI(Tl)) is 0.0098 counts/kg/keV/day, below the DAMA annual-modulation amplitude, which the abstract calls incompatible with interpretations that enhance the modulation such as inelastic dark matter (Phys. Rev. Lett. 108, 181301 (2012)).
result:kims-csi-spin-dependent-limits-20.why_it_matters: The abstract compares directly with the DAMA modulation amplitude.

claim.quote: These limits partially exclude the DAMA/LIBRA region of WIMP-sodium interaction with the same NaI(Tl) target detector. This 90% confidence level upper limit on WIMP-nucleon spin-independent cross section is 3.26*10^-4 pb for a WIMP mass at 10 GeV/c^2.

result:kims-nai-limits-2018.summary_technical: Two NaI(Tl) crystals, 2967.4 kg d (November 2013 - January 2015) at Y2L; pulse-shape analysis to extract nuclear recoils; 90% C.L. spin-independent limit 3.26e-4 pb at 10 GeV/c^2 (JHEP 03 (2019) 194).
result:kims-nai-limits-2018.why_it_matters: The first limit with the same target material as DAMA/LIBRA from the Korean NaI programme.

claim.quote: We present the analysis of a new data set corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 240 pb$^{-1}$. We have achieved a reduced systematic uncertainty with respect to previously published KLOE results.

notes: Chosen as KLOE's headline result because hadronic cross sections and the muon anomaly head the physics list in CERN Courier's 2018 summary; KLOE published several later updates of the same measurement.
result:kloe-pipi-muon-anomaly-measuremen.summary_technical: KLOE: σ(e⁺e⁻ → π⁺π⁻γ(γ)) with initial-state-radiation photons at small angle, inclusive of final-state radiation, from a new 240 pb⁻¹ data set with reduced systematic uncertainty; pion form factor and Δa_μ^ππ = (387.2 ± 0.5_stat ± 2.4_exp ± 2.3_th) × 10⁻¹⁰ for 0.592 < M_ππ < 0.975 GeV (Phys. Lett. B 670, 285).
result:kloe-pipi-muon-anomaly-measuremen.why_it_matters: The abstract gives the two-pion contribution to the muon magnetic anomaly obtained from the measured cross section; KLOE's hadronic cross sections are one of the stated physics outputs of the programme (CERN Courier).

claim.quote: The existence of a light dark force mediator has been tested with the KLOE detector at DAPHNE. This particle, called U, is searched for using the decay chain phi-->etaU, eta-->pi+pi-pi0, U-->e+e-. No evidence is found in 1.5 fb-1 of data.

notes: The arXiv listing credits the KLOE-2 Collaboration (author field); the data are KLOE data (1.5 fb^-1) and the result is attributed to experiment:kloe.
result:kloe-u-boson-search-limit-2011.summary_technical: KLOE: search for a light dark-force mediator U via φ → ηU, η → π⁺π⁻π⁰, U → e⁺e⁻ with 1.5 fb⁻¹: no evidence; exclusion for 5 < M_U < 470 MeV and α′/α ≤ 2×10⁻⁵ at 90% C.L. for 50 < M_U < 420 MeV.
result:kloe-u-boson-search-limit-2011.why_it_matters: CERN Courier lists searches for dark photons among the physics results of the KLOE data.

claim.quote: While the analysis of these datasets has not yielded statistically significant results, the developed methods provide a solid basis for future measurements with the KM3NeT detector.

notes: Added as an optional (non-mandatory) third result to give KM3NeT full flagship depth (2-4 results required; 3 provided). result_type 'limit' because the abstract reports upper limits and explicitly states no statistically significant excess was found.
result:km3net-arca-diffuse-flux-limit-20.summary_technical: Diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux search using KM3NeT/ARCA's first configurations (6, 8, 19, 21 active detection units; 640 days livetime): all-sky single-power-law fit φ₀ = 3.0(+2.1/−2.0)×10⁻¹⁸ GeV⁻¹ cm⁻² s⁻¹ sr⁻¹, γ = 3.00(+0.30/−0.35) at 68% credible level; no statistically significant results, upper limits derived for both the all-sky and Galactic Ridge searches.
result:km3net-arca-diffuse-flux-limit-20.why_it_matters: The abstract says upper limits are derived for the all-sky and Galactic Ridge analyses and compared with state-of-the-art measurements, and that the developed methods provide a solid basis for future measurements with the KM3NeT detector.

claim.quote: measured to be $\sin^2\theta_{23}= 0.51^{+0.04}_{-0.05}$, and $ \Delta m^2_{31} = 2.18^{+0.25}_{-0.35}\times 10^{-3}~\mathrm{eV^2} \cup \{-2.25,-1.76\}\times 10^{-3}~\mathrm{eV^2}$ at 68\% CL. The inverted neutrino mass ordering hypothesis is disfavoured with a p-value of 0.25.

claim.locator: Abstract, Nature 638, 376-382 (2025), as hosted on Europe PMC
claim.quote: We detect a muon with an estimated energy of 120-60+110 petaelectronvolts (PeV). ... the energy of this event is much larger than that of any neutrino detected so far.

notes: Describes the event KM3-230213A. Classified as an observation because the paper's title says 'Observation'.

Journal volume/issue (638/8050) and pages (376-382) are given by the Europe PMC record of the Nature paper (src:rv-r2-europepmc-km3net-nature-2025); nature.com redirects to a login wall, so the article itself was not read.
result:km3net-uhe-neutrino-observation-2.summary_technical: Single ultra-high-energy near-horizontal muon event (KM3-230213A), recorded on 2023-02-13 by KM3NeT/ARCA with 21 detection lines installed at the time; estimated muon energy 120 (−60/+110) PeV, produced most probably by a neutrino of even higher energy (about 220 PeV in the collaboration's estimate). The paper says the energy of this event is much larger than that of any neutrino detected so far. Published in Nature 638, 376-382 (2025).
result:km3net-uhe-neutrino-observation-2.why_it_matters: The abstract says the neutrino may have originated in a different cosmic accelerator than the lower-energy neutrinos, or may be the first detection of a cosmogenic neutrino produced by interactions of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays with background photons in the Universe.

claim.quote: We report on the final electroweak measurements performed with data taken at the Z resonance by the experiments operating at the electron-positron colliders SLC and LEP.

notes: The combination also includes SLD (SLC Large Detector), a fifth contributing experiment at the SLC; only the four LEP experiments are linked on this record.
result:lep-electroweak-precision-2006.summary_technical: ALEPH, DELPHI, L3, OPAL and SLD combination (Phys. Rept. 427, 2006, 257-454; arXiv:hep-ex/0509008): 17 million Z decays accumulated by ALEPH, DELPHI, L3 and OPAL at LEP and 600 thousand by SLD at SLC; cross-sections, forward-backward and polarised asymmetries; Z mass and width and couplings to fermions precisely measured; number of light neutrino species 2.9840 ± 0.0082. Electroweak radiative corrections beyond the running of the QED and QCD coupling constants are observed with a significance of five standard deviations and in agreement with the Standard Model; the largest Z-pole difference from the Standard Model expectation is the b-quark forward-backward asymmetry, at 2.8 standard deviations.
result:lep-electroweak-precision-2006.why_it_matters: The abstract says the results are compared to the predictions of the Standard Model, that the top-quark and W-boson masses predicted through radiative corrections are compared to the direct measurements, and that this provides a stringent test of the Standard Model.

claim.quote: A lower bound of 114.4 GeV/c2 is established, at the 95% confidence level, on the mass of the Standard Model Higgs boson.

result:lep-higgs-exclusion-2003.summary_technical: ALEPH, DELPHI, L3 and OPAL (the LEP Working Group for Higgs Boson Searches) combined 2461 pb⁻¹ of e⁺e⁻ data at centre-of-mass energies between 189 and 209 GeV in a likelihood test of the background and signal-plus-background hypotheses (Phys. Lett. B 565, 2003, 61-75; arXiv:hep-ex/0306033): a lower bound of 114.4 GeV/c² is established at the 95% confidence level on the mass of the Standard Model Higgs boson, and upper bounds are set on the HZZ coupling for various assumptions concerning the decay of the Higgs boson.
result:lep-higgs-exclusion-2003.why_it_matters: The abstract reports a lower bound of 114.4 GeV/c² at the 95% confidence level on the mass of the Standard Model Higgs boson, and upper bounds on the HZZ coupling for various assumptions concerning the decay of the Higgs boson.

claim.locator: ALEPH abstract, Phys. Lett. B 231, 519-529 (1989), printed p. 521
claim.quote: Within the constraints of the standard electroweak model, the number of light neutrino species is found to be Nν = 3.27 ± 0.30. This result rules out the possibility of a fourth type of light neutrino at 98% CL.

notes: This entity records the historic 1989 determinations of the number of light neutrino species; the final precision value (2.9840±0.0082, LEP+SLD, arXiv:hep-ex/0509008) is recorded separately as result:lep-electroweak-precision-2006 and is no longer used as this record's key_value (a review found it read as the 1989 result). date/date_kind reflect the 1989 papers.

The claim and the headline quote are the abstract of the ALEPH paper, read in the journal article itself (a scan; the number is checked against the printed page, whose abstract is on p. 521). The research-portal transcription of the same abstract (src:rv-r2-psu-aleph-nuspecies-1989) reads "this results rules out of the possibility", which the printed abstract does not. L3, DELPHI and OPAL used different titles for the same Z-lineshape analysis (see key_value_text).

Other 1989 abstracts (verbatim): L3 — "We also determined Γinvisible=0.567±0.080 GeV, corresponding to 3.42±0.48 number of neutrino flavors." (Phys. Lett. B 231, 509; https://collaborate.princeton.edu/en/publications/a-determination-of-the-properties-of-the-neutral-intermediate-vec/). DELPHI — "A two-parameter fit in the framework of the standard model yields for the number of light neutrino species Nν=2.4±0.4 (stat.) ±0.5 (syst.)" (Phys. Lett. B 231, 539; https://difusion.ulb.ac.be/vufind/Record/ULB-DIPOT:oai:dipot.ulb.ac.be:2013/116538/TOC). OPAL — "In the context of the standard model t these results imply 3.1 ± 0.4 neutrino generations." (Phys. Lett. B 231, 530; https://researchconnect.stonybrook.edu/en/publications/measurement-of-the-zsup0sup-mass-and-width-with-the-opal-detector/).
result:lep-three-neutrino-species-1989.summary_technical: ALEPH, DELPHI, L3 and OPAL each reported a number of light neutrino species from their 1989 Z-resonance measurements (Phys. Lett. B 231, 509-547): ALEPH Nν = 3.27 ± 0.30 within the constraints of the standard electroweak model ("rules out the possibility of a fourth type of light neutrino at 98% CL"); L3 3.42 ± 0.48 (from Γinvisible = 0.567 ± 0.080 GeV); DELPHI 2.4 ± 0.4 (stat) ± 0.5 (syst) from a two-parameter standard-model fit; OPAL 3.1 ± 0.4 in the context of the standard model. The final LEP+SLD combination, Nν = 2.9840 ± 0.0082, was published later (Phys. Rept. 427, 2006).
result:lep-three-neutrino-species-1989.why_it_matters: ALEPH's abstract states that its result rules out the possibility of a fourth type of light neutrino at 98% CL, within the constraints of the standard electroweak model. Fermilab's 2000 announcement of the tau neutrino says that in 1989 experimenters at CERN found proof that the tau neutrino is the third and last light neutrino of the Standard Model.

claim.quote: This is the first observation of $C\!P$ violation in the decay of charm hadrons.

result:lhcb-cp-violation-charm-observati.summary_technical: Measurement of the CP-asymmetry difference ΔA_CP between D⁰→K⁻K⁺ and D⁰→π⁻π⁺ decays using about 6 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV pp data; combined with previous LHCb results, ΔA_CP = (−15.4±2.9)×10⁻⁴, which the paper says differs from zero by more than five standard deviations. The paper states this is the first observation of CP violation in the decay of charm hadrons.
result:lhcb-cp-violation-charm-observati.why_it_matters: The paper says CP violation had been established in the K- and B-meson systems but that its observation in the charm sector had not been achieved despite decades of searches. It reports the result as consistent with, although in magnitude at the upper end of, Standard Model expectations (10⁻⁴ to 10⁻³), and says further measurements will help establish whether it is consistent with the Standard Model or indicates new dynamics in the up-quark sector.

claim.quote: Observation of the doubly charmed baryon $\Xi_{cc}^{++}$

result:lhcb-doubly-charmed-baryon-observ.summary_technical: A highly significant structure in the Λc⁺K⁻π⁺π⁺ mass spectrum is identified as the weakly decaying doubly charmed baryon Ξcc⁺⁺; the mass difference m(Ξcc⁺⁺)-m(Λc⁺) is measured to be 1334.94±0.72(stat)±0.27(syst) MeV/c², giving m(Ξcc⁺⁺)=3621.40±0.72±0.27±0.14 MeV/c².
result:lhcb-doubly-charmed-baryon-observ.why_it_matters: The quark model predicts doubly charmed baryons; in most calculations the Ξcc masses lie between 3500 and 3700 MeV/c², and the measured Ξcc⁺⁺ mass is 3621.40 MeV/c². The paper describes a longstanding puzzle: SELEX reported a Ξcc+ state at 3519 MeV/c², which FOCUS, BaBar, Belle and an earlier LHCb search did not find (the paper notes these null results do not exclude the original observations because the production environments differ).

claim.quote: Observation of $J/\psi p$ resonances consistent with pentaquark states in ${\Lambda_b^0\to J/\psi K^-p}$ decays

result:lhcb-pentaquark-observation-2015.summary_technical: Amplitude analysis of Λb⁰→J/ψK⁻p decays (3 fb⁻¹, 7 and 8 TeV pp collisions): a satisfactory fit of the J/ψ p mass spectrum needs two Breit-Wigner resonances, each with significance of more than 9 standard deviations, with masses 4380±8±29 MeV (width 205±18±86 MeV) and 4449.8±1.7±2.5 MeV (width 39±5±19 MeV). The preferred JP assignments are of opposite parity, with one state of spin 3/2 and the other 5/2. Interpreted as resonant states they must have minimal quark content ccuud.
result:lhcb-pentaquark-observation-2015.why_it_matters: Hadrons with more than the minimal quark content (qq̄ or qqq) were proposed by Gell-Mann in 1964 and by Zweig; the paper notes that past claimed observations of pentaquark states have been shown to be spurious, although there is at least one viable tetraquark candidate, the Z(4430)+. Resonances decaying strongly into J/ψ p must have a minimal quark content of ccuud.

claim.quote: Evidence for Neutrino Oscillations from the Observation of Electron Anti-neutrinos in a Muon Anti-Neutrino Beam

notes: Classified as evidence: the paper's own title, PRD 64, 112007 (2001), says 'Evidence'.
result:lsnd-antineutrino-appearance-evid.summary_technical: LSND search for ν̄μ→ν̄e oscillations with ν̄μ from μ+ decay at rest (the paper's introduction calls these the final results using all the data): a total excess of 87.9 ± 22.4 ± 6.0 events consistent with ν̄e p → e⁺ n scattering was observed above the expected background, corresponding to an oscillation probability of (0.264 ± 0.067 ± 0.045)%. In conjunction with other known limits, the paper says the data suggest oscillations in the 0.2–10 eV²/c⁴ Δm² range, indicating a neutrino mass greater than 0.4 eV/c².
result:lsnd-antineutrino-appearance-evid.why_it_matters: The paper notes that it is difficult to explain the solar neutrino deficit, the atmospheric neutrino anomaly and the LSND excess with only three flavours of neutrinos, so that a fourth, sterile neutrino has been proposed to explain all of the data.

claim.quote: At a WIMP mass of 50 GeV/c^2, WIMP-nucleon spin-independent cross sections above 2.2e-46 cm^2 are excluded at the 90% confidence level. When combined with the previously reported LUX exposure, this exclusion strengthens to 1.1e-46 cm^2 at 50 GeV/c^2.

notes: significance is null: this is an exclusion limit.
result:lux-complete-exposure-2016.summary_technical: WS2014-16 exposure of 3.35×10⁴ kg day (332.0 live days, 11 Sep 2014 - 2 May 2016) in a dual-phase xenon TPC with 250 kg of active mass, combined with the earlier WS2013 exposure. No evidence of WIMP nuclear recoils; spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross sections above 2.2 × 10⁻⁴⁶ cm² at 50 GeV/c² are excluded at 90% CL, strengthening to 1.1 × 10⁻⁴⁶ cm² when combined with the previously reported LUX exposure.
result:lux-complete-exposure-2016.why_it_matters: The paper reports the complete LUX exposure: no evidence of WIMP nuclear recoils, with roughly fourfold improvement in sensitivity for high WIMP masses relative to the collaboration's previous results.

claim.quote: allowing 90% confidence limits to be set on spin-independent WIMP-nucleon elastic scattering with a minimum upper limit on the cross section of 7.6 × 10⁻⁴⁶ cm² at a WIMP mass of 33 GeV/c²

notes: significance is null: this is an exclusion limit.
result:lux-first-wimp-search-2013.summary_technical: WS2013: 85.3 live days, 118 kg fiducial volume, April-August 2013. Data consistent with the background-only hypothesis; minimum 90% CL spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross-section upper limit 7.6 × 10⁻⁴⁶ cm² at 33 GeV/c². The paper reports the data to be in disagreement with low-mass WIMP signal interpretations of the results from several recent direct detection experiments.
result:lux-first-wimp-search-2013.why_it_matters: The paper states that its limit is a significant improvement over the sensitivities of earlier searches and that the LUX data are in disagreement with low-mass WIMP signal interpretations of the results from several recent direct detection experiments.

claim.quote: A profile-likelihood ratio analysis shows the data to be consistent with a background-only hypothesis, setting new limits on spin-independent WIMP-nucleon, spin-dependent WIMP-neutron, and spin-dependent WIMP-proton cross sections for WIMP masses above 9 GeV/c².

notes: significance is null: this is an exclusion limit, and the collaboration reports no significance for it.
The DOI of the journal version was not retrieved, so no DOI is given; the journal reference (Phys. Rev. Lett. 131, 041002 (2023)) comes from the arXiv record.
result:lz-first-wimp-search-2022.summary_technical: SR1: 60 live days, 5.5 t fiducial, 23 Dec 2021 - 11 May 2022. Data consistent with background only; spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross sections above 9.2 × 10⁻⁴⁸ cm² rejected at 90% CL at 36 GeV/c², with limits also set on spin-dependent WIMP-neutron and WIMP-proton couplings for WIMP masses above 9 GeV/c².
result:lz-first-wimp-search-2022.why_it_matters: This was LZ's first WIMP search (60 live days, 5.5 t fiducial mass); its most stringent limit is for spin-independent scattering at 36 GeV/c². In SURF's announcement of the result, LZ researchers reported that with the initial run 'LZ is already the world's most sensitive dark matter detector'.

claim.quote: Dark Matter Search Results from 4.2 Tonne-Years of Exposure of the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) Experiment

notes: significance is null: this is an exclusion limit.
Retrieval of the arXiv abstract for this paper was partial (the fetched rendering paraphrased parts of the abstract); claim.quote is therefore taken from the paper title, which was returned verbatim.
result:lz-ws2024-wimp-search-2024.summary_technical: WS2024: total exposure 4.2 ± 0.1 tonne-years from 280 live days, of which 3.3 ± 0.1 tonne-years and 220 live days are new, combined with the 60-live-day WS2022 exposure. A technique to tag 214Pb β-decay backgrounds is used for the first time, and enhanced recombination in 124Xe two-neutrino double electron capture decays is a noteworthy new background. No evidence for an excess over expected backgrounds; the strongest spin-independent exclusion is 2.2 × 10⁻⁴⁸ cm² at 40 GeV/c² (90% CL) and the best spin-independent median sensitivity is 5.1 × 10⁻⁴⁸ cm².
result:lz-ws2024-wimp-search-2024.why_it_matters: The paper combines a new 220 live-day exposure (WS2024) with the 60 live-day exposure of the first LZ result (WS2022), for 4.2 tonne-years in total, and reports world-leading constraints on spin-independent and spin-dependent WIMP-nucleon cross sections for masses of 9 GeV/c² and above. It features 214Pb β-decay tagging for the first time and identifies a new 124Xe double-electron-capture background.

claim.quote: A high-statistics measurement has been made of the process ... with the MAC detector at the SLAC storage ring PEP.

notes: The abstract (TeX markup on the APS page) also reports a ratio of axial-vector to vector couplings; only the asymmetry is recorded here.
result:mac-electroweak-muon-pairs-measur.summary_technical: MAC: high-statistics measurement of e⁺e⁻ → μ⁺μ⁻ at √s = 29 GeV; electroweak forward-backward charge asymmetry for about 16 000 events A_μμ = −0.063 ± 0.008 ± 0.002 (Phys. Rev. Lett. 55, 1831, 28 October 1985).
result:mac-electroweak-muon-pairs-measur.why_it_matters: The abstract reports the asymmetry as a test of electroweak effects in muon-pair production at PEP energies.

claim.quote: Here we report the detection of Very High Energy (VHE) gamma-ray emission from Crab Nebula above 80 GeV.

notes: No significance is recorded: the abstract states none.
result:mace-crab-first-light-2024.summary_technical: About 15 hours of low-zenith-angle data (November 2022 - February 2023): log-parabola spectrum with flux (3.46 +- 0.26 stat) x 10^-10 TeV^-1 cm^-2 s^-1 at 400 GeV, index 2.09 +- 0.06 stat; detection from 80 GeV to about 5 TeV; energy resolution about 34% at 80 GeV improving to about 21% above 1 TeV.
result:mace-crab-first-light-2024.why_it_matters: The paper presents the first-light results from the Crab Nebula for the newly commissioned telescope and notes that it is the only operational imaging Cherenkov telescope at such a high altitude.

claim.quote: The results are consistent for all the subsamples and indicate a flux deficit that depends on energy and path-length of neutrinos.

result:macro-atmospheric-nu-oscillation-.summary_technical: Final analysis of three atmospheric-neutrino event classes (rates, angular distributions, estimated energies): flux deficit depending on energy and path length; no-oscillation excluded at about 5 sigma, nu_mu to nu_tau fits all data, best two-flavour point sin^2(2 theta_m) = 1, delta m^2 = 0.0023 eV^2, independent of flux normalisation.
result:macro-atmospheric-nu-oscillation-.why_it_matters: The final, independent analysis of MACRO atmospheric-neutrino data at Gran Sasso: a flux deficit depending on energy and path length that favours nu_mu to nu_tau oscillation over no oscillation.

claim.quote: No candidates were detected and a 90% Confidence Level (C.L.) upper limit to the local magnetic monopole flux was set at the level of 1.4 × 10−16 cm−2 s−1 sr−1 .

result:macro-final-monopole-limit-2002.summary_technical: Combined scintillator, streamer-tube and track-etch searches, no candidates: 90 % CL upper limit 1.4e-16 cm^-2 s^-1 sr^-1 on the local GUT monopole flux for 4e-5 < beta < 1, the first direct-search limit well below the Parker bound over the whole range.
result:macro-final-monopole-limit-2002.why_it_matters: As the paper states, the first direct-search limit on grand-unified magnetic monopoles that lies well below the Parker bound over the whole velocity range where they are expected.

claim.quote: We derive an upper limit of m(νe ) ≤ 2.3 eV/c2 at 95% confidence level for the mass itself.

result:mainz-final-neutrino-mass-limit-2.summary_technical: Phase II final analysis of 1997-2001 tritium beta spectra: m²(νe) = (-0.6 ± 2.2 stat ± 2.1 syst) eV²/c⁴ and m(νe) ≤ 2.3 eV/c² (95% CL), ten times better signal-to-background than phase I.
result:mainz-final-neutrino-mass-limit-2.why_it_matters: A direct, model-independent limit on the electron-antineutrino mass from tritium beta decay; the paper names KATRIN as the follow-up experiment, and the Troitsk experiment reported a limit of similar size.

claim.quote: Evidence for Anomalous Lepton Production in ... Annihilation

notes: The paper title says "Evidence", so result_type is evidence; the tau was established as a lepton by later work (Perl Nobel lecture) and the 1995 Nobel Prize.
The SSRL history page says the tau was "discovered at SPEAR in 1976"; the paper is dated December 1975, used here.
result:mark-i-anomalous-lepton-evidence-.summary_technical: Mark I: e⁺e⁻ → e^± + μ^∓ + missing energy with no other charged particles or photons, mostly at or above 4 GeV centre-of-mass energy; the missing-energy and momentum spectra require at least two additional particles per event; 'we have no conventional explanation'. The Mark I authors suggested a pair of new particles of mass 1.6-2.0 GeV/c²; the interpretation as a heavy lepton (τ) was established over the following two years.
result:mark-i-anomalous-lepton-evidence-.why_it_matters: Martin Perl shared the 1995 Nobel Prize in Physics for the discovery of the tau lepton; SLAC's history calls it the third charged lepton after the electron (1897) and the muon (1937).

claim.quote: Discovery of a Narrow Resonance in ... Annihilation

notes: The paper title says "Discovery", so result_type is discovery; no sigma is quoted and the significance field says so.
The same resonance was found simultaneously at Brookhaven by S. Ting's group (fixed target); that experiment is not part of this record.
result:mark-i-psi-discovery-1974.summary_technical: Mark I: a very sharp peak in the cross section for e⁺e⁻ → hadrons, e⁺e⁻ and possibly μ⁺μ⁻ at a centre-of-mass energy of 3.105 ± 0.003 GeV, with an upper limit of 1.3 MeV on its full width at half-maximum (Phys. Rev. Lett. 33, 1406, 2 December 1974). The resonance, called ψ at SLAC and J at Brookhaven, is the bound state of a charm quark and its antiquark.
result:mark-i-psi-discovery-1974.why_it_matters: SLAC's own history says the discovery of this new quark (charm) served as convincing evidence that the quark substructure of matter was valid; Burton Richter shared the 1976 Nobel Prize in Physics for it with Samuel Ting.

claim.quote: Discovery of Three-Jet Events and a Test of Quantum Chromodynamics at PETRA

notes: result_type is discovery because the paper title says "Discovery"; the paper gives no sigma, so the significance field records the abstract wording.
result:mark-j-three-jet-discovery-1979.summary_technical: MARK-J analysis of the spatial energy distribution of e⁺e⁻ → hadrons at PETRA: the 'oblateness' variable describes the flat shape of the energy configuration; the data show three-jet structure, 'unambiguously observed for the first time', explained by QCD predictions for quark-antiquark production with hard non-collinear gluons (Phys. Rev. Lett. 43, 830, 17 September 1979).
result:mark-j-three-jet-discovery-1979.why_it_matters: The abstract states that the data can be explained by quantum chromodynamic predictions for quark-antiquark pairs accompanied by hard noncollinear gluons.

claim.quote: yielding an upper limit on the branching ratio of B($\mu^+\to e^+\gamma$) < $7.5 \times 10^{-13}$ (90% C.L.). The combination of this result and the limit obtained by MEG gives B($\mu^+\to e^+\gamma$) < $3.1 \times 10^{-13}$ (90% C.L.), which is the most stringent limit to date.

result:meg-ii-mu-to-e-gamma-limit-2024.summary_technical: Result from the first MEG II physics run (2021): no excess of events over the expected background, B(μ⁺→e⁺γ) < 7.5×10⁻¹³ (90% C.L.), with a median expected limit (sensitivity) of 8.8×10⁻¹³; combined with the limit obtained by MEG, B < 3.1×10⁻¹³ (90% C.L.), which the paper calls the most stringent limit to date. A ten-fold larger sample was being collected in 2022-2023 at the time of the paper.
result:meg-ii-mu-to-e-gamma-limit-2024.why_it_matters: MEG II is an upgrade of the MEG experiment that aims to improve the sensitivity to the μ⁺→e⁺γ branching ratio by one order of magnitude within the next few years (the paper's introduction); this is its first result.

claim.quote: a new upper limit on the branching ratio of this decay of $BR( \mu^{+} \rightarrow {\rm e^{+}} \gamma ) < 4.2 \times 10^{-13}$ (90\%\ confidence level) is established, which represents the most stringent limit on the existence of this decay to date.

result:meg-mu-to-e-gamma-limit-2016.summary_technical: Final results on the full 2009-2013 dataset (7.5×10¹⁴ stopped muons on target): no significant excess over the expected background; BR(μ⁺→e⁺γ) < 4.2×10⁻¹³ at 90% C.L., which the paper says is the most stringent limit on the existence of this decay to date.
result:meg-mu-to-e-gamma-limit-2016.why_it_matters: The paper's introduction says the Standard Model allows charged lepton flavour violating processes such as this only with extremely small branching ratios, even accounting for measured neutrino masses and mixing angles, so such decays are free from Standard Model physics backgrounds associated with processes involving hadronic states, and a positive signal would be unambiguous evidence for physics beyond the Standard Model.

claim.quote: the results are found to be consistent with the nominal electron neutrino rate expectations from the Booster Neutrino Beam and no excess of electron neutrino events is observed

notes: This 2021 multi-topology search targets the MiniBooNE low-energy excess (result:miniboone-low-energy-excess-2021) and found no corresponding excess of electron-neutrino events; the paper states that the MiniBooNE excess remains unexplained.
result:microboone-no-low-energy-excess-2.summary_technical: Three independent νe searches in the Booster Neutrino Beam (an exclusive search for two-body CCQE scattering, a semi-inclusive search for pionless events and an inclusive search): results consistent with the nominal νe rate expectations and no excess of νe events observed. The paper says this picture appears to disfavor an interpretation of MiniBooNE's excess as arising purely from an anomalously high rate of charged-current νe interactions, rejects the hypothesis that νe CC interactions are fully responsible for the excess at >97% CL for both the exclusive and the inclusive event classes, with the exception of the 1e0p0π selection (the least sensitive to a simple model of the MiniBooNE excess), and says the MiniBooNE excess remains unexplained.
result:microboone-no-low-energy-excess-2.why_it_matters: The paper says the multi-pronged search is aimed at investigating the as-yet unexplained low energy excess of electromagnetic activity observed by MiniBooNE. It concludes that its sensitive measurements are so far inconsistent with an electron-neutrino interpretation of the excess, while the excess itself remains unexplained.

claim.quote: An analysis of 7 years of Milagro data performed on a 10-degree angular scale has found two localized regions of excess of unknown origin with greater than 12 sigma significance.

result:milagro-10tev-excess-2008.summary_technical: Analysis of 7 years of data on a 10-degree angular scale finds two localized excesses of unknown origin above 12 sigma, both inconsistent with gamma-ray emission; one has a different energy spectrum from the isotropic cosmic-ray flux at 4.6 sigma, consistent with hard-spectrum protons with an exponential cutoff and the most significant excess near 10 TeV.
result:milagro-10tev-excess-2008.why_it_matters: The abstract says potential causes are explored but no compelling explanation is found.

claim.quote: The technique is used to detect TeV emission from the Crab nebula.

notes: The abstract gives no significance, so none is recorded; the 17 sigma Crab detection over the experiment's lifetime is from the later paper arXiv:1110.0409.
result:milagro-crab-background-rejection.summary_technical: A method to separate hadronic from electromagnetic air showers in Milagro, based on the ability to detect the energetic particles in an extensive air shower, is used to detect TeV emission from the Crab Nebula; the Crab flux is estimated with the spectral index assumed from HEGRA.
result:milagro-crab-background-rejection.why_it_matters: The abstract says that until then no background-rejection method had been used successfully in an air-shower array to detect a source of TeV gamma rays.

claim.quote: The TeV image shows at least one new source MGRO J2019+37 as well as correlations with the matter density in the region as would be expected from cosmic-ray proton interactions.

result:milagro-cygnus-region-2006.summary_technical: Spatial and flux measurements of TeV gamma-ray emission from the Cygnus Region: one new source MGRO J2019+37 and correlation with the matter density; the flux at about 12 TeV (excluding MGRO J2019+37) exceeds a conventional cosmic-ray production and propagation prediction.
result:milagro-cygnus-region-2006.why_it_matters: The abstract says the excess indicates hard-spectrum cosmic-ray sources and/or other TeV gamma-ray sources in the region.

claim.quote: This analysis shows that a $10^5$ rejection power is reachable for electron/recoil discrimination.

result:mimac-electron-recoil-discriminat.summary_technical: Multivariate analysis of experimental data from monochromatic neutron fields; electron-recoil rejection power 1e5 reachable; Monte-Carlo estimate 86.49 +/- 0.17% nuclear-recoil efficiency over the full energy range.
result:mimac-electron-recoil-discriminat.why_it_matters: Background rejection of this kind is what a directional gas detector needs to separate nuclear recoils from electrons.

claim.quote: Finding no significant excess of events in the direction of the Cygnus constellation, we set an upper limit on the spin-dependent WIMP-proton cross section of σSD−p < 6.65 × 10−36 cm2 at 90% confidence level.

result:mimac-first-directional-limits-20.summary_technical: Two chambers with effective exposures of 495.1 and 354.2 days; 30 mbar 50% i-C4H10 / 50% CHF3; BDT track selection and ON/OFF analysis on the galactic map with a moving kinematic cut; limit on the spin-dependent WIMP-proton cross section 6.65e-36 cm^2 (90% CL); the abstract does not state the WIMP mass.
result:mimac-first-directional-limits-20.why_it_matters: The title calls these the first directional limits from MIMAC. A preprint (arXiv v1, July 2026); not yet peer reviewed as far as the sources read show.

claim.quote: For the first time, a detector achieves the directional measurement of proton and carbon recoils with kinetic energies in the keV range without any restriction on the direction of the incoming particle.

result:mimac-kev-proton-carbon-direction.summary_technical: Three neutron fields; angular resolution better than 16 deg for proton recoils down to 4 keV and carbon recoils down to 5.5 keV kinetic energy; directional reach towards O(1 GeV) WIMP masses.
result:mimac-kev-proton-carbon-direction.why_it_matters: The abstract says this demonstrates that directional detection is around the corner for probing dark matter with masses down to O(1 GeV).

claim.quote: we report the first ionization energy and 3D track observations of nuclear recoils produced by the radon progeny.

result:mimac-radon-progeny-tracks-2015.summary_technical: Bi-chamber prototype at LSM (2012 and 2013 data sets): first ionization energy and 3D track measurement of nuclear recoils from radon progeny.
result:mimac-radon-progeny-tracks-2015.why_it_matters: The abstract says this shows the capability of the MIMAC detector and opens the possibility to explore the low-energy recoil directionality signature.

claim.quote: the first high-statistics measurement, to our knowledge, of the ν¯μp → μ+n cross-section from the hydrogen atom, using the plastic scintillator target of the MINERvA experiment, extracting FA from free proton targets and measuring the nucleon axial charge radius, rA, to be 0.73 ± 0.17 fm.

notes: The arXiv identifier for this paper was not retrieved; the DOI (from the OSTI record) is used as the publication reference.
result:minerva-axial-form-factor-2023.summary_technical: To the authors' knowledge the first high-statistics measurement of the ν̄μp→μ⁺n cross-section on hydrogen, using the plastic-scintillator target of MINERvA; it extracts the nucleon axial form factor F_A(Q²) from free proton targets, without the nuclear corrections that neutrino-deuterium extractions require, and gives the nucleon axial charge radius r_A = 0.73 ± 0.17 fm.
result:minerva-axial-form-factor-2023.why_it_matters: The abstract says the axial form factor had so far been extracted from neutrino-deuterium scattering, which requires uncertain nuclear corrections; the antineutrino-hydrogen scattering presented here can access it without the need for nuclear theory corrections and enables direct comparisons with lattice quantum chromodynamics computations.

claim.quote: The MiniBooNE experiment at Fermilab reports a total excess of $638.0 \pm 132.8$ electron-like events ($4.8 \sigma$) from a data sample corresponding to $18.75 \times 10^{20}$ protons-on-target in neutrino mode

notes: The collaboration's own wording is 'excess', never 'discovery' or 'observation'; result_type is 'anomaly' accordingly.

An earlier report (Phys. Rev. Lett. 121, 221801 (2018), arXiv:1805.12028, src:miniboone-prl-2018-excess) found a charged-current quasielastic νe excess of 381.2±85.2 events (4.5σ) in neutrino mode alone and 460.5±99.0 events (4.7σ) combined with antineutrino mode, with a smaller exposure; this record uses the 2021 combined/updated figure as the primary claim and cites the 2018 paper as a supporting source.
result:miniboone-low-energy-excess-2021.summary_technical: Neutrino-mode data (18.75×10²⁰ protons on target, a 46% increase over previously published results) and antineutrino-mode data (11.27×10²⁰ protons on target) show a total excess of 638.0 ± 132.8 electron-like events; the overall significance of the excess is 4.8σ, limited by systematic uncertainties, while its statistical significance is 12.2σ. Beam-timing and radius-distribution studies lead the collaboration to conclude that models of the excess based on entering and exiting photons are disfavored.
result:miniboone-low-energy-excess-2021.why_it_matters: The paper's introduction says LSND and MiniBooNE reported excesses of νe and ν̄e charged-current quasielastic events in νμ beams, and that exotic models beyond the three-neutrino paradigm, for example 3+N oscillation models with N additional sterile neutrinos, have been invoked to explain these anomalies.

claim.quote: ultimately a triplet lifetime of 3.480 $\pm$ 0.001 (stat.) $\pm$ 0.064 (sys.) $\mu$s was obtained, indicating ultra-pure argon. This is the longest argon triplet time constant ever reported.

notes: Technology measurement in gaseous argon during the cooling phase, not a dark matter search.
result:miniclean-gaseous-argon-triplet-l.summary_technical: Triplet lifetime of the scintillation light in cold gaseous argon (below 140 K, about 1.5 bar) from the February-April 2017 cold-gas run; the paper also studies the quenching of separate scintillation components.
result:miniclean-gaseous-argon-triplet-l.why_it_matters: The abstract reads the long lifetime as indicating ultra-pure argon.

claim.quote: Measurement of Neutrino and Antineutrino Oscillations Using Beam and Atmospheric Data in MINOS

result:minos-oscillation-measurement-201.summary_technical: Combined NuMI beam and atmospheric-neutrino analysis: |Δm²|=(2.41+0.09−0.10)×10⁻³ eV², sin²2θ=0.950+0.035−0.036 (identical ν/ν̄ assumption); separate antineutrino fit gives |Δm̄²|=(2.50+0.23−0.25)×10⁻³ eV², sin²2θ̄=0.97+0.03−0.08, using 37.88 kton-years of atmospheric data plus beam exposure.
result:minos-oscillation-measurement-201.why_it_matters: The paper notes that MINOS can separate neutrinos and antineutrinos event by event and, coupled with the world's only set of long-baseline accelerator antineutrino data, allows a comparison of the neutrino and antineutrino mass splittings, which it finds in excellent agreement: |Δm²| − |Δm̄²| = (0.12 +0.24 −0.26)×10⁻³ eV².

claim.quote: No evidence for $\nu_{\mu} \to \nu_{s}$ transitions is found and we set a world-leading limit on $\theta_{24}$ for values of $\Delta m^{2}_{41} \lesssim 1\,\mathrm{eV}^{2}$.

notes: experiment_ids lists experiment:minos only: the paper analyses 10.56×10²⁰ protons on target in the MINOS near and far detectors (1.04 km and 735 km baselines) and does not mention MINOS+.
result:minos-sterile-neutrino-limit-2016.summary_technical: Two-detector search for νμ→νs oscillations over 1.04 km and 735 km baselines using a νμ-dominated beam peaked at 3 GeV (10.56×10²⁰ POT) and a one-sterile-neutrino model, under the assumption that νe-νs mixing is negligible (|U_e4|²=0); no evidence for νμ→νs transitions is found, and the paper sets what it calls a world-leading limit on θ₂₄ for Δm²₄₁ ≲ 1 eV².
result:minos-sterile-neutrino-limit-2016.why_it_matters: The paper's introduction lists the LSND and MiniBooNE excesses, the reactor anomaly and the gallium-source deficit as anomalous oscillation signals that may potentially be reconciled with the three-flavor picture by adding one or more sterile neutrinos; this search found no evidence for νμ→νs transitions.

claim.quote: MOSCAB equipment, a geyser-concept bubble-chamber originally thought for the search of dark matter in the form of WIMPs, is employed for the detection of fast neutrons.

result:moscab-fast-neutron-detection-202.summary_technical: Operated background-free when the nucleation threshold for neutrons is above about 2.5 MeV; response studied with an AmBe source and Monte Carlo efficiency functions. A neutron-detection paper, not a dark matter result; recorded because it is the source for the move of the apparatus to LNGS.
result:moscab-fast-neutron-detection-202.why_it_matters: The abstract considers use for weak neutron sources in clean environments and for monitoring cosmic-ray variations.

claim.quote: First results obtained in a series of test runs taken in laboratory demonstrate that we have successfully built and tested a geyser-concept bubble chamber that can be used in particle physics, especially in dark matter searches

result:moscab-geyser-chamber-tests-2017.summary_technical: Detector paper: operating principles and technical solutions of the geyser bubble chamber, with 56 test runs (about 400 h live time) of a 2 L scale-up in May and June 2017 at Milano-Bicocca.
result:moscab-geyser-chamber-tests-2017.why_it_matters: The abstract says the team is ready to move underground for extensive data taking.

claim.quote: together the data yield a muon lifetime of tau_{mu}(MuLan) = 2196980.3(2.2) ps (1.0 ppm), thirty times more precise than previous generations of lifetime experiments.

result:mulan-detailed-report-2012.summary_technical: Detailed report: ~1.6 x 10^12 positrons with a magnetized ferromagnetic target (~4 kG) and a crystal quartz target (130 G); tau(MuLan) = 2196980.3(2.2) ps (1.0 ppm); G_F(MuLan) = 1.1663787(6) x 10^-5 GeV^-2 (0.5 ppm).
result:mulan-detailed-report-2012.why_it_matters: The abstract says the lifetime measurement yields the most accurate value of the Fermi constant and enables new precision studies of weak interactions via lifetime measurements of muonic atoms.

claim.quote: We report a measurement of the positive muon lifetime to a precision of 1.0 parts per million (ppm); it is the most precise particle lifetime ever measured.

result:mulan-fermi-constant-2010.summary_technical: Positive muon lifetime tau = 2196980.3(2.2) ps from more than 2 x 10^12 decays with two stopping-target configurations, more than 15 times more precise than any previous experiment; G_F(MuLan) = 1.1663788(7) x 10^-5 GeV^-2 (0.6 ppm); also used to extract the mu-p singlet capture rate and the induced pseudoscalar coupling g_P.
result:mulan-fermi-constant-2010.why_it_matters: The abstract says the muon lifetime gives the most precise value for the Fermi constant.

claim.quote: Measurement of the Positive Muon Anomalous Magnetic Moment to 0.46 ppm

result:muon-g-2-measurement-2021.summary_technical: First results of the Fermilab Muon g-2 Experiment: aμ(FNAL) = 116,592,040(54)×10⁻¹¹ (0.46 ppm), 3.3 standard deviations greater than the Standard Model prediction and in excellent agreement with BNL E821. Combined with previous measurements of both μ⁺ and μ⁻, the new experimental average is aμ(Exp) = 116,592,061(41)×10⁻¹¹ (0.35 ppm), which increases the tension between experiment and theory to 4.2 standard deviations.
result:muon-g-2-measurement-2021.why_it_matters: The paper compares the measured muon anomaly with the Standard Model prediction recommended by the Muon g−2 Theory Initiative: the Fermilab result alone is 3.3 standard deviations above it, and the new experimental average increases the tension between experiment and theory to 4.2 standard deviations.

claim.quote: Measurement of the Positive Muon Anomalous Magnetic Moment to 0.20 ppm

result:muon-g-2-measurement-2023.summary_technical: Run-2 and Run-3 data (collected in 2019 and 2020) with more than 4 times the number of positrons from muon decay than the previous result from 2018 data; the systematic error is reduced by more than a factor of 2. these data alone give aμ = 116,592,057(25)×10⁻¹¹ (0.21 ppm), and combined with the 2018 result aμ(FNAL) = 116,592,055(24)×10⁻¹¹ (0.20 ppm); the new experimental world average aμ(exp) = 116,592,059(22)×10⁻¹¹ (0.19 ppm) represents a factor of 2 improvement in precision.
result:muon-g-2-measurement-2023.why_it_matters: The paper's introduction says a precise measurement of the muon magnetic anomaly provides a stringent test of the Standard Model, whose prediction is made with high precision, and that any deviation between experiment and theory may be a sign of physics beyond the Standard Model.

claim.quote: Measurement of the Positive Muon Anomalous Magnetic Moment to 127 ppb

result:muon-g-2-measurement-2025.summary_technical: New data taken from 2020 to 2023 (over 2.5 times the total statistics of the previous results): aμ = 116,592,0710(162)×10⁻¹² (139 ppb) for the new datasets and 116,592,0705(148)×10⁻¹² (127 ppb) combined with the previous results; the new experimental world average, dominated by the measurements at FNAL, is aμ(exp) = 116,592,0715(145)×10⁻¹² (124 ppb). The paper says the measurements at FNAL have improved the precision on the world average by over a factor of four. Fermilab's announcement calls it the third and final result.
result:muon-g-2-measurement-2025.why_it_matters: Fermilab's announcement says the final result agrees with the published results from 2021 and 2023 but with a much better precision of 127 parts per billion, surpassing the original experimental design goal of 140 parts per billion.

claim.quote: Significant enhancement of the multiplicities of all observed strange particles relative to negative hadrons was observed in central S+S collisions

result:na35-strangeness-enhancement-s-s-.summary_technical: Lambda, anti-Lambda and K0s production in the NA35 streamer chamber at 200 GeV/nucleon: the multiplicities of all observed strange particles relative to negative hadrons are significantly enhanced in central S+S collisions compared with p+p and p+S; the Lambda polarisation in central S+S is compatible with zero up to pT = 2 GeV/c.
result:na35-strangeness-enhancement-s-s-.why_it_matters: Strangeness enhancement was a predicted signature of quark-gluon plasma; the 2026 SPS reviews describe this NA35 result as the first indication of QGP formation at the CERN SPS.

claim.quote: This feature, observed for the first time, is in agreement with predictions from quark-gluon plasma formation, although alternative explanations by hadronic effects cannot be ruled out at this stage.

result:na38-jpsi-transverse-energy-depen.summary_technical: Oxygen-uranium collisions at 200 GeV/nucleon show a significant transverse-energy dependence of the J/psi yield relative to muon pairs in the mass continuum; observed for the first time, in agreement with predictions from quark-gluon plasma formation although alternative explanations by hadronic effects cannot be ruled out.
result:na38-jpsi-transverse-energy-depen.why_it_matters: Started the J/psi suppression programme that NA50 and NA60 continued; the 2026 SPS review calls NA38's J/psi suppression report at Quark Matter 1987 a highlight of the first round of SPS measurements.

claim.quote: we are able to deduce a value of about 120 MeV for the temperature at thermal freeze-out

result:na44-particle-production-central-.summary_technical: Single-particle inclusive spectra of pi+-, K+-, p and anti-p versus transverse mass near mid-rapidity in central 158A GeV/c Pb+Pb: the mass dependence of the mT distributions gives about 120 MeV for the thermal freeze-out temperature; the rapidity-density ratios give light- and strange-quark chemical potentials and a chemical freeze-out temperature of approximately 140 MeV.
result:na44-particle-production-central-.why_it_matters: Part of NA44's measurement of collective (radial) flow and freeze-out, which the 2026 SPS review calls probably the most important NA44 contribution to the field.

claim.quote: A non-monotonic energy dependence of the ratio of K^+ to pi^+ yields is observed, with a maximum close to 40 AGeV

result:na49-pion-kaon-energy-dependence-.summary_technical: Charged pion and kaon production in central Pb+Pb at 40, 80 and 158 AGeV: mean pion multiplicity per wounded nucleon rises approximately linearly with s_NN^1/4 with a change of slope in the 15-40 AGeV region; pion suppression turns into enhancement near 40 AGeV; K+/pi+ shows a maximum close to 40 AGeV.
result:na49-pion-kaon-energy-dependence-.why_it_matters: First report of the 'horn' in the K+/pi+ ratio that later became a key signature of the onset of deconfinement.

claim.quote: The change is compatible with the prediction that the threshold for production of a state of deconfined matter at the early stage of the collisions is located at low SPS energies.

result:na49-pion-kaon-onset-of-deconfine.summary_technical: Charged pion and kaon yields and transverse-mass spectra in central Pb+Pb at 20A and 30A GeV compared with higher and lower energies: a rapid change of the energy dependence around 30A GeV for the yields and the shape of the transverse-mass spectra, compatible with the predicted threshold for deconfined matter at the early stage of the collisions.
result:na49-pion-kaon-onset-of-deconfine.why_it_matters: Located the low-energy edge of the quark-gluon-plasma region, motivating the NA61/SHINE scan and the future facilities (FAIR, NICA) that explore baryon-rich matter.

claim.quote: While the Drell-Yan production exhibits the normal expected behaviour, the yield of J/ψ in Pb-Pb interactions is abnormally low, as it lies 9 standard deviations below the expected value.

notes: Typed as an anomaly (abnormal suppression relative to normal nuclear absorption), not a discovery of quark-gluon plasma; the 1997 abstract does not make that claim.
result:na50-anomalous-jpsi-suppression-p.summary_technical: Comparison of the Drell-Yan and J/psi cross sections in Pb-Pb at 158 GeV/c per nucleon with values extrapolated from proton and light-ion reactions: normal Drell-Yan, but J/psi abnormally low (9 sigma below the expected value) with a departure growing from peripheral to central collisions.
result:na50-anomalous-jpsi-suppression-p.why_it_matters: The suppression of the J/psi was predicted as a signature of quark-gluon plasma, so the anomalous suppression was a key piece of the evidence CERN announced in February 2000.

claim.quote: this new measurement confirms our previous observation that the (J/psi)/Drell-Yan cross-sections ratio departs from the normal nuclear absorption pattern for semi-central Pb-Pb collisions

result:na50-jpsi-suppression-pb-pb-2000-.summary_technical: J/psi production in Pb-Pb at 158 GeV/nucleon from the year-2000 data sample taken with the target system in vacuum: the (J/psi)/Drell-Yan ratio in the most peripheral collisions matches the nuclear absorption pattern from proton-nucleus data, and departs from it for semi-central collisions, decreasing persistently with centrality.
result:na50-jpsi-suppression-pb-pb-2000-.why_it_matters: Closed the question whether the apparent suppression in peripheral collisions was due to interactions in air, supporting the anomalous-suppression pattern.

claim.quote: The K^0_S and Lambda R_CP(p_T) are similar in shape to those measured at sqrt{s_NN} = 200 GeV at RHIC, though they are larger in absolute value.

result:na57-central-to-peripheral-nuclea.summary_technical: Central-to-peripheral nuclear modification factors R_CP(pT) for K0s, Lambda, anti-Lambda and negatively charged particles at central rapidity in Pb-Pb at the top SPS energy, covering the 55% most central collisions; shape similar to 200 GeV RHIC measurements but larger in absolute value; K0s R_CP compared with a theoretical calculation.
result:na57-central-to-peripheral-nuclea.why_it_matters: Connects the SPS strangeness programme with the jet-quenching observables measured at RHIC and the LHC.

claim.quote: For collisions involving more than ~80 participant nucleons, we find that an extra suppression is present.

result:na60-jpsi-in-in-suppression-2007.summary_technical: J/psi centrality distribution in In-In at 158 GeV/nucleon compared with cold-nuclear-matter absorption alone: for collisions with more than ~80 participant nucleons an extra suppression is present, in qualitative agreement with the previous NA50 Pb-Pb measurements though no theory coherently describes both.
result:na60-jpsi-in-in-suppression-2007.why_it_matters: Tests whether the anomalous J/psi suppression seen in Pb-Pb is a function of collision geometry or system size.

claim.quote: A significant excess of pairs is observed above the yield expected from neutral meson decays.

result:na60-rho-spectral-function-in-in-.summary_technical: Precision measurement of low-mass muon pairs in 158 AGeV In-In: an excess above neutral-meson decays isolated in a 360000-dimuon sample with about 2% mass resolution, consistent with pi+pi- -> rho -> mu+mu-; the space-time averaged rho spectral function shows strong broadening with essentially no mass shift.
result:na60-rho-spectral-function-in-in-.why_it_matters: Distinguishes in-medium broadening from dropping-mass scenarios of chiral symmetry restoration, a key test for thermal dilepton radiation.

claim.quote: The NA61/SHINE collaboration studies at the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) the onset of deconfinement in hadronic matter by the measurement of particle production in collisions of nuclei with various sizes at a set of energies covering the SPS energy range.

result:na61-shine-bebe-pion-production-e.summary_technical: Spectra and mean multiplicities of pi- in 7Be+9Be collisions at beam momenta 19A, 30A, 40A, 75A and 150A GeV/c, compared with models and with p+p and Pb+Pb data in the energy scan of the onset of deconfinement.
result:na61-shine-bebe-pion-production-e.why_it_matters: Together with p+p and central Pb+Pb data, the system-size scan locates the changes in energy dependence interpreted as the onset of deconfinement.

claim.quote: These data are required to improve predictions of the neutrino flux for the T2K long baseline neutrino oscillation experiment in Japan.

result:na61-shine-pc-31gev-cross-section.summary_technical: Interaction cross sections and charged-pion spectra in p+C at 31 GeV/c from the first NA61/SHINE run (2007, graphite target of 4% of an interaction length): p+C inelastic and production cross sections of 257.2 ± 1.9 ± 8.9 mb and 229.3 ± 1.9 ± 9.0 mb, and inclusive pion production cross sections.
result:na61-shine-pc-31gev-cross-section.why_it_matters: Hadron-production data on the same targets as the neutrino beam line directly reduce the flux uncertainty of the T2K long-baseline neutrino oscillation experiment.

claim.quote: With results from data collected between 2016 and 2022, the analysis gives ${\rm B}_{\rm 2016-2024}(K^+\to\pi^+\nu\bar{\nu}) = \left(9.6^{+1.9}_{-1.8}\right)\times10^{-11}$, corresponding to a relative precision of $20\%$.

notes: Sourced to arXiv:2607.16413 (CERN-EP-2026-214, submitted 17 July 2026), 'Measurement of the branching ratio of the K+ -> pi+ nu nubar decay', which restates the (9.6+1.9−1.8) × 10⁻¹¹ central value first announced at the 2026 La Thuile conference. The earlier CERN news article about the conference talk is cited only as corroboration.

An intermediate conference-proceedings preprint, arXiv:2604.12649 ('New measurement of K+ -> pi+ nu nubar branching ratio at the NA62 experiment', submitted 14 April 2026), also restates this value from a preliminary analysis; the later, full measurement paper arXiv:2607.16413 is used instead as the primary claim source.
As of 2026-09-17 arXiv:2607.16413 has no journal DOI yet (CERN preprint report number CERN-EP-2026-214); publication.doi is left null rather than guessed.
result:na62-2026-refined-measurement.summary_technical: Branching ratio B(K⁺→π⁺νν̄) from the 2023-2024 data: (7.2 +2.3 −2.1)×10⁻¹¹; with the results from data collected between 2016 and 2022 the analysis gives B_2016-2024 = (9.6 +1.9 −1.8)×10⁻¹¹, a relative precision of 20%, which the paper says is consistent with Standard Model predictions. CERN's news item on the La Thuile presentation gives the uncertainty as 40% smaller than before.
result:na62-2026-refined-measurement.why_it_matters: CERN's news item says the branching ratio of this decay can be predicted theoretically with a very high degree of precision, so the decay is extremely sensitive to new physics beyond the Standard Model; the paper says the updated value is consistent with Standard Model predictions.

claim.quote: Measurement of the very rare $K^+\rightarrowπ^+ν\barν$ decay

result:na62-jhep-2021-measurement.summary_technical: Branching-ratio measurement of K⁺ → π⁺ ν ν̄ from the 2016-2018 NA62 data set: BR = (10.6+4.0−3.4|stat ± 0.9syst)×10⁻¹¹ at 68% CL, based on 20 signal candidates with an expected background of 7.0 events; the paper says this provides evidence for the decay, observed with a significance of 3.4σ.
result:na62-jhep-2021-measurement.why_it_matters: The abstract says the measurement provides evidence for the very rare K⁺→π⁺νν̄ decay and gives a single event sensitivity of (0.839 ± 0.054)×10⁻¹¹, corresponding to 10.0 events assuming the Standard Model branching ratio of (8.4 ± 1.0)×10⁻¹¹.

claim.quote: Observation of the $K^{+}\rightarrowπ^{+}ν\barν$ decay and measurement of its branching ratio

result:na62-jhep-2025-observation.summary_technical: Observation of K⁺ → π⁺ ν ν̄ (significance above 5σ; background-only p-value 2×10⁻⁷): B(K⁺ → π⁺ ν ν̄) = (13.0+3.3−3.0)×10⁻¹¹ combining 2016-2022 data, including the 2021-2022 data taken at higher beam intensity after modifications to the beamline and detectors; 51 signal candidates with an expected background of 18(+3/−2) events. The paper says the decay becomes the smallest branching ratio measured with a signal significance above 5σ.
result:na62-jhep-2025-observation.why_it_matters: The paper's introduction quotes Standard Model branching-ratio predictions of (8.4 ± 1.0)×10⁻¹¹ (from tree-level CKM inputs) and (7.86 ± 0.61)×10⁻¹¹ (from a full CKM parameter fit), with an intrinsic theoretical uncertainty of approximately 3%; the measured branching ratio is (13.0 +3.3 −3.0)×10⁻¹¹.

claim.quote: No signal associated with nuclear recoils from WIMP interactions was observed in any run with any crystal. This allowed us to set upper limits on the WIMP-nucleon spin-independent and WIMP-proton spin-dependent cross-sections.

result:naiad-final-limits-2005.summary_technical: 44.9 kg yr from 2 encapsulated and 4 unencapsulated NaI(Tl) crystals, pulse shape discrimination; the abstract states 'The NAIAD experiment has so far imposed the most stringent constraints on the spin-dependent WIMP-proton cross-section.'
result:naiad-final-limits-2005.why_it_matters: Final NaIAD results; a NaI target is the same technique as DAMA's, here with pulse-shape discrimination.

claim.quote: Data accumulated by four of them (10.6 kg x year exposure) have been used to set upper limits on the WIMP-nucleon spin-independent and WIMP-proton spin-dependent cross-sections.

result:naiad-first-limits-2003.summary_technical: 10.6 kg x year exposure from four crystals (six collecting data at the time of publication); pulse shape analysis to discriminate nuclear from electron recoils.
result:naiad-first-limits-2003.why_it_matters: First NaIAD limits; the paper also describes the detector.

claim.quote: We therefore derive a lower limit on the half-life of 0νββ decays in 100 Mo of T1/2 (0νββ) > 1.1 × 10^24 yr at the 90% Confidence Level

result:nemo-3-mo100-final-limit-2015.summary_technical: Full data set, live time 4.96 yr, exposure 34.3 kg y of 100Mo; background in [2.8-3.2] MeV 0.44 +- 0.13 counts/yr/kg, no events in [3.2-10] MeV; T1/2 > 1.1e24 yr (90 % C.L., light Majorana neutrino exchange); <m_nu> < 0.33-0.62 eV.
result:nemo-3-mo100-final-limit-2015.why_it_matters: The final result of the experiment that led to the SuperNEMO tracker-calorimeter design.

claim.quote: we obtain a 95% C.L. excluded region of $0.1<|\Delta m_{41}^2|<7$\,eV$^2$

result:neos-reno-joint-sterile-search-20.summary_technical: Reactor-model-independent comparison of 2509 days of RENO near-detector data with 180 days of NEOS data (baselines 294 m and 24 m): 95 % CL exclusion of 0.1 < |delta m^2_41| < 7 eV^2 and a 68 % CL allowed region at |delta m^2_41| = 2.41 +- 0.03 eV^2, sin^2(2 theta_14) = 0.08 +- 0.03 (p = 8.2 %).
result:neos-reno-joint-sterile-search-20.why_it_matters: A nearly flux-model-independent short-baseline sterile-neutrino search using two detectors at one commercial reactor complex.

claim.quote: It is found to be consistent with no oscillation.

result:neos-sterile-neutrino-search-2017.summary_technical: Spectral shape of 1976 IBD events/day (S/B ~ 22) consistent with no oscillation; excess near 5 MeV prompt energy as in longer-baseline experiments; sin^2(2 theta_14) below 0.1 for 0.2 < delta m^2_41 < 2.3 eV^2 and the RAA optimum excluded at > 90 % CL.
result:neos-sterile-neutrino-search-2017.why_it_matters: An early short-baseline test of the sterile-neutrino explanation of the reactor antineutrino anomaly at a commercial reactor.

claim.quote: We observed the oscillation effect at CL $3.5\sigma$ in the vicinity of $\Delta m^2_{14} \approx 7.26\textrm{eV}^2$ and $\sin^2 2\theta_{14} \approx 0.38$.

notes: Disfavoured by PROSPECT (arXiv:2406.10408), whose abstract says the Neutrino-4 best-fit point is ruled out at more than five standard deviations.
result:neutrino-4-first-oscillation-effe.summary_technical: Model-independent coherent addition of measurements over 6-12 m: oscillation effect at 3.5 sigma near delta m^2_14 ~ 7.26 eV^2, sin^2(2 theta_14) ~ 0.38; combined with the gallium anomaly sin^2(2 theta_14) ~ 0.35 +- 0.07 (5 sigma).
result:neutrino-4-first-oscillation-effe.why_it_matters: The only reactor-experiment claim of a sterile-neutrino signal; it motivated the PROSPECT, STEREO, DANSS and other tests.

claim.quote: we can conclude that at currently available statistical accuracy we observe the oscillations at the $2.9\sigma$ level

result:neutrino-4-results-2021.summary_technical: All Neutrino-4 data 2016-2021: oscillations at the 2.9 sigma level with delta m^2_14 = (7.3 +- 1.17) eV^2 and sin^2(2 theta_14) = 0.36 +- 0.12 (stat); Monte Carlo estimate 2.7 sigma.
