result:neutrino-4-results-2021.why_it_matters: The collaboration's final published statement of its claimed sterile-neutrino signal.

claim.quote: improved spin-dependent weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP)-proton cross section limits by a direction-sensitive method were achieved including a new record of 5400 pb for 150 GeV/c2 WIMPs

result:newage-0-3a-first-underground-201.summary_technical: NEWAGE-0.3a, CF4 at 152 Torr, 20x25x31 cm^3 fiducial volume (0.0115 kg), exposure 0.524 kg d (2008-09-11 to 2008-12-04): spin-dependent WIMP-proton limit 5400 pb at 150 GeV/c^2 (direction-sensitive method).
result:newage-0-3a-first-underground-201.why_it_matters: The abstract calls 5400 pb a new record for a direction-sensitive method at the time.

claim.quote: Thus a 90% confidence level upper limit on Spin-Dependent WIMP-proton cross section of 50 pb for a WIMP mass of 100 GeV/c2 was derived. This limit is the most stringent yet obtained from direction-sensitive dark matter search experiments.

result:newage-0-3b-double-prime-2021.summary_technical: NEWAGE-0.3b'' with the low-alpha mu-PIC, 2018, 107.6 live days = 1.1 kg d: two events in 50-60 keV against 2.5 expected background; no significant forward-backward asymmetry; 90% CL spin-dependent WIMP-proton limit 50 pb at 100 GeV/c^2.
result:newage-0-3b-double-prime-2021.why_it_matters: The abstract calls it the most stringent limit yet from direction-sensitive searches (as of 2021).

claim.quote: A 90 % confidence level upper limit on spin-dependent WIMP-proton cross section of $4.3 \times10^{2}$ pb for WIMPs with the mass of 150 GeV/$c^2$ is obtained.

result:newage-0-3b-prime-3d-vector-2020.summary_technical: NEWAGE-0.3b', July 2013 to August 2017 (Run14-Run18), 434.85 live days = 4.51 kg d: first directional search with 3D tracking and head-tail sensitivity (3d-vector analysis); 90% CL spin-dependent WIMP-proton limit 4.3e2 pb at 150 GeV/c^2.
result:newage-0-3b-prime-3d-vector-2020.why_it_matters: The abstract describes it as the first directional dark matter search with three-dimensional tracking with head-tail sensitivity.

claim.quote: No significant non-isotropic signal from the directional analysis was found and a 90% confidence level upper limit on spin-dependent WIMP-proton cross section of 25.7 pb for WIMP mass of 150 GeV/c2 was derived.

result:newage-3d-vector-2023.summary_technical: NEWAGE-0.3b'' (LAmu-PIC), December 2017 to March 2020, 318.0 live days = 3.18 kg d; new gamma-ray rejection (TOTsum-Length cut) and head-tail analysis; no significant non-isotropic signal; 90% CL spin-dependent WIMP-proton limit 25.7 pb at 150 GeV/c^2.
result:newage-3d-vector-2023.why_it_matters: The abstract calls this the most stringent upper limit in direction-sensitive dark matter searches (as of 2023).

claim.quote: set the first limit on the spin-dependent WIMP (Weakly Interacting Massive Particles)-proton cross section by a direction-sensitive method

notes: Surface laboratory (not Kamioka): the facility is not recorded on this result.
result:newage-surface-laboratory-limit-2.summary_technical: 150 Torr CF4 micro-TPC; surface-laboratory (not underground) run; first direction-sensitive limit on the spin-dependent WIMP-proton cross section. The abstract does not state a numerical limit.
result:newage-surface-laboratory-limit-2.why_it_matters: The abstract calls it the first limit set by a direction-sensitive method; it showed a WIMP search with a gaseous tracking device can set limits.

claim.quote: The application of the developed method to a sample exposed at the INFN Gran Sasso surface laboratory provided the first measurement of sub-MeV environmental neutrons

result:newsdm-environmental-neutron-gran.summary_technical: Nano Imaging Tracker emulsion with topological analysis of proton recoils; scanning speed 250 g/year/machine; 880 keV neutron calibration; first measurement of sub-MeV environmental neutrons at the INFN Gran Sasso surface laboratory.
result:newsdm-environmental-neutron-gran.why_it_matters: The abstract notes that neutrons are often an irreducible background for dark matter searches.

claim.quote: We have conducted for the first time a directional dark matter search in an unshielded location, at the sea level, by keeping an emulsion detector exposed for 39 days on an equatorial telescope mount.

notes: Surface exposure at Nagoya University, not at LNGS: no facility recorded on this result.
result:newsdm-first-directional-emulsion.summary_technical: Emulsion exposure equivalent to 0.59 g d, unshielded, at sea level (Nagoya); angular distribution agrees with the background model; exclusion in the mass-cross-section plane; the first direction-sensitive search with a solid-state tracking detector.
result:newsdm-first-directional-emulsion.why_it_matters: The abstract says it is the first direction-sensitive search for dark matter with a solid-state, particle tracking detector.

claim.quote: The updated lifetime is $\tau_n = (887.7 \pm 1.2 [\textrm{stat}] \pm 1.9 [\textrm{syst}])$ s.

result:nist-bl1-neutron-lifetime-2013.summary_technical: Direct calibration of the 6Li neutron monitor against a totally absorbing detector to 0.057% (five-fold improvement), without nuclear-data cross sections; the 2005 result 886.3 ± 1.2 stat ± 3.2 syst s becomes tau_n = 887.7 ± 1.2 stat ± 1.9 syst s.
result:nist-bl1-neutron-lifetime-2013.why_it_matters: The abstract says the dominant uncertainty of the 2005 beam measurement was the absolute neutron fluence (2.7 s), which this work reduces.

claim.quote: We demonstrate that charge exchange with molecular hydrogen can occur with trapped protons, and we determine the efficiency with which the molecular hydrogen ions in the trap are detected.

result:nist-bl2-molecular-hydrogen-2025.summary_technical: Measurements in the BL2 proton-trap apparatus (data July 2018 - October 2020) of the production and detection of molecular hydrogen ions via charge exchange with trapped protons and their detection efficiency; the BL1 lifetime result is unlikely to have been significantly affected.
result:nist-bl2-molecular-hydrogen-2025.why_it_matters: The abstract says the influence of molecular hydrogen is of particular interest because of its ubiquitous presence in ultrahigh vacuum systems and could introduce systematic error in a beam lifetime experiment.

claim.quote: The "blind analysis" of all topologies yields no evidence for an oscillation signal.

result:nomad-final-oscillation-limits-20.summary_technical: Full-statistics nu_tau appearance search with a new unified analysis of hadronic tau decays and a blind analysis of all topologies: no oscillation signal; 90 % CL region includes sin^2(2 theta) < 3.3e-4 at large delta m^2 and delta m^2 < 0.7 eV^2/c^4 at maximal mixing (nu_mu -> nu_tau); sin^2(2 theta) < 1.5e-2 and delta m^2 < 5.9 eV^2/c^4 for nu_e -> nu_tau.
result:nomad-final-oscillation-limits-20.why_it_matters: In the paper's own words significantly more stringent than the limits published before it for nu_mu to nu_tau mixing at large delta m^2; the CHORUS final paper notes that NOMAD's limit is more stringent than CHORUS's at large delta m^2.

claim.quote: We present new νμ→νe, νμ→νμ, ν̄μ→ν̄e, and ν̄μ→ν̄μ oscillation measurements by the NOvA experiment, with a 50% increase in neutrino-mode beam exposure over the previously reported results.

result:nova-oscillation-parameters-2022.summary_technical: Joint νμ/ν̄μ disappearance and νe/ν̄e appearance fit within the three-flavor framework, with a 50% increase in neutrino-mode beam exposure over the previously reported results: best-fit point in the normal mass ordering and the upper octant of θ23, with Δm²₃₂ = (2.41±0.07)×10⁻³ eV² and sin²θ₂₃ = 0.57 +0.03/−0.04; values of δCP in the vicinity of π/2 are excluded by >3σ for the inverted mass ordering, and values around 3π/2 in the normal ordering are disfavored at 2σ.
result:nova-oscillation-parameters-2022.why_it_matters: The abstract says the data disfavor combinations of oscillation parameters that give rise to a large asymmetry in the rates of νe and ν̄e appearance, including values of the CP-violating phase δCP near π/2 (excluded by >3σ for the inverted mass ordering) and values around 3π/2 in the normal ordering (disfavored at 2σ).

claim.quote: Here, we carry out the first joint analysis of data sets from NOvA and T2K, the two currently operating long-baseline neutrino oscillation experiments (hundreds of kilometers of neutrino travel distance), taking advantage of our complementary experimental designs and setting new constraints on several neutrino sector parameters.

result:nova-t2k-joint-oscillation-analys.summary_technical: First joint three-flavor oscillation analysis of NOvA and T2K data sets, taking advantage of the experiments' complementary designs (the νμ→νe oscillation probability depends on both δCP and the mass ordering, which must be teased apart). Reports |Δm²₃₂| = 2.43 +0.04/−0.03 (normal ordering) or −2.48 +0.03/−0.04 (inverted ordering) ×10⁻³ eV², and a 3σ interval on δCP of [−1.38π, 0.30π] (normal) / [−0.92π, −0.04π] (inverted). The data show no strong preference for either mass ordering.
result:nova-t2k-joint-oscillation-analys.why_it_matters: The paper says this is currently the smallest experimental uncertainty on |Δm²₃₂|, and that if the inverted ordering were assumed true within the three-flavor mixing paradigm its results would provide evidence of CP symmetry violation in the lepton sector.

claim.quote: The measured flux of muon neutrinos is in very good agreement with predictions and no anomaly has been found in the ratio between the rate of electron and muon neutrino events.

result:nusex-atmospheric-neutrino-flux-1.summary_technical: Fully contained events of the nucleon-stability data set analysed for flux anomalies: nu_mu flux in very good agreement with the calculation; no anomaly in the nu_e/nu_mu event-rate ratio.
result:nusex-atmospheric-neutrino-flux-1.why_it_matters: One of the early underground checks of the atmospheric-neutrino flux, done before the anomaly that Super-Kamiokande later explained by oscillations.

claim.quote: In that time four fully contained events with at least a 10 cm track in iron have been recorded. Three of these can be definitely attributed to neutrino interactions. The fourth event can be explained by a number of possible proton decay modes.

result:nusex-nucleon-decay-candidate-198.summary_technical: Four fully contained events with at least a 10 cm iron track since 1982: three attributed to neutrino interactions, one compatible with several proton-decay modes; a proton lifetime was calculated from it. The 1985 ICRC paper reports 31 fully contained events in 2.8 years, 3 of them nucleon-decay candidates. A 2004 review notes a NUSEX candidate in the p to mu+ K0 mode with an estimated background of 0.09.
result:nusex-nucleon-decay-candidate-198.why_it_matters: An early candidate event from a proton-decay detector. No first-generation experiment established nucleon decay: a 1992 review states that no experiment has observed proton decay.

claim.quote: is three standard deviations above the standard model prediction

result:nutev-weak-mixing-angle-2002.summary_technical: Extraction of sin^2(theta_W) from NC/CC cross-section ratios for neutrinos and antineutrinos: sin^2(theta_W)(on-shell) = 0.2277 +- 0.0013 (stat) +- 0.0009 (syst), 3 sigma above the Standard Model; also a model-independent analysis of the same data.
result:nutev-weak-mixing-angle-2002.why_it_matters: The most notable tension between a low-energy weak-mixing-angle measurement and the Standard Model; it motivated decades of work on neutrino-nucleus cross sections and parton-level effects.

claim.quote: Discovery of tau neutrino appearance in the CNGS neutrino beam with the OPERA experiment

notes: The record's title and claim.quote are the verbatim title of Phys. Rev. Lett. 115, 121802 (2015), which contains the word 'Discovery'.
result:opera-tau-neutrino-appearance-dis.summary_technical: OPERA νμ→ντ appearance analysis of the CNGS data taken from 2008 to 2012: a fifth ντ candidate event found in an enlarged data sample; five candidates observed against a total background expectation of 0.25 ± 0.05 events (expected signal 2.64 ± 0.53 events for Δm²23 = 2.44×10⁻³ eV² and sin²2θ23 = 1), corresponding to the discovery of νμ→ντ oscillations in appearance mode with a significance of 5.1σ (stated in the Results and Conclusions; the abstract says larger than 5σ).
result:opera-tau-neutrino-appearance-dis.why_it_matters: The paper says the observation of νμ→ντ appearance with four candidate events had been reported previously (its introduction calls the earlier 4.2σ claim the first observation of νμ→ντ oscillations in appearance mode); the fifth candidate, together with a further reduction of the expected background, raises the significance to 5.1σ, which the paper reports as the discovery of νμ→ντ appearance.

claim.quote: In this paper a general description of the experimental set-up, overall performance of the detector, and first results are presented.

result:orpheus-first-results-2004.summary_technical: 0.45 kg of Sn granules at 70 m.w.e.; Sec. 4.1 compares the single-flip rate (exposure 6.69e-3 kg d at the lowest threshold) with the expected spin-independent neutralino rate to draw a 90% C.L. exclusion plot; the paper notes it lies above other experiments' because of the relatively high background.
result:orpheus-first-results-2004.why_it_matters: The paper ends with projected exclusion plots for a background of 1 count kg-1 d-1, which it says would be attainable at a deeper underground site and with better shielding.

claim.quote: The results show that SSG are sensitive to recoil energies down to $\sim$1keV.

result:orpheus-ssg-nuclear-recoil-respon.summary_technical: Prototype SSG detectors (0.1 cm^3, Sn, Al and Zn) irradiated with a 70 MeV neutron beam, nuclear recoil energies from neutron scattering angles with a hodoscope; the abstract describes it as part of a project to develop an SSG detector for cold dark matter and neutrinos.
result:orpheus-ssg-nuclear-recoil-respon.why_it_matters: The abstract says the limited angular resolution of the hodoscope prevented measuring the sensitivity at even lower recoil energies.

claim.quote: The exposure-dependent single-electron rate (SER) of one of these sensors was measured $\sim$100~m underground, yielding $(1.8\pm 0.3)\times10^{-3}~e^-$/pix/day at 131K.

notes: Detector R&D measurement on prototype sensors, not an Oscura dark matter search.
result:oscura-single-electron-traps-2024.summary_technical: Pocket-pumping measurements of energy and cross section of defects/contaminants in buried-channel regions of three Oscura prototype skipper-CCDs from different fabrication batches; the type of defects is more closely linked to the batch than to the gettering method; SER of one sensor measured ~100 m underground at 131 K.
result:oscura-single-electron-traps-2024.why_it_matters: The abstract concludes that the exposure-dependent single-electron rate of Oscura prototype sensors would be lower in lower-background environments.

claim.quote: We present results from the tests of the first fabricated Oscura prototype sensors, evaluate their performance in the context of the established constraints and estimate the Oscura instrumental background based on these results.

notes: Technology milestone, not a dark matter result: no Oscura physics result has been published.
result:oscura-skipper-ccd-sensors-2023.summary_technical: Instrumental-background requirements for the Oscura skipper-CCDs (parameters of the sensors, 2-10 electron signal region, 0.01 dru radiation goal at SNOLAB depth 2070 m) and first tests of the prototype sensors made at a new foundry; the instrumental background is estimated from the measurements.
result:oscura-skipper-ccd-sensors-2023.why_it_matters: The paper states Oscura aims for less than one event in each electron bin in 2-10 electrons for the full 30 kg-year exposure, so the sensors' own backgrounds must be controlled.

claim.quote: This measurement is the first one based on the direct detection of the photon pair and one of the most precise for positron energies below 1 GeV.

notes: The arXiv listing's comment says 'Submitted to PRD'; no journal reference was fetched.
result:padme-ee-to-gg-cross-section-meas.summary_technical: PADME (Run I/II data): inclusive e⁺e⁻ → γγ cross-section from 430 MeV positrons on a thin diamond target, √s about 20 MeV, using the BGO electromagnetic calorimeter; the first measurement based on direct detection of the photon pair; agrees with the NLO QED prediction within the overall 6% uncertainty.
result:padme-ee-to-gg-cross-section-meas.why_it_matters: The abstract calls it the first measurement based on direct detection of the photon pair and a necessary step for dark-sector searches with PADME.

claim.quote: A blind analysis has been performed. The data are consistent with the expected background in most of the explored energy range, and limits are set in previously unexplored regions of the available parameter space.

notes: The abstract's deviation is not a claim of observation: the record's type is 'limit'.
result:padme-x17-resonance-search-limit-.summary_technical: PADME at the DAΦNE linac (Run III): resonant e⁺e⁻ → X17 scan with 262 to 296 MeV positrons (√s 16.4 to 17.4 MeV), spacing below half the expected line width, below 1% uncertainty per energy point; blind analysis; consistent with background, limits in unexplored parameter space, largest deviation at √s ≈ 16.90 MeV with about 2σ global significance (JHEP 11 (2025) 007).
result:padme-x17-resonance-search-limit-.why_it_matters: The abstract says the data are consistent with the background in most of the range, new limits are set, and the largest deviation is about 2 standard deviations globally.

claim.quote: There is no evidence for neutrino oscillation

result:palo-verde-final-results-2001.summary_technical: Complete data set (Sept 1998 - July 2000): no evidence for nu_e-bar oscillation; nu_e-bar -> nu_x excluded at 90 % CL for delta m^2 > 1.1e-3 eV^2 at full mixing and sin^2(2 theta) > 0.17 at large delta m^2.
result:palo-verde-final-results-2001.why_it_matters: With CHOOZ, one of the two long-baseline reactor experiments that showed the atmospheric-neutrino oscillation is not electron-neutrino disappearance and that theta-13 is small.

claim.quote: We find that the anti-neutrino flux agrees with that predicted in the absence of oscillations to better than 5%

result:palo-verde-initial-results-2000.summary_technical: Initial anti-nu_e flux and spectrum measurement at ~800 m with a segmented Gd-loaded scintillator: flux agrees with the no-oscillation prediction to better than 5 %; 90 % CL exclusion for delta m^2 > 1.12e-3 eV^2 (maximal mixing) and sin^2(2 theta) > 0.21 (large delta m^2).
result:palo-verde-initial-results-2000.why_it_matters: The first of the Palo Verde limits, published alongside the CHOOZ results.

claim.quote: The minimum upper limit, $3.7\times10^{-44}$\,cm$^2$, for the spin-independent isoscalar DM-particle-nucleon scattering cross section is obtained at a DM-particle mass of 49\,GeV/c$^2$ at 90\% confidence level.

result:pandax-i-first-results-2014.summary_technical: 37-kg liquid xenon target with 17.4 live days: no DM candidate; stringent limit for low-mass DM; the abstract says it disfavors the interpretation of previously-reported positive experimental results; minimum SI limit 3.7e-44 cm^2 at 49 GeV/c^2 (90% CL).
result:pandax-i-first-results-2014.why_it_matters: First result of the PandaX programme.

claim.quote: A profile likelihood analysis confirms our earlier finding that the PandaX-I data disfavor all positive low-mass WIMP signals reported in the literature under standard assumptions.

result:pandax-i-low-mass-full-exposure-2.summary_technical: Full 80.1 live-day exposure, 54.0 kg fiducial mass, photon detection efficiency 9.6%; a stringent bound on low-mass WIMPs below 10 GeV/c^2.

claim.quote: With a total exposure of 5.4$\times10^4$ kg day, the most stringent upper limit on spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross section was set for a WIMP with mass larger than 100 GeV/c$^2$, with the lowest exclusion at 8.6$\times10^{-47}$ cm$^2$ at 40 GeV/c$^2$.

result:pandax-ii-54-ton-day-2017.summary_technical: Combined 2016 and 2017 low-background data, new exposure of 77.1 live days with background reduced to 0.8e-3 evt/kg/day (factor 2.5 better than 2016); total exposure 5.4e4 kg day; lowest exclusion 8.6e-47 cm^2 at 40 GeV/c^2.
result:pandax-ii-54-ton-day-2017.why_it_matters: The abstract describes it as the most stringent spin-independent limit for masses above 100 GeV/c^2 at publication.

claim.quote: The best upper limit on the scattering cross section is found $2.5\times 10^{-46}$ cm$^2$ for the WIMP mass 40 GeV/c$^2$ at 90% confidence level.

result:pandax-ii-98-7-day-2016.summary_technical: First physics run combined with the commissioning run, total exposure 3.3e4 kg-day; the abstract says the most stringent limit on spin-independent interaction was set for WIMP masses between 3.5 and 1000 GeV/c^2; best limit 2.5e-46 cm^2 at 40 GeV/c^2.
result:pandax-ii-98-7-day-2016.why_it_matters: The abstract describes it as the most stringent spin-independent limit for masses between 3.5 and 1000 GeV/c^2 at the time.

claim.quote: No WIMP candidates are identified, and a 90\% upper limit is set on the spin-independent elastic WIMP-nucleon cross section with a lowest excluded cross section of 2.97$\times$10$^{-45}$~cm$^2$ at a WIMP mass of 44.7~GeV/c$^2$.

result:pandax-ii-commissioning-run-2016.summary_technical: WIMP search data set with an exposure of 306 x 19.1 kg-day; the dominant 85Kr background was used as the electron recoil calibration; no WIMP candidates; lowest excluded cross section 2.97e-45 cm^2 at 44.7 GeV/c^2 (90% CL).

claim.quote: The lowest 90% confidence level exclusion on the spin-independent cross section is $2.2\times 10^{-46}$ cm$^2$ at a WIMP mass of 30 GeV/$c^2$.

result:pandax-ii-full-exposure-2020.summary_technical: Full 132 ton day exposure including all data from March 2016 to August 2018; no significant excess above the expected background; lowest 90% CL spin-independent exclusion 2.2e-46 cm^2 at 30 GeV/c^2.

claim.quote: The minimum upper limit of $4.1\times 10^{-41}$ cm$^2$ at 90\% confidence level is obtained for a WIMP mass of 40 GeV/c$^{2}$.

result:pandax-ii-spin-dependent-2016.summary_technical: Total exposure 3.3e4 kg-days; axial-vector spin-dependent WIMP interaction with 129Xe and 131Xe; the abstract says the most stringent WIMP-neutron upper limits for masses above 10 GeV/c^2 in all dark matter direct detection experiments; minimum 4.1e-41 cm^2 at 40 GeV/c^2.
result:pandax-ii-spin-dependent-2016.why_it_matters: Spin-dependent limits from PandaX-II's first data.

claim.quote: The technology is successfully demonstrated by a prototype detector. The final detector has been constructed.

result:pandax-iii-status-final-detector-.summary_technical: Status report: Micromegas-based TPC performance validated in the prototype detector (Shanghai); final detector (about 140 kg Xe at 10 bar, 52 thermal-bonding Micromegas modules) constructed and commissioned before installation at CJPL-II; expected 0.49 background counts/year in the region of interest.
result:pandax-iii-status-final-detector-.why_it_matters: Marks the stage reached by PandaX-III; it is a technology and construction milestone, not a physics result.

claim.quote: From the electron spectra we obtain $\lambda = g_A/g_V = -1.27641(45)_\mathrm{stat}(33)_\mathrm{sys}$ which confirms recent measurements with improved precision.

result:perkeo-iii-axial-vector-coupling-.summary_technical: Beta asymmetry of polarized free neutrons with a pulsed cold neutron beam suppressing leading systematics: lambda = g_A/g_V = -1.27641(45) stat (33) sys, corresponding to A_0 = -0.11985(17) stat (12) sys; implications for V_ud and a limit on a left-handed tensor interaction.
result:perkeo-iii-axial-vector-coupling-.why_it_matters: The abstract says the pulsed beam method suppresses the leading sources of systematic uncertainty.

claim.quote: We obtain a limit of b = 0.017(21) at 68.27 C.L., improving the previous best limit from neutron decay by a factor of four.

result:perkeo-iii-fierz-term-limit-2019.summary_technical: Simultaneous fit of A and b to the beta asymmetry of spin-polarized neutrons: b = 0.017(21) at 68.27% C.L.; statistically less sensitive than the spectral-shape determination but with much cleaner systematics.
result:perkeo-iii-fierz-term-limit-2019.why_it_matters: The abstract says non-zero scalar or tensor interactions would imply an additional contribution to the neutron decay rate, the Fierz interference term.

claim.quote: We find that the state of matter created at RHIC cannot be described in terms of ordinary color neutral hadrons.

notes: PHENIX white paper evaluating the first three years of RHIC data, recorded with the collaboration's own title wording and result_type 'measurement' (not 'discovery').
result:phenix-perfect-liquid-whitepaper-.summary_technical: PHENIX's white paper (Nucl. Phys. A 757, 184-283) evaluates the measurements from the first three years of RHIC operation (charged-particle multiplicities, transverse energy, identified-hadron yields and spectra, elliptic flow, two-particle correlations, fluctuations and high-pT suppression) with an emphasis on implications for the formation of a new state of dense matter, and finds that the state of matter created cannot be described in terms of ordinary color neutral hadrons.
result:phenix-perfect-liquid-whitepaper-.why_it_matters: The abstract says the results are examined with an emphasis on implications for the formation of a new state of dense matter; the paper's title calls this dense partonic matter.

claim.quote: We present the first measurement of pseudorapidity densities of primary charged particles near mid-rapidity in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s} =$ 56 and 130 AGeV.

result:phobos-first-multiplicity-au-au-2.summary_technical: First measurement of the pseudorapidity density of primary charged particles near mid-rapidity in Au+Au at 56 and 130 AGeV: dN/deta (|eta|<1) = 408 ± 12 (stat) ± 30 (syst) at 56 AGeV and 555 ± 12 ± 35 at 130 AGeV for the most central collisions, an increase of more than 40% per participant relative to proton-antiproton collisions at the higher energy.
result:phobos-first-multiplicity-au-au-2.why_it_matters: A first look at the energy density reached at RHIC, which set the scale for the interpretation of all later results.

claim.quote: In the most central Au+Au collisions at the highest beam energy, evidence is found for the formation of a very high energy density system whose description in terms of simple hadronic degrees of freedom is inappropriate.

notes: The collaboration says "evidence is found for", so the result type is evidence, not discovery.
result:phobos-rhic-white-paper-2005.summary_technical: Conclusions from the PHOBOS data to date: evidence for a very high energy-density system in central 200 GeV Au+Au collisions whose description in terms of simple hadronic degrees of freedom is inappropriate, with interacting constituents, and simple scaling behaviours of particle production at RHIC energies.
result:phobos-rhic-white-paper-2005.why_it_matters: One of the four 2005 RHIC white papers assessing the nature of the matter created in heavy-ion collisions at RHIC.

claim.quote: The PICASSO collaboration observed for the first time a significant difference between the acoustic signals induced by neutrons and alpha particles in a detector based on superheated liquids.

notes: Date: first arXiv submission (v1, 10 Jul 2008); the abstract quoted is that of the latest arXiv version (v2, last revised 23 Sep 2008).
result:picasso-alpha-neutron-discriminat.summary_technical: Acoustic signals of alpha-induced and neutron-induced nucleations differ in superheated C4F10; the abstract attributes the effect to multiple bubbles forming on alpha tracks versus single nucleations from neutron recoils.
result:picasso-alpha-neutron-discriminat.why_it_matters: The abstract says the effect offers the possibility of improved background suppression for dark matter experiments.

claim.quote: No signal consistent with dark matter was observed. We set limits for spin-dependent interactions on protons of $\sigma_p^{SD}$~=~1.32~$\times$~10$^{-2}$~pb (90\%~C.L.) at a WIMP mass of 20 GeV/c$^{2}$.

notes: Date: first arXiv submission (v1, 4 Nov 2016); the abstract quoted is that of the latest arXiv version (v2, last revised 23 Mar 2017).
result:picasso-final-results-2016.summary_technical: 32 modules, 3.0 kg C4F10, 231.4 kg d at SNOLAB between March 2012 and January 2014, with acoustic localisation for fiducialisation: sigma_p(SD) = 1.32e-2 pb (90% C.L.) at 20 GeV/c^2; spin-independent exclusion of sigma_p(SI) = 4.86e-5 pb around 7 GeV/c^2.
result:picasso-final-results-2016.why_it_matters: The abstract says the pioneering efforts of PICASSO paved the way for a next-generation detector built on larger-mass bubble chambers.

claim.quote: No dark matter signal was found. Best exclusion limits in the spin dependent sector were obtained for WIMP masses of 20 GeV/c^2 with a cross section on protons of sigma_p^SD = 0.032 pb (90% C.L.).

notes: Date: first arXiv submission (v1, 6 Feb 2012); the abstract quoted is that of the latest arXiv version (v2, last revised 28 Mar 2012).
result:picasso-low-mass-wimp-limits-2012.summary_technical: Subset of 10 detectors with 0.72 kg of 19F and 114 kg d exposure: sigma_p(SD) = 0.032 pb at 20 GeV/c^2; sigma_p(SI) = 1.41e-4 pb excluded near 7 GeV/c^2 (90% C.L.).
result:picasso-low-mass-wimp-limits-2012.why_it_matters: The abstract notes that the low backgrounds allow thresholds as low as 1.7 keV, which increases the sensitivity to WIMPs with masses below 10 GeV/c^2.

claim.quote: no evidence for a WIMP signal was found. For a WIMP mass of 29 GeV/c2, limits on the spin-dependent cross section on protons of sigma_p = 1.31 pb and on neutrons of sigma_n = 21.5 pb have been obtained at 90% C.L.

notes: Date: first arXiv submission (v1, 15 Feb 2005); the abstract quoted is that of the latest arXiv version (v2, last revised 9 Aug 2005).
result:picasso-spin-dependent-limits-200.summary_technical: Superheated C4F10 droplets, exposure 1.98 +- 0.19 kg d at 2070 m depth: sigma_p(SD) = 1.31 pb and sigma_n(SD) = 21.5 pb at 29 GeV/c^2 (90% C.L.), also expressed as limits on the effective couplings a_p and a_n.
result:picasso-spin-dependent-limits-200.why_it_matters: The abstract states that some new parameter space at WIMP masses below 20 GeV/c2 was ruled out.

claim.quote: new limits have been obtained on the spin-dependent cross section on $^{19}$F of $\sigma_F$ = 13.9 pb (90% C.L.) which can be converted into cross section limits on protons and neutrons of $\sigma_p$ = 0.16 pb and $\sigma_n$ = 2.60 pb respectively (90% C.L).

notes: Date: first arXiv submission (v1, 2 Jul 2009); the abstract quoted is that of the latest arXiv version (v2, last revised 10 Nov 2009).
result:picasso-spin-dependent-limits-200.summary_technical: Two detectors with 65 g and 69 g of 19F, total exposure 13.75 +- 0.48 kg d; for WIMP masses around 24 GeV/c^2, sigma_F = 13.9 pb, sigma_p = 0.16 pb and sigma_n = 2.60 pb (90% C.L.).
result:picasso-spin-dependent-limits-200.why_it_matters: The abstract says the limits on protons restrict recent interpretations of the DAMA/LIBRA annual modulations in terms of spin-dependent interactions.

claim.quote: These data provide the most sensitive direct detection constraints on WIMP-proton spin-dependent scattering to date, with significant sensitivity at low WIMP masses for spin-independent WIMP-nucleon scattering.

result:pico-2l-first-results-2015.summary_technical: 2-litre C3F8 chamber, 211.5 kg-days at four recoil-energy thresholds from 3.2 to 8.1 keV; twelve single nuclear-recoil candidates whose timing is not consistent with a uniform distribution, 'no evidence for a dark matter signal is claimed'; excellent electron-recoil and alpha rejection at low threshold (Phys. Rev. Lett. 114, 231302).
result:pico-2l-first-results-2015.why_it_matters: The abstract states these are the most sensitive direct-detection constraints to date on WIMP-proton spin-dependent scattering.

claim.quote: These data provide the most stringent direct detection constraints on weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP)-proton spin-dependent scattering to date for WIMP masses $<$ 50$\,$GeV/c$^2$.

result:pico-2l-run2-2016.summary_technical: 129 kg-days at a 3.3 keV thermodynamic threshold; one single nuclear-recoil event, consistent with the predicted neutron background and the observed multiple-bubble neutron rate; the anomalous background events of run 1 absent after particulate-contamination controls (Phys. Rev. D 93, 061101).
result:pico-2l-run2-2016.why_it_matters: The abstract states these are the most stringent direct-detection constraints to date on WIMP-proton spin-dependent scattering for masses below 50 GeV/c^2.

claim.quote: These results set the most stringent direct-detection constraint to date on the WIMP-proton spin-dependent cross section at 3.4 $\times$ 10$^{-41}$ cm$^2$ for a 30-GeV$\thinspace$c$^{-2}$ WIMP, more than one order of magnitude improvement from previous PICO results.

result:pico-60-c3f8-2017.summary_technical: 52 kg C3F8; blind analysis of an efficiency-corrected 1167 kg-day exposure at a 3.3 keV thermodynamic threshold (taken November 2016-January 2017) reveals no single-scattering nuclear-recoil candidates, consistent with the predicted background; limit 3.4e-41 cm^2 for a 30 GeV/c^2 WIMP (Phys. Rev. Lett. 118, 251301). The abstract does not state the confidence level.
result:pico-60-c3f8-2017.why_it_matters: The abstract states the limit is the most stringent direct-detection constraint to date and more than one order of magnitude better than previous PICO results.

claim.quote: These results set the most stringent direct-detection constraint to date on the WIMP-proton spin-dependent cross section at 2.5 $\times$ 10$^{-41}$ cm$^2$ for a 25 GeV WIMP, and improve on previous PICO results for 3-5 GeV WIMPs by an order of magnitude.

result:pico-60-c3f8-complete-exposure-20.summary_technical: 52 kg C3F8 at thresholds as low as 1.2 keV; new blind 1404 kg-day exposure at 2.45 keV (taken April-June 2017) with about the same expected background as the earlier 1167 kg-day exposure at 3.3 keV; new optical tracking analysis enlarges the fiducial volume; limit 2.5e-41 cm^2 for a 25 GeV WIMP (Phys. Rev. D 100, 022001).
result:pico-60-c3f8-complete-exposure-20.why_it_matters: The abstract states the limit is the most stringent direct-detection constraint to date on the WIMP-proton spin-dependent cross section and an order-of-magnitude improvement for 3-5 GeV WIMPs.

claim.quote: Stringent limits on weakly interacting massive particles interacting via spin-dependent proton and spin-independent processes are set, and most interpretations of the DAMA/LIBRA modulation signal as dark matter interacting with iodine nuclei are ruled out.

result:pico-60-cf3i-2015.summary_technical: 36.8 kg CF3I, 92.8 analysed live days (3415 kg-days taken June 2013-May 2014); a large population of unknown background events with acoustic, spatial and timing behaviour inconsistent with dark matter was removed by analysis cuts that retain 48.2% of the exposure (Phys. Rev. D 93, 052014).
result:pico-60-cf3i-2015.why_it_matters: The abstract says most interpretations of the DAMA/LIBRA modulation signal as dark matter interacting with iodine nuclei are ruled out.

claim.quote: An analysis of data from the PICO-60 C$_{3}$F$_{8}$ bubble chamber sets leading constraints on spin-independent absorption for dark matter masses below 23 MeV/$\textit{c}^2$ and establishes the first limits on spin-dependent absorptive interactions.

result:pico-60-fermionic-absorption-2025.summary_technical: Effective-field-theory analysis of neutral-current absorption of fermionic dark matter on nuclei using the PICO-60 C3F8 data; spin-independent limits below 23 MeV/c^2 and the first spin-dependent absorptive limits (published 2025).
result:pico-60-fermionic-absorption-2025.why_it_matters: The abstract says the results demonstrate the sensitivity of bubble chambers to low-mass dark matter.

claim.quote: The analysis disfavors various scenarios, in a wide region of parameter space, that provide a feasible explanation of the signal observed by DAMA, assuming an inelastic interaction, considering that the PICO CF$_{3}$I bubble chamber used iodine as the target material.

result:pico-60-inelastic-dark-matter-202.summary_technical: Search for inelastic dark matter-nucleus scattering with the PICO-60 CF3I run (36.8 kg, 3415 kg-day, thresholds 7-20 keV) and C3F8 runs (52 kg, 1404 and 1167 kg-day) (Phys. Rev. D 108, 062003).
result:pico-60-inelastic-dark-matter-202.why_it_matters: The abstract says wide regions of parameter space that could explain the DAMA signal through inelastic interactions are disfavoured.

claim.quote: Using data from the PICO-60 bubble chamber leading limits for dark matter masses between 2.7 GeV/c$^2$ and 24 GeV/c$^2$ are reported for the coupling of these photon-mediated dark matter-nucleus interactions.

result:pico-60-photon-mediated-2022.summary_technical: Effective-field-theory limits on anapole, electric and magnetic dipole and millicharge-type couplings using the 52 kg C3F8 exposures of 1404 kg-day (2.45 keV threshold) and 1167 kg-day (3.29 keV threshold) (Phys. Rev. D 106, 042004).
result:pico-60-photon-mediated-2022.why_it_matters: The abstract reports leading limits on these photon-mediated couplings between 2.7 and 24 GeV/c^2.

claim.quote: The successful construction and operation of this prototype confirm the effectiveness of the right-side-up design, which will be used in future dark matter searches such as PICO-40L and PICO-500.

notes: Filed under PICO-40L and PICO-500 because the paper presents the prototype as the proof of the design both use; the chamber itself ran at Drexel University, not at SNOLAB.
result:pico-buffer-free-prototype-2019.summary_technical: Drexel Bubble Chamber, the PICO collaboration's first C3F8 buffer-free prototype: runs at and below the nuclear-recoil thresholds used for WIMP searches, down to 1.19 keV; sensitivity to 137Cs gammas and 244Cm spontaneous-fission neutrons; acoustic alpha discrimination possible but few alphas observed (JINST 14, P08019). It is a prototype at Drexel University, not PICO-40L itself.
result:pico-buffer-free-prototype-2019.why_it_matters: The abstract says the prototype confirms the right-side-up design to be used in PICO-40L and PICO-500.

claim.quote: A comprehensive analysis of PICO gamma calibration data demonstrates for the first time that electron recoils in C$_3$F$_8$ scale in accordance with a new nucleation mechanism, rather than one driven by a hot-spike as previously supposed.

result:pico-electron-recoil-nucleation-2.summary_technical: Semi-empirical electron-recoil nucleation model fit to all PICO C3F8 gamma-calibration datasets (including PICO-2L and PICO-60 runs and test chambers); projects thermodynamic thresholds as low as 2.8 keV for PICO-40L (Phys. Rev. D 100, 082006). The PICO-40L reach quoted in the abstract is a projection.
result:pico-electron-recoil-nucleation-2.why_it_matters: The abstract says the model lets thresholds be tuned to lower-energy nuclear recoils while keeping excellent electron-recoil rejection.

claim.quote: In this paper, we present the background stability of purity in the Ingot#94 NaI(Tl) detector, which was produced using the Ingot#85 purification method, along with the first annual modulation search conducted by the PICOLON experiment.

result:picolon-annual-modulation-test-20.summary_technical: Ingot #94 (1.34 kg), 156.0 d x 1.34 kg between 2021-11-11 and 2022-05-24: background about 1.5 /d/kg/keV in 2-6 keVee, no time dependence of the radiopurity; the fitted modulation amplitude is finite but attributed to non-physical causes (noise cuts); WIMP limits derived from the six-month modulation, sensitivity only slightly approaching the DAMA/LIBRA region (Prog. Theor. Exp. Phys. 2025).
result:picolon-annual-modulation-test-20.why_it_matters: The paper presents PICOLON as the only experiment to have demonstrated stable production of ultra-pure NaI(Tl) crystals of DAMA/LIBRA-level radiopurity.

claim.quote: The achieved level of radiopurity of NaI(Tl) crystals makes construction of a dark matter detector possible.

result:picolon-radiopure-nai-development.summary_technical: Hybrid purification: recrystallisation reduces 40K (natural K down to 20 ppb) and resins reduce the U and Th chains: thorium series 1.2 +- 1.4 uBq/kg, 226Ra 13 +- 4 uBq/kg, 210Pb below 5.7 uBq/kg at 90% C.L. (Prog. Theor. Exp. Phys. 2021, 043F01).
result:picolon-radiopure-nai-development.why_it_matters: It is the crystal development on which the PICOLON measurements rest.

claim.quote: The impurities in the Ingot #94, $^{232}$Th, $^{226}$Ra and $^{210}$Po radioactivity were $4.6\pm 1.2~\mathrm{\mu Bq/kg}$, $7.9\pm 4.4~\mathrm{\mu Bq/kg}$, and $19\pm 6~\mathrm{\mu Bq/kg}$, which are equivalent to those of the DAMA/LIBRA crystals.

result:picolon-radiopurity-ingot-94-2023.summary_technical: Alpha events selected by pulse-shape discrimination: 232Th 4.6 +- 1.2, 226Ra 7.9 +- 4.4 and 210Po 19 +- 6 uBq/kg; background rate 2-5 events/d/kg/keV in 2-6 keV without a veto trigger.
result:picolon-radiopurity-ingot-94-2023.why_it_matters: It shows that the Ingot #85 purification result was reproduced.

claim.quote: A new measurement of the branching ratio, ... This is in agreement with the standard model prediction and improves the test of electron-muon universality to the level of 0.1 %.

result:pienu-r-e-mu-2015.summary_technical: R_e/mu = Gamma(pi+ -> e+ nu(gamma)) / Gamma(pi+ -> mu+ nu(gamma)) = (1.2344 ± 0.0023 (stat) ± 0.0019 (syst)) x 10^-4 from a partial 2010 dataset of about 4 x 10^5 pi -> e nu decays, in agreement with the standard model prediction.
result:pienu-r-e-mu-2015.why_it_matters: The abstract states the result improves the test of electron-muon universality to the level of 0.1 per cent.

claim.locator: Phys. Lett. B 76 (1978) 243, paper title (Crossref record)
claim.quote: Observation of a narrow resonance formed in e+e− annihilation at 9.46 GeV

notes: The abstract could not be retrieved; the claim is the paper title only. The DASP II collaboration reported a companion observation in the same issue; not recorded here.
result:pluto-upsilon-observation-1978.summary_technical: PLUTO at DORIS: narrow resonance at 9.46 GeV in e⁺e⁻ annihilation (Phys. Lett. B 76 (1978) 243-245); the Υ had been discovered in hadron collisions at Fermilab in 1977; DORIS was upgraded to reach it.
result:pluto-upsilon-observation-1978.why_it_matters: Ziemann notes that the Upsilon, a bound state of two bottom quarks, was discovered at Fermilab in 1977 and that DORIS was upgraded to energies where Upsilons could be produced.

claim.quote: Including both systematic and statistical uncertainties, the hypothesis of no B-mode polarization power from gravitational lensing is rejected at 97.1% confidence.

result:polarbear-b-mode-power-spectrum-2.summary_technical: POLARBEAR 150 GHz, 25 deg^2 effective area, 3.5 arcmin resolution, multipoles 500 < l < 2100: A_BB = 1.12 +/- 0.61 (stat) relative to the lensing expectation; no-lensing hypothesis rejected at 97.1%.
result:polarbear-b-mode-power-spectrum-2.why_it_matters: It was one of the first measurements of the lensing-induced B-mode power spectrum that any search for inflationary B modes must subtract.

claim.quote: Evidence for the signal of polarization lensing and lensing $B$-modes is found at 4.2$\sigma$ (stat.+sys.) significance.

result:polarbear-lensing-evidence-2013.summary_technical: POLARBEAR first-season 30 deg^2: four-point correlations of E and B modes give polarization lensing and lensing B modes at 4.2 sigma (stat.+sys.); matter-fluctuation amplitude measured to 27%, consistent with LCDM.
result:polarbear-lensing-evidence-2013.why_it_matters: The abstract says "We report the first direct evidence for polarization lensing based on purely CMB information".

claim.quote: Our result, rp = 0.831 ± 0.007stat ± 0.012syst femtometres, is smaller than the most recent high-precision e–p measurement

notes: The PRad-II proposal and the target paper (arXiv:2103.01749) state that the PRad result agrees with the muonic-hydrogen value.
result:prad-proton-charge-radius-2019.summary_technical: Elastic e-p cross section at Q^2 from 2.1 x 10^-4 to 6 x 10^-2 (GeV/c)^2 from 1.1 and 2.2 GeV beams on a windowless hydrogen gas target, normalised to simultaneous e-e (Moller) scattering: r_p = 0.831 +- 0.007 stat +- 0.012 syst fm, 2.7 standard deviations below the average of all e-p experimental results.
result:prad-proton-charge-radius-2019.why_it_matters: An independent, low-systematics electron-scattering determination of the proton radius, bearing on the discrepancy between muonic-hydrogen and earlier measurements.

claim.quote: provides the first electroweak observation of the neutron skin which is expected in a heavy, neutron-rich nucleus

result:prex-neutron-radius-208pb-2012.summary_technical: First measurement of the parity-violating asymmetry A_PV = 0.656 ± 0.060 (stat) ± 0.014 (syst) ppm in elastic scattering of polarised electrons from 208Pb, corresponding to R_n - R_p = 0.33 +0.16 -0.18 fm: the first electroweak observation of the neutron skin.
result:prex-neutron-radius-208pb-2012.why_it_matters: The neutron skin of a heavy nucleus constrains the density dependence of the symmetry energy of nuclear matter and thus the structure of neutron stars.

claim.quote: The measurement accurately constrains the density dependence of the symmetry energy of nuclear matter near saturation density, with implications for the size and composition of neutron stars.

result:prex2-neutron-skin-208pb-2021.summary_technical: A_PV = 550 ± 16 (stat) ± 8 (syst) ppb for elastic scattering of longitudinally polarised electrons from 208Pb, giving the neutral weak form factor F_W(Q^2 = 0.00616 GeV^2) = 0.368 ± 0.013 and, with PREX-I, R_n - R_p = 0.283 ± 0.071 fm; also the first significant direct measurement of the interior weak density of 208Pb.
result:prex2-neutron-skin-208pb-2021.why_it_matters: Constrains the density dependence of the symmetry energy near saturation density, with implications for the size and composition of neutron stars.

claim.quote: The best-fit point of the Neutrino-4 reactor experiment's claimed observation of short-baseline oscillation is ruled out at more than five standard deviations.

result:prospect-final-sterile-search-202.summary_technical: Positron spectra from six reactor-detector distance ranges are statistically consistent; the data exclude at 95 % CL sterile-neutrino regions above 3 eV^2, including all space below 10 eV^2 suggested by the strengthened Gallium Anomaly, and rule out the Neutrino-4 best-fit point at more than 5 sigma.
result:prospect-final-sterile-search-202.why_it_matters: The final PROSPECT-I word on eV-scale sterile neutrinos at reactors, and a direct refutation of the one experiment that had claimed to see them.

claim.quote: disfavors the best fit of the Reactor Antineutrino Anomaly at 2.2σ confidence level

result:prospect-first-oscillation-search.summary_technical: Reactor-model-independent analysis of the IBD prompt-energy spectrum versus baseline (7-9 m) constrains significant portions of the previously allowed sterile-neutrino parameter space at 95 % CL and disfavours the Reactor Antineutrino Anomaly best fit at 2.2 sigma.
result:prospect-first-oscillation-search.why_it_matters: An early direct test of the reactor antineutrino anomaly from one compact core, without relying on a reactor flux model.

claim.locator: abstract of the collaboration's 1997 summary paper (Hyperfine Interactions 109, 191)
claim.quote: The production of eleven antihydrogen atoms is reported including possibly 2 ± 1 background signals, the observed yield agrees with theoretical predictions.

notes: Number of atoms: the CERN press release says nine atoms; the collaboration's 1997 abstract says eleven including possibly 2 ± 1 background signals. Both are reported; the later collaboration wording is used for the claim.
result:ps210-antihydrogen-production-199.summary_technical: Antihydrogen produced in flight in antiproton collisions with xenon in LEAR, mediated by e+e− pair creation via two photons; atoms identified by a unique detector signature. The collaboration reports eleven antihydrogen atoms including possibly 2 ± 1 background signals; the observed yield agrees with theory.
result:ps210-antihydrogen-production-199.why_it_matters: The collaboration says it concentrated on production because antihydrogen had not been observed before; in principle it is well suited to fundamental CPT-violation studies.

claim.quote: The measured value of the neutron EDM is $d_{\rm n} = (0.0\pm1.1_{\rm stat}\pm0.2_{\rm sys})\times10^{-26}e\,{\rm cm}$.

result:psi-nedm-neutron-edm-2020.summary_technical: Ramsey separated-oscillating-field measurement with ultracold neutrons at PSI using an Hg-199 co-magnetometer and an array of optically pumped Cs magnetometers, blinded analysis by two groups: d_n = (0.0 ± 1.1 stat ± 0.2 sys) x 10^-26 e cm from 54068 cycles taken in 2015-2016.
result:psi-nedm-neutron-edm-2020.why_it_matters: The abstract places the result in the long history of EDM experiments probing physics that violates time-reversal invariance.

claim.quote: The small Q^2 of this experiment has made possible the first determination of the weak charge of the proton

notes: Superseded by the final result (result:qweak-proton-weak-charge-2018).
result:qweak-first-weak-charge-determina.summary_technical: Commissioning-run result: A_ep = -279 ± 35 (stat) ± 31 (syst) ppb at Q^2 = 0.025 (GeV/c)^2; with earlier PVES data constraining hadronic corrections, Q_W^p(PVES) = 0.064 ± 0.012 versus the Standard-Model 0.0710 ± 0.0007; combined with atomic parity violation, constraints on the up- and down-quark weak charges.
result:qweak-first-weak-charge-determina.why_it_matters: First determination of the proton's weak charge, demonstrating the method that the full data set later sharpened.

claim.quote: Our value of Q_W^p is in excellent agreement with the SM, and sets multi-TeV-scale constraints on any semi-leptonic PV physics not described within the SM.

result:qweak-proton-weak-charge-2018.summary_technical: Final Qweak result from the combined two run periods: parity-violating e-p asymmetry A_ep = -226.5 ± 9.3 ppb, giving Q_W^p = 0.0719 ± 0.0045, in excellent agreement with the Standard Model and setting multi-TeV-scale constraints on semi-leptonic parity-violating physics beyond it.
result:qweak-proton-weak-charge-2018.why_it_matters: The weak charge of the proton is a precisely predicted Standard-Model quantity, so a precise measurement is an indirect search for new physics at mass scales above those reachable in direct collider searches.

claim.quote: Observation of Reactor Electron Antineutrino Disappearance in the RENO Experiment

result:reno-observation-2012.summary_technical: In a 229-day data-taking period (11 Aug 2011 - 26 Mar 2012) the far (near) detector observed 17102 (154088) electron-antineutrino candidates; the ratio of observed to expected antineutrinos in the far detector is 0.920±0.009(stat)±0.014(syst), giving sin²(2θ₁₃) = 0.113±0.013(stat)±0.019(syst) from a rate-only analysis; disappearance observed with a significance of 4.9 standard deviations.
result:reno-observation-2012.why_it_matters: The abstract reports the observed disappearance of reactor electron antineutrinos, consistent with neutrino oscillations, and determines sin²2θ13 from a rate-only analysis; the antineutrinos come from six 2.8 GWth reactors at the Yonggwang Nuclear Power Plant and are detected at 294 m and 1383 m from the reactor array centre.

claim.quote: Sapphire (25g, 50g) and germanium (67g) absorbers were used. Thresholds respectively lower than 1keV and 450 eV were achieved on these detectors.

result:rosebud-canfranc-2001-report-2001.summary_technical: Phase 1: 25 g and 50 g sapphire and 67 g germanium absorbers, thresholds below 1 keV and 450 eV; phase 2 prototypes of CaWO4 (54 g) and BGO (46 g) scintillating bolometers with high neutron/gamma discrimination and a 6 keV heat-channel threshold on BGO.
result:rosebud-canfranc-2001-report-2001.why_it_matters: Opened the multi-target scintillating-bolometer approach later pursued by CRESST and the planned EURECA.

claim.quote: We report in this paper the results of several runs (of about 10 days each) with successively improved energy thresholds, and the progressive background reduction obtained by improvement of the radiopurity of the components

result:rosebud-first-results-2000.summary_technical: Three sapphire bolometers (100 g in total) with NTD-Ge sensors at 20 mK in Canfranc (2450 m.w.e.); runs of about 10 days with successively lower thresholds and background after radiopurity improvements and the addition of old (Roman) lead shields.
result:rosebud-first-results-2000.why_it_matters: Set the baseline for low-mass WIMP searches with sapphire bolometers at Canfranc and showed where the background came from.

claim.locator: Rubin 'History' page, section 'First Look at Rubin imagery'
claim.quote: On June 23, 2025, Rubin released its first public images and video in a globally coordinated release, anchored by a press conference in Washington, D.C. and livestreamed at more than 300 watch parties around the world.

notes: A technology milestone, not a physics result. Source is the observatory's own history page (not a press release).
result:rubin-first-look-2025.summary_technical: Rubin Observatory First Look, 23 June 2025: first public images and video from the Simonyi Survey Telescope and LSST Camera, released in a globally coordinated event. The LSST began on 29 June 2026.
result:rubin-first-look-2025.why_it_matters: The Rubin history page records the First Look release as the first public demonstration of Rubin imagery, followed in October 2025 by the official transition from construction to operations and in June 2026 by the start of the 10-year LSST.

claim.quote: NaI-33 has a record low $^{39}$K contamination of 4.3$\pm$0.2 ppb as determined by mass spectrometry. We measured a light yield of 11.1$\pm$0.2 photoelectrons/keV and an energy resolution of 13.2% (FWHM/E) at 59.5 keV.

result:sabre-nai-33-direct-counting-2021.summary_technical: Underground counting of NaI-33 at LNGS (Hall B facility): 39K 4.3 +- 0.2 ppb (mass spectrometry), light yield 11.1 +- 0.2 photoelectrons/keV, 226Ra 5.9 +- 0.6 and 228Th 1.6 +- 0.3 uBq/kg, 210Pb out of equilibrium 0.51 +- 0.02 mBq/kg, alpha quenching factor 0.63 +- 0.01 at 5304 keV; about 1 count/day/kg/keV in the [5-20] keV region (Eur. Phys. J. C 81, 299).
result:sabre-nai-33-direct-counting-2021.why_it_matters: It is the first published characterisation of the crystal that the SABRE team later ran in the Proof-of-Principle detector.

claim.quote: By comparing this model to the results of the commissioning and production runs conducted prior to crystal growth, the distribution coefficients were determined for various impurities, contained in the powder at the parts-per-billion (ppb) level.

result:sabre-north-zone-refining-2026.summary_technical: Mathematical model of NaI zone refining fitted to commissioning and production runs; distribution coefficients of ppb-level impurities, used to predict the background of the SABRE North detectors in the region of interest.
result:sabre-north-zone-refining-2026.why_it_matters: Describes the purification step on which SABRE North's crystal production for the physics detector rests.

claim.quote: We find an average background of 1.39 $\pm$ 0.02 counts/day/kg/keV in the region of interest and a spectrum consistent with data previously acquired in the PoP setup, where the external veto background suppression was in place.

result:sabre-pop-dry-passive-shielding-2.summary_technical: NaI-33 in the PoP-dry set-up (17 March 2021 - 25 February 2022): 1.39 +- 0.02 cpd/kg/keV in 1-6 keV after a boosted-decision-tree noise rejection keeping >90% efficiency; 210Pb, partly in the PTFE reflector, dominates (Eur. Phys. J. C 82, 1158).
result:sabre-pop-dry-passive-shielding-2.why_it_matters: The authors use it to design the passive shielding of the SABRE North physics phase.

claim.quote: With the active veto, the average background rate in the crystal in the 1-6 keV energy region-of-interest (ROI) is $1.20\pm0.05$ counts/day/kg/keV, which is a breakthrough since the DAMA/LIBRA experiment.

notes: Recorded on SABRE North: the Proof-of-Principle phase is the first phase of that experiment.
result:sabre-pop-high-sensitivity-charac.summary_technical: Radiopurity measurement of crystal NaI-33 in the SABRE Proof-of-Principle detector (liquid-scintillator veto): 40K by direct counting 2.2 +- 1.5 ppb; 1-6 keV background 1.20 +- 0.05 cpd/kg/keV with the veto, dominated by 210Pb, about half of it in the PTFE reflector (Phys. Rev. D 104, L021302).
result:sabre-pop-high-sensitivity-charac.why_it_matters: The paper presents these results as a benchmark for the next-generation NaI(Tl) detector arrays, such as SABRE North and South.

claim.quote: The measured muon flux is f = (6.33 +/- 0.04_stat +/- 0.35_sys) x 10^{-8} [s^{-1} cm^{-2}].

result:sabre-south-muon-flux-supl-2026.summary_technical: Eight EJ200 plastic-scintillator panels with Hamamatsu R13089 PMT pairs (the SABRE South muon veto, data taken in 2024-2025): f = (6.33 +- 0.04 stat +- 0.35 sys) x 10^-8 cm^-2 s^-1, in excellent agreement with simulations.
result:sabre-south-muon-flux-supl-2026.why_it_matters: It is the first published data from the SABRE South installation and the first underground muon measurement at SUPL.

claim.quote: We estimate an overall background of 0.72 cpd/kg/keV$_{ee}$ in the energy range 1$-$6 keV$_{ee}$ primarily due to radioactive contamination in the crystals.

notes: A design projection (result_type technology_milestone), not a measured result.
result:sabre-south-simulation-background.summary_technical: Geant4 simulation of SABRE South (50 kg target): 0.72 cpd/kg/keVee in 1-6 keVee, mostly from crystal contamination; DAMA/LIBRA-like modulation excluded (confirmed) at 4 (5) sigma within 2.5 years (Eur. Phys. J. C 83, 2023). A design projection, not a measured background.
result:sabre-south-simulation-background.why_it_matters: The background figure fixes the physics reach quoted for SABRE South in the technical design report.

claim.quote: With an expected total background of 0.72 cpd/kg/keV, SABRE South can test the DAMA/LIBRA signal with 5$\sigma$ discovery or 3$\sigma$ exclusion after two years of data taking.

notes: A design projection (result_type technology_milestone), not a measured result.
result:sabre-south-tdr-executive-summary.summary_technical: TDR executive summary (JINST 20, T04001): seven NaI(Tl) crystals (35 or 50 kg) in copper enclosures with R11065 PMTs in an 11.6 kL LAB veto with at least 18 R5912 PMTs, eight EJ-200 muon-veto modules; the veto should suppress the background by 27% in 1-6 keV; expected background 0.72 cpd/kg/keV.
result:sabre-south-tdr-executive-summary.why_it_matters: It is the design document on which the assembly at SUPL is based.

claim.quote: Measurement of the solar neutrino capture rate with gallium metal

notes: This result record covers only the 1999 paper's 1990-1997 dataset and its own 67.2 SNU figure, sourced directly from the paper itself.
result:sage-capture-rate-1999.summary_technical: Solar neutrino capture rate on gallium, January 1990-December 1997, measured at 67.2 (+7.2/−7.0 stat) (+3.5/−3.0 syst) SNU, about half the Standard Solar Model prediction of 129 SNU.
result:sage-capture-rate-1999.why_it_matters: The paper's introduction says gallium experiments have a very low threshold (233 keV) and are therefore sensitive to low-energy pp neutrinos; the SAGE and GALLEX results are both well below the Standard Solar Model prediction.

claim.quote: A 30-g xenon bubble chamber, operated at Northwestern University in June and November 2016, has for the first time observed simultaneous bubble nucleation and scintillation by nuclear recoils in a superheated liquid.

notes: Operated at Northwestern University (not a SNOLAB or Fermilab detector); the SBC collaboration's 2025 paper (arXiv:2410.07241) calls it 'a device filled with pure xenon [that] first demonstrated the ability to operate simultaneously as a bubble chamber and scintillation detector in 2017'.
The paper is not signed 'SBC Collaboration'; its link to the collaboration is the 2025 SBC paper's description of the same device.
result:sbc-xenon-bubble-chamber-demonstr.summary_technical: 30-g xenon chamber with CCD camera, solar-blind PMT for 175-nm scintillation and a piezoelectric acoustic transducer; Seitz thresholds 4.2-15.0 keV; minimum nuclear-recoil energy to nucleate a bubble 19+-6 keV at 8.3 keV; no gamma-ray nucleation, 90% C.L. upper limit 6.3e-7 bubbles per gamma interaction at 4.2 keV (Phys. Rev. Lett. 118, 231301). Precursor device, operated before the SBC collaboration's detectors.
result:sbc-xenon-bubble-chamber-demonstr.why_it_matters: The abstract says these measurements establish the noble-liquid bubble chamber as a promising new technology for dark matter and CEvNS detection.

claim.quote: The bubble chamber has now been shown to have sensitivity to ~1 keV nuclear recoils while remaining insensitive to bubble nucleation by $\gamma$-rays.

notes: Result of the xenon bubble chamber operated at Northwestern University, signed 'SBC collaboration' (not an SBC-LAr10 or SBC-SNOLAB measurement).
result:sbc-xenon-bubble-chamber-low-thre.summary_technical: Thermodynamic thresholds as low as 0.50 keV (hardware limited); calibration of the nuclear-recoil nucleation response versus recoil energy and thermodynamic state; upper limit < 1.1e-6 on the probability of bubble nucleation by gamma-ray Auger cascades at 0.50 keV (Phys. Rev. D 111, 032002).
result:sbc-xenon-bubble-chamber-low-thre.why_it_matters: The abstract says the chamber is sensitive to ~1 keV nuclear recoils while insensitive to nucleation by gamma rays.

claim.quote: We find a well-detected peak in the correlation function at 100h^{-1} Mpc separation that is an excellent match to the predicted shape and location of the imprint of the recombination-epoch acoustic oscillations on the low-redshift clustering of matter.

notes: Result type is measurement: the title says "Detection", but the abstract does not say "first", so first_detection is not used. The paper used SDSS-I spectroscopy of luminous red galaxies.
result:sdss-lrg-baryon-acoustic-peak-200.summary_technical: Large-scale correlation function of 46,748 SDSS luminous red galaxies (3816 deg², 0.16<z<0.47): a well-detected acoustic peak at 100 h⁻¹ Mpc; distance ratio to z=0.35 and z=1089 to 4% and absolute distance to z=0.35 to 5%; Ωm h² to 8%.
result:sdss-lrg-baryon-acoustic-peak-200.why_it_matters: The abstract says the detection demonstrates linear growth of structure by gravitational instability between z=1000 and the present, and that the acoustic peak provides a standard ruler for cosmological distance.

claim.quote: Therefore, we have measured the K-series x rays of kaonic hydrogen atoms at the DAΦNE electron-positron collider of Laboratori Nazionali di Frascati, and have determined the most precise values of the strong-interaction energy-level shift and width of the 1s atomic state.

result:siddharta-kaonic-hydrogen-shift-w.summary_technical: SIDDHARTA at DAΦNE (2009 data): kaonic hydrogen K-series X-rays with large-area silicon drift detectors; 1s strong-interaction shift ε = −283 ± 36 (stat) ± 6 (syst) eV and width Γ = 541 ± 89 (stat) ± 22 (syst) eV (Phys. Lett. B 704 (2011) 113).
result:siddharta-kaonic-hydrogen-shift-w.why_it_matters: The abstract describes the shift and width as the most precise values determined and says they provide vital constraints on the theoretical description of the low-energy antikaon-nucleon interaction.

claim.quote: We report a new high-precision measurement of kaonic hydrogen X-ray transitions performed by the SIDDHARTA-2 experiment

result:siddharta2-kaonic-hydrogen-shift-.summary_technical: SIDDHARTA-2 at DAΦNE: kaonic hydrogen X-ray transitions from 237 pb⁻¹ taken from December 2023 to February 2024 and April to May 2024; 1s shift ε = −303.0 ± 17.0 (stat.) ± 2.5 (syst.) eV and width Γ = 607 ± 62 (stat.) ± 6 (syst.) eV, improving the precision by about a factor of two over SIDDHARTA.
result:siddharta2-kaonic-hydrogen-shift-.why_it_matters: The abstract says the values are the most precise determination to date and tighten the experimental constraints on the low-energy antikaon-nucleon interaction and the Λ(1405) description.

claim.quote: the first weeks of operation in the new underground laboratory of Rustrel-Pays d'Apt already provide a sensitivity to axially-coupled Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs) competitive with leading experiments

notes: Date: first arXiv submission (v1, 28 Jan 2000); the abstract quoted is that of the latest arXiv version (v3, last revised 29 Sep 2000).
result:simple-first-limits-2000.summary_technical: First SIMPLE modules of about 15 g active mass; the abstract gives no numerical limit and says the data sample was small and statistically limited.
result:simple-first-limits-2000.why_it_matters: The abstract says the result confirms superheated droplet detectors as a convenient, low-cost alternative for WIMP detection.

claim.quote: The combined results yield a contour minimum of \sigma_{p} = 4.2 x 10^-3 pb at 35 GeV/c^2 on the spin-dependent sector of WIMP-proton interactions, the most restrictive to date from a direct search experiment

notes: Date: the latest arXiv version (v3, 9 Apr 2012), whose abstract is quoted; the arXiv comment on it reads 'revised, PRL-accepted version with slightly weakened limit contours', so the first submission (v1, 15 Jun 2011) is not the version quoted.
result:simple-phase-ii-final-2012.summary_technical: Two run stages of 15 SDDs, the second with improved neutron shielding; revised nucleation efficiency. Contour minima: sigma_p(SD) = 4.2e-3 pb and sigma_p(SI) = 3.6e-6 pb at 35 GeV/c^2. Published as Phys. Rev. Lett. 108, 201302 (2012).
result:simple-phase-ii-final-2012.why_it_matters: The abstract says the result overlaps for the first time results previously obtained only indirectly. The data were re-analysed in the 2014 paper (arXiv:1404.4309).

claim.quote: In combination with the results of the neutron-spin sensitive XENON10 experiment, these results yield a limit of |a_p| < 0.32 for M_W = 50 GeV/c2 on the spin-dependent sector of weakly interacting massive particle-nucleus interactions

notes: Date: the latest arXiv version (v4, 20 Oct 2010), whose abstract is quoted; the arXiv comment on it reads '4 pages, 4 figures; PRL-accepted version with corrected SI contour (Fig. 4)', so the first submission (v1, 15 Mar 2010) is not the version quoted.
result:simple-phase-ii-first-results-201.summary_technical: 14.1 kg d with 15 detectors of 0.208 kg total active mass; |a_p| < 0.32 at 50 GeV/c^2 (with XENON10); spin-independent limit 2.3e-5 pb at 45 GeV/c^2.
result:simple-phase-ii-first-results-201.why_it_matters: The abstract states a 50% reduction in the previously allowed region of the phase space formerly defined by XENON, KIMS and PICASSO.

claim.quote: provides new contour minima of $\sigma_{p}$ = 4.3 $\times$ 10$^{-3}$ pb at 35 GeV/c$^{2}$ in the spin-dependent sector of WIMP-proton interactions and $\sigma_{N}$ = 3.6 $\times$ 10$^{-6}$ pb at 35 GeV/c$^{2}$ in the spin-independent sector

result:simple-phase-ii-reanalysis-2014.summary_technical: Removal of the 1.94 kg d Stage 1 installation data reduces the science exposure from 20.18 to 18.24 kg d; detection efficiency better than 97% (95% C.L.) and recoil identification better than 99%; the results are re-examined with respect to the fluorine spin and halo parameters.
result:simple-phase-ii-reanalysis-2014.why_it_matters: The abstract describes the paper as the detailed account of the Phase II detectors, instrumentation, analysis and data selection; it supersedes the 2012 numbers for the same data.

claim.quote: We report an improved SIMPLE experiment comprising four superheated droplet detectors with a total exposure of 0.42 kgd. The result yields ~ factor 10 improvement in the previously-reported results

result:simple-results-2005.summary_technical: Measurement with four of a seven-module test, in the GESA area of the LSBB at 1500 m.w.e.; the abstract compares the spin-dependent coupling restrictions with the larger NAIAD/CDMS/ZEPLIN searches.
result:simple-results-2005.why_it_matters: The abstract says that despite the low exposure the result restricts spin-dependent couplings almost as much as the larger-exposure NAIAD, CDMS and ZEPLIN searches.

claim.quote: Evidence for oscillation of atmospheric neutrinos

result:sk-atmospheric-oscillation-eviden.summary_technical: 33.0 kiloton-year (535-day) exposure; a zenith-angle-dependent muon-neutrino deficit inconsistent with expectations based on calculations of the atmospheric neutrino flux, consistent with two-flavour νμ↔ντ oscillation. The paper's title is 'Evidence for oscillation of atmospheric neutrinos'.
result:sk-atmospheric-oscillation-eviden.why_it_matters: The Super-Kamiokande history page says the collaboration discovered compelling evidence of neutrino oscillations, overturning the long-held assumption that neutrinos are massless, and that this discovery eventually led to Kamioka's second Nobel Prize in Physics.

claim.quote: We report the search result for the Diffuse Supernova Neutrino Background (DSNB) in neutrino energies beyond 9.3 MeV in the gadolinium-loaded Super-Kamiokande (SK) detector with 22,500x956.2 m^3·day exposure.

result:sk-dsnb-limit-2025.summary_technical: DSNB search using 552.2 days of SK-VI (0.01% Gd) and 404.0 days of SK-VII (0.03% Gd) data through September 2023, with two new machine-learning neutron-detection algorithms with Gd, an improved atmospheric-background reduction technique and two parallel statistical approaches. No significant excess over background predictions was found in the spectrum-independent analysis, and 90% C.L. upper limits on the astrophysical electron anti-neutrino flux (neutrino energies beyond 9.3 MeV) were set. A spectral fit exhibited a ~1.2σ disagreement with the null DSNB hypothesis, comparable to a previous result from 5823 days of all SK pure-water phases.
result:sk-dsnb-limit-2025.why_it_matters: The paper describes the diffuse supernova neutrino background as the cumulative neutrino flux from all past supernovae in the Universe, and says the magnitude and shape of that flux provide unique information about the cosmic history of massive star formation.

claim.quote: We report the first search result for the flux of astrophysical electron antineutrinos for energies O(10) MeV in the gadolinium-loaded Super-Kamiokande (SK) detector. ... No significant excess over the expected background in the observed events is found for the neutrino energies below 31.3 MeV. Thus, the flux upper limits are placed at the 90% confidence level.

result:sk-gd-first-antineutrino-search-2.summary_technical: Initial stage of SK-Gd (26 Aug 2020 - 1 Jun 2022): 22.5×552 kton·day exposure at 0.01% Gd mass concentration, searching for astrophysical electron antineutrinos via inverse beta decay with enhanced neutron tagging. No significant excess over the expected background below 31.3 MeV; flux upper limits placed at the 90% confidence level. The paper calls this the first search result for the flux of astrophysical electron antineutrinos for energies O(10) MeV in the gadolinium-loaded detector; limits and sensitivities are already comparable with the previous pure-water SK result (22.5×2970 kton·day).
result:sk-gd-first-antineutrino-search-2.why_it_matters: The paper describes this as the first search result for the flux of astrophysical electron antineutrinos for energies O(10) MeV in the gadolinium-loaded Super-Kamiokande detector, and says the limits and sensitivities are already comparable with the previous pure-water result owing to the enhanced neutron tagging.

claim.quote: Solar neutrino measurements using the full data period of Super-Kamiokande-IV

notes: key_value and key_value_text numbers were re-checked against the text of the paper (arXiv:2312.12907) on 2026-10-25 and match.
result:sk-solar-neutrino-measurement-202.summary_technical: Combines SK-I through SK-IV (5,805 live days total); SK-IV alone contributes 2,970 days (Oct. 2008 - May 2018) and 65,443 +390/−388 (stat.) ± 925 (syst.) solar-neutrino events. 8B flux (2.314 ± 0.014 ± 0.040)×10⁶ cm⁻² s⁻¹ for SK-IV (assuming no neutrino oscillations) and (2.336 ± 0.011 ± 0.043)×10⁶ cm⁻² s⁻¹ combined with all SK phases up to SK-IV. From all solar experiments including SK's 5805-day data set, sin²θ12 = 0.306 ± 0.013 and Δm²21 = (6.10 +0.95 −0.81)×10⁻⁵ eV², a deviation of about 1.5σ from the Δm²21 obtained by KamLAND.
result:sk-solar-neutrino-measurement-202.why_it_matters: The paper tests for an energy-dependent 'upturn' of the electron-neutrino survival probability (from about 0.3 at high energy, above 10 MeV, to about 0.6 at low energy, below 1 MeV) and reports a solar Δm²21 that deviates by about 1.5σ from the KamLAND value.

claim.quote: This first direct observation of parity nonconservation in Moller scattering leads to a measurement of the electron's weak charge at low energy Q^e_W = -0.053 +/- 0.011.

result:slac-e158-parity-nonconservation-.summary_technical: A_PV = -175 +- 30 stat +- 20 syst ppb in fixed-target e-e (Moller) scattering, giving the electron's weak charge at low energy Q_W^e = -0.053 +- 0.011 and sin^2 theta_W(M_Z) (MSbar) = 0.2293 +- 0.0024 stat +- 0.0016 syst +- 0.0006 theory, consistent with the Standard Model.
result:slac-e158-parity-nonconservation-.why_it_matters: First direct observation of parity nonconservation in Moller scattering and a low-energy measurement of the electron's weak charge.

claim.quote: The measurement sets constraints on new physics effects at the TeV scale.

result:slac-e158-weak-mixing-angle-2005.summary_technical: A_PV = -131 +- 14 stat +- 10 syst ppb, giving sin^2 theta_W^eff = 0.2397 +- 0.0010 stat +- 0.0008 syst at Q^2 = 0.026 GeV^2; combined with Z-pole values, the running of the weak mixing angle is observed with over 6 sigma significance and TeV-scale new-physics effects are constrained.
result:slac-e158-weak-mixing-angle-2005.why_it_matters: A low-energy measurement of the weak mixing angle in a purely leptonic process, and the benchmark the MOLLER experiment aims to improve on by a factor of five.

claim.quote: Observed Behavior of Highly Inelastic Electron-Proton Scattering

notes: The paper title says "Observed Behavior", so the type is observation; the quark-model interpretation is in the Nobel press release, not the Letter's abstract.
date is the August 1968 Vienna presentation (month precision); the Letter appeared on 20 October 1969 and its companion (Bloom et al., PRL 23, 930) in the same issue.
result:slac-mit-bjorken-scaling-observat.summary_technical: Inelastic e-p scattering at 6 and 10 degrees: the structure function νW₂ can be expressed as a function of ω = 2Mν/q² alone within experimental errors for q² > 1 (GeV/c)² and ω > 4.
result:slac-mit-bjorken-scaling-observat.why_it_matters: The 1990 Nobel Prize in Physics went to Friedman, Kendall and Taylor "for their pioneering investigations concerning deep inelastic scattering of electrons on protons and bound neutrons, which have been of essential importance for the development of the quark model in particle physics".

claim.quote: The results of the measurement of the $e^+e^- \to n \bar{n}$ cross section and effective neutron timelike form factor are presented.

notes: Chosen as a recent SND headline result; SND also published many other exclusive hadron cross sections.
result:snd-neutron-form-factor-measureme.summary_technical: SND at VEPP-2000: e⁺e⁻ → n n̄ cross section and effective neutron timelike form factor for √s from 1891 to 2007 MeV; data of 2020-2021; neutron-antineutron events selected by time of flight in the nonmagnetic SND; measured cross section 0.4-0.6 nb, neutron form factor from 0.3 to 0.2.
result:snd-neutron-form-factor-measureme.why_it_matters: The abstract reports the cross section and the effective neutron timelike form factor over the energy range studied.

claim.quote: Comparison of φ^CC(ν_e) to the Super-Kamiokande Collaboration's precision value of φ^ES(ν_x) yields a 3.3 sigma difference, providing evidence that there is a non-electron flavor active neutrino component in the solar flux.

result:sno-cc-evidence-2001.summary_technical: Charged-current 8B solar-neutrino flux measured at SNO, φ^CC(νe) = 1.75 ± 0.07 (stat) +0.12/−0.11 (sys) ± 0.05(theor) × 10⁶ cm⁻² s⁻¹; comparison to Super-Kamiokande's elastic-scattering flux yields a 3.3σ difference, evidence for a non-electron-flavour active component in the solar 8B flux; total active flux 5.44±0.99 × 10⁶ cm⁻² s⁻¹, consistent with solar models.
result:sno-cc-evidence-2001.why_it_matters: The abstract says the comparison provides evidence for a non-electron-flavour active neutrino component in the solar flux, and that the total flux of active 8B neutrinos, 5.44 ± 0.99 ×10⁶ cm⁻² s⁻¹, is in close agreement with the predictions of solar models; the introduction notes that one explanation for the solar neutrino deficit is the transformation of electron neutrinos into other active flavours.

claim.quote: Direct Evidence for Neutrino Flavor Transformation from Neutral-Current Interactions in the Sudbury Neutrino Observatory

result:sno-nc-evidence-2002.summary_technical: Observations of neutral-current (NC) interactions on deuterium. Using the NC, elastic-scattering and charged-current reactions and assuming the standard 8B shape (5 MeV kinetic-energy threshold), the electron-neutrino component of the 8B flux is 1.76±0.05(stat)±0.09(syst) ×10⁶ cm⁻² s⁻¹ and the non-electron-neutrino component is 3.41±0.45(stat)+0.48/−0.45(syst) ×10⁶ cm⁻² s⁻¹, 5.3 standard deviations above zero; the total flux measured with the NC reaction, 5.09 (+0.44/−0.43 stat, +0.46/−0.43 syst) ×10⁶ cm⁻² s⁻¹, is consistent with solar models.
result:sno-nc-evidence-2002.why_it_matters: The title calls the result direct evidence for neutrino flavor transformation, and the abstract says the non-electron-neutrino component, 5.3 standard deviations above zero, provides strong evidence for solar electron neutrino flavor transformation; the total flux measured with the NC reaction is consistent with solar models.

claim.quote: A search for disappearance of antineutrinos to a sterile state has been conducted using complementary model-dependent frequentist and Bayesian fits, providing constraints on the allowed region of the Reactor Antineutrino Anomaly.

result:solid-very-short-baseline-search-.summary_technical: 280 reactor-on days (55 MW mean power) and 172 reactor-off days; 29,479 +- 603 (stat.) candidates (105/day, S/B 0.27); model-dependent frequentist and Bayesian disappearance fits constrain the RAA allowed region.
result:solid-very-short-baseline-search-.why_it_matters: The first physics result from a very-short-baseline experiment using a highly granular 6Li/PVT detector at a highly enriched uranium reactor.
