claim.quote: The effects of oscillations of atmospheric νµ are observed in the 5.90 fiducial kiloton-year exposure of the Soudan 2 detector.

result:soudan-2-atmospheric-neutrino-osc.summary_technical: Unbinned maximum-likelihood analysis of the neutrino L/E distribution (Feldman-Cousins) of the 5.90 fiducial kt-yr exposure: probability of no oscillation 5.8e-4; 90 % CL allowed region consistent with Super-Kamiokande.
result:soudan-2-atmospheric-neutrino-osc.why_it_matters: A second, independent detector technology (a tracking calorimeter rather than water Cherenkov) seeing atmospheric-neutrino oscillations.

claim.quote: For proton decay into the fully visible final states µ+ K0s and e+ K0s , zero and one event candidates are observed respectively. The lifetime lower limits (τ /B) thus implied are 1.5 × 1032 years and 1.2 × 1032 years, respectively.

result:soudan-2-nucleon-decay-lepton-k0-.summary_technical: 5.52 kt-yr total (4.41 kt-yr fiducial) exposure of the 963 t calorimeter: zero (mu+ K0s) and one (e+ K0s) candidate; lifetime lower limits tau/B > 1.5e32 and 1.2e32 yr; limits also for l+ K0l and n to nu K0s.
result:soudan-2-nucleon-decay-lepton-k0-.why_it_matters: The paper notes that final states with strange mesons are expected in supersymmetric grand unified models, with predicted lifetimes of about 10^31 to 10^32 years; these limits reach that range.

claim.quote: We present measurements of the temperature and E-mode polarization angular power spectra of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) from observations of 4% of the sky with SPT-3G, the current camera on the South Pole Telescope (SPT).

result:spt-3g-d1-power-spectra-cosmology.summary_technical: SPT-3G D1 (2019-2020 Main field, 4% of sky): TT/TE/EE spectra; LCDM parameters consistent with Planck and ACT-DR6; H0 = 66.66 +/- 0.60 km/s/Mpc (6.2 sigma from SH0ES); SPT+ACT+Planck H0 = 67.19 +/- 0.38, sigma_8 = 0.8137 +/- 0.0037; 2.8 sigma CMB-DESI DR2 BAO difference in LCDM.
result:spt-3g-d1-power-spectra-cosmology.why_it_matters: The abstract says that for the first time "combined ground-based (SPT+ACT) CMB primary and lensing data have reached Planck's constraining power on some parameters, a milestone for CMB cosmology".

claim.quote: We report the four most significant SPT detections of SZ clusters in this field, three of which were previously unknown and, therefore, represent the first galaxy clusters discovered with an SZ survey.

result:spt-first-sz-selected-clusters-20.summary_technical: SPT 40 deg^2 BCS field, two seasons at 95/150/225 GHz: four clusters detected at >5 sigma in the 150 GHz map, three new, with SZ spectrum confirmed in the 95 and 225 GHz maps and optical confirmation (z ~ 0.4 and z > ~ 0.8).
result:spt-first-sz-selected-clusters-20.why_it_matters: The abstract says these first four clusters demonstrate "that SZ surveys, and the SPT in particular, can be an effective means for finding galaxy clusters".

claim.quote: In this Letter we present the first detection of gravitational lensing B modes, using first-season data from the polarization-sensitive receiver on the South Pole Telescope (SPTpol).

result:sptpol-b-mode-lensing-first-detec.summary_technical: SPTpol first season: E modes combined with a Herschel-SPIRE CIB lensing-potential estimate form a lensing B-mode template; correlation with the measured B modes at 7.7 sigma, amplitude and scale dependence as expected.
result:sptpol-b-mode-lensing-first-detec.why_it_matters: The abstract says the lensing B-mode signal "provides a measure of the projected mass distribution over the entire observable Universe and also acts as a contaminant for the measurement of primordial gravity-wave signals".

claim.quote: central Au+Au collisions at RHIC produce dense, rapidly thermalizing matter characterized by: (1) initial energy densities above the critical values predicted by lattice QCD for establishment of a Quark-Gluon Plasma (QGP); (2) nearly ideal fluid flow

notes: Recorded with the collaboration's own title wording and result_type 'measurement', never 'discovery' or 'observation': the abstract hedges that the measurements themselves do not yet establish unequivocal evidence for a transition to this new form of matter.
result:star-perfect-liquid-whitepaper-20.summary_technical: STAR's 2005 critical assessment (Nucl. Phys. A 757, 102-183) reviews the most important results of the first three years of RHIC nucleus-nucleus collisions, with emphasis on STAR, and compares them with theory. The comparison suggests that central Au+Au collisions produce dense, rapidly thermalizing matter with (1) initial energy densities above the lattice-QCD critical values for QGP formation, (2) nearly ideal fluid flow, established most probably before hadron formation, and (3) opacity to jets. The collaboration states that the measurements themselves do not yet establish unequivocal evidence for a transition to this new form of matter, and it poses open questions and suggests additional measurements.
result:star-perfect-liquid-whitepaper-20.why_it_matters: A critical assessment by the STAR Collaboration of the RHIC evidence for a quark-gluon plasma: it says many of the observations are consistent with models incorporating QGP formation in the early collision stages and have not found ready explanation in a hadronic framework, but that the measurements themselves do not yet establish unequivocal evidence for a transition, and it lists open questions and additional measurements needed to conclude definitively that thermalized, deconfined quark-gluon matter has been produced.

claim.quote: The best-fit point of the reactor antineutrino anomaly is rejected at more than 99.9% C.L.

result:stereo-179-days-sterile-neutrino-.summary_technical: Direct comparison of the antineutrino spectra of all cells (largely independent of any flux prediction) with 179 d reactor-on and 235 d reactor-off data: compatible with the null oscillation hypothesis; RAA best fit rejected at > 99.9 % CL.
result:stereo-179-days-sterile-neutrino-.why_it_matters: One of the three reactor experiments (with PROSPECT and DANSS) that closed most of the allowed region for an eV-scale sterile neutrino explanation of the reactor anomaly.

claim.quote: the same data reject the hypothesis of a light sterile neutrino

result:stereo-235u-spectrum-sterile-reje.summary_technical: Full STEREO data set (October 2017 - November 2020): accurate 235U antineutrino energy spectrum that confirms the spectral anomalies, while the segmented detector at ~10 m rejects the light sterile-neutrino hypothesis.
result:stereo-235u-spectrum-sterile-reje.why_it_matters: A new reference measurement of the 235U antineutrino spectrum and a strong disfavouring of the sterile-neutrino explanation of the reactor anomalies.

claim.quote: We currently hold the world record for the highest instantaneous luminosity ever achieved at a particle accelerator: 5.319 x 1034 cm−2s−1 achieved on June 30, 2026.

notes: Earlier values from other sources: 2.22 × 10³⁴ cm⁻² s⁻¹ on 15 June 2020 (KEK IPNS release, https://www2.kek.jp/ipns/en/release/20200626/: "At 20:34 on 15th June 2020, SuperKEKB achieved the world’s highest instantaneous luminosity for a colliding-beam accelerator, setting a record of 2.22×1034 cm-2 s-1.") and a peak of 5.1 × 10³⁴ cm⁻² s⁻¹ (Belle II input to the 2025 European Strategy update, https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.24155: "SuperKEKB reached a peak luminosity of 5.1×1034 cm−2 s−1"). These are separate records, not recorded as separate results.
Attributed to experiment:belle-ii because the atlas has no result owner for a bare accelerator; the machine is accelerator:superkekb.
result:superkekb-luminosity-world-record.summary_technical: SuperKEKB reached a peak instantaneous luminosity of 5.319 × 10³⁴ cm⁻² s⁻¹ on 30 June 2026, which the Belle II collaboration states is the highest ever achieved at a particle accelerator. Earlier values from other sources are in the notes (2.22 × 10³⁴ on 15 June 2020; 5.1 × 10³⁴ quoted in March 2025). The Belle II input to the 2025 European Strategy update describes the machine's novel nano-beam scheme, based on a large horizontal crossing angle.
result:superkekb-luminosity-world-record.why_it_matters: Instantaneous luminosity is the collision rate the machine delivers to the Belle II detector. The Belle II input to the 2025 European Strategy update states a plan to reach a peak luminosity of 1.0 × 10³⁵ cm⁻² s⁻¹ by 2026 and an integrated luminosity of 50 ab⁻¹; the 2026 record, 5.319 × 10³⁴ cm⁻² s⁻¹, is below that peak-luminosity goal.

claim.quote: A time alignment of about 120 ps and a time resolution around 615 ps have been achieved. Concerning the energy, an alignment of 7.5% has been obtained.

result:supernemo-demonstrator-calorimete.summary_technical: First time and energy calibration of the Demonstrator calorimeter with gamma rays from calibration sources and ambient radioactivity: time alignment ~120 ps, time resolution ~615 ps, energy alignment 7.5 %; to be improved when electrons from calibration sources are added.
result:supernemo-demonstrator-calorimete.why_it_matters: A step towards the first physics data of the SuperNEMO Demonstrator; no physics result has been published yet.

claim.quote: The overall results may be interpreted as an upper limit on the absolute value of the neutron EDM of |d_n| < 2.9 x 10^{-26} e cm (90% CL).

result:sussex-ral-ill-nedm-limit-2006.summary_technical: ILL search for the neutron EDM using stored ultracold neutrons and a cohabiting atomic-mercury magnetometer, two independent analyses: |d_n| < 2.9 x 10^-26 e cm (90% CL).
result:sussex-ral-ill-nedm-limit-2006.why_it_matters: The abstract states that spurious signals from magnetic-field fluctuations were reduced to insignificance by the cohabiting mercury magnetometer and that geometric-phase false EDMs were carefully studied.

claim.quote: We obtain a net result of ... which may be interpreted as a slightly revised upper limit on the magnitude of the EDM of

result:sussex-ral-ill-nedm-revised-limit.summary_technical: Re-analysis including gravity-depolarisation effects, an improved neutron spectrum calculation and conservative systematics: d_n = -0.21 ± 1.82 x 10^-26 e cm, |d_n| < 3.0 x 10^-26 e cm (90% CL) or 3.6 x 10^-26 e cm (95% CL).
result:sussex-ral-ill-nedm-revised-limit.why_it_matters: The abstract calls it the first detailed and comprehensive analysis of the experimental results that set the current world sensitivity limit on the neutron EDM.

claim.quote: Here the T2K collaboration reports a measurement that favors large enhancement of the neutrino oscillation probability, excluding values of dCP which result in a large enhancement of the observed anti-neutrino oscillation probability at three standard deviations (3 sigma). ... Our results show an indication of CP violation in the lepton sector.

result:t2k-cp-violation-constraint-2020.summary_technical: Combined neutrino- and antineutrino-mode appearance and disappearance data give 3σ intervals for δCP of [−3.41, −0.03] (normal ordering) and [−2.54, −0.32] (inverted ordering): δCP = 0 is excluded at 3σ in both orderings, π only for the inverted ordering. The collaboration reports 'an indication of CP violation in the lepton sector'.
result:t2k-cp-violation-constraint-2020.why_it_matters: It excludes the CP-conserving value δCP = 0 at 3σ — an indication that neutrinos and antineutrinos oscillate differently (CP violation in the lepton sector), a possible ingredient of the matter-antimatter asymmetry of the universe through leptogenesis. The paper closes by saying that future measurements with larger data samples will determine whether the leptonic CP violation is larger than the quark-sector CP violation.

claim.quote: The T2K experiment has observed electron neutrino appearance in a muon neutrino beam produced 295 km from the Super-Kamiokande detector with a peak energy of 0.6 GeV. A total of 28 electron neutrino events were detected with an energy distribution consistent with an appearance signal, corresponding to a significance of 7.3σ when compared to 4.92 ± 0.55 expected background events.

notes: T2K's own news item of 3 December 2013 (https://t2k-experiment.org/?p=1967) describes the paper as "reporting the definitive observation of electron neutrino appearance in a high-purity muon neutrino beam"; the abstract itself says "The T2K experiment has observed electron neutrino appearance".
result:t2k-electron-neutrino-appearance-.summary_technical: 28 νe candidate events at Super-Kamiokande (295 km, peak energy 0.6 GeV) against 4.92 ± 0.55 expected background events: 7.3σ. Best-fit sin²2θ13 = 0.140 (+0.038/−0.032) for normal ordering and 0.170 (+0.045/−0.037) for inverted ordering at δCP = 0, assuming |Δm²32| = 2.4×10⁻³ eV² and sin²θ23 = 0.5; combined with reactor θ13 measurements, some values of δCP are disfavored at the 90% CL.
result:t2k-electron-neutrino-appearance-.why_it_matters: The paper's introduction notes that, to date, there had not been an observation of the explicit appearance of a different neutrino flavor from neutrinos of another flavor through neutrino oscillations; the appearance signal depends on θ13 and δCP, and combining with reactor θ13 data the paper finds that some values of δCP are disfavored at the 90% CL.

claim.quote: The T2K experiment observes indications of νμ→νe appearance in data accumulated with 1.43×10²⁰ protons on target. Six events pass all selection criteria at the far detector. ... the probability to observe six or more candidate events is 7×10⁻³, equivalent to 2.5σ significance.

notes: Classified as a measurement because the collaboration's own wording is 'indications' (title: 'Indication of Electron Neutrino Appearance'); 2.5σ is also below the conventional 3σ evidence threshold (the T2K Nature paper, arXiv:1910.03887, calls a 99.73% (3σ) confidence level 'considered as evidence in the particle physics community').
result:t2k-electron-neutrino-indication-.summary_technical: Six events pass all selection criteria at the far detector (Super-Kamiokande) in data corresponding to 1.43×10²⁰ protons on target; the expected number is 1.5 ± 0.3 (syst.) for |Δm²23| = 2.4×10⁻³ eV², sin²2θ23 = 1 and sin²2θ13 = 0. The probability to observe six or more candidate events is 7×10⁻³, equivalent to 2.5σ. At 90% C.L. the data are consistent with 0.03 (0.04) < sin²2θ13 < 0.28 (0.34) for δCP = 0 and a normal (inverted) hierarchy.
result:t2k-electron-neutrino-indication-.why_it_matters: The collaboration's 15 June 2011 press release says that, for the first time, it was possible to observe an indication that muon neutrinos are able to transform into electron neutrinos over a distance of 295 km; the paper itself concludes that more data are required to firmly establish νe appearance and to better determine the angle θ13.

claim.quote: A total of 163.5 excess events were detected, with a statistical significance of 8.5 sigma.

result:taiga-crab-nebula-detection-2023.summary_technical: Random-forest gamma/hadron separation on 85 h of first-IACT data at mean zenith 33.5 degrees, threshold 6 TeV; 163.5 excess events at 8.5 sigma; power-law spectrum above 6 TeV with index -2.74 ± 0.16.
result:taiga-crab-nebula-detection-2023.why_it_matters: The abstract states the analysis tracked the Crab Nebula for 85 hours and detected a significant signal with the first TAIGA IACT, a step toward the hybrid HiSCORE-plus-IACT technique aimed at PeV gamma rays.

claim.locator: Phys. Lett. B 86 (1979) 243, paper title (Crossref record)
claim.quote: Evidence for planar events in e+e− annihilation at high energies

notes: The paper title says "Evidence", so result_type is evidence; DESY and CERN Courier call the 1979 PETRA three-jet results the discovery of the gluon, but the TASSO paper title is followed.
The abstract of the Phys. Lett. B paper could not be retrieved (publisher site blocks automated access); the claim is the paper title only.
result:tasso-planar-events-evidence-1979.summary_technical: TASSO paper 'Evidence for planar events in e⁺e⁻ annihilation at high energies' (Phys. Lett. B 86 (1979) 243): hard non-collinear gluon bremsstrahlung seen as planar three-jet topologies at PETRA energies above about 22 GeV. The first event (Event 13177, Run 447) was shown by B. Wiik at Neutrino 79, Bergen, on 18 June 1979; TASSO scientists Söding, Wiik, Wolf and Wu received the 1995 EPS HEPP Prize.
result:tasso-planar-events-evidence-1979.why_it_matters: DESY describes the three-jet events as the signature expected if a quark radiates a gluon, the carrier of the strong force; the four PETRA collaborations all showed three-jet analyses at the August 1979 Lepton-Photon Symposium.

claim.quote: In our final dataset, we report a world-leading energy resolution of 258.5$\pm$0.4 meV in the 1 mm thick detector.

notes: Attached to experiment:spice as well: the TAUP 2025 slides list this resolution under SPICE.
result:tesseract-bulk-silicon-phonon-bur.summary_technical: Measurements for 12 days after cooldown of 1 cm^2 silicon athermal-phonon detectors differing only in substrate thickness (1 mm vs 4 mm): channel-correlated shot noise and near-threshold shared LEE relax with time and scale linearly with thickness, pointing to the bulk substrate; the sub-threshold noise energy scale is estimated at 0.68 +- 0.38 meV; final baseline resolution 258.5 +- 0.4 meV (1 mm detector).
result:tesseract-bulk-silicon-phonon-bur.why_it_matters: The paper argues these bursts are likely a significant source of quasiparticle poisoning in superconducting qubits, and that the low energy excess is a limiting background for low-threshold dark matter detectors.

claim.quote: With an exposure of 0.233g $\times$ 12 hours, we place the most stringent constraints on dark matter masses between 44 and 87 MeV/$c^2$, with the lowest unexplored cross section of 4 $\times 10^{-32}$ cm$^2$ at 87 MeV/$c^2$.

notes: Attached to experiment:spice as well: the TAUP 2025 slides list this limit under SPICE ('Dark Matter limit published: arXiv:2503.03683v2'); the paper itself says only 'TESSERACT Collaboration'.
The abstract prints the resolution as '361.5 +- 0.4 MeV/c^2' (a unit slip in the abstract; the paper's resolution is a few hundred meV), so it is not used as a number here.
result:tesseract-first-limits-2025.summary_technical: Spin-independent dark matter-nucleon limit from a 1 cm^2 x 1 mm (0.233 g) silicon athermal-phonon detector with two-channel rejection of sensor-coupled low-energy backgrounds, operated above ground at UC Berkeley; exposure 0.233 g x 12 hours; a conservative salting technique reaches the lowest mass probed. A prototype of the TESSERACT programme (a SPICE-type detector per the TAUP 2025 slides), not the Modane setup.
result:tesseract-first-limits-2025.why_it_matters: The abstract states that the result reaches the lowest dark matter mass ever probed via a direct detection experiment, using a detector small enough to be scaled into the TESSERACT payload.

claim.quote: Here, we show that a silicon crystal glued to its holder exhibits a rate of low-energy phonon events that is more than two orders of magnitude larger than in a functionally identical crystal suspended from its holder in a low-stress state.

notes: Listed on the TESSERACT papers page; the TAUP 2025 slides cite it under SPICE ('suppress a stress induced LEE source from the holder'). The arXiv paper itself carries no collaboration tag.
result:tesseract-stress-induced-phonon-b.summary_technical: Comparison of a glued and a suspended silicon crystal: the excess phonon event rate in the glued crystal decreases with time since cooldown, consistent with relaxation of thermally induced stress between glue and crystal; relevant to quasiparticle poisoning in qubits and to the low-energy events of cryogenic calorimeters.
result:tesseract-stress-induced-phonon-b.why_it_matters: The abstract ties the stress mechanism to low-energy events seen in cryogenic calorimeters, one of the main limiting backgrounds for sub-GeV dark matter searches.

claim.quote: We derived new upper limits on couplings of electrons with the pseudoscalar and vector bosonic super-WIMPs in the sub-keV mass region, assuming they are the dominant contributions to the dark matter density of our galaxy.

result:texono-bosonic-dm-npcge-2019.summary_technical: 314.15 kg d from an n-type point-contact germanium detector at Kuo-Sheng; super-WIMPs absorbed in the detector give spectral peaks at their mass; no significant excess; limits on the electron couplings of pseudoscalar and vector bosons in the sub-keV mass region.
result:texono-bosonic-dm-npcge-2019.why_it_matters: Extends TEXONO's dark matter work from WIMP-nucleon scattering to absorption of light bosons.

claim.quote: We report new limits on spin-independent WIMP-nucleon interaction cross-section using 39.5 kg-days of data taken with a p-type point-contact germanium detector of 840 g fiducial mass at the Kuo-Sheng Reactor Neutrino Laboratory.

result:texono-pcge-wimp-limits-2013.summary_technical: p-type point-contact germanium (840 g fiducial, 926 g crystal) in an NaI(Tl) anti-Compton and plastic-veto shield at 30 m.w.e.; bulk-surface event differentiation calibrated with gamma sources and an n-type point-contact detector; part of the cross-section versus WIMP-mass space implied by various experiments is probed and excluded.
result:texono-pcge-wimp-limits-2013.why_it_matters: An independent germanium test of the CoGeNT low-mass region, from a different site and with a different background.

claim.quote: With a data acquisition live time of 0.338 kg-day at the Kuo-Sheng Laboratory, constraints on WIMPs in the galactic halo were derived. The limits improve over previous results on both the spin-independent WIMP-nucleon and the spin-dependent WIMP-neutron cross-sections for WIMP mass between 3-6 GeV.

result:texono-ulege-220ev-wimp-limits-20.summary_technical: Four-channel ultra-low-energy germanium detector, 5 g per channel, (220 +- 10) eV threshold at 50% efficiency; 0.338 kg d live time at Kuo-Sheng (30 m.w.e.); improved spin-independent and spin-dependent limits for 3-6 GeV/c^2; projections for full-scale experiments.
result:texono-ulege-220ev-wimp-limits-20.why_it_matters: First sub-keV germanium WIMP search; it showed the technique later adopted by CDEX and CoGeNT-type point-contact detectors.

claim.quote: This is the first detection of photons with $E>100$ TeV from an astrophysical source.

result:tibet-asgamma-crab-above-100-tev-.summary_technical: Tibet air-shower array with the underground water-Cherenkov muon-detector array: 99.92% of cosmic-ray background above 100 TeV suppressed by the muon criterion; 24 photon-like events with E > 100 TeV against 5.5 background events from the Crab Nebula, 5.6 sigma.
result:tibet-asgamma-crab-above-100-tev-.why_it_matters: The abstract says this is the first detection of photons above 100 TeV from an astrophysical source, using the muon number in an air shower to suppress 99.92% of the cosmic-ray background.

claim.quote: We report, for the first time, the long-awaited detection of diffuse gamma rays with energies between 100 TeV and 1 PeV in the Galactic disk.

notes: The significance is not stated in the abstract and is therefore not recorded.
The brief for this stream cited arXiv:1909.12535 for this paper; that identifier is an unrelated computer-science preprint. The Tibet ASgamma paper is arXiv:2104.05181.
result:tibet-asgamma-diffuse-subpev-gamm.summary_technical: Tibet AS + muon-detector array: diffuse gamma rays at 100 TeV - 1 PeV from the Galactic disk; all gamma rays above 398 TeV are seen away from known TeV sources and are compatible with the hadronic scenario (pi0 decay from proton-gas interactions), evidence that PeV cosmic rays are accelerated and spread in the Galactic disk.
result:tibet-asgamma-diffuse-subpev-gamm.why_it_matters: The abstract says this is strong evidence that cosmic rays are accelerated beyond PeV energies in the Galaxy and spread over the Galactic disk.

claim.quote: With a total exposure of 4.1 kg days, we derived the limits in the a_p-a_n (WIMP-nucleon couplings) plane and excluded a large part of the parameter space allowed by the UKDMC experiment.

result:tokyo-lif-bolometer-kamioka-2002.summary_technical: 168 g LiF bolometer array, 4.1 kg d (22 November 2001 to 12 January 2002), 2700 m.w.e.: limits in the WIMP-proton / WIMP-neutron coupling plane excluding a large part of the region allowed by UKDMC NaI results; spin-dependent proton cross-section limit improved by about a factor of 5 over the shallow-site pilot run (body of the paper).
result:tokyo-lif-bolometer-kamioka-2002.why_it_matters: First underground spin-dependent dark matter result with a fluorine bolometer in Japan, complementary to the sodium-iodide results.

claim.quote: With an exposure of 3.38 kg days, we derived the limits on the WIMP-nucleon coupling coefficients, ap and an . These limits confirmed and tightened those derived from our previous results with the lithium fluoride (LiF) bolometer.

result:tokyo-naf-bolometer-kamioka-2003.summary_technical: 176 g NaF bolometer array, 3.38 kg d (December 2002 to January 2003), 2700 m.w.e.: limits on a_p and a_n; the 23Na target is complementary to 19F and to the UKDMC NaI results.
result:tokyo-naf-bolometer-kamioka-2003.why_it_matters: A second target (sodium) closed part of the spin-dependent parameter space left open by the LiF result.

claim.locator: Phys. Lett. B 234 (1990) 525, paper title (Crossref record)
claim.quote: Measurement of the total hadronic cross sections in ... annihilation and determination of the standard model parameters

notes: The abstract could not be retrieved (publisher site blocks automated access); the claim is the paper title only. The summary sentences about the top quark and the R-ratio come from the KEK historian's overview of TRISTAN, not from this paper's abstract.
result:topaz-total-hadronic-cross-sectio.summary_technical: TOPAZ at TRISTAN: total hadronic cross sections in e⁺e⁻ annihilation and determination of standard-model parameters (Phys. Lett. B 234 (1990) 525-533). Kondo (KEK) notes that all TRISTAN results were consistent with the standard model and showed no sign of the top quark; the R-ratio's gentle rise was explained by γ-Z⁰ interference.
result:topaz-total-hadronic-cross-sectio.why_it_matters: Kondo notes that the three TRISTAN groups' first results in 1988 were all consistent with the standard model and showed no sign of the top quark, because TRISTAN's energy was too low to produce top-quark pairs.

claim.quote: By achieving a low energy threshold of 1 keV$_{ee}$ and a background level of 80 counts keV$^{-1}$ Kg$^{-1}$ day$^{-1}$ in the region from 1 to 7 keV$_{ee}$, the experiment demonstrates its potential to search for low-mass WIMPs.

result:trex-dm-achievements-2023.summary_technical: Data-taking campaigns with argon and neon mixtures at 1 to 4 bar since the 2018 commissioning; the paper also describes the Micromegas + GEM readout under development and the alpha-detector programme for material selection.
result:trex-dm-achievements-2023.why_it_matters: The abstract says the two main challenges are reducing both the background level and the energy threshold.

claim.quote: we successfully detected both characteristic emissions from $^{37}$Ar decay (2.82 keV and 270 eV) and achieved unprecedented energy threshold performance in TREX-DM, approaching the single-electron ionization energy of argon.

notes: Date: first arXiv submission (v1, 7 Oct 2025); the abstract quoted is that of the latest arXiv version (v2, last revised 23 Dec 2025).
result:trex-dm-argon37-calibration-2025.summary_technical: 37Ar produced by fast-neutron activation of CaO powder at the HiSPANoS facility (CNA, Seville), O(1) kBq; detected in the TREX-DM chamber with a combined GEM-Micromegas readout. Published in J. Cosmol. Astropart. Phys. 2026 (April).
result:trex-dm-argon37-calibration-2025.why_it_matters: The abstract frames this as a low-energy threshold demonstration for low-mass dark matter searches.

claim.quote: The background model developed for the detector presently installed in Canfranc points to levels from 1 to 10 counts keV-1 kg-1 d-1 in the region of interest, making TREX-DM competitive in the search for low-mass WIMPs.

notes: Date: first arXiv submission (v1, 11 Dec 2018); the abstract quoted is that of the latest arXiv version (v2, last revised 22 Sep 2019).
result:trex-dm-background-assessment-201.summary_technical: Geant4 model using measured gamma, muon and neutron fluxes at the LSC and assayed component activities; the abstract quotes 1 to 10 counts keV-1 kg-1 d-1 with a roadmap to 0.1 counts keV-1 kg-1 d-1. A model prediction, not a measurement. Published as Eur. Phys. J. C 79 (2019) 782.
result:trex-dm-background-assessment-201.why_it_matters: The abstract says a roadmap to decrease the background further is underway.

claim.quote: We set a new upper limits to the neutrino mixing matrix element U^2_{e4} which improve existing limits by a factor from 2 to 5 in the mass range 0.1-2 keV.

result:troitsk-kev-sterile-neutrino-limi.summary_technical: First measurement of the tritium beta spectrum over 16-18.6 keV electron energy; upper limits on |Ue4|² for sterile-neutrino masses 0.1-2 keV, a factor 2-5 better than previous limits.
result:troitsk-kev-sterile-neutrino-limi.why_it_matters: Shows the tritium-endpoint technique can search for keV sterile neutrinos, a dark-matter candidate, and motivates the TRISTAN detector upgrade of KATRIN.

claim.quote: This gives an experimental upper sensitivity limit of mν < 2.2 eV , 95% C . L. and upper limit estimates mν < 2.12 eV , 95% C .L. for Bayesian statistics and mν < 2.05 eV , 95% C .L. for the Feldman and Cousins approach.

result:troitsk-neutrino-mass-limit-2011.summary_technical: Re-analysis of the 1994-2004 data with careful data selection: m² = -0.67 ± 2.53 eV²; sensitivity limit mν < 2.2 eV, Bayesian limit 2.12 eV and Feldman-Cousins limit 2.05 eV (95% CL).
result:troitsk-neutrino-mass-limit-2011.why_it_matters: A direct limit of about 2 eV on the electron-antineutrino mass, of similar size to the final Mainz result of 2.3 eV that the paper cites.

claim.quote: We present the all-particle energy spectrum, based on 7 seasons of operation.

result:tunka-133-energy-spectrum-2020.summary_technical: All-particle spectrum from the Cherenkov light flux at 200 m core distance, 7 seasons (2175 h of good-weather operation, about 1.4 × 10⁷ events), covering 6 × 10¹⁵ to 10¹⁸ eV.
result:tunka-133-energy-spectrum-2020.why_it_matters: The abstract describes the time and amplitude calibration and the event reconstruction methods and presents the all-particle spectrum over 6 × 10¹⁵ to 10¹⁸ eV; the TAIGA collaboration later reports features such as a change of index near 20 PeV.

claim.quote: A simultaneous measurement of the muon decay parameters {\rho}, {\delta}, and (P_{\mu}){\xi} tests the Standard Model (SM) in a purely leptonic process and provides improved limits for relevant extensions to the SM.

result:twist-muon-decay-parameters-2010.summary_technical: Simultaneous measurement of rho, delta and P_mu xi from the positron energy-angle spectrum of highly polarized muon decays; for the generalized left-right symmetric model |(g_R/g_L) zeta| < 0.020 and (g_L/g_R) m_2 > 578 GeV/c^2 (both 90% C.L.).
result:twist-muon-decay-parameters-2010.why_it_matters: The abstract says the measurement tests the Standard Model in a purely leptonic process and provides improved limits for relevant extensions of it.

claim.quote: Experimental Observation of Isolated Large Transverse Energy Electrons with Associated Missing Energy at sqrt(s)=540 GeV

result:ua1-w-boson-observation-1983.summary_technical: UA1 Collaboration, Phys. Lett. B 122 (1983) 103-116: isolated high-transverse-energy electrons with missing transverse energy at √s = 540 GeV, with the signature of a two-body decay of a particle of mass ~80 GeV/c² and read as p-p̄ → W± + X, W → e + ν. Six candidate events were presented by C. Rubbia at a CERN seminar on 20 January 1983; the discovery was announced at a CERN press conference on 25 January 1983.
result:ua1-w-boson-observation-1983.why_it_matters: CERN announced the discovery of the W boson on 25 January 1983; UA1 read its events as production of the charged W, the Intermediate Vector Boson of the unified theory of weak and electromagnetic interactions.

claim.locator: Title, Phys. Lett. B 126 (1983) 398 (facsimile at the cited URL)
claim.quote: Experimental Observation of Lepton Pairs of Invariant Mass Around 95 GeV/c^2 at the CERN SPS Collider

result:ua1-z-boson-observation-1983.summary_technical: UA1 Collaboration, Phys. Lett. B 126 (1983) 398: four e⁺e⁻ pairs and one μ⁺μ⁻ pair with the signature of a two-body decay of a particle of mass ~95 GeV/c²; the events fit well the hypothesis p-p̄ → Z⁰ + X with Z⁰ → l⁺ l⁻, where Z⁰ is the Intermediate Vector Boson postulated by the electroweak theories as the mediator of weak neutral currents.
result:ua1-z-boson-observation-1983.why_it_matters: The paper identifies the Z⁰ as the Intermediate Vector Boson postulated by the electroweak theories as the mediator of weak neutral currents, and CERN announced the discovery of the Z boson on 1 June 1983, after the W announcement of 25 January 1983.

claim.quote: Observation of Single Isolated Electrons of High Transverse Momentum in Events with Missing Transverse Energy at the CERN anti-p p Collider

result:ua2-w-boson-observation-1983.summary_technical: UA2 Collaboration, Phys. Lett. B 122 (1983) 476-485: four candidate events with a single isolated high-p_T electron and missing transverse energy, consistent with p-p̄ → W± + anything, W → e + ν. The result was presented by Luigi Di Lella at a CERN seminar (22 January 1983 per CERN's UA2 page; 'the following afternoon' after UA1's 20 January seminar per CERN's 2013 article), before the CERN announcement of the W discovery on 25 January 1983.
result:ua2-w-boson-observation-1983.why_it_matters: A second experiment at the CERN proton-antiproton collider reporting events consistent with W production: four candidate events in UA2, alongside UA1's six.

claim.quote: Evidence for Z0 -> e+ e- at the CERN anti-p p Collider

result:ua2-z-boson-evidence-1983.summary_technical: UA2 Collaboration, Phys. Lett. B 129 (1983) 130: from a search for electron pairs in p-p̄ collisions at √s = 550 GeV, eight events interpreted as p-p̄ → Z⁰ + anything with Z⁰ → e⁺e⁻ or e⁺e⁻γ, where Z⁰ is the neutral Intermediate Vector Boson postulated by the unified electroweak theory; four of the events are used to measure Mz = 91.9 ± 1.3 (stat) ± 1.4 (syst) GeV/c². Received 11 August 1983; issue dated 15 September 1983.
result:ua2-z-boson-evidence-1983.why_it_matters: A second CERN collider experiment's measurement of the Z⁰ mass from four of its eight Z⁰ → e⁺e⁻ candidate events, 91.9 ± 1.3 (stat) ± 1.4 (syst) GeV/c², published in the same year as UA1's Z paper.

claim.locator: Phys. Lett. B 117 (1982) 126, paper title (Crossref record)
claim.quote: Measurement of the proton-antiproton elastic and total cross section at a centre-of-mass energy of 540 GeV

notes: The abstract could not be retrieved (publisher site blocks automated access); the claim is the paper title only.
result:ua4-elastic-and-total-cross-secti.summary_technical: UA4 at the CERN SppS: p̄p elastic and total cross section at √s = 540 GeV (Phys. Lett. B 117 (1982) 126-130), from the experiment whose Greybook title is 'Measurement of elastic scattering in the Coulomb interference region at the CERN pbarp collider'.
result:ua4-elastic-and-total-cross-secti.why_it_matters: The paper title states the measurement of the elastic and total proton-antiproton cross sections at 540 GeV, the energy of the SppS collider in 1982.

claim.locator: Phys. Lett. B 167 (1986) 476, paper title (Crossref record)
claim.quote: Scaling violations in multiplicity distributions at 200 and 900 GeV

notes: The abstract could not be retrieved (publisher site blocks automated access); the claim is the paper title only.
result:ua5-multiplicity-scaling-violatio.summary_technical: UA5 at the CERN SppS: multiplicity distributions of charged particles in p̄p collisions at 200 and 900 GeV c.m. energy and their scaling violations (Phys. Lett. B 167 (1986) 476-480).
result:ua5-multiplicity-scaling-violatio.why_it_matters: The paper title reports scaling violations in the multiplicity distributions between 200 and 900 GeV.

claim.quote: the lifetime reported here (877.7 $\pm$ 0.7 (stat) +0.4/-0.2 (sys) s) is the first modern measurement of $\tau_n$ that does not require corrections larger than the quoted uncertainties.

result:ucntau-lifetime-2018.summary_technical: Polarized UCN levitated in an asymmetric magneto-gravitational trap with in situ detection: tau_n = 877.7 ± 0.7 stat +0.4/-0.2 syst s; the beam (887.7 ± 2.2 s) and bottle (878.5 ± 0.8 s) results differed by 3.9 sigma when the paper was written.
result:ucntau-lifetime-2018.why_it_matters: The abstract frames the result against a 3.9 standard deviation discrepancy between the beam and material-trap storage results.

claim.quote: Both techniques achieve consistent results and find a value $\tau_{n}=877.75\pm0.28_{\text{ stat}}+0.22/-0.16_{\text{ syst}}$~s.

result:ucntau-lifetime-2021.summary_technical: About 38 x 10^6 surviving UCN counted after storage in the magneto-gravitational trap over two campaigns (2017, 2018); three blinded analyses (paired long/short storage runs and a global likelihood fit with the beta-decay lifetime): tau_n = 877.75 ± 0.28 stat +0.22/-0.16 syst s.
result:ucntau-lifetime-2021.why_it_matters: The abstract says that with this sensitivity, neutron lifetime experiments now directly address the impact of recent refinements in our understanding of the standard model for neutron decay.

claim.quote: when all the data from UCNtau are averaged we report an updated value for the lifetime of 877.82+/-0.22 (statistical)+0.20-0.17 (systematic) s.

result:ucntau-lifetime-final-2024.summary_technical: Runs from 2020-2022: tau_n = 877.94 ± 0.37 s; combined with the earlier data the updated UCNtau lifetime is 877.82 ± 0.22 (stat) +0.20/-0.17 (syst) s, with improved monitor detectors, reduced upscattering corrections and four main UCN detector geometries.
result:ucntau-lifetime-final-2024.why_it_matters: The abstract says the goals were to better understand and quantify systematic uncertainties and to improve the statistical precision of the lifetime.

claim.quote: The results constitute the first observation of direct photons in ultrarelativistic heavy-ion collisions which could be significant for diagnosis of quark gluon plasma formation.

result:wa98-direct-photons-central-pb-pb.summary_technical: Direct-photon invariant yield in central 208Pb+208Pb collisions at 158A GeV extracted as a function of transverse momentum for 0.5 < pT < 4 GeV/c; a significant signal compared with statistical and systematic errors is seen at pT > 1.5 GeV/c (points at lower pT are upper limits).
result:wa98-direct-photons-central-pb-pb.why_it_matters: Direct photons escape the collision zone without further interaction, so they probe the hot early stage; the 2026 SPS review says the excess showed high temperatures (up to 200 MeV) were reached, consistent with QGP formation.

claim.quote: The specific activity measured for Ar-39 is 1.01 +/- 0.02(stat) +/- 0.08(syst) Bq per kg of natural Ar.

result:warp-argon-39-specific-activity-2.summary_technical: Specific activity of 39Ar in natural argon measured with the 2.3 l two-phase chamber operated for more than two years at LNGS (3,400 m w.e.).
result:warp-argon-39-specific-activity-2.why_it_matters: The abstract describes the detector as the WArP prototype for WIMP dark matter searches with argon as a target.

claim.quote: First physics results from this method are reported, based on a small 2.3 litre test chamber filled with natural Argon and an accumulated fiducial exposure of about 100 kg x day

notes: result_type is 'limit' because the paper's introduction states it reports a first upper limit; the abstract itself gives no limit value (the 2013 review quotes 1e-42 cm^2 for the WIMP-nucleon cross section but that number is not recorded here).
key_value_text is quoted from the paper's introduction (Sec. 1), not from the abstract.
result:warp-first-physics-results-2007.summary_technical: First WIMP-search results of the WArP method (simultaneous scintillation and ionisation signals) with a 2.3 l chamber of natural argon (96.5 kg d, 52.76 days live in the body of the paper). The body derives a 90% C.L. upper limit from zero events above 55 keV_ion and compares it with CDMS, EDELWEISS and CRESST; the abstract states no number.
result:warp-first-physics-results-2007.why_it_matters: The abstract says it supports the future validity of the method with isotopically purified 40Ar and with a much larger unit then under construction.

claim.quote: a detection is reported at the 9.0-sigma level, corresponding to a flux of 1.8 x 10 to the -11th photons sq cm/s above 0.7 TeV (with a factor of 1.5 uncertainty in both flux and energy)

notes: The Whipple page supports the statement that this was the first TeV gamma-ray source: "detected the first TeV gamma-ray source, the Crab Nebula in 1989".
result:whipple-crab-observation-1989.summary_technical: Selection of gamma-ray images by their predicted shape rejects more than 98 percent of the background; the Crab Nebula is detected at 9.0 sigma, flux 1.8e-11 photons cm-2 s-1 above 0.7 TeV, with less than 25 percent of the flux pulsed and no variability from months to years.
result:whipple-crab-observation-1989.why_it_matters: The Whipple page says the telescope "detected the first TeV gamma-ray source, the Crab Nebula in 1989" and that the collaboration pioneered the imaging atmospheric Cherenkov technique.

claim.quote: We report here the detection of such photons from an extragalactic source, the giant elliptical galaxy Markarian 421.

notes: No significance is recorded: the abstract text as retrieved garbles the significance symbol ("6er above background"), so the value is not copied.
The Whipple page states "the first extragalactic source detected at TeV energies by a ground-based instrument in 1992 (Punch et al 1992)".
result:whipple-mrk421-detection-1992.summary_technical: Observations in March-June 1992 with the Whipple Observatory gamma-ray telescope show a signal from Mrk 421 (redshift 0.031) with a flux above 0.5 TeV of 0.3 that of the Crab Nebula; the source position agrees within the 6 arcminute uncertainty.
result:whipple-mrk421-detection-1992.why_it_matters: The Whipple page records it as the first extragalactic source detected at TeV energies by a ground-based instrument, in 1992, and the abstract links the non-detection of more distant active galaxies to absorption of TeV photons by extragalactic starlight.

claim.quote: excludes previously unexplored parameter space, setting a new 90% C.L. upper limit for the WIMP-nucleon spin-independent cross-section of 8.8 x 10^{-44} cm^2 for a WIMP mass of 100 GeV/c^2, and 4.5 x 10^{-44} cm^2 for a WIMP mass of 30 GeV/c^2

result:xenon10-first-wimp-search-2007.summary_technical: 58.6 live days (6 Oct 2006 - 14 Feb 2007), 5.4 kg fiducial mass, blind analysis, nuclear-recoil energy down to 4.5 keV. 90% CL spin-independent WIMP-nucleon limits of 8.8e-44 cm^2 (100 GeV/c^2) and 4.5e-44 cm^2 (30 GeV/c^2).
result:xenon10-first-wimp-search-2007.why_it_matters: It was the first science result of the XENON programme and the paper reports it as excluding previously unexplored parameter space.

claim.quote: Considering spin-independent dark matter-nucleon scattering, we exclude cross sections \sigma_n>3.5x10^{-42} cm^2, for a dark matter particle mass m_{\chi}=8 GeV.

result:xenon10-light-dark-matter-2011.summary_technical: Trigger sensitive to a single electron; analysis threshold of 5 electrons, corresponding to 1.4 keV nuclear recoil energy; excludes sigma_n > 3.5e-42 cm^2 at m_chi = 8 GeV. The abstract states that the data strongly constrain recent elastic dark matter interpretations of excess events observed by CoGeNT and CRESST-II, as well as the DAMA annual modulation signal.
result:xenon10-light-dark-matter-2011.why_it_matters: Opened the light dark matter window to xenon detectors, a method later used by other experiments.

claim.quote: Based on the non-observation of a WIMP signal in 5.4 kg of fiducial liquid xenon mass, we exclude previously unexplored regions in the theoretically allowed parameter space for neutralinos.

result:xenon10-spin-dependent-2008.summary_technical: Spin-dependent WIMP-nucleon interactions with 129-Xe and 131-Xe from 58.6 live days at LNGS; also excludes a heavy Majorana neutrino with a mass in the range of 10 GeV - 2 TeV as a dark matter candidate under standard assumptions.
result:xenon10-spin-dependent-2008.why_it_matters: First xenon-based spin-dependent limits of the XENON programme.

claim.quote: This leads to the most stringent limit on dark matter interactions today, excluding spin-independent elastic WIMP-nucleon scattering cross-sections above 7.0x10^-45 cm^2 for a WIMP mass of 50 GeV/c^2 at 90% confidence level.

result:xenon100-100-live-days-2011.summary_technical: 100.9 live days (January-June 2010), 48 kg fiducial target; three candidate events in a pre-defined signal region with an expected background of 1.8 +/- 0.6 events; spin-independent limit 7.0e-45 cm^2 at 50 GeV/c^2 (90% CL).
result:xenon100-100-live-days-2011.why_it_matters: The paper describes this as the most stringent limit on dark matter interactions at the time of publication.

claim.quote: A blind analysis of 224.6 live days \times 34 kg exposure has yielded no evidence for dark matter interactions.

result:xenon100-225-live-days-2012.summary_technical: 224.6 live days x 34 kg; two candidates in 6.6-30.5 keVnr against 1.0 +/- 0.2 expected background events; profile likelihood limit on spin-independent elastic WIMP-nucleon scattering with a minimum of 2e-45 cm^2 at 55 GeV/c^2 (90% CL), the most stringent for WIMP masses above 8 GeV/c^2 according to the abstract.
result:xenon100-225-live-days-2012.why_it_matters: The abstract reports the most stringent spin-independent limit for WIMP masses above 8 GeV/c^2 at the time.

claim.quote: A profile likelihood analysis using an energy range of (6.6 - 43.3) keV$_{\mathrm{nr}}$ sets a limit on the elastic, spin-independent WIMP-nucleon scattering cross section for WIMP masses above 8 GeV/$c^2$, with a minimum of 1.1 $\times 10^{-45}$ cm$^2$ at 50 GeV/$c^2$ and 90% confidence level.

result:xenon100-477-live-days-2016.summary_technical: Three runs summing to 477 live days (January 2010 - January 2014), exposure 48 kg x yr, blind analysis of the last run (April 2013 - January 2014); spin-independent minimum 1.1e-45 cm^2 at 50 GeV/c^2; spin-dependent WIMP-neutron (proton) minimum 2.0e-40 cm^2 (52e-40 cm^2) at 50 GeV/c^2, 90% CL.
result:xenon100-477-live-days-2016.why_it_matters: The complete XENON100 WIMP-search result, with updated spin-dependent constraints.

claim.quote: A profile likelihood analysis of 224.6 live days $\times$ 34 kg exposure has shown no evidence for a signal.

result:xenon100-axion-2014.summary_technical: Axio-electric effect in liquid xenon: solar-axion search rejects g_Ae larger than 7.7e-12 (90% CL), best limit to date at publication; DFSZ and KSVZ QCD axions heavier than 0.3 eV/c^2 and 80 eV/c^2 excluded; for axion-like particles as all of the dark matter, g_Ae lower than 1e-12 (90% CL) for 1 to 40 keV/c^2.

claim.quote: In the selected fiducial target of 40 kg, and within the pre-defined signal region, we observe no events and hence exclude spin-independent WIMP-nucleon elastic scattering cross-sections above 3.4 x 10^-44 cm^2 for 55 GeV/c^2 WIMPs at 90% confidence level.

result:xenon100-first-results-2010.summary_technical: 11.17 live days of non-blind data (October-November 2009), 40 kg fiducial target; 90% CL limit of 3.4e-44 cm^2 at 55 GeV/c^2. Below 20 GeV/c^2 the result constrains the interpretation of the CoGeNT and DAMA signals as spin-independent elastic light-mass WIMP interactions, as the abstract states.

claim.quote: This leads to the most stringent upper limits on WIMP-neutron cross sections for WIMP masses above 6 GeV, with a minimum cross section of 3.5 x 10^{-40} cm^2 at a WIMP mass of 45 GeV, at 90% confidence level.

result:xenon100-spin-dependent-2013.summary_technical: 224.6 live days x 34 kg exposure (2011-2012): no excess signal from axial-vector WIMP interactions with 129-Xe and 131-Xe nuclei; WIMP-neutron minimum cross section 3.5e-40 cm^2 at 45 GeV (90% CL).
result:xenon100-spin-dependent-2013.why_it_matters: Reported as the most stringent WIMP-neutron limit for masses above 6 GeV at the time.

claim.quote: An excess over known backgrounds is observed at low energies and most prominent between 2 and 3 keV.

notes: This is explicitly not a discovery, observation or confirmed dark-matter signal: the abstract reports 'An excess over known backgrounds' and treats each explanation (axion, neutrino magnetic moment, tritium, bosonic dark matter) as a hypothesis, with a trace of tritium that can 'neither be confirmed nor excluded'.

Later XENONnT electronic-recoil analysis (https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.11330): "we observe no excess above background"; its abstract also gives a background about 5 times lower than in XENON1T ("(15.8 ± 1.3) events/(tonne×year×keV), the lowest ever achieved in a dark matter detector and ~5 times lower than in XENON1T").
result:xenon1t-electronic-recoil-excess-.summary_technical: XENON1T low-energy electronic-recoil search, 0.65 t-y exposure, background rate 76 ± 2 events/(t y keV) between 1 and 30 keV. An excess over known backgrounds is observed, most prominent between 2 and 3 keV. Solar axion 3.4σ, enhanced neutrino magnetic moment 3.2σ, tritium β decay 3.2σ (the first two fall to 2.0σ and 0.9σ if an unconstrained tritium component is included in the fit); for bosonic dark matter the excess favors a monoenergetic peak at (2.3 ± 0.2) keV with 3.0σ global (4.0σ local) significance. The abstract reports an excess over known backgrounds; it does not claim a discovery.
result:xenon1t-electronic-recoil-excess-.why_it_matters: The abstract reports an excess over known backgrounds and weighs three explanations (solar axions, an enhanced neutrino magnetic moment, tritium); it says the axion and neutrino-magnetic-moment results are in strong tension with stellar constraints and that a trace of tritium can neither be confirmed nor excluded. The later XENONnT electronic-recoil analysis, with a background about five times lower, reports no excess above background.

claim.quote: The background-only hypothesis is rejected with a statistical significance of 2.73 sigma.

notes: Classified as a measurement, not a first detection, evidence or observation: the collaboration's own title says "First Indication" and the paper reports only a 2.73σ rejection of the background-only hypothesis, below the 99.73% (3σ) confidence level that the T2K Nature paper (arXiv:1910.03887) describes as "considered as evidence in the particle physics community". The same classification is used for result:t2k-electron-neutrino-indication-2011, a 2.5σ "indication" paper; "first detection" would read as an actual detection to a reader.
result:xenonnt-b8-cevns-indication-2024.summary_technical: Blind analysis, 3.51 tonne-year exposure: 37 events observed above 0.5 keV, (26.4 +1.4/−1.3) expected from backgrounds; the background-only hypothesis is rejected at 2.73σ. Measured 8B solar-neutrino flux (4.7 +3.6/−2.3) × 10⁶ cm⁻² s⁻¹, consistent with results from the Sudbury Neutrino Observatory; neutrino flux-weighted CEνNS cross section on Xe (1.1 +0.8/−0.5) × 10⁻³⁹ cm², consistent with the Standard Model prediction. The collaboration's title calls it a 'First Indication'.
result:xenonnt-b8-cevns-indication-2024.why_it_matters: The paper describes this as a 'first' in three respects: the first detection of elastic nuclear recoils from astrophysical neutrinos, the first measurement of the CEνNS process with a xenon target, and the first step into the 'neutrino fog' by a dark-matter experiment.

claim.quote: A blind analysis of nuclear recoil events with energies between 3.3 keV and 60.5 keV finds no significant excess. This leads to a minimum upper limit on the spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross section of 2.58 × 10−47 cm2 for a WIMP mass of 28 GeV/c2 at 90 % confidence level.

result:xenonnt-first-nr-search-2023.summary_technical: About 1.1 tonne-year exposure, 5.9 t sensitive liquid-xenon mass; intrinsic 85Kr and 222Rn concentrations reduced to unprecedentedly low levels, giving an electronic-recoil background of (15.8 ± 1.3) events/(t·y·keV) in the region of interest. A blind analysis of nuclear recoils between 3.3 and 60.5 keV finds no significant excess: minimum upper limit on the spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross section 2.58 × 10⁻⁴⁷ cm² at 28 GeV/c² (90% CL). Spin-dependent limits are also provided; limit and sensitivity improve on XENON1T for the same exposure.
result:xenonnt-first-nr-search-2023.why_it_matters: The abstract says the intrinsic 85Kr and 222Rn concentrations in the liquid target were reduced to unprecedentedly low levels, giving an electronic-recoil background of (15.8 ± 1.3) events/(t·y·keV), and that both the limit and the sensitivity improve on previous XENON1T results for the same exposure.

claim.quote: the exclusion upper limit for the WIMP-nucleon cross section was improved by a factor of 2 to 1.9$\times$10$^{-41}$cm$^2$ at 8 GeV/c$^2$ at 90\% confidence level

result:xmass-annual-modulation-2-7-years.summary_technical: 800 live days with the 832 kg target; model-independent p-value 0.11 in the 1-20 keV energy region; no significant amplitude for periods between 50 and 600 days.
result:xmass-annual-modulation-2-7-years.why_it_matters: An exposure larger than DAMA/LIBRA's and no modulation found.

claim.quote: the exclusion upper limit of the WIMP-nucleon cross section 4.3$\times$10$^{-41}$cm$^2$ at 8 GeV/c$^2$ was obtained and we exclude almost all the DAMA/LIBRA allowed region in the 6 to 16 GeV/c$^2$ range at $\sim$10$^{-40}$cm$^2$

result:xmass-annual-modulation-2015.summary_technical: 359.2 live days x 832 kg between November 2013 and March 2015. WIMP-nucleon limit 4.3e-41 cm^2 at 8 GeV/c^2; the model-independent modulation analysis showed a slight negative amplitude with p-values 0.014 and 0.068 for the null hypothesis (two analyses).
result:xmass-annual-modulation-2015.why_it_matters: The abstract describes it as the first extensive annual-modulation search probing this region with an exposure comparable to DAMA/LIBRA.

claim.quote: The obtained upper limit on a spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross section was ${\rm 2.2 \times 10^{-44} \, cm^{2}}$ for a WIMP mass of ${\rm 60 \, GeV/c^{2}}$ at the $90\%$ confidence level, which was the most stringent limit among results from single-phase liquid xenon detectors.

result:xmass-direct-search-705-days-2018.summary_technical: 705.9 live days in a 97 kg fiducial volume; event rate (4.2 +/- 0.2) x 10^-3 /day/kg/keVee at 5 keVee with 20% signal efficiency; mostly mis-reconstructed events from 210Pb in the copper plates.
result:xmass-direct-search-705-days-2018.why_it_matters: The abstract describes it as the most stringent limit among single-phase liquid xenon detectors.

claim.quote: Searching for a WIMP signal in the detector's 97~kg fiducial volume yielded a limit on the WIMP-nucleon scattering cross section of ${\rm 1.4\times 10^{-44}\, cm^{2}}$ for a ${\rm 60\,GeV/c^{2}}$ WIMP at the 90$\%$ confidence level.

result:xmass-full-dataset-2022.summary_technical: Full data set (20 Nov 2013 - 1 Feb 2019, analysis threshold 1.0 keVee, 0.5 keVee in the later half). Annual-modulation search in the whole 832 kg: 2.3e-42 cm^2 at 8 GeV/c^2; at 0.5 GeV/c^2 the Migdal effect and bremsstrahlung give 1.4e-35 cm^2 and 1.1e-33 cm^2.

claim.quote: No significant modulation signal was observed and 90% confidence level upper limits of $1.6 \times 10^{-33}$ cm$^2$ at 0.5 GeV was set for the DM-nucleon cross section. This is the first experimental result of a search for DM mediated by the bremsstrahlung effect.

result:xmass-sub-gev-annual-modulation-2.summary_technical: 0.32-1 GeV dark matter via inelastic nuclear scattering with bremsstrahlung emission down to 1 keV electron-equivalent; 2.8 years live time (2.38 ton-years); 1.6e-33 cm^2 at 0.5 GeV; also multi-GeV (4-20 GeV) elastic search with a 2.3 keV nuclear-recoil threshold, 2.9e-42 cm^2 at 8 GeV.
result:xmass-sub-gev-annual-modulation-2.why_it_matters: The abstract calls it the first experimental search for dark matter mediated by the bremsstrahlung effect.

claim.quote: These events have an abnormally high fraction of muons, which is beyond current model predictions.

notes: Anomaly, not a discovery: the authors raise the exotic-primary possibility without claiming it.
result:yakutsk-giant-showers-muon-excess.summary_technical: Two extensive air showers of about 10^20 eV registered at the Yakutsk array in 1974-2024, both near the array centre and triggering all surface and underground muon detectors (threshold 1.0 cos(theta) GeV), with an abnormally high muon fraction beyond model predictions.
result:yakutsk-giant-showers-muon-excess.why_it_matters: The abstract says this may change our understanding of hadron interactions at ultra-high energy, but that the showers could also have been initiated by exotic primary particles.

claim.quote: From the 90% confidence limit on the latter a limit is derived on the spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross-section versus particle mass with a minimum at 1.1 × 10−6 pb.

notes: Astropart. Phys. 23 (2005) 444 (Alner et al.). The paper itself is not on arXiv; the abstract was read from a university repository record. A published critique (astro-ph/0512120) and reply (astro-ph/0701859) exist.
result:zeplin-i-first-limits-2005.summary_technical: Three runs totalling 293 kg d fiducial exposure with a 3.2 kg fiducial liquid xenon target at 2800 mwe; neutron calibration shows nuclear recoil pulses with a time constant about 0.5 that of gamma and beta events; spin-independent WIMP-nucleon limit with a minimum at 1.1e-6 pb. The discrimination claim was disputed in astro-ph/0512120 and answered in astro-ph/0701859.
result:zeplin-i-first-limits-2005.why_it_matters: The first published limit from the ZEPLIN programme.

claim.quote: These figures provide a 90% c.l. upper limit to the number of nuclear recoils of 10.4 events in this acceptance window, which converts to a WIMP-nucleon spin-independent cross-section with a minimum of 6.6x10^-7 pb following the inclusion of an energy dependent, calibrated, efficiency.

result:zeplin-ii-first-limits-2007.summary_technical: 31 live days, 225 kg d exposure after cuts; 29 events observed in the 5-20 keVee nuclear recoil acceptance window against a summed expectation of 28.6 +/- 4.3 background events; a radon-progeny background population was identified.
result:zeplin-ii-first-limits-2007.why_it_matters: First limit from a two-phase xenon detector run underground at Boulby.

claim.quote: assuming standard xenon quenching factor (qXe) of 0.19, our ZEPLIN-II limits strongly suggest the exclusion of iDM signal claims at >99% C.L., for Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs) masses >100 GeV.

result:zeplin-ii-inelastic-dark-matter-2.summary_technical: Constraints on inelastic dark matter (iDM) from ZEPLIN-II results, using previously published estimates of the residual background; excludes iDM signal claims at >99% C.L. for WIMP masses >100 GeV assuming a xenon quenching factor of 0.19.
result:zeplin-ii-inelastic-dark-matter-2.why_it_matters: A re-interpretation of the ZEPLIN-II first run, relevant to the DAMA signal.

claim.quote: The minimum of the curve for WIMP-neutron cross-section corresponds to 0.07 pb at a WIMP mass of around 65 GeV.

result:zeplin-ii-spin-dependent-2007.summary_technical: First underground ZEPLIN-II data converted to spin-dependent WIMP-proton and WIMP-neutron cross-section limits; WIMP-neutron minimum 0.07 pb at about 65 GeV.
result:zeplin-ii-spin-dependent-2007.why_it_matters: Spin-dependent limits from the ZEPLIN-II first run.

claim.quote: has excluded a WIMP-nucleon elastic scattering spin-independent cross-section above 8.1x10(-8)pb at 55GeV/c2 with a 90% confidence limit

result:zeplin-iii-first-science-run-2008.summary_technical: 12 kg two-phase xenon TPC; data from 27 Feb - 20 May 2008; WIMP-nucleon spin-independent limit 8.1e-8 pb at 55 GeV/c^2 (90% CL); the abstract states better low-energy discrimination between electron and nuclear recoils than previously achieved by other xenon-based experiments.
result:zeplin-iii-first-science-run-2008.why_it_matters: The first science result of ZEPLIN-III.

claim.quote: This is the tightest constraint on that explanation of the DAMA result yet presented using a xenon target.

result:zeplin-iii-inelastic-dark-matter-.summary_technical: Limits on inelastic dark matter from the 2008 run: 63 kg d net exposure in 20-80 keV nuclear recoil, 6 events observed; a small region consistent with the 1.17 ton-yr DAMA modulation signal remains at 90% CL in the mass range 45-60 GeV with a minimum CL of 88%.
result:zeplin-iii-inelastic-dark-matter-.why_it_matters: States itself as the tightest xenon-target constraint on the inelastic-dark-matter explanation of DAMA at the time.

claim.quote: This allows the exclusion of the scalar cross-section above 4.8E-8 pb near 50 GeV/c^2 WIMP mass with 90% confidence. Combined with data from the first run, this result improves to 3.9E-8 pb.

result:zeplin-iii-second-science-run-201.summary_technical: Raw fiducial exposure of 1,344 kg d over 319 days (June 2010 - May 2011); eight events in the 7-29 keV nuclear recoil signal acceptance region, compatible with background; scalar limit 4.8e-8 pb near 50 GeV/c^2 (3.9e-8 pb combined with the first run); WIMP-neutron spin-dependent limit 8.0e-3 pb.
result:zeplin-iii-second-science-run-201.why_it_matters: The abstract describes it as the conclusion of the ZEPLIN programme at Boulby.

claim.quote: Analysis of $\sim$450 kg$\cdot$days fiducial exposure revealed a most likely signal of zero events, leading to a 90%-confidence upper limit on the pure WIMP-neutron cross-section of $\sigma_n=1.8\times 10^{-2}$ pb at 55 GeV/$c^2$ WIMP mass.

result:zeplin-iii-spin-dependent-2009.summary_technical: ~450 kg d fiducial exposure from the first science run; 90% CL pure WIMP-neutron limit 1.8e-2 pb at 55 GeV/c^2; recent Bonn CD nuclear structure calculations indicate xenon is much less sensitive to WIMP-proton spin-dependent interactions than previously thought.

notes: The same ACT paper also reports the site as "on the slopes of Cerro Toco" (ACTPol instrument paper) and 5190 m altitude. POLARBEAR's James Ax Observatory stands about 150 m from this point, CLASS about 300 m (see their sites).
site:act-cerro-toco.summary_technical: Site of the 6 m Atacama Cosmology Telescope on the slopes of Cerro Toco at 5190 m in the Parque Astronómico Atacama; ACT took its final data in 2022 and has been decommissioned.

site:akeno-observatory.summary_technical: Akeno Observatory of the University of Tokyo's Institute for Cosmic Ray Research, Akeno-cho, Hokuto, Yamanashi, at 35 deg 47' N, 138 deg 30' E and 900 m; centre of the AGASA surface array.

site:angra-npp-connie-container.summary_technical: Shipping-container laboratory outside the main Angra 2 reactor building (surface, no overburden), 30 m from the core of a 3.8 GW_th reactor. Marked with a campus-grade point for the plant.

notes: The detector is not attached to a facility record. According to the two-decades ANTARES paper, the onshore control building was at the Institut Michel Pacha, La Seyne-sur-Mer; it has no separate record in the Atlas.
site:antares-toulon.summary_technical: Deep-sea site 40 km offshore from Toulon, France, at 2475 m depth in the Mediterranean Sea, hosting the ANTARES 12-line neutrino telescope from first-line deployment (2006) to shutdown (2022).

site:apache-point-sdss-2-5m-telescope.summary_technical: Position of the Sloan Foundation 2.5-m telescope at Apache Point Observatory, New Mexico (32.780 N, 105.820 W, 2788 m), used by SDSS, BOSS and eBOSS.

site:argonne-campus.summary_technical: Argonne National Laboratory campus, southwest DuPage County, Illinois (Lemont address), 9700 Cass Avenue.

notes: The Ash River laboratory is not part of Fermilab, and the Atlas has no separate facility record for it.

Coordinates are coarse. The only coordinate found in a collaboration publication is "(48.4°N, 92.8°W)". Secondary compilations give 48.37917°N, 92.83361°W; that value is not recorded because it has no rank<=7 or collaboration source.
site:ash-river-nova-far-detector.summary_technical: Surface (slightly below grade) laboratory near Ash River, Minnesota, 810 km from the NuMI target and 14.6 mrad off the beam axis, housing the 14 kt NOvA far detector under a 3.6 m water-equivalent overburden.

site:baikal-gvd-lake-baikal.summary_technical: Southern basin of Lake Baikal, ~3.6 km offshore at 51°46'N 104°24'E, lakebed depth ~1366 m; site of the expanding Baikal-GVD neutrino telescope's clusters.

site:baksan-bust-hall.summary_technical: Hall (12,000 m^3 excavation) 550 m from the start of the horizontal tunnel, effective overburden 850 m w.e. (8.5e4 g/cm^2); marked with the main adit entrance point, approximate.

site:baksan-sage-underground-lab.summary_technical: Underground laboratory of the Baksan Neutrino Observatory, under about 2100 m of rock (4700 m.w.e.) in the Caucasus Mountains, Kabardino-Balkaria, Russia, housing the SAGE gallium detector.

notes: A17: the coordinate rests on a geocoder (rank 8), so it is a campus-grade point marked approximate; it is not relabelled as a detector or underground-lab position. No rock-overburden length is published in the sources read.
site:bern-underground-laboratory.summary_technical: Approximate point of the Laboratory for High Energy Physics address (Sidlerstrasse 5), not of the underground rooms themselves; overburden 70 m.w.e.

notes: Campus point only; no fetched source locates the collider rings or detector halls.
site:binp-novosibirsk-akademgorodok.summary_technical: BINP SB RAS, 11 Acad. Lavrentieva Pr., Akademgorodok, Novosibirsk. Geocoder (OpenStreetMap/Nominatim) polygon centroid, about 300 m precision; hosts the VEPP-2000 and VEPP-4M colliders and, formerly, VEPP-2M.

notes: Interaction-point assignment from arXiv:nucl-ex/0503018; building identity inferred (see coordinate note).
site:bnl-rhic-ip10-phobos.summary_technical: RHIC interaction region 10 (10 o'clock) experimental area, Brookhaven National Laboratory; the point is the centroid of the OpenStreetMap building 1010 (about 100 m precision), identified by the RHIC building-numbering pattern, not a surveyed detector position.

notes: Interaction-point assignment from arXiv:nucl-ex/0503018; building identity inferred (see coordinate note).
site:bnl-rhic-ip2-brahms.summary_technical: RHIC interaction region 2 (2 o'clock) experimental area, Brookhaven National Laboratory; the point is the centroid of the OpenStreetMap building 1002 (about 100 m precision), identified by the RHIC building-numbering pattern, not a surveyed detector position.

notes: STAR has operated continuously at this interaction point since RHIC's first collisions in 2000 through RHIC's final run on 2026-02-06 (src:heavy-ions-rhic-final-collisions-2026).

Secondary sources (search-engine summaries of physics papers, not checked against the papers) describe this as RHIC's 6 o'clock interaction point. That clock-position label is not recorded as a sourced fact because no primary or official source consulted states it.
site:bnl-rhic-ip6-star.summary_technical: One of the two interaction-region halls that remained active on the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider ring at Brookhaven National Laboratory, housing the STAR detector from RHIC's first collisions (2000) through its final run (2026). The recorded point is the centroid of the hall's building footprint as traced in OpenStreetMap (about 100 m precision), not a geodetic survey point.

notes: This hall housed PHENIX from RHIC's first collisions in 2000, then its successor sPHENIX; both STAR and sPHENIX were the two active RHIC detectors named in the official announcement of RHIC's final run on 2026-02-06 (src:heavy-ions-rhic-final-collisions-2026: 'crashed into one another ... inside the STAR and sPHENIX detectors').

Secondary sources (search-engine summaries of physics papers, not checked against the papers) describe this as RHIC's 8 o'clock interaction point. That clock-position label is not recorded as a sourced fact because no primary or official source consulted states it.
site:bnl-rhic-ip8-phenix-sphenix.summary_technical: One of the two interaction-region halls that remained active on the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider ring at Brookhaven National Laboratory; occupied first by the PHENIX detector and later by its successor sPHENIX, through RHIC's final run in 2026. The recorded point is the centroid of the hall's building footprint as traced in OpenStreetMap (about 100 m precision), not a geodetic survey point.

notes: This is the single site record for the whole BNL campus. The RHIC ring's two active interaction-region halls are recorded separately as site:bnl-rhic-ip6-star and site:bnl-rhic-ip8-phenix-sphenix (both physically within this campus but without an independently sourced coordinate of their own; see their notes).
site:bnl-upton-campus.summary_technical: Brookhaven National Laboratory's main site in Upton, Suffolk County, New York, built on the former U.S. Army Camp Upton; hosts the AGS/Booster injector chain, the RHIC ring with its STAR and sPHENIX detector halls, and other DOE user facilities.

site:boulby-mine.summary_technical: Underground laboratory hosted within the ICL-UK Boulby mine (potash/polyhalite), North Yorkshire, at ~1.1 km depth beneath the North York Moors.

notes: The CONUS detector itself sat 17.1 m from the reactor core inside the plant (arXiv:2011.00210); no separate, more precise detector-hall coordinate was found in a fetched source, so this campus-level point is used for the site record.
site:brokdorf-nuclear-power-plant-campus.summary_technical: Surface site of the (now shut down) Brokdorf pressurised water reactor, Schleswig-Holstein, Germany; hosted the CONUS CEvNS detector 17.1 m from the reactor core, 2018-2022 data taking before the 2023 move to Leibstadt.

site:bugey-npp-detector-halls.summary_technical: Detector positions at 15, 40 and 95 m from a 2,800 MW_th core at the Bugey plant (Bugey-3), and 15 m for the Bugey-4 integral measurement. Marked with a campus-grade point for the plant.

site:cascadia-basin-p-one.summary_technical: Cascadia Basin seafloor site on Ocean Networks Canada's NEPTUNE cabled observatory, 2660 m depth, roughly 200 km off the coast of Vancouver Island/British Columbia; coordinates (47°46'N, 127°46'W, to 1 arcminute) are the position the STRAW pathfinder paper gives for the Cascadia Basin site, not a surveyed seafloor mooring position.

notes: The same OSM footprint is drawn as a context feature in map:cern (geometry:antiproton-decelerator-hall), with entity_id null; it could now point at accelerator:cern-ad.
site:cern-antiproton-decelerator-hall.summary_technical: AD hall (surface building on the Meyrin campus) hosting the AD, ELENA and the AD-ELENA experiments; location is the centroid of the OSM building footprint, approximate.

notes: The link between CAST and the SR8 building rests on an internal CERN cryogenics document that lists 'CAST_COLDBOX /SR8' under 'CERN Axion Solar Telescope (CAST) - LHC Point 8'. No official CAST or CERN page, Greybook entry or CAST detector paper consulted states the building name directly; any of these would be a stronger source.
site:cern-cast-sr8.summary_technical: SR8, a service building associated with LHC Point 8 (Ferney-Voltaire, Ain, France), identified from an internal CERN cryogenics document listing 'CAST_COLDBOX /SR8' under 'CERN Axion Solar Telescope (CAST) - LHC Point 8'; houses the CAST decommissioned-LHC-test-dipole helioscope from 2003 to 2022.

notes: The point is the centroid of the ECN3 access building as traced in OpenStreetMap, a campus-grade point at 150 m precision: no source consulted gives a surveyed point for this cavern.
Shared by experiment:na48, experiment:na62 and (planned) experiment:ship.
site:cern-ecn3-north-area.summary_technical: ECN3 underground cavern (with its TCC8 target/beam area) in the CERN SPS North Area on the Prevessin site, fed by the P42 and K12 beamlines; successive home of NA48 (1997-2001), NA62 (2015-present) and the planned SHiP experiment.

notes: EHN1 (building 887) is the neighbouring hall; the existing site:cern-neutrino-platform-ehn1 carries a coarser campus point for it.
COMPASS is placed here on the strength of the AMBER letter of intent ("the existing spectrometer in EHN2"), which describes the COMPASS spectrometer being reused.
site:cern-ehn2-north-area.summary_technical: EHN2 (CERN building 888) in the SPS North Area, Prévessin site: hall of the M2 muon/hadron beam line hosting the COMPASS spectrometer (2002-2022) and its successor AMBER; the point is the centroid of the building outline in CERN's MapCERN GIS layer.

notes: Point number inferred by chaining two official CERN sources: 'the detector is ... based on the current magnet of LEP's L3 experiment ... When LEP switches off, the L3 magnet will be left in place whilst ALICE is installed' (src:lep-cern-courier-l3-magnet-alice) plus the voisins.cern and home.cern pages placing ALICE at Point 2 (src:lep-cern-voisins-point-2, src:lep-cern-alice-experiment-page). No single fetched sentence states 'L3 was at Point 2' verbatim. (src:lep-cern-alice-experiment-page was checked for an explicit L3-legacy statement and found none, but corroborates ALICE's own location, which is Point 2.)
site:cern-lep-point-2-l3.summary_technical: LEP interaction point 2, in Sergy (Ain, France); housed the L3 detector for the full LEP programme. L3's solenoid magnet was left in place and is now ALICE's central magnet at the same point.

notes: The point number is directly sourced ('Located at point 4 of the LEP ring', CERN Courier ALEPH page). The coordinates are an OpenStreetMap/Nominatim centroid for the surface marker 'CERN - Point 4', by the same method used for the ATLAS Point 1 record. No official CERN or geodetic publication consulted (checked 2026-09-17) gives surveyed coordinates for this cavern.
site:cern-lep-point-4-aleph.summary_technical: LEP interaction point 4, in the commune of Echenevex (Ain, France); housed the ALEPH detector for the full LEP programme. The same tunnel point today carries only accelerating RF equipment for the LHC, not a detector.

notes: Point number inferred from a CERN news article describing 'a miniature model of the underground cavern featuring the DELPHI and LHCb detectors', displayed at the LHCb exhibition at CERN's Point 8 (src:lep-cern-lhcb-exhibition-news, src:lep-cern-lhcb-experiment-page): the two detectors are stated to share the same cavern, and LHCb's own page and the voisins.cern Point 8 page both place LHCb at Point 8 / Ferney-Voltaire, so DELPHI is placed there too. No single fetched sentence states 'DELPHI was at Point 8' in so many words. (src:lep-cern-lhcb-experiment-page corroborates LHCb's own location at Ferney-Voltaire/Point 8.)
site:cern-lep-point-8-delphi.summary_technical: LEP interaction point 8, in Ferney-Voltaire (Ain, France); housed the DELPHI detector for the full LEP programme, later re-equipped for LHCb.

notes: CERN's main site has been at Meyrin since 1954 (src:cern-meyrin-site-point-1: 'the location of its main site since 1954').
site:cern-meyrin.summary_technical: Main CERN campus (surface), 80 ha across the Swiss communes of Meyrin and Satigny and the French communes of Prevessin-Moens and Saint-Genis-Pouilly; hosts Linac4, the PS Booster, the PS, the CERN Data Centre and LHC Point 1.

notes: Coordinates are shown at campus (Prévessin-site) precision; see the coordinate note. The marker is not a claim of survey-grade precision for the EHN1 building.
site:cern-neutrino-platform-ehn1.summary_technical: EHN1 extension in the CERN North Area on the Prévessin site, housing the CERN Neutrino Platform test beams and the ProtoDUNE single-phase and dual-phase cryostats, as well as ICARUS refurbishment and Baby MIND.

notes: No official CERN or geodetic publication giving WGS84 coordinates for LHC Point 1 was found (checked 2026-09-17; cds.cern.ch is behind bot protection, and home.cern and atlas.cern state only that ATLAS 'sits in a cavern 100 m below ground near the main CERN site, close to the village of Meyrin'). The coordinate value is a geocoder estimate; see the coordinate note.
site:cern-point-1-atlas.summary_technical: LHC interaction point 1 on the CERN Meyrin site: the UX15 experimental cavern ~100 m below the surface housing the ATLAS detector, together with its surface buildings and the ATLAS control room.

notes: The coordinate is a geocoder-derived estimate, not a survey, so it is shown as a campus-grade point with large uncertainty. See the coordinate note for the sources checked.

This is a separate record from LEP Point 2 (L3), which documents the same physical LHC point during the earlier LEP/L3 era. The two coexist deliberately: same point, different eras, cross-referenced in prose rather than merged.

detector:alice's placements[] cites this site with role 'main' despite the campus-kind coordinate, following the same pattern used at site:cern-point-1-atlas (an uncertain/approximate coordinate that is still the best available point for the marker).
site:cern-point-2-alice.summary_technical: LHC interaction point 2, in the commune of St. Genis-Pouilly (Ain, France): the UX25 experimental cavern, whose floor is 52 m underground with 28 m of rock overburden, houses the ALICE detector inside the L3 solenoid magnet reused from LEP.

notes: The experiment cavern (UXC55) is quoted by CMS as 53 m long, 27 m wide and 24 m high, 100 m underground; the detector centre is 89 m below the surface and 420 m above sea level.
Altitude is left null: the only sourced altitude (420 m a.s.l.) is that of the detector centre underground, not of the surface site.
site:cern-point-5-cms.summary_technical: Interaction Point 5 of the LHC, near Cessy (Ain, France). The CMS experiment cavern UXC55 is about 100 m below the surface; the detector centre is 89 m below ground and 420 m above sea level, under roughly 50 m of moraine and 20 m of molasse.

notes: This record is distinct from site:cern-lep-point-8-delphi, which documents the same physical point during the LEP/DELPHI era. The two are not duplicates: they describe the same cavern at different eras with independently sourced facts.

The coordinate is a geocoder value, shown as a campus-grade point with large uncertainty; no primary or official source consulted (checked 2026-09-17) gives a detector-grade coordinate. See the coordinate note.
site:cern-point-8-lhcb.summary_technical: LHC interaction point 8, Ferney-Voltaire (Ain, France); houses the LHCb forward-spectrometer detector approximately 100 m below the surface. Previously the site of the LEP-era DELPHI detector (see site:cern-lep-point-8-delphi).

notes: Created by the hadron-2 stream as a placement of last resort for historical SPS North Area experiments; EHN1 and EHN2 have their own site records.
