site:cern-prevessin-north-area.summary_technical: Campus-grade location for the CERN Prévessin site (SPS North Area): used for North Area heavy-ion experiments whose experimental hall is not identified in the sources fetched.

notes: The point is the centroid of the SPS access building BA4 as traced in OpenStreetMap: a campus-grade point, shown as approximate, not a surveyed position of the underground hall. For this reason the UA2 detector has no placement of its own at this site: the link is stated in the text and through the collaboration's host site.
site:cern-sps-lss4-ua2.summary_technical: One of the SPS's experimental insertion points, conventionally identified as Long Straight Section 4, where UA2 was installed around the beam pipe for the 1981-1990 SppS collider programme.

notes: The point is the centroid of the SPS access building BA5 as traced in OpenStreetMap: a campus-grade point, shown as approximate, not a surveyed position of the underground hall. For this reason the UA1 detector has no placement of its own at this site: the link is stated in the text and through the collaboration's host site.
site:cern-sps-lss5-ua1.summary_technical: One of the SPS's experimental insertion points, conventionally identified as Long Straight Section 5, where UA1 was installed around the beam pipe for the 1981-1990 SppS collider programme.

notes: TI12 is a former LEP-era transfer tunnel, 480 m downstream of ATLAS interaction point 1, reused to house the FASER detector.
The coordinate is a reused neighbouring-point placeholder (campus-grade, large uncertainty); see the coordinate note.
site:cern-ti12-faser.summary_technical: TI12, a former LEP transfer tunnel 480 m downstream of LHC interaction point 1 along the beam collision axis; houses the FASER detector, installed during Long Shutdown 2 (2019-2021).

notes: TI18 is a former LEP-era transfer tunnel on the opposite side of ATLAS interaction point 1 from FASER's TI12; now houses the SND@LHC detector.

The official SND@LHC site (sndlhc.web.cern.ch, sndlhc.cern, home.cern/science/experiments/snd-lhc) remains unreachable as of 2026-09-17 (DNS failure / 404, re-checked); the INSPIRE experiment record and the collaboration's own detector paper (arXiv:2210.02784) were used instead.
The coordinate is a reused neighbouring-point placeholder (campus-grade, large uncertainty); see the coordinate note.

The TI18 / 480 m siting is confirmed by the SND@LHC detector paper (arXiv:2210.02784: 'The experiment is located 480 m downstream of the ATLAS interaction point, in the TI18 tunnel'). Only the numeric coordinate value itself remains an unverified placeholder.
country/place set to CH to match the reused anchor point (site:cern-point-1-atlas, Meyrin CH); the true tunnel geography for TI18 was not independently confirmed to finer precision.
site:cern-ti18-snd-lhc.summary_technical: TI18, a former LEP transfer tunnel near LHC interaction point 1, on the opposite side from FASER's TI12; houses the SND@LHC detector.

notes: Other published values: the Ivezić et al. LSST overview paper gives S 30° 14′ 40.68″, W 70° 44′ 57.90″, elevation 2652 m (Mamajek 2012); the NOIRLab Rubin Seeing Monitor page, a different instrument, gives 2612 m. The NOIRLab Simonyi page is used as the official facility source.
site:cerro-pachon-simonyi-survey-telesco.summary_technical: Position of the Simonyi Survey Telescope on El Peñón, Cerro Pachón, Chile (30.245 S, 70.749 W, 2663 m), host of the LSST Camera.

site:cerro-tololo-blanco-telescope.summary_technical: Position of the Víctor M. Blanco 4-m telescope on Cerro Tololo, Chile (30°10.11’S, 70°48.24’W, 2207 m), host of DECam.

notes: This site is distinct from any Double Chooz near or far detector site: NUCLEUS is described in its own papers as sited 'very near' the reactor cores, much closer than Double Chooz's near detector. Its position is derived from the NUCLEUS baselines of 72 m to reactor unit B-1 and 102 m to B-2 (see the coordinate note), not from a surveyed point.
site:chooz-very-near-nucleus.summary_technical: NUCLEUS's 'very-near' site at the EDF Chooz B nuclear power plant, Ardennes, France; its position is derived from the NUCLEUS baselines of 72 m to reactor unit B-1 and 102 m to B-2.

site:cjpl-i.summary_technical: CJPL-I: the original CJPL hall beside the Jinping traffic tunnel, Sichuan, inaugurated 2010, with ~2400 m of rock overburden (~6720 m.w.e.), among the deepest overburdens of any underground laboratory in the world.

notes: The completion date for CJPL-II civil engineering (reported elsewhere as December 2023) was not confirmed on an official page and is therefore not recorded as a sourced interval on the facility.
site:cjpl-ii.summary_technical: CJPL-II: a second-phase extension of CJPL, ~500 m west of CJPL-I along the same traffic tunnel, with four planned caverns (14 m × 14 m × 130 m each) and ~2400 m of vertical rock overburden (~6720 m.w.e.); civil engineering credited elsewhere to Tsinghua University and Yalong River Hydropower Development Company (not confirmed on an official page).

site:class-cerro-toco.summary_technical: CLASS site on Cerro Toco at about 5140 m, in the Parque Astronómico Atacama, near the ACT and POLARBEAR sites.

notes: Campus point only; the CLEO and CUSB experimental halls are not separately located by any source consulted.
site:cornell-wilson-lab.summary_technical: Wilson Synchrotron Laboratory, 161 Synchrotron Drive, Cornell University, Ithaca NY. Geocoder (OpenStreetMap/Nominatim) building centroid, about 300 m precision; the CESR tunnel lies beneath the surrounding campus.

notes: Represents all three Daya Bay experimental halls (Daya Bay near, Ling Ao near, far) as one site record pending hall-specific sourced coordinates; see detector:daya-bay-antineutrino-detectors placements for the three distinct roles (near/near/far) recorded against this shared point.
No overburden or depth figure for any hall was found in the sources consulted (checked 2026-09-17).
site:daya-bay-experimental-halls.summary_technical: Underground experimental complex comprising the Daya Bay near hall, Ling Ao near hall and far hall, at baselines of 470 m, 576 m and 1648 m respectively from six 2.9 GW_th reactor cores at the Daya Bay/Ling Ao nuclear power complex, Shenzhen, Guangdong, China.

notes: DESY's PETRA IV location page puts DESY in Bahrenfeld: "The DESY research and technology centre, parts of the University of Hamburg and other top scientific institutes already ensure that the Bahrenfeld location has international appeal."
site:desy-hamburg-campus.summary_technical: DESY's main site in Hamburg-Bahrenfeld, Germany; a second DESY site exists at Zeuthen near Berlin, which has no site record of its own in the Atlas.

notes: No official DESY page or H1 detector paper consulted gives a coordinate for the North Hall; the point recorded is an OpenStreetMap tracing of the hall building (see the coordinate note).

DESY's brochure "HERA - Pointing the way" (2007) confirms the North Hall/H1 pairing: "In 1992, the first two HERA experiments went into operation: H1 in the North Hall and ZEUS in the South Hall." DESY's ALPS cryoplatform page says the HERA North Hall "has recently been partially renovated to accommodate the ALPS II experiment in the HERA tunnel".
site:desy-hera-north-hall-h1.summary_technical: HERA North Hall, DESY campus, housing the H1 detector (1992-2007); now used for the ALPS experiment. The recorded point is the centroid of the hall building as traced in OpenStreetMap (about 50 m precision).

notes: No official DESY page or ZEUS detector paper consulted gives a coordinate for the South Hall; the point recorded is the DESY campus centroid, not the hall (see the coordinate note).
DESY's brochure "HERA - Pointing the way" (2007) confirms the South Hall/ZEUS pairing: "In 1992, the first two HERA experiments went into operation: H1 in the North Hall and ZEUS in the South Hall."
site:desy-hera-south-hall-zeus.summary_technical: HERA South Hall, DESY campus, housing the ZEUS detector (1992-2007). The recorded point is the DESY campus centroid, not the hall itself (see note).

notes: The Double Chooz far detector was installed in the existing underground laboratory of the original CHOOZ experiment (collaboration's 2022 detector paper), at 1050 m from the reactor cores (2012 discovery paper's abstract).
site:double-chooz-far-detector.summary_technical: Double Chooz far-detector hall, 1050 m from the Chooz-B reactor cores, under ~300 m.w.e. of rock shielding.

notes: No overburden or depth figure for the near-detector hall was found in the sources consulted (checked 2026-09-17).
site:double-chooz-near-detector.summary_technical: Double Chooz near-detector hall, approximately 400 m from the Chooz-B reactor cores.

notes: Approximate region marker; see the coordinate note. Fly's Eye I and Fly's Eye II (3.4 km apart) are not separately located.
site:dugway-flys-eye.summary_technical: Approximate marker for the two original Fly's Eye stations (Fly's Eye I with 67 mirrors; Fly's Eye II, 3.4 km away) on the Dugway Proving Ground; the position is only known to about a degree from the sources read.

site:dugway-hires-i.summary_technical: HiRes-I fluorescence station (22 telescope modules) at 40.1952 N, 112.8358 W, 1596 m, on a hilltop about 130 m above the desert floor on the Dugway Proving Ground, Utah; 12.6 km from HiRes-II.

site:dugway-hires-ii.summary_technical: HiRes-II fluorescence station (42 telescope modules with FADC readout) on Camel's Back Ridge, Dugway Proving Ground, at 40.1321 N, 112.9590 W, 1552 m; in operation from spring 1999.

site:ess-lund.summary_technical: ESS campus at Brunnshog, Lund; the ESSnuSB design places a 1 kt near detector underground on the ESS site 250 m from the neutrino target station. Marked with a campus-grade point.

notes: The FAIR facility is "being built in Darmstadt" (FAIR home page); the point is not a hall or tunnel position.
site:fair-construction-site.summary_technical: FAIR (Facility for Antiproton and Ion Research) construction site next to GSI, Darmstadt: campus-grade point from the OSM landuse=construction area; location of the SIS100, the Super-FRS, the storage rings and the CBM and PANDA experiments.

notes: The point is the centroid of the 'CDF Hall' building as mapped in OpenStreetMap (see the coordinate note). No survey or official source consulted gives a dedicated lat/lon for this interaction hall.

The INSPIRE experiment record long_name for CDF is "Study of Proton Anti-proton Collisions Using a Large Detector at B0 -- the CDF Detector" (src:colliders-historical-cdf-inspire-experiment-record), confirming the B0 location name, though not coordinates.
site:fermilab-cdf-collision-hall-b0.summary_technical: CDF collision hall (Tevatron B0): one of the Tevatron ring's interaction regions, at Fermilab, Batavia, Illinois. No survey coordinate for the hall itself was found; the marker is the centroid of the hall building as mapped in OpenStreetMap (about 40 m), shown as approximate.

notes: The point is the centroid of the D0 Assembly Building as mapped in OpenStreetMap (see the coordinate note). No survey or official source consulted gives a dedicated lat/lon for this interaction hall.

fnal.gov states "DZero is one of two detectors positioned along the four-mile Tevatron accelerator ring. It takes its name from its location on the ring, D0." (src:colliders-historical-d0-fnal-tevatron-experiments-page), confirming the D0 location name, though not coordinates.
site:fermilab-d0-collision-hall.summary_technical: D0 collision hall (Tevatron D0): one of the Tevatron ring's interaction regions, at Fermilab, Batavia, Illinois. No survey coordinate for the hall itself was found; the marker is the centroid of the hall building as mapped in OpenStreetMap (about 40 m), shown as approximate.

notes: The coordinates reuse the Fermilab main-campus point rather than a separate lookup; see the coordinate note.
site:fermilab-ktev-hall.summary_technical: Fixed-target experimental hall on the Fermilab site (Batavia, Illinois) housing the KTeV (E799-II/E832) kaon spectrometer; no surveyed coordinate for this specific hall was found, so the Fermilab campus point is used at reduced precision.

notes: Coordinates are shown at campus precision; see the coordinate note. The marker is not a claim of survey-grade precision for any one hall.
site:fermilab-main-campus.summary_technical: Surface campus in Batavia, Illinois hosting the Fermilab accelerator complex (linac, Booster, Recycler, Main Injector, PIP-II), the NuMI and BNB targets, the LBNF near site and the DUNE near detector hall.

notes: No official source consulted (checked 2026-09-18: fnal.gov paths returned 403; muon.fnal.gov PDF paths returned 404/403) gives building-level coordinates for MC-1. The point recorded is the centroid of the MC-1 building as traced in OpenStreetMap (see the coordinate note).
site:fermilab-mc-1-muon-campus.summary_technical: MC-1 building on the Fermilab site (Muon Campus), housing the Muon g-2 (E989) storage ring, cryogenics plant and counting room. No official building-specific coordinate was found; the recorded point is the centroid of the MC-1 building as traced in OpenStreetMap (about 40 m precision), shown as approximate.

notes: No official source reachable (checked 2026-09-17; mu2e.fnal.gov returned 403) gives building-level coordinates for the Mu2e hall. The point recorded is a general Fermilab-site geocoder point, not specific to the Mu2e hall.
site:fermilab-mu2e-hall.summary_technical: Mu2e experimental hall on the Fermilab site, housing the production, transport and detector solenoids, straw tracker, crystal calorimeter and cosmic ray veto of the Mu2e experiment. No building-specific sourced coordinate was found; the recorded point is a campus-level approximate point.

notes: Coordinates reuse the same honestly-approximate Fermilab campus point as site:fermilab-main-campus rather than duplicating a fresh geocoder lookup; see coordinates.note.

The hall name ('New Muon 4 (NM4) Hall') is taken from the U.S. DOE categorical-exclusion determination CX-002672 (19 May 2010) for the Drell-Yan SeaQuest project, which describes the E906/SeaQuest spectrometer as proposed for that hall.
site:fermilab-nm4-hall.summary_technical: NM4 Hall on the Fermilab fixed-target beamlines (Batavia, Illinois), housing the SeaQuest/E906 dimuon spectrometer on the 120 GeV Main Injector proton beam; proposed site of the DarkQuest dark-sector upgrade. No surveyed coordinate for this specific hall was found, so the Fermilab campus point is used at reduced precision.

site:grandproto300-dunhuang.summary_technical: Gobi Desert site near Xiaodushan, north of Dunhuang, Gansu, China, hosting the GRANDProto300 prototype radio array; coordinates are the XiaoDuShan site position published by the GRAND Collaboration (E 93.94177°, N 40.99434°), not a surveyed antenna position.

site:gsi-fair-darmstadt-campus.summary_technical: GSI Helmholtzzentrum für Schwerionenforschung, Darmstadt: campus-grade point (centroid of the OSM site outline) for the existing GSI accelerators (UNILAC, SIS18, ESR) and the HADES experiment.

site:hanbit-neos-tendon-gallery.summary_technical: Tendon gallery of Hanbit reactor unit 5, 10 m below ground level directly under the containment-building wall; minimum overburden 20 m.w.e. Marked with a campus-grade plant-centre point.

site:hanford-site.summary_technical: Whole-site point for the Hanford Site (Benton County, Washington), the Manhattan Project plutonium-production site with nine reactors along the Columbia River. site:hanle-gamma-ray-site.summary_technical: Hanle (Ladakh, Himalayas), 4270 m a.s.l.: site of the HAGAR wavefront-sampling array (2008) and the 21 m MACE imaging Cherenkov telescope (2021), the highest-altitude Cherenkov telescopes in the world.

site:hawc-sierra-negra.summary_technical: HAWC array site on the Sierra Negra volcano, Puebla, Mexico, at 4100 m altitude.

site:ihep-beijing-campus.summary_technical: IHEP Beijing campus, 19B Yuquan Road, Shijingshan District, Beijing; hosts BEPC/BEPCII, the BES detectors and the Beijing Synchrotron Radiation Facility. The point is a geocoder (OpenStreetMap/Nominatim) campus marker, about 500 m precision.

site:ill-grenoble-reactor-hall.summary_technical: Reactor hall of the ILL research reactor (58 MW thermal power), Grenoble, France; hosts the Ricochet CEvNS detector array 8.8 m from the reactor core.

site:imb-fairport-mine.summary_technical: Morton Salt mine near Fairport Harbor, Lake County, Ohio, hosting the IMB water Cherenkov detector at 1570 m.w.e. (nearly 2,000 feet underground). The detector hall is not separately geolocated by any source consulted.

site:infn-lnf-frascati.summary_technical: INFN Laboratori Nazionali di Frascati, Via Enrico Fermi 54, Frascati (Rome). Geocoder (OpenStreetMap/Nominatim) polygon centroid, about 500 m precision; hosts DAΦNE, its Beam Test Facility and SPARC_LAB.

site:inr-troitsk-nu-mass-facility.summary_technical: Surface site: Institute for Nuclear Research RAS, Troitsk (Moscow); marked with a campus-grade point.

site:isis-rutherford-appleton.summary_technical: STFC Rutherford Appleton Laboratory campus, Harwell Science and Innovation Campus, Didcot, Oxfordshire (postcode OX11 0QX); site of the ISIS pulsed spallation source and, 1990-2001, of the KARMEN liquid-scintillator neutrino detector at a mean distance of 17.7 m from the ISIS target.

site:j-parc-hadron-hall.summary_technical: Hadron Experimental Facility (Hadron Hall) at J-PARC, Tokai-mura, Ibaraki, fed by the 50 GeV Main Ring slow-extracted beam; hosts COMET Phase-I among other hadron/kaon experiments. site:j-parc-main-ring.summary_technical: Surface site at Tokai-mura, Naka-gun, Ibaraki, holding the linac, the 3 GeV RCS, the 30 GeV main ring and the neutrino experimental facility (target station, decay volume, beam dump).

site:j-parc-mlf.summary_technical: J-PARC MLF (3 GeV RCS-fed muon and neutron facility, surface building); hosts the muon beamlines used by the J-PARC muon g-2/EDM experiment (H line, H2 area) and DeeMe. Location is the OSM building centroid, approximate.

site:j-parc-neutrino-near-detector-hall.summary_technical: Vertical pit 17.5 m in diameter and 37 m deep, 280 m downstream of the T2K production target, housing the on-axis INGRID modules and the off-axis ND280 detector at 2.5 degrees.

site:jaduguda-underground-science-labora.summary_technical: JUSL, 555 m deep; the point recorded is the centre of the town of Jaduguda, not the laboratory.

site:jinr-dubna-campus.summary_technical: JINR, Dubna: institute-level point (OSM node of the JINR office); laboratories are spread over the town, the high-energy accelerators being at the VBLHEP site to the north-east.

site:jlab-hall-b.summary_technical: CEBAF experimental Hall B (Jefferson Lab building 94): a dome-roofed experimental hall, partly below grade, receiving the recirculated CEBAF electron beam. Point = centroid of the City of Newport News building footprint (about 50 m precision).

site:jlab-hall-c.summary_technical: CEBAF experimental Hall C (Jefferson Lab building 96): a dome-roofed experimental hall, partly below grade, receiving the recirculated CEBAF electron beam. Point = centroid of the City of Newport News building footprint (about 50 m precision).

notes: Hall-level site created for the hadron-2 coverage stream. The same hall is drawn as geometry:jlab-hall-d (map:jefferson-lab); the map's site_ids and that geometry record's site_id were not edited by this stream (for the integrator).
site:jlab-hall-d.summary_technical: CEBAF experimental Hall D (Jefferson Lab building 203): a dome-roofed experimental hall, partly below grade, receiving the recirculated CEBAF electron beam. Point = centroid of the City of Newport News building footprint (about 50 m precision).

site:jlab-newport-news.summary_technical: DOE national-laboratory campus in Newport News, Virginia, hosting the CEBAF recirculating superconducting electron linac.

site:juno-jiangmen-underground-lab.summary_technical: Underground experimental hall of facility:juno-jiangmen, excavated beneath Dashi Hill near Kaiping, Jiangmen, Guangdong, with over 700 m of granite overburden, 52.5-53 km from the Yangjiang and Taishan nuclear power plants.

site:kalinin-npp-reactor-building.summary_technical: Room below the core of a VVER-1000 reactor at the Kalinin NPP, 350 km NW of Moscow; the reactor building supplies about 50 m.w.e. of cosmic-ray shielding. Marked with a campus-grade point.

site:kamioka-candles-lab-d.summary_technical: Lab-D of the Kamioka Underground Laboratory (ICRR, University of Tokyo), 2700 m.w.e.; marked with a campus-grade point for the Kamioka mine.

site:kamioka-hyper-kamiokande-tochibora.summary_technical: Underground site under Mt. Nijuugo-yama in the Tochibora mine; 69 m diameter by 94 m high dome-capped cylindrical cavern, 600 m below surface, 650 m of rock overburden at the detector centre, at the same 2.5 degree off-axis angle to the J-PARC beam as Super-Kamiokande.

C 81, 025807), and is very likely an error or a different overburden metric. It is deliberately not recorded; depth, water-equivalent depth and muon flux below come from the KamLAND paper.
site:kamioka-kamland.summary_technical: Underground cavity within the Kamioka mine (facility:kamioka-observatory), reusing the original Kamiokande excavation, housing the KamLAND liquid-scintillator antineutrino detector.

site:kamioka-mozumi-mine-super-kamiokand.summary_technical: Underground site under the peak of Mt. Ikenoyama with 1000 m of rock (2700 m.w.e.) mean overburden; geodetic position from the GPS survey reported in the Super-Kamiokande detector paper.

site:kek-ps-k2k-beamline.summary_technical: Campus-grade stand-in for the KEK-PS (12 GeV proton synchrotron) and the K2K primary proton line and target station. site:kek-tsukuba-belle-ii.summary_technical: The Tsukuba straight section of the KEKB/SuperKEKB double-ring collider, housing the interaction point and final-focus system; home of the Belle detector (1999-2010) and, after the roll-in of 11 April 2017, of Belle II.

site:khomas-highland-hess.summary_technical: H.E.S.S. array site on Farm Göllschau, Khomas Highland, Namibia, at 23.2717S, 16.5E, 1800 m altitude, about a 2-hour drive south-west of Windhoek.

site:kirchhoff-institute-for-physics-hei.summary_technical: Surface site: Kirchhoff-Institut für Physik, Im Neuenheimer Feld 227, Heidelberg; coordinating institute of ECHo and cleanroom for its MMC arrays; campus-grade point.

site:kitt-peak-mayall-telescope.summary_technical: Position of the Nicholas U. Mayall 4-m telescope on Kitt Peak, Arizona (31.964 N, 111.600 W, 2123.2 m MSL), host of the DESI instrument.

site:km3net-arca-capo-passero.summary_technical: KM3NeT-It deep-sea installation site, ~100 km offshore Portopalo di Capo Passero, Sicily, at 36°16'N 16°06'E, 3500 m depth; hosts the KM3NeT/ARCA detector.

site:km3net-orca-toulon.summary_technical: KM3NeT-Fr deep-sea installation site, ~40 km offshore Toulon, France, at 42°48'N 06°02'E, 2450 m depth; hosts the KM3NeT/ORCA detector.

site:kolar-gold-fields-mines.summary_technical: Deep gold-mine levels at Kolar Gold Fields, Karnataka (Champion Reef mine and others): sites of the 1965 atmospheric-neutrino telescopes and of the Phase I (7000 m.w.e.) and Phase II (6045 m.w.e.) proton-decay detectors. site:ksnl-kuo-sheng-nuclear-power-statio.summary_technical: Kuo-Sheng Nuclear Power Station (Wanli District, New Taipei); KSNL is on the ground floor of the reactor building, 28 m from core #1, ~12 m below sea level (~30 m.w.e.).

site:lanl-fenton-hill-milagro.summary_technical: Fenton Hill site of Los Alamos National Laboratory, about 35 miles west of Los Alamos, at 2630 m altitude (750 g/cm2); location of the Milagro water-Cherenkov observatory.

site:leibstadt-nuclear-power-plant-campu.summary_technical: Surface site of the Leibstadt boiling water reactor, Aargau, Switzerland; hosts the CONUS+ CEvNS detector 20.7 m from the reactor core since November 2023.

site:lhaaso-haizi-mountain.summary_technical: LHAASO array site on Haizi Mountain, Daocheng County, Sichuan, China, at 4410 m altitude.

site:lngs-hall-c.summary_technical: Underground experimental hall of LNGS, about 100 × 20 × 18 m under ~1400 m of rock, one of the laboratory's three main halls (A, B, C).

site:lsbb-rustrel.summary_technical: LSBB galleries under the Grande Montagne of the Plateau d'Albion; deepest hall under 500 m of calcite rock, about 1500 m.w.e. The recorded point is an approximate surface position; the underground galleries extend over kilometres.

site:mainz-institute-of-physics.summary_technical: Surface site: Institut für Physik, Johannes Gutenberg-Universität Mainz (Staudingerweg 7), host of the Mainz MAC-E-filter tritium beta-spectroscopy experiment.

site:mainz-mesa-experimental-hall.summary_technical: Experimentierhalle MESA (CFP I) at Johann-Joachim-Becher-Weg 41, Mainz: campus-grade point of the building for MESA and its experiments P2, MAGIX and DarkMESA.

site:malargue-auger.summary_technical: Headquarters/campus site of the Pierre Auger Observatory in Malargue, Mendoza Province, Argentina; the 3000 km² surface-detector array and fluorescence buildings extend around this administrative point at an average altitude reported elsewhere as roughly 1400 m (not sourced in this record).

site:mcmurdo-ldb-launch-site.summary_technical: NASA long-duration-balloon launch site (LDB Camp / Williams Field) near McMurdo Station, Antarctica, used for the ANITA balloon flights; a launch point, not a detection location.

topic:accelerator-dark-matter-searches.overview: Accelerator searches assume dark-matter particles escape the detector without interacting, leaving missing energy and momentum. At the LHC, ATLAS and CMS look for an imbalance in transverse momentum recoiling against a Standard Model particle, for bumps in dijet or dilepton mass spectra from a mediator, and for excesses in dijet angular distributions; no signal has been seen and limits are set on masses, couplings and cross sections. Fixed-target experiments increasingly probe lighter, sub-GeV dark sectors, where thermal relic targets are sharp and largely model-independent. A collider signal alone cannot prove that what was produced is the cosmological dark matter.

topic:antimatter.overview: Antimatter experiments compare antiparticles and anti-atoms with their matter counterparts, testing charge-parity-time (CPT) invariance and the weak equivalence principle for antimatter. At CERN’s Antiproton Decelerator (AD), which produces low-energy antiprotons for studies of antimatter and “creates” antiatoms, and its ELENA ring, antiprotons are either confined in Penning traps and compared directly with the proton, or combined with positrons to make antihydrogen. ALPHA observed the 1S–2S transition in trapped antihydrogen at a frequency consistent with that expected for hydrogen; BASE measured the antiproton magnetic moment at the parts-per-billion level, consistent with the proton’s; and ALPHA-g found that released antihydrogen atoms fall towards Earth like ordinary matter. None of these measurements has found a matter–antimatter difference.

topic:astroparticle-physics.overview: Astroparticle physics uses the universe as a laboratory. Cosmic rays are a non-thermal population pervading the universe, with charged-particle energies from tens of MeV to close to 1 ZeV; gamma rays and high-energy neutrinos are detected alongside them, and combining these messengers with gravitational waves is called multi-messenger astrophysics. Instruments include extensive air-shower arrays, atmospheric fluorescence detectors, imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes, cubic-kilometre neutrino telescopes in ice and water, and space-borne spectrometers. Central questions are the origin of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays, the identity of the sources of astrophysical neutrinos, and astrophysical signatures of dark matter and of new light particles.

topic:atmospheric-neutrinos.overview: Cosmic rays interacting in the atmosphere produce mesons whose decays yield muon and electron neutrinos and antineutrinos over a very wide energy range and over baselines from a few tens of kilometres for downward-going neutrinos to the Earth diameter for upward-going ones. Because the same detector sees both, the zenith-angle and energy dependence of the observed rates maps the oscillation pattern directly. Atmospheric samples constrain the atmospheric mixing angle and mass-squared difference, and, through matter effects during passage through the Earth, carry sensitivity to the neutrino mass ordering. Flux predictions rely on cosmic-ray spectra and hadronic-interaction models.

topic:axions-alps.overview: Axions and axion-like particles are hypothetical light bosons arising from the spontaneous breaking of a global symmetry; a small explicit breaking gives them mass. The QCD axion, from the Peccei-Quinn mechanism, is of particular interest because it offers a compelling scheme to preserve CP symmetry in QCD, and the cold dark matter of the universe may consist of axions. Couplings to Standard Model particles are suppressed by the symmetry-breaking scale, so the particles interact very weakly and detecting them would open a window on physics far beyond accelerator reach. Searches run in laboratories, in stars and in the Galactic halo.

topic:b-physics.overview: The b quark is the lighter member of the third-generation doublet, so b-flavored hadrons decay through generation-changing transitions; loop and box diagrams, flavor oscillations and large CP asymmetries are all accessible. Measurements cover production and spectroscopy, lifetimes, mixing, hadronic, rare hadronic and electroweak-penguin decays. Semileptonic decays determine the CKM elements Vcb and Vub, where inclusive and exclusive determinations remain inconsistent enough that the Particle Data Group scales the averaged uncertainty. Measured b to s lepton-pair branching fractions sit consistently below Standard Model expectations, while lepton-universality ratios, once discrepant, are now consistent after a background reassessment.

topic:cevns.overview: In coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering a low-energy neutrino scatters from a nucleus acting as a single particle. The total cross section is large by neutrino standards, but the process eluded detection for four decades because the nuclear recoil deposits only about a keV. COHERENT observed it at 6.7σ in 2017 using a 14.6 kg caesium-iodide scintillator at the Oak Ridge Spallation Neutron Source, and derived improved constraints on non-standard neutrino interactions with quarks. The process bears on nuclear structure and astrophysics as well as particle physics, and sets an irreducible neutrino background for dark-matter detectors.

topic:charm-physics.overview: Charm hadrons provide the only accessible up-type-quark system in which meson mixing and CP violation can be studied. A meson created as a D⁰ time-evolves into a D̄⁰, and the mixing parameters are measured to be small and positive. CP violation in decay has been established in the difference of asymmetries for D⁰ to K⁺K⁻ and D⁰ to π⁺π⁻, with the Particle Data Group quoting (-0.159 ± 0.029) per cent. Interpretation is limited because long-distance contributions are not calculable from first principles. Charm decays also provide decay constants, form factors and precise Vcs and Vcd.

topic:cmb.overview: The cosmic microwave background, discovered in 1965, dominates the photon number and energy content of the radiation reaching us from beyond the Galaxy. Its spectrum is very well described by a blackbody with T = 2.7255 K, with temperature anisotropies at the 10^-5 level and polarization anisotropies at the 10^-6 level and below. After the COBE, WMAP and Planck satellites, ground-based and balloon-borne experiments, notably the Atacama Cosmology Telescope and the South Pole Telescope, extended maps to small angular scales; the PDG states that the programme to map temperature anisotropies is effectively wrapping up and that attention is increasingly focusing on polarization. Polarization splits into E modes and B modes: inflationary scalar perturbations give only E modes, whereas tensor perturbations generate roughly equal amounts of E and B, so a non-zero primordial B-mode signal would measure the gravitational-wave contribution and potentially the energy scale of inflation. CMB lensing converts E modes into B modes, complicating the extraction of a tensor signal. The current limit on the tensor-to-scalar ratio is r < ~0.04 from BICEP/Keck Array and Planck data, and experiments including the Simons Observatory are expected to push the sensitivity toward r ~ 0.001.

topic:collider-bsm-searches.overview: Direct searches look for hypothetical new particles produced in collisions and identified by their decay products. Supersymmetry, one of the most studied extensions, would pair every Standard Model fermion and gauge boson with a partner differing by half a unit of spin: squarks, sleptons, gluinos, and the charginos and neutralinos formed by mixing gauginos with higgsinos. Since no such particle has been seen, supersymmetry would have to be broken. Other targets include heavy gauge bosons, leptoquarks, vector-like quarks, extra Higgs bosons, extra dimensions and compositeness. Results are reported as cross-section limits interpreted in simplified or complete models.

topic:collider-physics.overview: Collider physics studies particle collisions at the highest centre-of-mass energies reachable in the laboratory. LHC Run 3 began in July 2022 at 13.6 TeV, building on electron-positron data from LEP and SLC and on the proton-antiproton Tevatron programme. The field combines precision Standard Model measurements - of the Higgs boson, the electroweak sector, the top quark and QCD - with direct searches for new particles. Events are reconstructed as jets, leptons, photons and missing transverse momentum and compared with perturbative predictions. The Snowmass 2021 Energy Frontier report and the 2023 P5 report set out the next steps, including the High-Luminosity LHC and a proposed offshore Higgs factory.

topic:cosmic-rays.overview: Cosmic rays are a non-thermal population of particles pervading the universe, characterised by their spectrum, composition and arrival directions. Charged cosmic rays extend from tens of MeV to close to 1 ZeV, with an intensity of about 10⁴ per square metre per second per steradian above 1 GeV and a steeply falling power-law spectrum. The striking spectral features are the knee at a few PeV, where the index changes from about 2.7 to about 3, a second knee near 100 PeV, and the ankle at a few EeV; the flux is largely suppressed above a few tens of EeV. Arrival directions are mostly isotropic.

topic:cosmology.overview: Observational cosmology has established a precision cosmological model. The Universe is taken to be a perturbed Robertson-Walker space-time governed by Einstein's equations, with a matter budget built from baryons, photons, neutrinos, dark matter and dark energy; typical comparisons of models with data now feature between five and ten parameters. In the flat LambdaCDM model that the Particle Data Group adopts, fits to Planck CMB temperature, polarization and lensing data give a matter density parameter of 0.315 ± 0.007 and a cosmological-constant density parameter of 0.685 ± 0.007; adding ACT CMB data and DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations moves them to 0.300 ± 0.004 and 0.700 ± 0.004. The highest-precision CMB data come from the Planck satellite, with the ground-based Atacama Cosmology Telescope and South Pole Telescope extending to smaller angular scales, while large galaxy surveys add baryon acoustic oscillations and weak lensing. The PDG notes that LambdaCDM contains two ingredients, dark matter and dark energy, not yet verified by laboratory experiments, and that existing indications against it, the Hubble tension and hints of evolving dark energy, are not securely established.

topic:cp-violation.overview: CP combines charge conjugation with parity. The weak interactions violate C and P maximally but preserve CP in most processes; CP violation appears in interference effects, discovered in neutral kaon decays in 1964 and established later in B decays (2001) and D decays (2019). In the Standard Model all quark-sector CP violation follows from one irreducible phase of the unitary CKM matrix, whose unitarity relations form triangles. Experiments test whether magnitudes measured in semileptonic and leptonic decays and mixing, and angles measured from CP asymmetries, describe a single consistent triangle.

topic:dark-energy.overview: In the late 1990s supernova surveys by two independent teams provided direct evidence for accelerating cosmic expansion, and CMB evidence for a spatially flat Universe cemented the case. A cosmological constant, with equation-of-state parameter w = -1, is the simplest explanation; a new form of energy with negative pressure, or a modification of General Relativity, are alternatives, and the PDG follows common usage in treating "dark energy" as a catch-all term for the origin of cosmic acceleration. The main probes are Type Ia supernovae, baryon acoustic oscillations, weak lensing, galaxy clusters and redshift-space distortions. The PDG describes most Stage III experiments as having completed observations; DESI began full operations in May 2021 and its three-year data set includes over 30 million galaxies and quasars. Within LambdaCDM the DESI Collaboration reports a tension of about 2 sigma between BAO and CMB alone, and in all the data combinations the PDG shows, the LambdaCDM values (w0 = -1, wa = 0) lie outside the 95% contour of the w0wa fit; the quoted significance depends on the combination, from 2.8 sigma to 4.2 sigma with supernovae added, and 3.1 sigma for DESI plus CMB. The PDG treats the indications of evolving dark energy as not securely established.

topic:dark-matter.overview: Cosmological models include a non-baryonic, electromagnetically near-neutral matter species with negligible velocity, generically called cold dark matter. In the benchmark LambdaCDM fit adopted by the Particle Data Group it accounts for 26.4 per cent of the critical density and 84.4 per cent of the total matter density; only a small fraction of the non-baryonic content, the three Standard Model neutrinos, is identified. Its particle nature is hypothetical. Searches follow three complementary strategies - direct detection of Galactic dark matter scattering underground, indirect detection of annihilation or decay products, and production at accelerators. No non-gravitational detection has been established.

topic:dark-photons-dark-sectors.overview: A dark sector is a set of hypothetical particles neutral under the Standard Model forces, connected to ordinary matter only through weak portal interactions. The dark photon is a conjectured gauge boson of such a sector, detectable through kinetic mixing with the ordinary photon; vector, Higgs and neutrino portals and axion-like-particle portals are the minimal renormalizable or dimension-five options. Because such sectors are generically weakly coupled and can naturally have MeV-to-GeV masses while respecting Standard Model symmetries, they are only mildly constrained by high-energy collider data, and intensity-frontier experiments, including those on neutrino beams, offer the strongest reach.

topic:detector-rd.overview: Detector research and development turns measurement requirements into working technology. The Particle Data Group review chapters catalogue the working principles and performance of the main families: vacuum, gaseous, solid-state and superconducting photon detectors; organic and inorganic scintillators; Cherenkov, gaseous and transition-radiation detectors; time projection chambers including liquid-argon ones; large rare-event time projection chambers; sub-kelvin detectors; and low-radioactivity background techniques. The Snowmass 2021 Instrumentation Frontier report groups the needed research and development for collider, neutrino, rare-process and cosmic experiments and lays out priority areas for keeping that capability healthy.

topic:direct-dark-matter-detection.overview: Direct detection looks for nuclear or electron recoils left when Galactic dark matter passes through a low-background detector operated deep underground. Interpretation needs the local dark-matter density and velocity distribution, which are themselves uncertain at the level of a factor of a few. Dual-phase liquid-xenon time projection chambers currently lead for masses around tens of GeV: the Particle Data Group tabulates a spin-independent cross-section limit of 2.2 × 10⁻⁴⁸ cm² near 40 GeV from LUX-ZEPLIN, with XENONnT and PandaX-4T close behind. Sensitivity is approaching the irreducible background from coherent neutrino scattering, which those detectors have now begun to observe.

topic:electroweak-physics.overview: The electroweak Standard Model is a renormalizable gauge theory based on SU(2) x U(1). Because the W and Z masses, the Higgs and top masses, the electromagnetic and strong couplings and the weak mixing angle are related through radiative corrections, a global fit tests the theory at the quantum level. Inputs include low-energy observables, Z-pole lineshape parameters and asymmetries from LEP and SLC, W and Z masses and widths and W and Z decays. The Particle Data Group fit does not include the CDF Run II W-mass measurement, which dominates the tension among direct determinations.

topic:flavor-physics.overview: Flavor physics studies transitions between the three generations of quarks and leptons. In the Standard Model the masses and mixings of quarks have a common origin in the Yukawa interactions with the Higgs condensate, and quark flavor change is governed by the unitary Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix, which carries three real parameters and one complex phase. Flavor-changing neutral currents arise only through loops, so meson mixing, rare decays and CP asymmetries in kaon, charm and beauty hadrons are sensitive to hypothetical new particles far above direct collider reach - the Snowmass Rare Processes and Precision Frontier report quotes scales up to thousands of TeV.

topic:gamma-rays.overview: Gamma rays trace non-thermal processes and identify sites where particles are accelerated. The Particle Data Group counts roughly 6660 catalogued sources above 50 MeV and about 300 at TeV energies, plus diffuse Galactic and extragalactic emission that largely follows power laws. Space-borne pair-conversion telescopes cover the MeV-GeV range; above about 100 GeV the flux is too low for satellites, so ground-based imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes and particle-detector arrays observe the air showers gamma rays initiate. Observations address particle acceleration in supernova remnants, pulsars, binaries, active galaxies and gamma-ray bursts, and are also used to search for new physics.

topic:hadron-structure.overview: Hadron structure and spectroscopy asks how the strongly interacting particles arise from quarks and gluons. Structure experiments scatter electrons, muons and hadron beams off nucleons and nuclei to map their momentum, spatial and spin structure; the proton spin puzzle and the transverse structure of the nucleon remain central open questions. The planned Electron-Ion Collider is designed to collide high-energy electron beams with proton and ion beams, reaching the regions of nucleons and nuclei where structure is dominated by gluons, and polarized beams give access to the spatial and spin structure of the proton, neutron and light ions. Spectroscopy tests whether QCD's allowed exotic states exist beyond the quark-antiquark and three-quark scheme: tetraquarks, pentaquarks, hybrids with active gluonic degrees of freedom and glueballs, and a 2019 review counted many new hadrons, found in the preceding fifteen years in the quarkonium spectrum, that do not match the expected properties of ordinary states. Parity-violating electron scattering, in which the parity-violating asymmetry isolates the weak interaction, measures the weak charge of the proton and the neutron skin of heavy nuclei, linking this topic to precision electroweak tests.

topic:heavy-ion-physics-qgp.overview: Heavy-ion collisions quickly form a droplet of quark-gluon plasma with a remarkably small viscosity - the hottest and smallest droplet of liquid made on Earth. The physics spans highly energetic quarks and gluons described by perturbative QCD down to a bath of strongly interacting gluons at lower energy scales; those gluons thermalize quickly and form the plasma, while energetic partons traverse it and emerge as jets. Analysing the final particles in different ways probes the plasma properties and the multi-scale QCD dynamics governing its formation and evolution. The Snowmass Energy Frontier report stresses the connection to nuclear structure and the nuclear medium.

topic:heavy-neutral-leptons.overview: Non-zero neutrino masses point to the likely existence of additional Standard Model neutral fermions. When such hypothetical states are heavy enough that they cannot be produced in oscillations they are called heavy neutral leptons. They would mix with the active neutrinos and could be produced in meson and tau decays, in beam dumps and at colliders, then decay to visible final states after a possibly macroscopic flight distance. Searches span beta decay, accelerator experiments and colliders, and are complemented by astrophysical and cosmological constraints; the parameter space is usually presented as mixing angle versus mass for each lepton flavour.

topic:higgs-physics.overview: Electroweak symmetry breaking posits a self-interacting complex scalar doublet whose CP-even neutral component acquires a vacuum expectation value of about 246 GeV; the remaining component is the Higgs boson, discovered at the LHC in 2012 with a mass near 125 GeV. Measurements cover inclusive, differential and simplified-template cross sections in each production and decay channel, couplings expressed in the kappa framework or as effective field theory coefficients, the mass, the width, and spin and CP properties. The Higgs self-coupling and possible exotic or beyond-Standard-Model Higgs decays remain open.

topic:high-energy-astrophysical-neutrino.overview: Astrophysical neutrinos have energies far beyond those of solar, supernova, atmospheric and accelerator neutrinos, and probe fundamental physics from the TeV to the EeV scale and beyond. Because they are weakly interacting and electrically neutral they escape regions opaque to electromagnetic radiation and point back to their sources, carrying unique information about extreme non-thermal environments. The Particle Data Group notes that the observed distribution is largely isotropic, with evidence for two extragalactic sources and for a contribution from the Galactic plane. Detection uses cubic-kilometre Cherenkov arrays in ice and water, with radio and air-shower techniques targeting the highest energies.

topic:indirect-dark-matter-detection.overview: Indirect detection looks for Standard Model particles produced by hypothetical dark-matter annihilation or decay in astrophysical environments, using photons, charged cosmic rays and neutrinos. Substantial advances in observational data sets, complemented by numerical simulations, have enabled strong constraints on particle models and revealed several intriguing hints of possible signals whose astrophysical interpretation remains debated. Targets include dwarf spheroidal galaxies, the Galactic Centre, galaxy clusters, the Sun and the diffuse background. Limits depend strongly on the assumed dark-matter density profile of the target and on the modelling of astrophysical backgrounds and cosmic-ray propagation.

topic:instrumentation.overview: Instrumentation covers the sensors, electronics, readout and analysis techniques that set what an experiment can measure. The Particle Data Group treats accelerator and non-accelerator detectors in separate review chapters covering photon detectors, organic and inorganic scintillators, Cherenkov and gaseous detectors, liquid-argon time projection chambers, air-shower and atmospheric-fluorescence detectors, neutrino telescopes, sub-kelvin detectors and low-radioactivity background techniques. The Snowmass 2021 Instrumentation Frontier report organises the research and development needed for future collider, neutrino, rare-process and cosmic experiments, and identifies priority areas for sustaining that capability.

topic:lepton-flavor-violation.overview: Charged lepton flavour violating transitions would be a clear signal of physics beyond the Standard Model, in which they are forbidden or utterly negligible. Searches cover a variety of channels, the most sensitive involving muons - radiative decay to an electron and a photon, decay to three electrons, and conversion to an electron in the field of a nucleus - as well as tau decays and transitions of heavier states. No positive evidence has been found. The Snowmass topical group report notes that these processes already probe mass scales up to thousands of TeV, so an observation would be unambiguous evidence of new particles.

topic:long-lived-particles.overview: Particles beyond the Standard Model can generically have lifetimes long compared with weak-scale Standard Model particles. Produced at the LHC, such long-lived particles would decay far from the primary proton-proton interaction vertex, giving signatures unlike those of the promptly decaying particles most searches target. Identifying them needs customized techniques: significantly displaced decay vertices, tracks with atypical properties, and short track segments. A joint effort by theorists and the ATLAS, CMS and LHCb collaborations, together with dedicated experiments such as MoEDAL, milliQan, MATHUSLA, CODEX-b and FASER, has surveyed the signature space to avoid overlooking discovery avenues.

topic:multimessenger-astrophysics.overview: Multimessenger astrophysics combines photons, gravitational waves, neutrinos and cosmic rays, which carry inherently complementary information about individual cosmic sources and about source populations. The Particle Data Group describes combined observations of charged cosmic rays, gamma rays, neutrinos and gravitational waves as giving valuable insight into the most extreme astrophysical environments. Key achievements include measuring the ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray spectrum to the highest observable energies, discovering the diffuse high-energy neutrino background, the first direct gravitational-wave detections, and the first joint electromagnetic and gravitational-wave identification. The practical challenge is rapid alert distribution and follow-up across observatories.

topic:muon-precision-physics.overview: Quantum loop effects make the muon magnetic moment deviate slightly from the Dirac value, and the anomaly can be both measured in storage rings and predicted precisely, testing the Standard Model at loop level. After the final Fermilab E989 result the experimental world average is 116 592 071.5(14.5) × 10⁻¹¹, against a Standard Model prediction of 116 592 033(62) × 10⁻¹¹ compiled by the Muon g-2 Theory Initiative; the difference, 38(63) × 10⁻¹¹, is compatible with zero and now dominated by theory uncertainty. A permanent electric dipole moment would directly signal time-reversal and, assuming CPT, CP violation; only upper limits exist.

topic:neutrino-interactions.overview: Neutrino cross sections are an essential ingredient of every neutrino experiment, and uncertainties in neutrino-nucleus scattering remain a dominant systematic in oscillation measurements. The Particle Data Group surveys measurements from roughly 0.1 to 1000 GeV with emphasis on inclusive, deep inelastic, quasi-elastic and resonance-production processes on a range of nuclear targets. Nuclear effects distort the observed kinematics and bias reconstructed neutrino energy, so precise flux estimates, theoretical input and complementary electron-nucleus scattering data are all needed. Modern measurements come from ArgoNeuT, ICARUS, MicroBooNE, MINERvA, NOvA, T2K, IceCube and FASERnu, among others.

topic:neutrino-mass-direct.overview: Oscillations fix only mass-squared differences, so the absolute scale must come from elsewhere. The only model-independent information comes from energy-momentum conservation in weak decays: a non-zero mass distorts the beta spectrum near its endpoint, and tritium is favoured because its decay energy is small. KATRIN has found no indication of a non-zero mass and sets an upper limit of 0.45 eV at 90 per cent confidence, improving on the roughly 2.2 eV bounds from Mainz and Troitsk, and should approach a sensitivity near 0.3 eV. Holmium-163 electron-capture calorimetry and cyclotron-radiation spectroscopy are complementary approaches.

topic:neutrino-oscillations.overview: Neutrino flavour oscillations follow from neutrinos having mass and from flavour states being superpositions of mass states, described by a lepton mixing matrix with three angles, one Dirac CP phase and, for Majorana neutrinos, two further phases. Two independent mass-squared differences are measured. Solar, atmospheric, accelerator and reactor experiments each constrain different combinations, and propagation through matter modifies the pattern, notably through the Mikheyev-Smirnov-Wolfenstein effect for solar neutrinos. A combined three-neutrino analysis leaves the mass ordering, the octant of the largest atmospheric angle, and the size of leptonic CP violation as the principal open questions.

topic:neutrino-physics.overview: Neutrino physics addresses the least understood Standard Model fermions. Oscillation experiments established that neutrinos have mass and mix, which the minimal Standard Model does not accommodate; oscillations depend only on mass-squared differences, so the absolute mass scale and the Dirac or Majorana nature must be probed by other means. Sources span reactors, accelerator beams, the Sun, the atmosphere, supernovae, the Earth and distant cosmic accelerators, covering more than twenty orders of magnitude in energy. Detection uses charged-current and neutral-current scattering in large water, ice, scintillator and liquid-argon detectors, and precision spectroscopy of weak decays.

topic:neutrinoless-double-beta-decay.overview: Neutrinoless double beta decay is a hypothetical ultra-rare nuclear decay that would violate total lepton number by two units and require neutrinos to be Majorana particles. Under the assumption that Majorana neutrino mass is the only low-energy source of lepton-number violation, the half-life relates to an effective Majorana mass through phase space and nuclear matrix elements, whose uncertainty spreads the inferred mass by a factor of two to three; other new-physics mechanisms could dominate instead. No decay has been seen. The strongest limits come from xenon-136 and germanium-76, exceeding 10²⁶ years.

topic:neutron-physics.overview: Free-neutron experiments at reactors, spallation sources and ultracold-neutron (UCN) sources probe the Standard Model at low energy. Dubbers and Schmidt note that experiments with cold and ultracold neutrons have reached a precision at which problems beyond the Standard Model become accessible to experimental investigation, with neutron decay measurements, the neutron electric dipole moment and baryogenesis among the linked questions. A permanent neutron EDM would signal time-reversal violation and, assuming CPT symmetry, CP violation; the nEDM experiment at PSI measured d_n = (0.0 ± 1.1 stat ± 0.2 sys) × 10⁻²⁶ e cm, consistent with zero. The UCNτ experiment at Los Alamos measured the free-neutron lifetime as 877.75 ± 0.28 (stat) +0.22/−0.16 (syst) s, a precision at which lifetime measurements address refinements in the Standard Model description of neutron decay.

topic:nuclear-and-heavy-ion.overview: This area covers the interface between nuclear and particle physics where the questions are materially particle-physics questions: quantum chromodynamics at extreme temperature and density in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, and the structure of nucleons and nuclei. Heavy-ion collisions quickly form a droplet of quark-gluon plasma with a remarkably small viscosity; energetic partons traversing that plasma emerge as jets whose modification probes its properties. The Snowmass Energy Frontier QCD and heavy-ion report emphasises the connections to nucleon structure and to the Electron-Ion Collider. Low-energy nuclear structure and applied nuclear science are outside the atlas scope.

topic:nucleon-decay.overview: Nucleon decay is the hypothetical decay of a proton, or of a neutron bound in a nucleus, into lighter particles such as a positron or a muon together with a pion. The Standard Model forbids it, but proton instability is a generic prediction of unified models of particle interactions: the review of Nath and Fileviez Perez surveys the status of proton stability in non-supersymmetric and supersymmetric grand unified theories, in extra-dimensional unification and in string and M-theory models, and lists the proposed next-generation proton-decay experiments (Hyper-Kamiokande, UNO, MEMPHYS, ICARUS, LANNDD and LENA). No decay has been observed. The Super-Kamiokande analysis of 450 kton-years of data found no candidate for p to e+ pi0 and one for p to mu+ pi0, consistent with the atmospheric-neutrino background, and set 90 % confidence-level lower limits on the partial lifetimes of 2.4 x 10^34 years (p to e+ pi0) and 1.6 x 10^34 years (p to mu+ pi0). Searches therefore need very large detector masses and long exposures deep underground.

topic:precision-and-rare-processes.overview: This area covers searches for extremely rare processes and for tiny deviations from the Standard Model, studied with intense sources and high-precision detectors. Quantum corrections from hypothetical heavy or feebly interacting states shift observables such as the muon anomalous magnetic moment, electric dipole moments and rare-decay rates, so measurements at the part-per-billion or 10⁻¹³ branching-fraction level probe mass scales far above collider energies. The same facilities search directly for light, long-lived or feebly coupled states - heavy neutral leptons, dark photons and other long-lived particles - at beam dumps, fixed-target experiments and the forward regions of colliders.

topic:qcd.overview: Quantum chromodynamics is the SU(3) gauge field theory describing the strong interactions of coloured quarks and gluons within the Standard Model. Its coupling runs, so hard scattering is computed perturbatively while confinement and hadron structure need lattice QCD or non-perturbative modelling. The Particle Data Group review organises experimental QCD around hadronic final-state observables and collider measurements, and determines the strong coupling from hadronic tau decays, heavy-quarkonium decays, parton-distribution fits, electron-positron final states, hadron-collider observables, the electroweak precision fit and lattice QCD, which are then combined into a world average.

topic:rare-kaon-physics.overview: Rare kaon decays divide into searches for explicit Standard Model violations, the golden modes, other constraints on Standard Model parameters, and studies of low-energy strong interactions. The golden modes K⁺ to π⁺ neutrino antineutrino and K_L to π⁰ neutrino antineutrino are dominated by short-distance physics and calculable with negligible theoretical uncertainty. NA62 at the CERN SPS reported in 2026, using data through 2024, a branching fraction of 9.6 (+1.9/−1.8) × 10⁻¹¹ against a Standard Model estimate of (8.2 ± 0.6) × 10⁻¹¹; KOTO at J-PARC pursues the neutral mode. Lepton-flavor and lepton-number violating kaon decays are also searched for.

topic:reactor-neutrinos.overview: Nuclear reactors are intense sources of electron antineutrinos from the beta decays of fission fragments, detected mainly through inverse beta decay in liquid scintillator. Reactor antineutrinos provided the first direct detection of the neutrino, and later experiments found clear evidence for oscillation, giving unique input to neutrino mass and mixing. Kilometre-baseline experiments measured the smallest mixing angle, and a medium-baseline detector about 53 km from two Chinese power plants is designed to determine the mass ordering from the fine structure of the disappearance spectrum. Ongoing questions include reactor flux and spectrum predictions and short-baseline searches for hypothetical sterile states.

topic:solar-neutrinos.overview: The Sun produces energy through two main chains, the proton-proton chain and the CNO cycle, each emitting electron neutrinos with characteristic spectra; mean energies are low, with the pp neutrinos carrying only a fraction of an MeV. Radiochemical and water-Cherenkov experiments found fewer electron neutrinos than the standard solar model predicts, which is explained by flavour conversion, enhanced inside the Sun by the Mikheyev-Smirnov-Wolfenstein matter effect. Borexino, a liquid-scintillator detector at Gran Sasso operating from 2007 to 2021, made the first real-time measurements of several low-energy components, including the CNO neutrinos.

topic:sterile-neutrinos.overview: Sterile neutrinos are hypothetical neutral fermions without Standard Model gauge interactions that could mix with the three active neutrinos; the Particle Data Group treats light sterile states as one way of extending the Standard Model to give neutrinos mass, and devotes a section to additional neutrinos at the eV scale. Four canonical short-baseline anomalies - from decay-at-rest and decay-in-flight accelerator experiments, from reactors and from radioactive-source gallium measurements - remain unresolved, and the Snowmass white paper argues that disappearance and appearance data do not fit consistently within a minimal 3+1 picture. Heavier sterile states are candidate dark matter.

topic:supernova-neutrinos.overview: Neutrinos govern the infall of a collapsing stellar core, help trigger and fuel the explosion, and drive the cooling and deleptonization of the newly formed neutron star, so they offer the only direct probe of conditions at the centre of a supernova. A core-collapse supernova produces a burst of neutrinos of all flavours in the few-tens-of-MeV range over seconds. Extracting source properties requires separating them from effects imprinted on the way out: self-induced flavour conversion from neutrino-neutrino interactions in the deepest regions, and matter effects in the envelope. Neutrinos from past cosmic supernovae form a diffuse background that is also observable in principle.

topic:top-physics.overview: The top quark is the weak-isospin partner of the bottom quark, with a mass of about 172.5 GeV and therefore a Yukawa coupling of order unity. Being heavier than the W boson it is the only quark that decays weakly into a real W and a b quark, and its lifetime is shorter than the timescale of non-perturbative strong interactions, so it does not hadronize and its spin information survives into its decay products. Abundant LHC production enables precise measurements of the mass, couplings, production cross sections and branching ratios; the Particle Data Group notes a 1.7σ tension between the top-quark mass inferred indirectly from the electroweak fit and the value combined directly from LHC measurements.
